So, do you know what’s on TV tonight? I saw this show about food and it’s like,  so  good. I think it’s called  Cooking with the Stars  or something. It's like, a reality show where people cook, and they get judged by famous chefs. It’s actually pretty funny, and there’s this one guy who’s like,  so  bad at cooking, but he’s so confident. It’s ridiculous. Oh, I’ve seen that. It’s not bad, honestly. I mean, I don’t know if I’d want to be on it, but it’s kind of entertaining. Though I still can’t get over the guy who accidentally burned his own house down in the first episode. That was  so  dramatic. Oh, I’ve seen that too. He was basically just trying to make scrambled eggs and ended up with a smoke alarm going off. I still laugh every time I think about it. You know, I think the show’s kind of like a comedy, even if it’s about cooking. It’s like  MasterChef  meets  The Great British Bake Off  with more drama. Yeah, it is. And the host is like, this super serious guy who always says, “This is about passion, not perfection.” But then he’s like,  so  strict with the contestants. It’s like the opposite of fun. But somehow, it still works. I don’t know, I think the people who watch it are just looking for something to laugh at. Like, it’s not really about the cooking, it’s about the chaos. I mean, it’s kind of like watching  Keeping Up with the Kardashians , but with food. Exactly! And the fact that they’re all from different countries too—that’s part of the fun. One episode had this guy from Germany who insisted on using his grandma’s recipe for sausages, even though the others were like,  what are you doing?  And he was all, “This is how it’s done.” Oh, I remember that. He ended up burning the sausages and then tried to blame the chef. It was  so  funny. I think the chef just rolled his eyes and said, “Can you just get your own knife?” Yeah, and then the guy just stormed off. It was the most dramatic thing I’ve seen all week. I mean, it’s not even a real cooking show, it’s just a bunch of people trying to make food and getting into arguments.

I've been thinking a lot about that trip to London, you know. I was just talking to old Fred about it, and he said he'd love to go again. I think it's about time we actually did it, don’t you? Oh, I agree. I’ve been meaning to suggest it for ages. But I don’t know, with all the money problems and the house to sell, I just haven’t had the chance. But I still think the trip to London would be a better idea. You know, for the history, the museums, and watching the football. Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that too. But I’m not sure if it's the best idea. With the election coming up and all the politics going on, I’d rather just stay local for now. Although, I did hear someone at the school talking about a new development near the town. Maybe we could look into buying a house there. You know, I’ve been thinking about selling the old one as well. It’s about time I got rid of it. I mean, the garden’s in a bit of a state, and the roof is leaking again. I’d rather have something a bit more modern. That’s true. I was thinking the same thing. But I just don’t know where to start. I’ve been looking online, but it all seems so expensive. I don’t know if we can afford that kind of money. Maybe we can look into buying something cheaper. Some of the estates in the town are getting a bit run-down, and the prices are not as high as they used to be. If we go at the right time, we might even get a good deal.

So, do you know what’s going to happen with the baby? I mean, it’s only a week old, but I feel like we’re already drowning in bottles and wipes. I know, it’s terrifying. I can’t even remember the last time I did anything without a baby in the way. I mean, I’ve been on maternity leave, but I still feel like I’ve lost my identity. I’ve been so busy with feeding and changing and just trying to keep up with the basics. Yeah, I can totally relate. It’s like the whole world has shifted. I mean, I went to a seminar last week about baby feeding, and it was the most intense thing I’ve ever done. I mean, I’ve never had to worry about whether I’m producing enough milk or if the baby is getting enough nutrition. It’s like a whole new language. Oh, you’re not the only one. My sister said she’s still confused about the whole thing. I asked her if she thought the baby was getting enough, and she just said, “I hope so.” I mean, you get so used to the routine, and then you don’t even think about it anymore. I know, it’s so easy to take for granted. When I got home from work yesterday, I had to check the baby’s weight, and I was like, “Is this real?” It’s so bizarre how something that’s so small can have such an impact on your life. And then there’s also the whole aspect of family. I’ve been trying to get my mum to come over more often, but she’s been so busy with her own stuff. It’s like she’s still in denial about the whole situation. She keeps saying, “It’s just a baby, isn’t it?” and I’m like, “Yes, but it’s not just a baby anymore!” I know, it’s so funny how quickly things change. My cousin had her baby a year ago, and she was so stressed about it, but now she’s like, “Oh, it’s all so easy.” I’m not sure if I want to be like that or not. I think it’s just a learning curve. I mean, the baby is still so tiny, and we’re still figuring things out.

Morning everyone. I’ve just made some toast and tea, anyone want some? Morning, love. Yes, I’ll take some tea, thanks. And I think I’ll have a toast as well. I don’t want to be in a situation where I can’t afford something important. That sounds like a good plan. I’ve been thinking about setting up a savings account as well. It’s just hard to keep track of where everything goes, and I know I’ve spent more than I should on some things. I do the same. I think I need to start tracking my spending more carefully. So, do you know what’s happening with the school tests? I’ve been trying to study for maths, but I keep forgetting my times tables. Yeah, I know what you mean. I tried to memorize them last night, and I still got confused between 7 times 8 and 6 times 9. I think I’m just bad at maths. It’s not just you. I think the teacher is making it way too hard. We had to do a science project on plants in class, and I got an A+ on it. I even got to plant some seeds in a pot. That’s great! I can’t wait to see your plant grow. By the way, did you hear about the Christmas play at school? No, what’s that? It’s supposed to be a nativity play, but I think the teacher is going to make it more modern.

Well, I've been meaning to ask you both, what's with the rat puppet? I saw it in the corner of the living room, and it's got more personality than most of the people I know. Oh, that's old Fred. He's been with me since the days when I was a childminder, and I used to use him to entertain the kids. He was a real crowd-pleaser. You know, he's got this little squeaky voice and a big, bushy tail. The kids just loved him. Didn’t you say once that he was a gift from the local church? Or was it the school? He's been through a lot, but he's still in one piece, if you know what I mean. Well, he’s definitely in one piece. I’ve seen him in every room, even in the attic when I was clearing things out last summer. Speaking of clearing things out, I’ve been thinking about getting my eyes tested. I’ve had a bit of trouble seeing clearly lately, especially when reading the newspaper. I don’t want to miss any of the news. I know what you mean. I had my eyes tested a few months ago, and they said I need new glasses. I’ve been meaning to get around to it, but I just haven’t found the time. And I know how much time you both spend reading the paper—especially you, Mike. It’s true. I like to stay up to date with what’s happening in the world. And besides, I can’t afford to miss any of the sports pages. Yeah, that’s right. I remember when I used to run the local bus route, I used to read the paper on the way home. It was a habit I picked up a long time ago. Although, I can’t say I ever read the sports page. I was too busy trying to figure out where the next stop was. That’s typical of you, Bill. Always more focused on where you’re going than what you’re reading. Anyway, I think it’s time I went to the optician. I just need to make an appointment.

So, do you think we’ll get a good view of the canals from here? I mean, it’s a bit crowded in the square, but maybe from the café we can see something. Yeah, I think we’ll be fine. I mean, Venice is always busy, especially in the mornings. But I like this spot—it’s got a nice view of the water and the little boats that go by. Yeah, I can see the boats, but I can’t really tell what’s going on. I mean, what was Venice like before all the tourists came? Do you know? Oh, I do. When I was a kid, the canals were quieter. There were fewer tourists, and people actually lived in the buildings along the water. You could walk down the streets and hear the sounds of the city—people talking, little shops, and of course, the smell of fresh seafood. It wasn’t like this place now, with all the tourists running around and the big cruise ships. Wow, that sounds like a different Venice. I mean, I’ve only been here a couple of times, but I always feel like the city is so full of energy and noise. It is, but it’s also beautiful. The architecture, the way the buildings are built on the water—it’s something you can’t find anywhere else. But I think the real Venice is hidden behind all the tourists. You have to go to the quieter areas, the ones that aren’t on the tourist maps. That sounds like a good plan. I mean, I’m not sure I want to be in the middle of it all. I’d rather take it slow and really experience the city, not just take pictures for Instagram. Exactly. I think that’s a good idea. Maybe we can plan to visit some of the lesser-known parts of Venice tomorrow. I know there’s a little island called Murano that’s known for glass-making. I’ve heard it’s a really peaceful place to walk around. That sounds perfect. I could do with a bit of peace. Also, I heard the food here is amazing. I mean, what’s the best thing to eat in Venice? Oh, there’s so much to choose from. But I think the best is risotto al nero di seppia. It’s squid ink risotto—it’s dark, creamy, and really tasty.

So, did you go to the gym last week? I saw you on the treadmill, but I didn’t get a chance to say hi. Yeah, I did. I actually felt really good after. I’ve got a few ideas for nights out. Maybe we can do a themed night? Like a 80s night or something? I think it would be fun. That sounds like a great idea! I’ll text you later and let you know what I think.

I just got a text from my daughter. She's got a baby now – a girl, beautiful, just like her mother. I’m so proud of them both. That’s wonderful. I remember when I first saw her – she was so small, so fragile. Just like a little doll. She’s grown up now, isn’t she? Oh yes, she’s got that same stubbornness as her mother, but in a good way. I suppose that’s just how it goes. You know, I was thinking the other day about how different things are now. You know, like, when I was growing up, people were much more nationalistic, and now, with all these international connections… you know, I’ve met so many people from all over the world, even from France. Yes, but I still find it strange how people in France view property and enterprise. I mean, I’ve heard stories about how they treat land in a completely different way. It’s almost like they see it as something sacred, isn’t it? Oh, it’s not just that. I’ve heard they have these anarchists and bureaucrats who just don’t play by the rules. It’s quite a culture shock sometimes. I remember once I met a French visitor in London, and he was fascinated by how everything here is so efficient – the transport, the public services. You know, I think it was Porden who designed the spire of Chichester Cathedral. I remember reading about how it collapsed a few years back. It was quite a big deal. Some said it was due to poor maintenance, others thought it was just bad luck. I suppose it’s about how people take care of their heritage. I had an open day at the museum last week, and there was a photo exhibition of the city. It looked so different back then. I tried to enter an art competition myself last year, but I’m not sure I was good enough. I was just trying to show my perspective of the city through my lens. You know, I’ve also been writing a book – about my experiences living in London and my time in Spain. I visited the Spanish archives a couple of years ago, and the stories I found were so fascinating. They reminded me of our own history – of Philip of Spain and Mary Tudor, how they were connected.

So, do you know what’s on the menu today? I mean, I know it's Chinese, but like... what's the special? Oh, I think it's the stir-fried noodles. Or was it the chicken with vegetables? Well, do you think we've got everything ready for Jonathan's birthday tomorrow? Honestly, I’m still not sure. So, do you know what you're going to do for GCSEs? I’m trying to work it out, but honestly, I’m just so confused. Yeah, I know, me too. Well, I've been meaning to ask you, what do you think about the new internet software they've been pushing? It's supposed to make things easier, but I find it more confusing than ever. I don’t know, mate. I tried it last week and it just messed up my emails. I think I've got more problems with it than with my old system. Yeah, I remember when we had to use those old computers with floppy disks. At least you could tell what was going on. Now it's all just clicks and buttons, and I can't figure out what half of it does. Honestly, I've been using the latest software for years now. It's actually made my work a lot easier. I just have to remember to take regular breaks, or I end up working late into the night. I suppose it's all about adapting, isn't it? I've been trying to learn more about computers, but I’m not sure if I’m ever going to get the hang of it. I still remember the days when you had to type in commands and wait for the screen to respond. You're not alone. I still use a dial-up modem for some things. It's slower, but it works. And it gives me a chance to remember what life was like before all this digital nonsense. I’ve got a new car, you know. Just bought it last month. It's a bit of an old model, but it runs fine. I still prefer the reliability of a classic car, though. Nothing like the sound of a V8 engine at full throttle. That’s something I’ve always liked about cars. You can hear them, you can feel them. I remember the days when you had to drive on winding roads and you really had to know your way around. Now everything's got GPS, and you don’t even need to think. I can see that. But technology has its place. You know, I was just reading an article about how wildlife is being affected by the increase in traffic. It's a bit of a shame, but also a necessary part of modern life. I suppose it is. You can't have everything. But then again, the countryside is still beautiful. I've been walking through the fields near Costessey lately, and the views are just as nice as ever.

I don’t know, I just don’t think schools are what they used to be. You know, when I was a kid, we had to walk miles to school and we all had to do our lessons properly. Now, it’s all computers and social media and kids don’t even know how to behave in class. I saw a report the other day about some school in Manchester where the kids just sat all day on their phones. Oh, I’ve heard about that. I think it’s called “digital learning” or something. It’s supposed to be modern, but honestly, it’s just glorified watching YouTube videos. I mean, I couldn’t even imagine sitting in a classroom like that when I was young. I had to write essays by hand, and I used to think that was the most boring thing ever. Yeah, and I think it’s worse now because the kids aren’t even learning properly. I’ve got a nephew who’s in Year 11 and he can’t spell anything. He just says, “I’ll do it on the iPad.” And I’m thinking, what’s the point of learning if you can just type it up? Exactly! And I don’t even know what the teachers are doing. I mean, I used to teach in a school, and it was all about discipline. Now, they’re not even allowed to slap a kid on the wrist, and if they do, they get in trouble. It’s all about being nice and not being firm. I think it’s also the generation thing. My son is a teacher now, and he’s always talking about how he can’t control his classes. The kids come in all day with phones, they’re not listening, and they don’t even care about their grades. It’s like they’re looking for a free ride. I know, I know. And the problem is, if the system isn’t working, then the kids aren’t getting the education they need. I mean, I’ve got a friend who got into trouble because he couldn’t write his own name properly. He’s 17 and he can’t even fill out a form. That’s just sad. I remember when I was at school, we had to write our names in the register every day. It was a bit of a ritual.

I can't believe we've got snow again. It’s like we’re back in the 1980s or something. Yeah, it’s ridiculous. I was just walking to the uni and it was like walking through a Christmas fairytale. I mean, I'm glad it’s snowing because I was going to go out and plant some bulbs in the garden. Yeah, I was thinking about that too. Or like a sign that the world is going to hell in a handbasket. I’m not sure which. But I think I’ll go out and dig up some compost and try to get the planters sorted. Yeah, I could help. I was planning on doing some garden work anyway. That’d be great. It’s been ages since we did anything serious in the garden. Right, as long as we don’t end up with more snow than we can handle. Oh, we’re not going to – it’s just a light covering, I think. Yeah, but it’s already messing with my schedule. I was meant to go to a Come Dine With Me event in London next week. That sounds like a good idea. I’ve always wanted to try something like that. It’s supposed to be a really fun evening, with a nice menu and some good conversation. I can imagine. I mean, I’ve been to some of those events with friends. They’re great for meeting new people. Yeah, and I’ve got a few colleagues who are going. They’re all into cooking and it’s a chance to show off. I can see that. We should talk about going to one of those events together sometime. That sounds like a plan. I’ve also been thinking about stag and hen parties. My friend’s getting married next year. Oh yeah? I think mine is planning something, but it’s not set in stone yet. I can’t wait. I think the hen party is going to be the one to remember. You say that now, but I think the stag party will be the real showstopper. Fair enough. But I think we’re both going to need a holiday after all that.

Well, I've just made the stew, lass. It's proper thick and hearty, just like it used to be. Oh, thank you, Dad. It smells lovely. I haven’t had a proper stew like that since the days when we used to have Sunday roasts. Yeah, I know. It’s all about tradition, isn’t it? Though I don’t know how you lot young folk would know what a real stew tastes like. Honestly, it’s not that different from the ones we make now. Just slower and with more love, I reckon. Yeah, and it’s got that proper depth of flavour. You can’t just throw ingredients in a pot and call it a day. I’m telling you, love, it’s got to simmer slow. You can’t rush it, or it doesn’t come out right. Well, I suppose I could try it again, but I always end up burning the onions. That’s just how it is. You learn by doing. I used to make a mean Sunday roast when I was a student. Yeah, and I’ve got a few recipes I’ve picked up from my Nan. She was a real wizard with food. My Nan was the same. She could make anything taste like home. Even if it was just a plate of beans and bread. I wonder if we could get her to come over and show us how to make it properly. That’d be nice. I’d love to see how she does it. Yeah, I could help too. I’ve got a few tricks up my sleeve. You lot are too young to know what you’re missing. You should appreciate food more. I do, really. It’s just that sometimes life gets in the way. Well, I think we’ve all got our own little ways of doing things. As long as we’re feeding ourselves, we’re doing alright. Yeah, and it’s not just about the food, it’s about the company. Absolutely. That’s what makes it special. You’re all right, luv. I’d say we’re doing alright. So, shall we eat? I’m starving. I’m with you. It’s been a long day. Yeah, and I’m ready for a proper meal. Right, then. Let’s dig in. And don’t forget to pass the salt, alright? Always. You can’t have a proper meal without it.

I can't believe it's already dinner time. I’ve been slicing the potatoes and it feels like I’ve been doing it for ages. It’s not that bad, honestly. I think we’ve been doing a good job. Mum’s got the roast chicken on the go, and Dad’s in the kitchen fiddling with the gravy. It’s all good. Yeah, I think she’s been working on that gravy for over an hour now. She’s been watching the stew as well, like it’s some sort of sacred thing. You know how she is. Honestly, I think she’s been trying to outdo herself. Last week it was a soufflé, and it collapsed like a turkey. I don’t know how she got through that. Oh, you remember that, don’t you? She turned the oven off and everyone was just staring at the mess. I still have the photo of it on my phone. Oh, you do? I thought that was lost in the chaos of the kitchen. I remember thinking that if that was the worst, maybe we should just stick to the basics. Yeah, and she tried to make a shepherd’s pie last time, but it turned out like a concrete block. I swear she put too much potato in it. And it was  so  cold. I didn’t even want to eat it. I just sat there with a spoon and stared at the top of the pie like someone had put an ice cube in it. That’s the thing about her cooking, though—there’s always a story behind it. Even if it ends up in the bin, there’s a tale about how it happened. I think the real story is that she’s cooking for the whole family and it’s not just about the food. It’s about the tradition, the memories, the way she’s always been doing it. Yeah, I think that’s it. She probably thinks that every meal is a celebration, even if the food ends up being a bit of a disaster. You can’t really argue with that. She told me once that when she was young, she used to cook for her entire family and the village. She said that even the most complicated dishes were just a way to bring people together. And she’s always talking about how the food brings people together.

So, do you think we could bring some of these start-up ideas into the classroom? I mean, think about it—students are used to consuming content in a more dynamic way now. If we can integrate some of these viral video techniques or social media storytelling into the curriculum, it might actually make learning more engaging. That’s an interesting thought. I mean, I’ve always thought about how we could make lessons more interactive. But I also worry that if we focus too much on the digital side, we might lose the traditional elements of teaching. Like, the human connection. Do you think that’s something we can keep? I think it’s possible. I mean, the key is balance. You can have a well-structured lesson plan with some digital elements to spice it up. For example, if you’re teaching history, maybe you could have students create their own short documentaries or even a social media campaign about a historical event. It would teach them research skills, storytelling, and digital literacy at the same time. That does sound like a good approach. I actually had a student last year who created a YouTube channel about biology. He used animations and voiceovers to explain complex topics. It was amazing. Maybe we could encourage more of that kind of thing. Exactly. And what if we used some of the problem-solving techniques I’ve read about in the entrepreneurial world? Like, how do startups deal with ambiguity? Maybe we could use that in the classroom too. Instead of just giving students the answers, we could pose problems and let them work through solutions in a group setting. That’s something I’ve been thinking about too. I’ve seen some great examples where students are given a real-world problem and have to come up with a solution. It helps them develop critical thinking skills. But I guess the challenge is how to integrate that into the existing curriculum without it feeling too disruptive. That’s the thing—entrepreneurs often have to pivot when things don’t go as planned. Maybe we could use that as a metaphor. If a lesson isn’t working, we don’t just give up—we adapt. Maybe we could teach students to embrace failure as part of the learning process. Yeah, that’s a good point. I think a lot of students are afraid of getting things wrong.

So, how’s your week going? I’ve been swamped with work stuff, but it’s all good. I got the conference sorted out for next month, so I’m just trying to get the last bits of admin done before the final deadline. Honestly, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. Oh, that’s a good idea. Maybe we could go together? I don’t know if you’ve heard, but someone said there’s a costume contest with a prize. I might just have to rock up in something really ridiculous. A superhero? That’s a classic. But I’m thinking of something more… unusual. Maybe a robot? I’ve been into robotics lately. It’s something I’ve been trying to get into as a hobby. Robots? That’s clever. You always have interesting ideas. What about your five-year plans? I know you mentioned before you wanted to do more research in mental health. Yeah, I’ve been really thinking about it. I’d love to go back to university and do a PhD.

I just got a call from the doctor. You know, about that thing with your leg. They said it's not too bad, but they want you to come in for a check-up next week. Oh, really? I thought it was just a minor sprain. But I guess better safe than sorry. When’s the appointment? They said next Tuesday at 10 a.m. I’ll make sure to book it for you. You haven’t been to that art gallery on the corner in ages, have you? No, not really. I’ve been too busy. But I do miss the weekend walk we used to take. You always said it was the best way to clear your head. It was. And it’s a shame you’re not doing it anymore. You need to get out more, and not just for work. You should start planning something. Maybe a trip? A trip? You mean like a holiday? Yes, of course! You’ve been working so hard, you deserve a break. I can help you plan it. We could go somewhere nice, like the coast. You’ve always wanted to go to Cornwall, haven’t you? Corn? Yes, I think that’s a good idea. I’ve been thinking about it. It’s been a while since I last went anywhere. Then we should start planning soon.

So, do you know what’s up with the rugby match tomorrow? I heard it’s gonna be a big game. Yeah, I think it’s between Leeds and Manchester, or was it Newcastle? I’m not sure. Either way, it’s gonna be a tough one. I heard the pitch is a bit wet, though. Oh, yeah, I think that’s the case. I remember reading something about it. Do you think it’s gonna affect the game? The ball kept slipping, and the players had to be really careful not to trip. It made the game really slow, I think. Yeah, and I heard the weather forecast says it’s gonna be drizzly again. I guess we’ll just have to wait and see. Although, I’m not really a big rugby fan, to be honest. Yeah, I get that. I mean, I enjoy it when I’m at the stadium, but I’m not sure I’d ever watch it on TV. It’s too much of a physical sport for me. I prefer something a bit more tactical. Oh, I get that. I actually like football more than rugby, even though I’m not really into the actual sport. I just like the way teams play and the strategy behind it. There’s something about that. Yeah, I can see that. I guess it’s a matter of personal taste. Speaking of sports, how’s uni going for you? Still all right? Kinda, I guess. It’s not the worst, but the lectures are a bit boring sometimes. I’m trying to stay focused, but it’s hard when you’re not really into the subject. My friends say I should just take it easy, but I don’t want to fall behind. I know what you mean. I feel the same way sometimes. I’m just trying to make the most of it, though. Even if it’s not the most exciting, it’s still something to do. Yeah, I guess so. I’m just hoping I can go out with my mates more this term. I feel like I’ve been stuck inside all week. You should. Time to relax and have some fun.

I swear, I’ve had more spiders in this house than in any other I’ve ever lived in. Oh, really? You must be more of a target than I thought. Honestly, I don’t know what it is—maybe the house is just full of them. I saw one on the window sill the other day, and I thought,  “Oh no not again.”  I know what you mean. I’ve had a few of those in my place too. But you know what’s worse? Mice. Mice? You’ve got mice? Oh, I’ve had mice for years. You know, they come in through the gaps under the floorboards, and I’ve found them in the kitchen, in the pantry, even in the fridge. Wow, that’s a nightmare. Do you ever see them? Not really. I just hear them scuttling around at night, and then I find little bits of fur in the corners or crumbs on the floor. I’ve even had to get a trap up once. Did it work? It worked for a while, but then they came back. I think they’re just too smart for traps. I suppose they are. But I’ve never seen a mouse in my place. Although I’ve had birds. Birds? Yes, the ones that come to the feeders. I’ve had a few in the garden, and one even got into the house through the window. I had to chase it out with a broom. That’s not safe. You could get bitten. I know, but it was just a small bird. I think it was a sparrow. I’ve had pigeons in my garden too. They’re everywhere now. I don’t know if it’s because there are fewer people around or what. Maybe they’re just looking for food. I’ve noticed more birds coming to the garden recently. Yeah, I guess they’re adapting. I’ve even seen a couple of them in the street outside my house. Maybe they’re getting braver. I’m not sure if I like that. Me neither. But at least they’re not spiders or mice. True, I’ll take birds over both of those any day. I agree. Although I do miss the days when there wasn’t so much wildlife around. Yeah, I guess it’s a bit of a blessing and a curse, isn’t it?

So, do you know much about your family history? I’ve been trying to piece together my own family tree and it’s been a bit of a challenge. Oh, I know a fair bit, actually. My mother was quite into genealogy. She spent a lot of time researching our family roots. I think she even met some distant relatives in Wales once. But I’ve only just started getting into it myself. That’s interesting. I’ve heard stories about my great-grandfather who came over from Ireland. But I never got the full story. I guess it’s hard to piece things together when you’re not close to family. I know what you mean. My mother passed away last year, and since then, I’ve been going through her things. She left behind a lot of old letters, photographs, and even some old school reports from her days as a teacher. It’s amazing how much you can learn from that. I’m sorry to hear about your mother. I’m sure she was a remarkable woman. I lost my mother a few years ago too. She had Alzheimer’s, and it was heartbreaking to watch her lose her memory. It made me think a lot about how important it is to preserve stories and memories. Oh, I know. It’s so sad. I remember how she would talk about her childhood, how she grew up in a small village in Bristol and how her father was a carpenter. She used to describe it in such vivid detail, like it was yesterday. It’s funny how those stories stay with you, even when the person is gone. That’s true. I’ve been trying to write down some of my own family stories. I’ve even started a journal where I note down the things my parents used to say. It’s a bit of a hobby now, but it’s also a way of keeping them close. That sounds like a great idea. I’ve thought about doing something like that too. I’ve been meaning to start a family history project. I’ve got a few old photos I could use. Maybe we could help each other out with it? That would be lovely. I’d love to learn more about your family too. I’ve always been curious about the Welsh side of things. I know your family is from Wales, right?

You know, I just thought of something – I remember when we first came here, we saw those hot air balloons over the fields. It was absolutely breathtaking, like something out of a dream. Yeah, I remember that. We had to walk for ages to get a good view, but it was worth it. I still can't believe how high they go. I reckon they must be as high as those power lines we saw the other day. Oh, those power lines are a bit of a hazard, aren't they? I mean, they're so high up, but still, you can’t help but look up and think,  where do they go?  It’s like they’re almost part of the sky. Definitely. I remember telling my niece once that if you could reach the top of those lines, you’d be flying. She laughed so hard she almost dropped her hot chocolate. I love that kind of thinking. You know, I’ve been thinking about camping again. Maybe we could go somewhere near here next weekend. There’s a campsite just a few miles away, and it’s supposed to be really peaceful. That sounds great. I’ve actually been reading up on some camping gear. I think I need a better tent. The one we had last time was a bit too small for both of us, and it got pretty windy. Oh, right, and the dogs were so excited. They were running around the tent like it was a playground. I swear, if we weren’t so worried about the weather, we’d have had a perfect camping trip. I know. The dogs were amazing. I think they’ve got a special connection to the countryside. They always seem to know when it’s going to rain or when the wind is going to pick up. I can’t argue with that. They’re like little weather experts. And the wildlife – you know, the birds, the deer, the foxes. It’s all so peaceful here. I feel like we’re living in a storybook. Exactly. I just feel so lucky to be here with you. I mean, the money situation isn’t the best, but you know, it’s not about the money. It’s about the moments we get to share, like this walk, or watching the sun set over the fields. You’re right. It’s the little things that make life meaningful.

So, how’s the weather been down there in Leeds? I mean, I know it’s supposed to be colder than here, but I’ve been hearing about these weird weather patterns lately. Oh, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster, honestly. One day it’s sunny and warm, the next it’s pouring with rain. I swear, sometimes it feels like the seasons are just flipping around on us. Yeah, I’ve noticed that too. I was in Manchester last week, and it was like winter in July. I had to wear a coat and a hat. It’s like the UK is trying to mess with us. I don’t know, maybe it’s the climate change thing. I’ve heard some people say the weather’s getting more unpredictable. But hey, at least we don’t have to worry about extreme heat like in some other parts of the world. True, but I still feel like we’re getting more storms than ever. I was reading this article the other day about how the number of severe weather events has increased over the past decade. It’s pretty worrying. Yeah, I’ve read that too. It’s strange, though—every time there’s a big storm, people talk about climate change, but then the next week it’s sunny again, and suddenly it’s all forgotten. It’s frustrating, isn’t it? I mean, we’re all affected by the weather, whether it’s someone who works in the gym or someone who teaches languages. It just messes with your plans. For me, it’s more about the fitness side of things. If it’s raining, I can’t take people outside for their sessions. Sometimes I have to move classes indoors or cancel them altogether. I know what you mean. I’ve had to adjust my lessons depending on the weather too. If it’s too hot, I switch to more speaking activities, and if it’s too cold, I just keep it indoors. It’s a bit of a hassle, but you learn to adapt. That’s the thing, isn’t it? We’ve all had to adapt over the years. I mean, I started out in the gym when it was more of a local thing, and now it’s a chain, so I have to deal with all sorts of people—some who’re really into fitness, some who just want to burn off stress.

Right, right, so I've got this load of cards that need sorting out, and I was wondering if you’d like to help me out with it, Tom? Yeah, sure, I can help. What’s the deal with the cards? Are they for something like a sale or just old stuff? Well, they’re mostly just old stuff. I’ve been trying to go through the attic and I’ve got this box of old letters, tickets, and even some old photographs. I thought maybe we could go through them and decide what to do with them. Oh, I’ve got some old photos too. My husband used to take them, and I’ve been trying to find the ones I liked best. I think some of them are from when we first moved to Hull. I’ve got some too. I remember one of them is of the old factory when I worked there. It’s been years, though — I think it was knocked down ages ago. That sounds cool. Maybe we could put some of them in a scrapbook, or maybe even frame them? I’ve seen some really old photos in museums and they’re amazing. Yeah, that’s a good idea. I was also thinking about the old letters – some of them are from my mum and dad, and they’re really touching. I think some of them might be worth keeping. Oh, I’ve got a letter from my mum that I haven’t opened in years. I read it a while back, but it was so emotional. I’d like to keep it, but I’m not sure if I should show it to anyone. I think it’s okay to keep the ones that mean something to you. I’ve got some letters from my old friends that I barely remember, but they’re still special to me. I agree. It’s like going back in time, isn’t it? You can remember so much just by looking at those old things. I think it’s a nice way to preserve our family history. Yeah, and it’s a chance to learn more about our grandparents and how they lived back then. I mean, it’s not like we can just go back and ask them, are we? True, Tom. I remember my dad used to talk a lot about the old days, but he’s not around anymore.

I can't believe we've got to this point and still don't know where we're going. I thought I’d got the satnav sorted. I know, I thought I’d got it too. I was just about to ask you if you had checked the address again. It’s not like we’re going to a place that’s on a map, is it? No, it’s not. It’s a little gig in one of those back roads near Wetherby. I remember the name, but I can’t place it. It’s the one that’s supposed to be a local favorite, like, a real hidden gem. Yeah, the one that only turns up on the festival flyer. I still can’t believe you found it. I thought you’d be stuck on the A61 for the next hour. Well, I did, but then I saw a sign that said “Farrington Lane” and I thought, “That’s the one.” But then I thought, “Wait, I’ve never heard of this place.” Then I saw a red barn and thought maybe it’s a farm or something. It’s like they’re hiding it from us. I know, it’s kind of funny. I mean, who would want to hide a gig? It’s not like it’s a secret cult or something. Just a bunch of people with a passion for music. Yeah, but it’s about time they stopped hiding. I mean, the last time we had a gig like this, we ended up at a pub that was two miles away and had to listen to a terrible acoustic set. I don’t know if I can take another one of those. I know, it was a disaster. I still remember that guy with the acoustic guitar who played “Sing a Simple Song” for over ten minutes. I nearly fell asleep. I was just about to suggest he take a break. Still, I’m glad we made it here. It’s got that rustic vibe, right? I like the idea of a gig in a barn. It’s like a real community thing.

So, did you get the final brief from the university? I was hoping we could start cranking out some designs this week. Yeah, I got it this morning. It’s pretty straightforward, actually. They want a sustainable student housing complex that can accommodate up to 200 people. They mentioned communal living and low maintenance, so it’s going to be a bit of a challenge. Sounds ambitious. I mean, sustainable student housing—do they even have a clear idea of what that means? I’ve seen some pretty outdated designs in the past that called themselves “green,” but ended up being just another concrete jungle with solar panels. Yeah, I know what you mean. But I think this one’s a bit more serious. The head of the architecture department mentioned they want to integrate green spaces, maybe even a rooftop garden or something. It’s all about enhancing the student experience and reducing the carbon footprint. That’s interesting. I’d be curious to see how they approach communal areas. I mean, do they want private rooms with shared bathrooms, or more open-plan spaces? They’re leaning towards the latter. They want to encourage interaction and collaboration. I think they’re trying to counteract the isolation that comes with living in a big city. Plus, it’ll be cheaper to build and maintain. That makes sense. But I wonder how students will react. Some might like the idea of shared spaces, others might feel like it’s too much. I mean, I remember when I was in university, my dorm was just a basic room with a shared kitchen and bathroom—there was no real community space. It got pretty lonely at times. Yeah, I get that. But maybe this time around, the focus is different. I mean, they mentioned integrating some social hubs, like a study area or a café. It’s all about creating that student-friendly environment. That’s a good point. So, if we’re going to design it, we have to think about the flow of movement, how people will interact, and what kind of activities they’ll be doing in those spaces. It’s not just about building a structure—it’s about building a culture. Exactly. I think it’s a great opportunity to push the boundaries of what student housing can be. If we can pull it off, it’ll be a really unique project.

So, do you know when you're going to see your old friends again? It's been ages since you've had a proper catch-up. Oh, I remember when you used to bring your friends there and we’d all end up having a full-blown group chat. It was always so lively. I always tell myself that I should be more active in socialising, but it’s easy to let things slide. I haven’t seen some of my old friends in months. I know. It’s funny how things can change so quickly. I think I’ve been trying too hard to keep up with everything, and in the process, I’ve lost sight of the simple things—like just hanging out with friends. That’s the thing, though.

So, do you think you've got a good chance with that media job, ANON? I hope so. I've been thinking about it a lot. I mean, the role is for a producer, right? And I do have some experience in radio, so I think it could work. Yeah, I think that’s a good point. But have you thought about tailoring your application to the specific role? Like, maybe highlighting your experience in content creation or storytelling? Honestly, I haven’t. I just wrote a generic cover letter and CV. Maybe I should have done more research on the company. I mean, I know they do a lot of local news, but I wasn’t sure what kind of tone they prefer. That’s a good idea. I mean, if you can pick up on the kind of content they’re most proud of, you can tailor your application to show you understand their values. Like, if they’re big on community engagement, you can mention your work on local radio shows or any projects that highlight that. Right, and I should maybe include some examples of my work. Oh, I did take a short course in radio production last year. It was part of my postgrad. I think that’s a good point to include. I just need to make sure it’s on the CV. Exactly. And if you’re nervous about the interview, maybe practice some common questions.

So, do you think we're ready to take the plunge? I mean, starting this small business thing. It’s got to be a big change, especially for someone like me, coming from the corporate world. I think we are. Look, I’ve been thinking about this for a while. I want to use my teaching experience to do something more meaningful. Maybe create an online platform for self-directed learning? Something that’s flexible, but still structured. Oh, that sounds interesting. I like that. You’ve always had that passion for education. And it’s not like we’re starting from scratch—there’s already a market for online learning. Plus, we could blend your teaching background with my entrepreneurial skills. Exactly! I mean, think about it. We could offer courses on personal development, mental health, and even skills like time management. It’s something that’s really needed these days. People are overwhelmed with work and life, and they need tools to manage it better. Yeah, and the way remote work is going, people are more open to learning from anywhere. We could even target international markets. I’ve got contacts in Australia, and we’re already here—maybe that’s a good place to launch. That’s a good point. We’re in Australia for a while, so it makes sense to think about setting up a base here. But I’m not sure how much we should invest right now. I mean, we’re not exactly flush with cash. I get that. Maybe we can start small. Like, run a few pilot courses first. Use social media to build a following and see what kind of response we get. If it works, we can scale up. It’s not like we’re throwing everything into the fire at once. Yeah, that does sound safer. I’d feel better if we could test the waters. But, honestly, I’m excited. I’ve been feeling like I need a change for a while. I want to do something that aligns with my values, not just what’s expected of me. I can relate. I’ve always been the type to keep pushing forward, but now I’m starting to think that maybe it’s time to slow down and do something that gives me more satisfaction. I mean, if we can make it work, it could be really rewarding.

I just got a delivery from the local supermarket, and it was so heavy I had to put it in the hallway. I don’t know how they expect us to carry all this stuff with a toddler running around. Oh, I know the feeling. When I was teaching, I used to get deliveries of all the supplies, and I’d have to take them home on my bike. It was madness, but I’ve got used to it now. I remember when I was a publisher, we used to have delivery men come in with crates of books. I’d be sitting at my desk, and the door would burst open, and there’d be a man with a cart full of books. It was like a comedy of errors. Yeah, but this is more of a problem now with the housing shortage. We’ve got nowhere to put all the stuff, and the schools are struggling too. I heard the local primary school is having trouble with teacher shortages. It’s a real mess. I agree. I think the system is overburdened. I remember when I was a teacher, there were more staff, and the kids had a better chance. Now, with fewer teachers and more kids in each class, it’s just not working. And don’t even get me started on the healthcare system. I had a relative who was in the hospital for weeks, and they couldn’t get a proper bed. It’s a disgrace. I know, but I’m also dealing with my own issues. I’ve been looking after my toddler all day, and I’m exhausted. I can’t even think about going out. [giggling] Mummy’s tired! Oh, shut up, you little devil. You make it worse. Speaking of which, have you noticed the number of Polish migrants coming into the area? It’s quite a sight. They’re all eager to work and make a life here. Yeah, I’ve heard that. They’re good workers, and they’re filling the gaps in the workforce. But I keep thinking, what about the people who are already here? We’re not getting any support, and we’re being pushed to the side. It’s frustrating. I think the government just wants to fill the gap without thinking about the long-term effects. Exactly. And with the rising cost of living and the housing crisis, it’s hard to see how people can survive without some sort of support system.

So, how’s the new house? I heard you moved into Fradley last month. Oh, it’s lovely, really. It’s not too big, but it’s got a garden and it’s only a few minutes from the town centre. That’s great. I remember when we used to go to the local market together. It was always so busy back then. Yeah, I miss that too. I used to love watching the kids running around, chasing each other and trying to catch the pigeons. Oh, those were the days. You remember when we used to go to the cinema on Saturday afternoons? How could I forget? You always insisted on getting the cheapest tickets, and you’d sit in the back row with your legs crossed, trying not to be seen. That’s right. I still do that now, even though I’m not really in the back row anymore. You still have that sense of adventure, I’ll give you that. Well, I’d say it’s about the same as ever. Still trying to keep up with the latest trends, even though I’m not sure what they are half the time. You know, I’ve been thinking about the referendum again. It’s been on my mind a lot. Yeah, I know. It’s a big decision, isn’t it? I just don’t know what the right choice is. I can’t decide either. I’d like to think the country’s moving forward, but at the same time, I feel like we’re losing something. I hear you. I’m just worried about how it might affect things locally. You know, the school and the local events. Yeah, that’s true. I’ve been thinking about the local music festival. It’s been going on for years, but I don’t know if it’ll still be around if things change. That’s sad. I love that festival. It’s always such a great time, and the kids love it. I know. I was thinking the other day about the piano room in the old manor house. You remember how we used to play in there when we were kids? Oh, how we used to play! We’d get into all sorts of trouble, trying to make those loud noises. I still remember the day we broke the keys. We were so young, we didn’t know any better.

So, do you still use Twitter for work stuff, or have you given it up? Honestly, I’ve kind of switched to LinkedIn more. It’s more professional, you know? But I still check Twitter sometimes for the news or just to see what people are saying. I’ve been thinking about doing the same. I follow a few education folks and it’s actually been pretty insightful. But I’m still not sure if it’s worth the time. It’s like that. You can get lost in the scroll. But if you’re strategic about it, it can be really useful. Like, I’ve made connections through Twitter that led to some great collaborations. My job’s pretty digital, so I use social media a lot. But I’m always trying to balance work and personal stuff. Do you ever find it hard to switch off? Yeah, honestly. I’m constantly in work mode, even when I’m not at the office. There’s this expectation to be always reachable. But I’ve started setting boundaries. I turn off notifications after a certain time, and I try to have actual conversations with people instead of just tweets. That sounds like a good move. I’ve been meaning to do that. I’ve got this friend who’s a writer, and he’s always posting really interesting stuff. I follow him, but I wish I could just have a real chat with him instead of just reading his updates. I get that. It’s not the same as a face-to-face conversation. I think what’s happening with social media is it’s changing the way we communicate. It’s more about seeing what people are doing, rather than actually talking to them. It’s like the whole idea of social media has shifted. It used to be about connecting, but now it feels like it’s more about validation. Like, you post something and then you check how many likes you get. Exactly. And that can be pretty intense. I remember a time when I was working on a project and I got a lot of criticism on Twitter. It was really hard to take, but I had to remember that not everyone who comments is a real person. Some of them are just trolls. I’ve had that happen too. But I guess the key is to not let it affect your confidence.

So, did you get that email from Sarah about the group dinner next week? Yeah, I got it. She said it’s on Friday at her place, and she wants everyone to bring a dish. That’s not bad. I’m glad she’s trying to get us all together again. It’s been a while since we all hung out. I know, right? It’s nice to have that kind of social event. But I’m not sure if I should go. Why not? Didn’t you say you wanted to get out more? I mean, I do, but I’ve been so busy with work lately. And then there’s the kids. I’m still getting used to the shift patterns. I get it. It’s been a hectic week for me too. Work’s been really demanding. Yeah, I feel you. But I think it’s worth it. We haven’t had a proper catch-up in ages. True. I mean, it’s not like we have to do anything too fancy. Just bring a dish, right? Exactly. Sarah’s going to be cooking something, so it’s not like we’re expected to be the stars of the show. That’s a relief. I’m actually quite bad at cooking, but I’ll manage. I’ll make something simple like pasta. That sounds good. I’ll bring a meatball dish. It’s something I can do quickly and it’s always a hit. Perfect. So, what time are we meeting? She said around 6.30. She’s got a few people coming over, so she wants to make sure she’s not left alone. That’s fair. Should I bring anything else? Maybe some snacks? I think she’s expecting people to bring something for the kids. Oh right, the kids. I didn’t think about that. Is there anything specific you want me to bring? Just some biscuits or something like that. You know, for the kids. Got it. I’ll make some chocolate chip cookies. They’re always a crowd-pleaser. Nice. And what about the adults? Maybe a small bottle of wine or something. Perfect. I’ll bring a bottle of red. Alright, that sounds like a solid plan. I just hope I can get everything done in time. You’ll be fine. You’re not the only one juggling work and life. Yeah, I know.

So, do you think we've got everything ready for the brother’s visit? I was just checking the fridge and it's looking a bit sparse. Honestly, I think we've got the basics covered. But we might need to do a bit of shopping later today. The meal’s not gonna be good if we run out of ingredients. I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about that all morning. I think I'll go with you. Maybe we can pick up some fresh veggies and a few things from the butcher. I also need to check if the car’s all set for the trip. The car’s fine, don’t worry. I checked it before I went to bed. It’s a bit old, but it still runs. I just hope it doesn’t break down on the way. We don’t want to be stuck somewhere with no phone signal again. That was the worst trip last year. We were stuck in the middle of nowhere with no signal and no petrol. I remember the brother getting really frustrated. It was like a real-life episode of  The Office . Oh, I remember that. You were both so stressed. I think it was the only time I saw you two argue over something. I thought you were going to start a real fight. I wouldn’t say that. We were just arguing about the best way to get to the next town. It was a bit of a heated debate, though. He wanted to take the back roads and I wanted to take the main road. It ended up being a bit of a mess. So, I guess it’s better to plan ahead this time. Maybe we should try to get some petrol before we leave. I’m not sure how much we have left. Yeah, that’s a good idea. I’ll check the car again when I go. I also need to make sure the GPS is working. I remember last time it wasn’t, and we ended up going the wrong way for an hour. You’re right. We should make sure everything’s in order. Also, I was thinking about the meal. I’ve got some steak in the freezer, but I think we should also bring some side dishes. I was just going to say that. I’ve got a few potatoes and some carrots in the fridge.

I've been trying to learn Spanish for years, Len, but I still can't get it right. It's like trying to learn to ride a bike when you're 60. You’re not 60, you’re 69, Lorna. And you’ve got more patience than most people I know. But I think you’re just overthinking it. You’ve got to go with the flow, not force it. I tried going to a language exchange in Liverpool last week. We had this guy from Madrid, and he said I was using the wrong accent. I said, “What accent?” He said, “Oh, you’re using the British one, but you should sound like the people from Spain.” Oh, you know, I had the same problem when I first started learning French in school. I kept trying to sound like the teachers, but it never felt right. I think the key is to immerse yourself in the language. I tried listening to Spanish music and watching telenovelas, but I still can’t understand much. Sometimes I think I’m just too old to pick things up quickly. You’re not too old, Lorna. I’ve known people who started learning Spanish in their 70s and they picked it up pretty well. The secret is consistency, not speed. You’ve got to put in the hours. I know, I know. I just get frustrated because I feel like I’m not making progress. I was thinking about going to Spain for a holiday next year. Maybe that would help. That’s a good idea. I’ve heard that living in a Spanish-speaking country is the best way to learn. But you don’t have to go all the way. Maybe you could take a course in a local language school. I’ve been to a few language classes, but they’re all so basic. I feel like I’m not learning anything useful. Do you think there’s a better way? Maybe you should try using apps like Duolingo or Babbel. They’re a bit more interactive and fun. I’ve heard they work well for beginners. Then again, some people swear by the traditional method—just sitting in a classroom and drilling vocabulary. I tried the classroom method, but I just hate it. It’s so boring. I’d rather be watching a film or chatting with someone. That’s the way to go.

So, Dad, I've been trying to sort out these documents for the tax return, but I can't get the scanning to work properly. It keeps giving me an error message. That’s a shame. Let me check the printer. Oh, wait—do you have the right drivers installed for that scanner? I remember you had trouble with one before. I think I did. But I’ve been using it for a while now. Maybe I should check again. I don’t want to mess up the documents just before the deadline. Yeah, it’s always better to be safe than sorry. You know, I used to work in customer services, and I’ve seen people get stressed over things like this. Just take your time. It’s just that I’m trying to do everything on my own these days. I don’t want to bother anyone, but honestly, sometimes it’s easier to ask for help. You know, if you ever need help with anything—whether it’s ordering flights or even cooking—just say the word. I’m not as tech-savvy as you, but I can still help in my own way. Thanks, Dad. I know you’re not a tech genius, but I appreciate the support. You’ve always been there for me, even when I was still at uni. That’s what family’s for, mate. Anyway, let’s get back to the documents. Did you manage to scan the bank statements yet? No, not yet. I’ve been trying to do it in between other things, but it’s been a bit of a headache. I was hoping to get it done by the weekend, but I’m not sure if I can. You’re going to be fine. I’ll help you tomorrow, if you want. I’ve got some time in the afternoon, and I’d rather do it with you than leave it to last minute. That would be great. Thanks, Dad. I don’t know what I’d do without you. You’ll be fine. And if you ever want to take a break from all this paperwork, just grab a book, or even a sandwich. You’ve got a life outside of tax returns. I know. I just feel like I’m always on top of things, but sometimes I need a reminder that it’s okay to slow down.

I just saw a really weird thing at the petrol station. There was this biker in a leather jacket, like, completely covered in stickers and chains. He looked like he could’ve been in a movie. Bikers? You mean like the ones who ride around on motorbikes? Yeah, exactly. I don’t know if they’re just into bikes or if they’re part of a gang. I mean, they had this one guy who was riding a really big bike, like, a dirt bike. And he had these big boots and this hat that looked like it was made for a superhero. Haha, maybe he’s a biker and a superhero? That’s a good combo. I don’t know, maybe. But I just thought, "Oh my God, are they all like that?" Like, are they all into leather, chains, and tattoos? I think it depends on the subculture. Some bikers are just into the lifestyle, others might be part of a motorcycle club. They might have their own rules and codes. Yeah, I heard that some motorcycle clubs have really strict rules. Like, you don’t just join because you like bikes. You’ve got to prove yourself, right? I think that’s part of it. I mean, I know some people who ride bikes, and they’re not even part of any club. They just enjoy the freedom of riding. That’s what I thought. But then again, I saw a few of them just hanging around outside the petrol station, like, waiting for someone. It was strange. Maybe they were waiting for someone to meet up with. I mean, I’ve heard stories about biker meetings, like, going out for drinks or something. Though I don’t know if they’re all that friendly. I guess they could be. But I still feel like they’re a bit of a mystery. I mean, they’re always got that whole look, like, they’re not just passing through. They’re there for a reason. Maybe. But I’ve never been into it myself. I like driving, but I don’t think I’d ever be into joining a biker group or anything. I think I’d be more of a regular driver. Yeah, I guess so. Although, I might have to be more careful if we ever see them again. I mean, I don’t want to get into any trouble.

Alright, Jamie, you've got your racket out, so are you ready to talk about your tennis? Ugh, Mum, I’m not ready to talk about tennis. Come on, lad, you’ve been practicing for weeks. You’ve got to be thinking about it. Yeah, Jamie, you’ve been out on the court every Saturday morning with your dad. You’ve got to be interested in this. I’m not interested in tennis. I just do it because Dad makes me. That’s not true. You like it. You even won that match against Harrison last week. Yeah, well, that was easy. He’s not even that good. You’re not being fair, Jamie. You used to love it. You were the one who was obsessed with Roger Federer when you were ten. Yeah, but I’m not a pro. I just want to play with my mates. That’s not the point. You know, you’ve got the natural talent. You’ve got the speed, the reflexes. You just need to work on your technique. Exactly. And it’s not just about being good at it. It’s about the discipline, the way it makes you feel when you hit that perfect shot. I don’t know. I just don’t see the point. I mean, someone’s going to win the Wimbledon, not me. That’s not the point. It’s about what you get out of it. It’s about the challenge, the competition, the way it keeps you on your toes. And you know what? There’s a lot more to tennis than just the matches. There are the coaches, the clinics, the tournaments. You could even think about taking it seriously. Taking it seriously? I don’t want to take it seriously. I just want to play. Well, maybe you should think about it. I’ve seen how much you’ve improved. You’ve got the potential. And you know, Jamie, if you really wanted to, you could go to a coach. There are some pretty good ones in the area. I don’t need a coach. I can do it myself. Yeah, but you’re not the only one out there. There are people who are better than you, and they’ve got coaches. That’s true. But the point is, you’ve got the ability. You’ve just got to want to take it further.

So, did you get the turkey today, Mummy? Yeah, I did. We got a big one, just like last year. I was thinking, though, are we going to have the traditional Christmas dinner like we always do? Yeah, I think so. But I don’t think we’re going to have the wishbone this year. Why not? I think it got lost in the washing machine. Oh, that’s tragic. Didn’t you get it out of the turkey? No, I thought it was just part of the turkey, you know? You know, I remember my mum always said the wishbone brings good luck. I think I’ve heard that somewhere. But I’m more interested in the Christmas music. Yeah, I love the carols. I think we should play the old ones again this year, the ones from when I was a kid. I like the ones with the choir. They sound really special. Did you know that the Queen once gave a speech on Christmas Day? Oh, yes. I remember that. She always talks about togetherness and family. I’m glad she’s still doing that. It’s nice to hear her voice again. I also heard someone say that one of the family friends is going to America this Christmas. Is that the one who works in Florida? Yeah, he’s going to visit his parents. I heard he’s been there for a while now. I wonder if he’ll be able to come back in time for Boxing Day. I heard he’s got a lot of stuff to do. I think he’s got a lot of Christmas shopping to do too. I can’t wait for Christmas. I think we’re going to have the best Christmas ever. I think so too. And remember, even if things don’t go the way we expect, we still have each other. Yeah, and the turkey. And the wishbone. And the Christmas music. And the dancing after dinner. Oh, and the wishbone. Yeah, the wishbone. I think I’ll make a wish. Me too. Let’s all make a wish and then we’ll see what happens. Sounds good to me. I think I’m going to wish for a really good Christmas. Me too. Me too. Me too. Me too. Let’s all make our wishes. Alright, let’s do it. Okay, let’s make our wishes.

So, do you know if we’ve got anything planned for the weekend? I was just thinking maybe we could all go out and have some proper food. I’m feeling like I’ve been cooking the same thing for weeks. Hmm, honestly, I haven’t really thought about it. I’ve been so busy with the exams and the new timetable. I was just saying to Bill yesterday that I need to get out more. But I’d be happy to go if everyone else is up for it. Well, I suppose we could do something smaller. Maybe a family meal and then go out for ice cream? It’s been a while since we had something like that. That sounds nice. I’d like that. I’ve been so caught up in work that I haven’t even had time to think about going out with the family. I’ll let you know if we decide on anything. Maybe we can pick up some takeaway and bring it back here? I’m not sure if we’re up for going out to a restaurant. Yeah, that’s probably safer. I mean, the last time we tried going out, we ended up arguing about the menu because someone wanted seafood and someone else didn’t. I’m not sure we’re ready for that again. That’s true. I think I’d rather have something simple. Maybe we can do something like a Sunday roast? I’ve got some chicken in the freezer. I could cook that. That sounds nice. I could help you with that. You know, I’ve been meaning to try out some new recipes. I’ve got this one for roast potatoes that I think is really good. Oh, I’d love to try that. I’ve been meaning to learn how to make better roast potatoes.

I can't believe we've got to make our own supper tonight. I thought we’d just order takeout like usual. Yeah, I know, but I thought maybe we could try something new. You know, since we’re both working so much, we haven’t cooked together in ages. That’s true. I’ve been making my own meals most nights. I’ve even started using a blender for smoothies and sauces now. That’s what I keep telling myself. But still, I keep thinking, what if I mess up? What if my presentation isn’t good enough? You’re overthinking it. So, do you guys know what we're doing tonight? I was thinking maybe a night out, like a bit of shopping and then some drinks. I was actually thinking the same thing! I’ve got this outfit I saved for a special occasion. Maybe we can all dress up and make it an event. Perfect! I think it’ll be fun. We can hit a few places, maybe grab some food, then go to a bar or something. I was thinking about getting some drinks. I’ve been wanting to try that new cocktail bar downtown. They have this amazing mojito. Yeah, I heard about that place too. I think they have a good selection of drinks and the ambiance is really cool. Cool, but I’m not a big fan of cocktails. I just thought I'd mention, I've been feeling a bit restless lately. Like, I don't know—maybe it's the weather or maybe it's just me—but I’ve been thinking about those kinds of spiritual journeys we talked about before. You know, like the ones where people say they meet their soul mate in a different time or place. Yeah, I remember you were really into that book about the spiritual journeys through history. I wonder what it would be like to live a life that’s not so structured, to just… be free for a second. I get that. I’ve been thinking about that too. You know, all those brilliant minds discussing things like gravity, light, and the nature of time. It was like a party for the mind. I could picture it. You’d probably be the one trying to argue with Newton about gravity. I’d be the one lost in the corner, just trying to make sense of it all. You’d be the one who would want to ask him, "Sir, are you sure the moon is made of cheese?" I think you’d still be that curious kid at heart.

So, how’s the new job going, Sophie? I heard you got promoted to a senior role in the civil service last month. Oh, thank you, Lucy. It’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. I always said you had the potential for more. But I know it’s not all smooth sailing, is it? Didn’t you mention something about dealing with some pretty difficult colleagues? Yeah, honestly, it’s been tough. There are a few people in the department who don’t take kindly to new blood. They’re a bit resistant to change, and I’ve had some pretty pushy moments. But I’m learning to navigate it, and I’ve got a good mentor who’s been helping me out. That’s reassuring. I remember when I first started, I was so green and didn’t know where to begin. It took me ages to get the hang of the company culture. Do you think there’s a generational divide in the workplace? I’ve heard a lot about stereotypes between older and younger workers. Definitely. I think there’s a lot of misunderstanding. Sometimes, I feel like the older staff don’t take us newbies seriously, and we feel like we’re not being given the same opportunities. But I’m also aware that some of the older staff have been through a lot and have a lot of experience. I agree. I’ve seen it in my own workplace too. There’s this assumption that younger people are less reliable or not as committed. But I think it’s the other way around. I’ve seen some of the younger staff take initiative and be proactive in ways the older ones haven’t. That’s a good point. I’ve always thought that age doesn’t dictate capability. It’s more about how you approach your work. Speaking of work, have you been keeping up with the news? I’ve been reading about the recent safety concerns at some factories. Yeah, it’s been in the papers a lot. It’s a bit scary. I mean, the number of accidents in the workplace is still way too high.

So, do you know what’s happening with the new flat in town? I heard it's supposed to be like a real student-friendly place with all the amenities. Yeah, I saw something about it on the uni website. They said it's got a kitchen, a study area, and even a common room. But I’m not sure if it’s worth the extra cost. I mean, I can’t afford to move out right now. My parents are still paying for my rent, and I’ve got so many bills to pay. Plus, I’ve got this annoying debt from that takeaway I ordered three times last week. Oh no, I feel you. My mates and I had this thing where we all agreed to split the cost of takeaways, but then one of them got a job and started charging extra. Now we’re all in a mess. That sounds familiar. I had that with my flatshare last year. We all ordered from the same place, but one of the guys started adding extra charges for “shared meals” and “shared drinks.” It got so bad, I ended up cooking everything myself. I tried that once. Cooking for four people is a nightmare. I tried making a stir-fry, and it turned out like a science experiment. Half the ingredients didn’t go together, and the other half just burned. Now I just order takeaway and pretend I’m a grown-up. Haha, I’ve been there. But honestly, I’ve been thinking about the football match next week. I know it’s not the biggest game, but I really want to go. Yeah, I heard it’s about the same as the last one. But the problem is, I can’t afford to buy a ticket. My sister offered to lend me some money, but she said she’s not paying for me to go to a football match. That’s so unfair. I mean, it’s a game, not a luxury trip. I think I’ll just go with my mates. We can chip in. Yeah, that’s what I’m thinking. I’ve got this friend who’s got a season ticket, so we can just sit together and not have to worry about the cost. That sounds good. I just need to work out how to get the tickets. But wait, what about all the other stuff we have to do?

So, do you think I should get my tattoo done before I go back to Bolton? Yeah, I mean, it’s not like you’re going to be stuck with it forever, right? You know, I had one once. It was a heart with a ‘B’ in the middle, for my brother. Really? That’s sweet. But I’m thinking of something more... edgy. Maybe a dragon or something. A dragon? That’s a classic. I got one when I was your age. It’s on my upper arm. Cool. But I don’t think I want one. I’m still trying to figure out what I even like. That’s okay. You don’t need to rush into anything. I mean, I didn’t get mine until I was about 30. Yeah, I mean, I’ve been thinking about it for ages. But I’m also worried about the cost. It depends on the artist. I paid like £200 for mine. But I think it was worth it. I’d rather just get a body piercing. That’s cheaper. You know, I actually had a piercing for a while, too. It was a nose ring. That’s cool. I always thought nose rings were more for girls. Not anymore. It’s totally gender-neutral now. People are more open-minded these days. Yeah, but I still think it’s weird. I mean, I don’t even like the idea of having a hole in my face. I get that. I had a few piercings when I was younger, but I took them out when I got married. Oh, I totally get that. I can see how it might be a bit too much for some people. Speaking of which, how’s your mum doing? We haven’t talked about her much. She’s fine, thank you. She’s been busy with the kids and everything. Yeah, I know. I’ve been meaning to call her, but I keep getting distracted by other things. I’ve been trying to call her too. She’s been asking about you. That’s nice. I think it’s important to stay in touch with your family, even when you’re far away. I agree. I’m just worried about how often I can actually get in touch. Yeah, it’s not easy. I mean, I’m at school, and I have to do all this work.

Well, I've just got back from Cornwall, and I must say, it was absolutely beautiful. I’ve been volunteering with the YHA, helping out at a youth hostel near Falmouth. Oh, that sounds lovely! Did you enjoy it? I did. It was a nice change of scenery. The weather was a bit on the cool side, but the views from the lighthouse were amazing. I even got to take some photos, which I’ll show you later. That’s great! I remember when I was teaching, I used to take my students on trips to the coast. I’d always tell them about the history of the lighthouses and how they’ve helped sailors for centuries. Yeah, I tried to do a bit of that too. I told the kids about the lights and how they warn people of the rocks. One of them even asked if the lighthouse still works the same way now. I bet it does, especially with the technology they have these days. But I still think nothing beats the sight of a real lighthouse at night. Definitely. I also did a bit of cycling around the area. I joined a local cycle race, and it was a bit of a challenge. The hills were tough, but the scenery made it worth it. Cycling’s a great way to explore. I’ve always been a fan. I used to ride my bike to work every day, all the way from Birmingham to the school. It was a long commute, but it kept me fit and happy. I can imagine. I’ve never been much of a cyclist, but I did do a ‘Yorkshire in a Day’ tour once. It was quite an adventure. I remember getting lost a few times, but the people along the way were really helpful. That sounds like the kind of thing I’d like to do. I’ve always wanted to go on a long-distance bike ride. Maybe one day I’ll try it. You should. It’s a great way to see the countryside and meet new people. Speaking of people, I took some pictures of the local crab fishermen. They had this huge crab on their boat, and it looked like it could have been the size of a cat! Crabs! I remember when I was a teacher, I had a student who was obsessed with crabs. He used to bring in all sorts of pictures and facts about them.

So, do you know what’s for dinner tonight? I’ve been cooking something nice, but I’m not sure if it’s going to be good enough for three people. Oh, you’re making pasta again? I thought you said you were trying to eat healthier. I  was ! But I got a bit bored with salads and quinoa. Plus, I heard that a bit of cheese and garlic actually helps your digestion. I’m not entirely sure if that’s true, but it sounds better than nothing. Yeah, I’ve heard that. But I think you’re mixing up digestion with something else. I mean, cheese is fine, but don’t go overboard. I know, I know. I’m not going to go full cheese-fest. It’s just a little bit of Parmesan on top. That’s not a lot. I mean, I’m not here to judge, but I do miss the days when we used to have proper meals. Like, real food. Not just processed stuff and instant meals. Yeah, I remember when I was working in London, I used to skip dinner for weeks because I was too busy. Now that I’m working from home, I actually cook more. It’s weird how things change. That’s true. I’ve noticed that too. But I think it’s also because we're all more conscious about what we eat now. I mean, someone’s got to be the healthiest in the group, right? Oh, don’t start. I’m not into all that ‘healthy’ stuff. I’m more of a ‘treat yourself’ kind of person. Although, I do try to eat better when I’m with you all. That’s the spirit. But seriously, we should all try to be a bit more balanced. I mean, I’m not perfect, but I do try. Yeah, I guess. I don’t want to be the one who’s always eating chips and burgers. I mean, I did once. Oh, you had the worst time with your ex, didn’t you? I remember hearing about it. That was one of the worst breakups I’ve ever heard of. Yeah, it was a mess. He used to take me out to McDonald’s all the time. I don’t know why I ever stayed with him. I had a similar thing with my ex. He used to say he loved me, but he never cooked.

So, did you have a good time in Barcelona? I heard you went there for the weekend. Oh, it was absolutely amazing. I’m still reeling from it. The sun, the food, the beaches… it was like a dream come true. I can’t believe you managed to go away without me. I was stuck with my sister and her baby for the whole weekend. I didn’t even get a chance to watch my favourite show. I know, I feel bad about that. You should have come. You would have loved it. The weather was perfect, and we went to this amazing little tapas bar. The food was incredible. Yeah, I’m still jealous. I wish I had gone. I left my laptop at home, so I couldn’t even catch up on work. I feel like I’m missing out on everything. You’ll get your chance. You need to take some time for yourself.
