You’ve been working so hard lately. Maybe we can plan something for the next weekend? I’m thinking of going to Paris for a few days. Paris? I’d love that. What’s the plan? Do you have any ideas? I was thinking of going to the Louvre and maybe the Eiffel Tower. I want to take some photos, but I also want to explore the city. We could even try some French pastries. I heard the croissants there are the best in the world. Sounds perfect. I’d love to go with you. I can definitely take some time off. But I need to check with my manager first. That’s a good idea. I’ll let you know what I decide. But I’m really looking forward to it. It’s been too long since I’ve been on holiday. I know, I’ve been thinking about it too. Maybe we can do something like that. It would be nice to have a weekend getaway without all the responsibilities. Definitely. I’ll keep you updated. We could even plan a few days together. I’d love to have some quality time with you. That sounds perfect. I’ll let you know as soon as I can. I can’t wait to escape my routine for a while. Me too. Barcelona was just the beginning. I can’t wait for the next adventure. Maybe we can even plan a trip to the south of France next?

So, do you live in London still? You sound like you're from there. Yeah, I do. I was born and raised in London. I’ve been an entrepreneur for over ten years now, running my own tech start-up. I moved to Cyprus a few months ago for a bit of a change of scenery, though. It’s nice here. The sea, the weather—everything’s different. That’s interesting. I’ve never thought about moving abroad, but I can see how it could be tempting. I’ve been teaching for over fifteen years, mostly in Dorchester. It’s not the most exciting job, but I’ve always loved working with children. You sound like you’ve had a stable life. I’ve had my fair share of ups and downs. I started in finance, then moved into tech, and now I’m managing a small team. It’s not always easy, but I love the challenge. That’s amazing. I’ve always been more of a steady person. I think I’d struggle with the fast-paced nature of entrepreneurship. My days are pretty routine—teaching, marking, planning lessons. But I’ve got a few friends who’ve tried starting their own businesses and it’s been a rollercoaster for them. Yeah, I know a few people like that. One of them, a friend of mine, started a café in London and it’s doing well. But he’s always talking about how hard it is to keep the business running. He mentions things like rent, staffing, and customers. I’d imagine it’s a lot of work. I’ve always thought that running your own business is like being a parent—you’re always responsible for everything. But I guess that’s the trade-off. You get to be your own boss. Exactly. And the rewards are there if you’re willing to put in the work. I’ve had some really good moments, like landing big clients or launching a successful product. But it’s not always smooth sailing. That must be hard. I can’t imagine doing that every day. I’ve never been the adventurous type. I like knowing what my day is going to look like. That’s totally fine. I think everyone has their own way of finding happiness. I’m just lucky that my work gives me a sense of purpose, even if it’s not always easy.

So, do you think we should get a dog? A dog? Are you serious? I thought we were just talking about housemates. No, I mean, we’ve got this spare room, and we’ve got the garden. It wouldn’t be a bad idea. I mean, if we had a dog, it’d keep us busy. Busy? You mean constantly cleaning up after it? Or trying to find time to walk it? Yeah, but we’d be doing it together. It’d be a shared responsibility. Plus, I think it’d help with the loneliness. Loneliness? You think we’re lonely? Well, I’m not sure. I mean, we’re together, but we’re not always together. We’ve got our own lives. And with uni, and work, sometimes it’s just me and the flat. I get that. But I’m not sure I’m ready for a dog. I mean, I’ve never had one before. I don’t know if I’d be a good owner. You’d be fine. I think you’d be good with a dog. You’re pretty responsible. Yeah, but what if it’s a barker? Or it doesn’t like other dogs? Or it’s too expensive? I know, I know. It’s a lot. But maybe we could just get a cat? Less work. A cat? You’re not serious, are you? You’re the one who’s always being like, “I want a dog, I want a dog.” Okay, okay, I’m not saying we have to get one immediately. Maybe we could just talk about it. See how things go. Yeah, I guess. But I still think it’s a big decision. I know. It’s just… I feel like we’re in a good place right now. Maybe we could take the next step. I guess. But we need to make sure we’re both on the same page. Yeah, totally. I don’t want to rush into anything. But I do think it’s something we should consider. Alright. I’ll think about it. Maybe I’ll do some research. Yeah, and if we do get a dog, I’ll be the one who feeds it, walks it, and cleans up after it. Oh, I get it. You’re going to take the lead. Yeah, I think I’m the dog person. You’re more of a cat person.

Well, I've just been to the shops, Elsie. I bought a few things, mostly groceries, but I got a bit distracted by the local news stand. Oh, did you? What did you see? There was a picture of a new park being built near the river. I thought it looked nice, but I couldn’t help but think about all the old places we used to go when I was younger. Oh, I remember those days. We used to walk down to the river every Sunday and sit on the rocks, watching the ducks. You used to bring your flask of tea, and I’d bring a sandwich. Yes, and the children used to run around, chasing each other and the dogs. I suppose that’s the way it was back then, before everything got so modern. It’s true. I sometimes think that the world has changed too much. When I was your age, we didn’t have all these gadgets and things, but we had time to do the simple things. Exactly. I remember reading somewhere that people used to have more time, even if they didn’t have as much money. Now, we’re always rushing from one thing to another. I suppose that’s the way of the world. But I still enjoy the quiet moments, like sitting by the fire in the evening or taking a walk in the garden. That’s what I like about the older days. You didn’t have to worry about everything being so fast-paced. I think it’s good to slow down a bit and take in the things that matter. I agree. I’ve been thinking about buying a new pair of gardening gloves. The old ones are getting a bit worn out. That sounds like a good idea. You should also consider getting a new set of cutting shears. I’ve been meaning to fix the hedges, but I’ve been too busy. I’ll keep that in mind. I could always use a bit of help with the garden. It’s not as big as it used to be, but it still needs some attention. I’d be happy to help. I’ve been meaning to get out more, and this would be a good way to spend some time. That would be lovely. I think we could do with some company, especially after the long week.

Oi, lass, you’ve been lazezing about all mornin’! What’s the plan for today? I was just finishing my maths homework, Grandma. I’ve got a test tomorrow. Aye, well, you’ll need to be sharp for that. I’ve got a few tricks up my sleeve if you need help. Oh, don’t you start, Mavis. You know that test’s got to be easier than the ones we had back in the day. Aye, that’s true, Nell. I remember one time, I had to solve a geometry problem so tough, I ended up spilling tea on the exam paper. Ooh, you did? What was the question? It was about triangles, I think. The teacher asked me to find the area, and I panicked. I remember I just stared at it for ages. That’s not fair, Grandpa. You were supposed to be the smart one. Aye, but I was still a child, love. I didn’t know I’d be the one teaching you all this now! Well, there’s something to be said for experience, isn’t there? Though I’ll admit – I still get confused with fractions sometimes. Fractions are the devil, Mavis. You know what they say – if you can’t divide, you’ll always be in trouble. That’s a bit harsh. I mean, I’ve got a calculator on my phone now. It does all the hard work. That’s the modern way, I suppose. Though I did it all with paper and pencil back in the day. Aye, and you know what? You were better at it than most of the lads in my class. My brother had to cheat on his exams! Really? That’s not nice. Aye, it was. I remember he tried to copy off me, but I caught him. We had a right row. Oh, I’ve got a story about that too. Once, when I was a teacher, I caught a pupil trying to copy off another. I gave them both a week of detention. That’s the way to do it. No tolerance for cheating. So, you think I should take the calculator to the test? I mean, it’s just a bit of a safety net. Well, if you’re not confident, then by all means. But I’d rather you worked it out for yourself. It’s the only way to really learn.

So, do you think the new health supplement is actually worth it? I’ve been reading about it online, and it’s supposed to boost energy and stuff. Honestly, I’m not sure. I tried it once, and honestly, I felt like I was just paying for a placebo. I mean, I didn’t feel any different, but I guess some people do. Yeah, I saw a review on YouTube where this guy said it changed his life, but then he was like, “Oh, it’s just me.” You know, like, “it’s subjective.” Maybe it works for some people, but I’m not convinced. I think the real key is what you’re doing alongside it. Like, if you’re already eating healthy and exercising, maybe it helps, but if you’re just sitting on the couch eating pizza, then no. It’s just a supplement, not a magic pill. I agree. I mean, I’ve been using a fitness tracker for a while now, and it’s kind of helped me stay on top of my routine. But I still feel like I need more motivation. Like, I can track my steps, but do I actually want to do something about it? Yeah, that’s the thing, isn’t it? Technology can help, but it’s not a substitute for actually making the effort. I’ve seen people get obsessed with their fitness apps and still end up sedentary. And let’s be honest, someone’s gotta be the one who actually gets up and does the work. I mean, I’m not saying it’s easy, but if you want it, you’ve got to make it happen. I mean, I’m not the most motivated person in the world, but I do try to keep things interesting. Like, I got this new playlist for my workouts, and it’s kind of helping. You know, music can really get you moving. I’m into that. I used to have this old gym playlist, but it got too repetitive. I started making my own, and now I feel like I’m actually getting somewhere. I’ve even been running more lately. That’s cool. I think I need to do that too. Maybe I can go to the gym with someone, like, a friend or something. You know, it’s easier to stay consistent if you’re not doing it alone.

Alright, right, so I was thinking, we need to make a shopping list for tomorrow, yeah? Yeah, I was just about to say that. We need to get some essentials, you know, like bread, milk, and maybe some fruit. Can I get some chocolate? Yeah, sure, but just a little bit. You know how it is with you, always asking for sweets. And don’t forget the eggs, we’re running low. Oh, and maybe some vegetables too. I saw some fresh carrots at the market. Yeah, that sounds good. I’d also like to get some pasta. Can I get some crisps too? You already had them last week, Rob. You’re not going to eat them again. But they’re my favorite! Okay, fine, but just one packet. No more, or I’m taking the crisps away. That’s the spirit. Now, what about the insect problem? You’ve been complaining about it all week. Yeah, I found a spider in my room last night. It was quite big. I saw one in the kitchen too. You know, I think we should set up some traps or something. Oh, you know what I do? I just pour some vinegar in the corners. They don’t like that. I heard that you can use garlic too. Or maybe some essential oils. Garlic is a good idea. I’ve heard that it keeps insects away. Yeah, but I’m not sure if that works. I mean, I’ve seen some people use it, but I don’t know if it actually helps. It might not work for everything, but it’s worth a try. What about if someone gets bitten? I got bitten by a wasp yesterday. It hurt like hell. Yeah, I had a bee sting last week. My arm was swollen for days. That’s not good. So what do you do when you get bitten? I usually put some ice on it. That helps reduce the swelling. I used antiseptic cream. And I took some painkillers. Yeah, and maybe some anti-itch cream too. It helps a lot. Right. Speaking of bites, I heard you were talking about football earlier. Yeah, I was just saying that my team is going to win the match tomorrow. I don’t know, Rob. They’re not that strong. But they’ve been training a lot. I think they’re ready. Well, let’s just hope they don’t get too many injuries.

So, do you know what’s up with Mrs. Thompson? She’s been acting super weird lately. Like, she’s always on her phone during P.E. and she’s never actually talking to us. Yeah, I noticed that too. I think she’s been watching some YouTube videos about how to do yoga or something. I saw her scrolling through her feed during gym class. Oh yeah, I saw that! She even had this weird vibe where she’d pause the class and just stare at her screen like she was trying to figure out how to do a handstand. It was so awkward! I mean, I get that people like to watch videos, but she’s a teacher. She should be teaching, not scrolling through TikTok. I know, right? But I heard she’s been doing some kind of online course for teachers. Like, how to use social media in class or something. Maybe she’s trying to be cool? Maybe, but I still think she’s being rude. I mean, she’s supposed to be guiding us, not copying what we do. I mean, we all use Instagram to post our school stuff, but she’s like, “I’m not part of that.” Yeah, and she even blocked us on Instagram! I tried to tag her in a post about the science fair, and she didn’t even reply. It was so frustrating. I know! Like, she’s our science teacher, and she’s blocking us? That’s not fair. I think she’s just being stubborn. I heard she’s been watching  How I Met Your Mother  on Netflix. I mean, I don’t know, maybe that’s why she’s so… spaced out. Seriously? I mean, it’s a classic show, but do you think that’s why she’s acting so weird? I mean, she’s been watching it for like weeks. I don’t know, but I think she’s just trying too hard to be  with it . Like, she always says she’s not into the whole social media thing, but then she’s on YouTube and Instagram all the time. Exactly! It’s like she’s trying to be both old and new at the same time. I think she might be getting a bit lost in the digital world. Like, I saw her trying to post a video of her cat on Instagram the other day, but she kept messing it up.

I’m not sure if I’ve got a cold or if it’s something more serious. I’ve been coughing all day and my throat hurts like hell. I think I might have caught it from the office last week. You should’ve seen the state of the office last week. Half the team was on antibiotics and the other half was wiping their sore throats with tissues. I’m surprised you haven’t caught anything yet. I tried to keep my distance, but it’s not like I could avoid it. We’ve been working from the same desk for weeks. It’s like a big, smelly bunker. Yeah, I remember you talking about the smell of coffee and stale printer paper. It’s like a sensory overload in there. I think I’m going to start wearing a mask just to be safe, even if I’m not sick. That’s a good idea. I’ve heard about those masks that have filters. They’re supposed to help with respiratory stuff. I might need one if this turns into something worse. Speaking of which, I was thinking about the vaccination thing again. I’ve been meaning to get my booster, but I keep putting it off. What’s your take on it? Honestly, I think it’s better to be safe than sorry. I got the vaccine last year, and I haven’t had a single issue. Plus, I’ve heard that the new variants are more concerning, so it’s probably worth it. I know, but I’m just not sure about the long-term effects. I mean, what if something happens? I’ve heard some stories about people having strange side effects, but I can’t shake the feeling that I’m being told what to think. I get that. There’s a lot of conflicting information out there. But then again, I think it’s better to be proactive. My sister had the vaccine and she’s been fine. She even said it helped her feel more confident about going out. Yeah, I guess that makes sense. I’ll have to think about it more. I’m also worried about the vaccine passing on to my dog. I heard something about animals being affected, but I’m not sure. I think the chance of that is really low. The vaccines are specifically designed for humans.

I can't believe we've got a 7-letter word in there. I thought we were out of letters. Maybe we're just not thinking straight. I mean, it's not like we’re playing with a dictionary or anything. You know, I used to play Scrabble all the time when I was a headmistress. I reckon it's the only time I ever felt like I was actually using my brain. And now you're just talking about it like it's some sort of pastime. You used to chase kids around the school with a clipboard and a clipboard. Oh, don't start. I still have the same clipboard. It’s been through five schools. Yeah, but you’re not the only one who’s been playing Scrabble for years. I remember when I was a student, my dad used to play it with me every Sunday. It was just us and a board in the living room. You know, I think the only time I've actually won a game was when I was a child and my mum was too busy cooking to notice. You’re not the only one who has dodged responsibility like that. I once got away with not doing my homework by telling the teacher I had a family emergency. You mean like the time you told the headmaster you were going to the shops? That was the time I actually did go to the shops. But I got caught trying to buy a new dictionary for the school magazine. I think the only way we're going to win this game is if we stop talking and actually focus on the board. Yeah, but what if we’re just not using the right letters? I know that ‘gridlock’ is a word, but I can't remember how to spell it. Oh, it's G-R-I-D-L-O-C-K. You just have to remember the order. Or you could just Google it. I mean, we live in the 21st century. That’s not the point. The point is, we’re trying to play a game with actual letters. I think I’m going to give up and just post a photo of the board on Facebook. That might be easier than trying to figure out Scrabble. You know, I think I'm going to do that too. It's not like we're going to win anyway.

I've just been thinking about the old days, you know, when I was running my gallery and dealing in antiques. It's funny how time flies, isn’t it? Aye, it does. I remember when I was working in Germany—back in the ‘80s, I think—setting up exhibitions for those printing systems you were so proud of. You had a real knack for it. Oh, that was a long time ago, but I still get a kick out of thinking about how we used to present those machines. The way people would come in, fascinated by the detail, the way it all worked—like magic, really. You know, I still remember one particular exhibition in Munich. The room was packed, and people were captivated by the way the printing system worked. I think it was your idea to use the lighting to create an almost theatrical effect. Yes, that was mine! I used to say, “You don’t just sell machines—you sell an experience.” And it worked. People didn’t just buy the system, they bought the story behind it. That’s the kind of thinking that made you successful. I always thought you had a real eye for marketing. Even when you got into antiques, it was the same—every piece had a history, and you made people see the value in it. Aye, and it wasn’t just about the product, it was about the people who used it. I remember one customer who was a teacher, and he used the printing system in his classroom to teach kids about design. It was brilliant. That’s the stuff dreams are made of. I was always the kind of man who just wanted to keep working, but I suppose when you get to my age, you start to wonder if it’s all worth it. Well, you’ve got to do what you love. I mean, I used to say, “If you’re not working, you’re not living.” You know, even after I retired, I still kept busy with the gallery. It’s the only way I kept myself from going stir-crazy. I suppose I’ve done the same. Though I must admit, I miss the rush of getting up early, heading to the office, and seeing the day unfold. It’s a bit strange being retired and not having that structure. I know what you mean.

Dad, do you remember when we learned about etymology in school? I still think it's so cool that words have such interesting origins. Oh, I remember! You used to love that. I think it was your year when we started learning about the history of words. You were always asking why some words sound the way they do. Yeah, and I still do! Like “quinoa” – I love how it’s from the Quechua language. It’s so interesting how words travel across the world. That’s right. And it’s not just about the origin of words, but also how they change over time. I remember learning about the word “lightning” – it’s from the Old English “fyrnleþing,” which means “fiery thing.” That’s pretty cool, isn’t it? Yeah, I think that’s why I like learning about the history of English. It makes me feel connected to the past. And I love how words like “lightning” still have that original meaning, even though the language has changed so much. That’s true. And I think that’s what makes English so special – it’s constantly evolving. I remember when we were watching the news, and they said that people are now pronouncing “aerial” as “air-ree-ul” instead of “air-ee-ul.” It’s like the language is changing all the time. I heard that too! It’s kind of funny, but it’s also kind of weird. I like the old way, though. I think it’s easier to say “air-ee-ul” – it just flows better. You know, I remember when I was a kid, we didn’t have all these fancy words. It was just simpler. I think it’s easier to spell and pronounce things now, but I guess that’s just how language changes. Maybe you’ll look back one day and think the way we speak now is the old way. I guess so. But I think it’s still important to learn how words came to be. I’ve started learning some Latin words recently, just to help with spelling. It’s actually working! That’s great! I think the more you study, the more you’ll see patterns. It’s like solving a puzzle. Yeah, and I’ve also been trying to learn more about the different regions of England. I’ve been learning to pronounce the names of counties correctly.

Alright, do you reckon we’ve got enough for three? I mean, I know it’s just a basic meal, but I don’t want to be the one who’s hungry at the end. Nah, we’re fine. I’ve seen you cook before, and you’re not that bad. Got a good eye for what’s needed. Though I still don’t get how you managed to put that on the table without burning it. Oh, I’ve had a few lessons. It’s not like I’ve never done it before. I mean, I’ve had to feed people at work too. You know, when we’re hosting conferences and stuff. Though, honestly, I think the first time I cooked for a hundred people, I was more nervous than the guests. You didn’t burn anything, did you? I’ve seen people burn toast and then cry about it. I mean, it’s breakfast, not a funeral. No, no, it was fine. Just a bit of a mess, honestly. But the point is, I’m trying to help out here. I don’t know what it is, but I feel like we’re not as close as we used to be, you know? It’s like we’ve all drifted apart a bit, even though we’re still friends. I think it’s just because we’re all working different hours and stuff. It’s not like we can always meet up. And honestly, with the job I do, I’m out all the time. But I’m trying. I promise, I’ll come over more. You know, just to see what’s going on. That’s good. Look, I know I’m not about to start doing any heavy lifting or anything, but I’m still here. I’m not going anywhere. I mean, I’m retired, but I still like to keep things going. And besides, I’ve got the best stories to tell if you’re ever interested. I could tell you about the time I tried to grow vegetables in my garden and ended up with a whole mess of weeds. Oh, I’ve heard those stories. You’ve told them so many times, I’m starting to believe them. Still, I think it’s good that we’re all still here. Even if it’s just for dinner. Yeah, I agree. It’s nice to see everyone.

So, do you go to the gym often? I mean, I know it's supposed to be good for you, but I’m not really into it. I more of a bar stool kind of guy. Yeah, I do go a couple of times a week. I think it helps with my stress, and since I teach languages, I need to stay on top of my energy levels. Plus, I’ve been trying to get into running, so the gym helps me warm up. That sounds good. I guess I just don’t see the point in spending so much time on it. I like to keep it simple—bar, football match, and then home. I get that. It’s all about what you enjoy. I used to be into cycling, but I haven’t had the time lately. I think I need to make more time for it. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’m a bartender, so my days are pretty busy. I try to get in some kind of exercise, but it’s usually just walking around the bar or doing some stretching after shift. That’s not a bad way to stay active. I think it’s better than nothing. I always tell my students that it’s better to be moving than sitting still. I guess. I just don’t like the idea of getting on a treadmill or going to the gym. It feels too much like work. I can see that. But maybe if you start with something like a short walk or a cycle ride, it could make a difference. It’s all about finding something you enjoy. Maybe. I’ve been thinking about getting a bike. I used to ride when I was younger, but I haven’t done it in years. Maybe that’s something I could get back into. That’s a good idea. If you start small, you might actually stick with it. Plus, it’s a great way to meet people. I know a few people through the gym, and it’s always good to have that kind of social connection. Yeah, I guess. I just need to find the right balance. I don’t want to overdo it, but I also don’t want to be completely sedentary. That’s the key, really. It’s about finding what works for you and making it a habit.

Right, right, we've got to get going, we're late for break time. Oh, don’t worry, I’ve got the coffee ready. Just need to pour it into the mugs. That’s the thing, you know, I’ve been trying to get the donation box up in the village hall, but the council won’t let me put it on the wall. Why not? It’s just a donation box for the school. Yeah, and the plants we got from the charity shop last week—they’re doing really well. I’ve even put a little banner on the box saying “Donations for the school garden.” That’s a good idea. I was thinking of putting a banner on the front of the donation box too. But the council said it’s too much of a distraction. Yeah, I suppose they’re worried about safety or something. Maybe, but the school needs that money, you know. They’ve got the new playground being built, and they need extra funds for the outdoor area. You know, I’ve been thinking about Munchausen Syndrome as well. It’s so strange how people can create such elaborate fakery. Yeah, I remember reading about that in the newspaper last week. One guy actually faked his own illness for years, and his wife was in on it. That’s terrifying. I mean, how do you even know when someone is faking it? It’s like a game of Russian roulette with their own health. You never know when it’s going to blow up in their face. Speaking of which, I had to drive out to Gambia last year for that charity event. I didn’t know what to expect, to be honest. Oh, was that the one where you were supposed to ring a bell for the cause? I think that’s the one. I was going to go too, but I had to take care of the business with the donation box and the plants. That’s a shame. You know, it’s funny how the bell ringing in church is supposed to be about community, but it’s also a way to raise money, isn’t it? Exactly. And the banners we put up at the church—people were really into it. I think we should set up a banner on the donation box too, just to make it more eye-catching.

So, do you guys ever just get bored of scrolling through your phones all the time? I feel like I’m addicted to Instagram and TikTok. It’s like I can’t even think without checking my phone. Yeah, honestly, I feel the same. It’s like we’re all just glued to our screens. But I try to remind myself that there’s more to life than just scrolling. Like, I’ve been trying to actually cook something instead of just ordering takeaway. That’s a good point. I haven’t even cooked for myself in weeks. I just get takeaway or whatever. But I’m like, “Okay, I’m going to try cooking tonight.” And then I end up burning the toast. Oh, I’ve been there. I tried making a stir-fry once, and I burned the noodles and the veggies. I ended up eating them with ketchup. It was better than nothing, honestly. Haha, I’m sure it was. You ever think about how much time we waste on our phones? I mean, we’re all like, “Oh, I need to check my notifications,” but I don’t even remember the last time I had a real conversation without my phone in my hand. Yeah, it’s like we’re so used to being connected all the time. I mean, even when we’re out with friends, we’re on our phones. It’s like the only way we can communicate now. I guess it’s just part of growing up in this generation. I mean, we’ve never known a time without smartphones. But it’s weird how much we rely on them. I mean, I had a friend who got a new phone and couldn’t function without it for a day. It was like watching someone try to survive without Wi-Fi. I know! I tried it once. No phone, no internet. It was like, “I can’t even remember how to text.” I just sat there for an hour staring at the wall, thinking, “What am I even doing here?” That sounds like a nightmare. I’ve never gone without my phone. I mean, I tried once when I was traveling, but I just got so lost and freaked out. I had to ask for directions, and I didn’t even know how to use Google Maps. I remember when I first started using Google Maps.

So, do you know what’s happening with the car, Reg? I’ve been trying to get it started first thing this morning, and it just sputters and dies. Not a good start to the day. Yeah, I know, I saw you trying to start it earlier. You’ve got a bit of a problem with the ignition, haven’t you? It’s been acting up for a while now. I told you, John, it’s not just the ignition. It’s the whole damn engine. It’s been making that funny noise for weeks. I don’t know what’s going on with it. I’ve been thinking, maybe it’s the fuel pump? I remember reading somewhere that if the fuel pump is failing, it can cause all sorts of issues, like stalling and not starting properly. Yeah, that might be it, but I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve been trying to work it out myself, but I don’t have the tools for that kind of thing. I think I need to get it checked out by a mechanic. You should. I mean, I don’t want to be stuck on the road again. Last time it broke down, I had to walk two miles to get help. That was in the middle of nowhere, and it got pretty cold, and I was really worried. I know, I know. That was a nightmare. I’m just trying to make it through the week. I’ve got to get to work on time every day. I can’t afford to be stuck on the side of the road again. I hear you. I’ve got the same problem, actually. My car’s been giving me trouble for a while now. I just haven’t had the money to get it sorted. I think it’s time to get a new one, but I don’t know where to start. You could always look into buying a second-hand car. I know a few people who have got good deals on used cars. It’s not the best, but it’s cheaper than getting a new one. Yeah, that’s a thought. But I’ve got to be careful. I don’t want to get something that breaks down the first week. I’ve had my fair share of that. True, but you can’t afford to sit around waiting for a car that works.

I just can’t believe how long this journey is taking, even with the motorway. I thought it would be quicker with the traffic lights out of the way. I know, it’s been a while since we’ve had to drive this route. I think it’s been years since I was last on the M6 southbound. I remember when I was working in the city, I used to do this a couple of times a week. Yeah, it’s funny how things change. I used to drive this route every day to get to work. Didn’t even think about the miles. Now I’m not driving at all. I’m still trying to get used to the idea of not having a car. That must be tough, especially with the weather like this. I was just thinking about the move. We’re still trying to figure out where we’re going to settle. My cousin in Cork said she could help us if we wanted. That’s kind of what I was just thinking too. I mean, I’ve been working from home for a while, so maybe it’s time to get out of this city and see something new. But honestly, I’ve got this grief of moving, you know? It’s like watching a house fall apart and not being able to fix it. I know the feeling, and I know the feeling of not being able to fix it. I did try to fix my own place when I got back from the job. It’s just... things changed. I still get this sense of not knowing what the next step is. I think the key is just to take it one step at a time. I mean, I’ve been reading about people who moved from place to place all their lives, and they found happiness in the change. I just need to not worry so much about the unknown. That’s what I keep telling myself. And I also keep thinking about how much easier it would be if I had a car. I mean, it was so simple to get around before. I miss that. I could just pop to the shops and not have to worry about public transport or waiting for a bus. I remember when I was working in the oil industry, I used to fly everywhere. Yeah, go to a client meeting in London, or Germany, or even Dubai.

Mummy, I’m so upset! I can’t believe my bike got stolen! I know, sweetheart, I’m really sorry. But I just got a call from the police saying they found your bike near the bridge. They’re bringing it back to the shop to check it out. Oh, really? So they’re going to return it to me? Yeah, they said they’ll contact the shop and then they’ll get it to you. But I just want to make sure it’s safe and nothing was taken from it. I hope it’s not too damaged. I was really excited about going to college next week, and the bike was going to be my main way of getting around. I know, I’m sorry about that. But you know, I remember when I was your age, I had a similar experience with my bike. It was a bit of a nightmare. What happened? Well, I was out with my friends, and we left the bike outside the shop for a minute. When we came back, it was gone. I was so upset I cried for hours. But in the end, it turned out someone had found it and was holding on to it, waiting for the owner to come back. Oh, that’s not so bad, I guess. Yeah, it was a bit of a relief when it was returned. But it also made me more careful about where I left my bike. I started locking it every time, even if it was just for a minute. I should do that too. Maybe I’ll get a better lock next time. But how do I know if it’s safe to ride it again? Well, the police said they checked it and nothing was taken. So you can ride it again, but just be more careful. Maybe even put a sticker on it so people know it belongs to you. That’s a good idea. I’ll ask the shop if they can put a little label on it. Great. And also, maybe you should start using your phone a little more to keep track of your bike. I know you’re not into social media much, but sometimes it can help go viral if something happens. Yeah, I guess. I just don’t want to be on social media all the time. It’s a bit weird for me.

I can't believe we've got all these train pieces out. It’s like we’re trying to build a real railway system in this cottage. Yeah, I know. I've always thought this game was a bit of a gimmick, but I guess it's fun when you’re with friends. Especially on holiday. It’s not just about the trains, though. It’s about the strategy. I mean, I’ve got the best route from Cardiff to London, but I’m not sure if I should use the green or the red line for the next leg. You could always use the blue one. I've used that one before and it's the shortest way to get to Manchester. But you have to be careful with the red—you might end up going the long way around. Oh, I used the red one the other day. It actually worked out better than I thought. I ended up with more points than I expected, which was nice. That’s the thing, though. You never know what’s going to happen. One minute you’re on the right track, and the next you’re stuck waiting for a train that’s not even on the board. Exactly. It’s like real life sometimes. You think you've got everything planned, and then something happens that throws you off track. I know. And I think the worst part is when you’ve got all the pieces laid out and you realize you’ve missed a crucial connection. That’s the real test. Keeping your head clear and not getting frustrated. Some people just get too focused on the pieces and forget the bigger picture. Yeah, I've definitely been there. I think the key is to take it slowly and not rush. It’s a game, after all. You don’t have to win every time. True. And besides, even if you don’t win, you can always eat while you play. I brought some of those spicy sausages you love. Oh, you did? I thought I was the only one who remembered to bring them. What’s the catch? Is it going to be too spicy? No, no, they’re not too bad. They’re just the usual kind. But I think you’ll like them. They’re made with some of the local ingredients from the market. That sounds good.

Alright, do you think we've got this game figured out yet? I still can’t get my head around the scoring system. Honestly, I think I’ve given up trying to understand it. I just play to win, or at least to not lose too badly. Haha, I feel the same. I mean, it’s supposed to be a strategic game, but every time I think I’ve got a plan, something goes wrong. Oh, don’t get me started. I remember one time when I thought I had the perfect strategy, only to realize that the rules had changed halfway through the game. I was so confused, I ended up moving my pieces in the opposite direction by accident. Oh no, that’s not fair! I’ve been through that too. You know, I think part of the fun is just playing with the rules, breaking them, and seeing what happens. Yeah, but sometimes I wonder if it’s more about the culture of the game than the game itself. Like, how people from different regions play it differently. That’s interesting. I’ve heard about that in some of the lectures I teach. Different cultures have different interpretations of the same game, sometimes even the same rules. It’s like a social ritual, almost. Exactly! And I think that’s why I love playing board games with people from different backgrounds. You get to see how the same game can be played so differently, and it's just fascinating. I agree. It’s like a microcosm of the world—everyone brings their own way of doing things. It’s not just about winning; it’s about the experience. Yeah, and I think that’s why I prefer playing with people I know well. We can have that kind of conversation while we’re playing, like how we talk about the rules, the strategies, and even the way we drink during the game. Oh, right! I remember when we first started playing this, we tried to have a little competition with our drinks. Whoever got the highest score got to have a shot. It was a bit of a disaster, but it was also hilarious. I still remember that night. You started with a glass of wine, then moved to a beer, and by the end, you were sipping on a gin and tonic like it was nothing. Yeah,

So, do you think we should bring the leftover lasagna from last night? It’s in the fridge, and it’s still edible, I think. I don’t know, we’re having a proper meal tonight. Not sure we need the lasagna. Unless you want to have it for breakfast tomorrow? Maybe. Or we could just throw it out. I’m not sure how much longer it’s going to last. I think it’s been in there for three days now. Oh, don’t throw it out. You can always repurpose it. Maybe make some lasagna rolls or something. It’s not like we can’t use it. That’s a good idea. My mum used to do that all the time. She’d take leftover food and turn it into something new. I guess it’s a bit of a waste if you just throw it away. Yeah, I guess that makes sense. Although I’d be honest, I’d rather have something fresh. I’m not a huge fan of using leftovers. It just doesn’t taste the same. Well, it’s up to you two. But I think it’s better to use it than let it go to waste. You can always say we’re being eco-friendly. That’s true. Plus, I’ve got some herbs and garlic in the fridge. Maybe we can make a new dish out of it. If we’re being creative, at least we can say we’re making something out of nothing. Yeah, I suppose that’s a way to look at it. Also, I think we should start looking at moving house eventually. I mean, we’ve been here for nearly two years now. It’s time to think about the future. I agree. But I don’t know if we’re ready yet. I still need to finish my postgrad course, and I’m not sure if I want to move too soon. Plus, I’m not sure what we’d do with all our stuff. You can always sell or donate the furniture. I had that problem when I moved out of my old place. I ended up selling half the stuff and giving the rest away. It was a relief. That’s a good point. I think we could do that. But I don’t know if we’d have enough space in our new place.

So, do you think we’ll get through this traffic any time soon, Mum? I mean, it’s like a complete gridlock out here. I know, I know. I saw a sign saying it’s “East London to North London – 45 minutes, but don’t expect to get there in time.” Honestly, I’m starting to think that’s the official advice now. I’ve heard about this. I think it’s all because of the new building site near Tottenham. Everyone’s trying to get to work, and the lanes are just… gone. You’re right. It’s like they’ve phased out the motorway entirely. I mean, I can almost hear the sound of the cars groaning as they try to get through. It’s ridiculous. You know, I was thinking about what you said the other day about digital versus print. I mean, we’re all driving around with tablets and phones, but I still prefer reading a real book. It’s like, I can’t even focus on a screen for more than 10 minutes without my brain just… zoning out. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to get back into reading more, but it’s so easy to get distracted by notifications. I got a subscription to TLS – The London Review of Books – last month, and I’ve only read one article so far. It’s got me hooked, though. That’s a good one. I should check out that magazine. I’ve been meaning to read more about literature. Besides, I’ve got an essay due next week on postmodernism and I need a solid reference. Oh, you’re doing a literature essay? That’s a relief. I thought it was going to be about French philosophy or something. No, no, no. It’s a classic topic. I just need to make sure I don’t go too deep into the theoretical stuff. The professor said we should focus on examples – like, you know, how it’s used in modern fiction. Sounds good. You’ll do fine. And if you ever want to talk about the writing process, I’m always happy to chat. I’m a literary editor, after all. Actually, I was thinking of going to France this summer – maybe for a short trip. I’m trying to get out of London for a bit. France? That’s a great idea.

So, do you remember that time we tried to go on that holiday to the Lake District and ended up in a minibus full of people who thought they were on a stag do? Oh yeah! That was the year we all tried to be like, "We’re going on a proper holiday" but ended up with a group of blokes who thought they were on a hunting trip. I remember that! One of them kept trying to tell us about his dad’s hunting dog. It was like he was trying to impress us with his "wild side." And then we got stuck in the middle of nowhere because the minibus broke down. We had to walk for like two hours to get to the nearest town. I was wearing my best hiking boots and they were still muddy by the time we got there. Oh, and don’t even get me started on the accommodation. It was this tiny cottage with no heating, and everyone was sleeping in the same room. I ended up sharing a bed with a guy who kept snoring so loudly I thought he was a chainsaw. That’s nothing. I remember one of the nights we were all sitting around the fire and someone dared someone to try and catch a frog. It was like something out of a horror movie. The guy who tried it ended up falling into the river and had to be pulled out by the local farmer. And the worst part? We all got food poisoning from the "home-cooked" meals someone made. I think they used something from the shed. It was vile. I still have nightmares about that. I swear I still see that guy in the river, trying to save his dignity. Honestly, the only good thing that happened was when we had to climb a mountain and everyone collapsed. We were all like, "This is it, we’re done," but then we got to the top and saw the view. It was worth it. You know what’s funny? We all thought we were being adventurous, but in the end, we just ended up as a group of blokes with blisters, hungover, and no idea what we were doing. Still, it’s one of those stories that you can’t forget. You know, the kind of thing you’ll tell your kids when they’re like, "What’s the worst thing that ever happened to you?"

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about going wild camping again this winter. It’s been a while since I did it properly, and I’ve been feeling a bit restless lately. The city just doesn’t do it for me anymore. Oh, you’re talking about the kind of wild camping where you’re out in the hills, with no electricity, no heating, just the stars above you? I remember when I used to do that with my kids. It was so peaceful, and it really brought us closer. But now, with the weather being so unpredictable, I’m not sure. Yeah, but it’s not just about the cold. I think it’s more about the connection with nature. Being in the wild, you get that sense of being part of something much bigger. I’ve been reading about how immersion in nature helps with mental health. It’s like a reset for the mind. Exactly. I’ve been feeling a bit stuck in my routine lately. The pressure of work and responsibilities have been taking their toll. I think a few nights under the stars would help me get some perspective. That sounds really nice, but don’t you think it might be too risky in the winter? I’ve read about people getting lost or suffering from hypothermia. You have to be careful with the weather, the terrain, and the equipment you bring. That’s true, but as long as you plan properly, it can be safe. I’ve done some research into winter camping techniques. You need the right gear: a good tent, thermal clothing, a sleeping bag rated for the temperature, and a reliable source of heat. Even a small fire can make a big difference. I’ve always been a bit of a gear-head, so I’m not going to be too worried about that. But I do think I need to get out more, not just to enjoy the scenery but to clear my head. There’s something about being away from technology and the noise that helps me think more clearly. I agree. I’ve been trying to get out more myself, even if it’s just a walk in the park with a thermos and a book. It’s amazing how a little bit of time in nature can make such a big difference. I hope you have a great time, though.

So, do you know what’s the best film you’ve ever seen? I’m trying to think if there’s anything I’ve seen lately that’s really stuck with me. Hmm, that’s a tough one. I think I’d have to go with  Blade Runner 2049 . The visuals were just incredible. It’s such a haunting portrayal of the future. But then again, I’ve always been a fan of  The Dark Knight —how do you top Heath Ledger’s performance? Oh, I agree. That Joker was just... perfect. But I don’t know, I’ve been really into  Everything Everywhere All At Once  lately. It’s wild, chaotic, and somehow manages to be both heartbreaking and hilarious. I’ve heard a lot about that one. I think I’ve seen a few clips. It’s got that sort of everything-you-need-to-know-is-in-the-title vibe, right? Yeah, exactly. It’s like, you can’t really summarize it in one sentence. But I love how it takes the concept of multiverse and makes it feel really personal. It’s not just about the action or the visuals—it’s about the emotional journey. That’s a good point. I think that’s what makes it stand out. I’ve been thinking about reading  The Road  too. I’ve heard it’s a really powerful book. Oh, that’s a good one. I’ve read it before. It’s such a bleak, raw story, but it’s also got this strange beauty to it. It makes you think about what’s really important in life. Yeah, I mean, it’s not the easiest read, but the emotional weight is there. I think I’ll try it. Have you read  1984 ? Definitely. I think it’s still one of the most important books ever written. It’s so relevant now, with all the talk about surveillance and government control. It’s scary how much of it is actually happening in real life. No kidding. I think I’ve read it a few times, but every time, it feels like something new. It’s like the book is alive. I know, right? It’s strange how literature can still feel so powerful even after all these years. Yeah, and then there’s food. I’ve been obsessed with trying different cuisines lately. I think I’m going to start cooking more at home instead of relying on takeaways.

Alright, do you remember the story about the time we went to the seaside and the pier collapsed? Oh, I remember that! You were so scared when the waves came in and the whole thing started to fall apart. I thought we were going to be washed away! I was so nervous! I clung onto your hand the whole time. I didn’t even want to go on the ride with the horses because I thought they might fall too. Oh, you were such a little coward. But you did grow up, didn’t you? Now you’re talking about things like Excel and PlayStation, which is even more impressive. Yeah, I guess I have grown up. But I still like stories. I remember you telling me about the Brownie Promise evening, the one where you had to do all these things like helping the community and cleaning up the park. That was so fun! We got to wear our Brownie uniforms and help clear the litter. I remember we found a bottle full of old coins and we thought it was treasure. That was the best part, wasn’t it? I still remember the look on your face when you opened the bottle and saw the coins inside. It felt like we were really on an adventure. Yeah, it was amazing. I wonder what became of those coins. I bet they were worth nothing, though. Maybe they were meant to be a lesson in patience. Like, you can’t always find treasure in the most obvious places. Sometimes it’s just about doing the right thing. Mom, can we play some games on the PlayStation now? I’ve got a new level on my favorite game. Not yet, sweetheart. We need to finish talking about the story. Maybe after you’ve done your bedtime reading and we’ve talked about the Brownie Promise again. That way, you can remember it for a long time. I think I’ll go and get a book from the shelf. I remember you used to read me stories about typewriters and how they worked. You said they were like magic machines. They were! I still remember the clatter of the keys and the smell of the paper. I think I still have that old typewriter in the attic. Maybe one day we can find it and try it out again. Can we go looking for it after we finish our stories?

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about that old house of yours, Anton. It’s been on the market for ages, hasn’t it? I mean, I know you’re not in a rush, but it’s got to be nice to have somewhere to call your own, even if it’s not your current home. Yeah, it’s been on the market for quite a while. I mean, I’ve had a few people come in, but nothing really stuck. Some people just seem to be looking for a quick sale, and others are like, “well, it’s not in a prime location.” Not that I’m trying to sell quickly, but I do miss the place, you know? It was my first home, after all. Yeah, I can see that. I mean, you’ve got a bit of a history there. I remember when you used to bring me jam from the garden when you were still growing herbs. That’s how I got hooked on homemade preserves, really. I still have a jar or two tucked away in my kitchen. Oh, I still do that, actually. I’ve got a little patch of land out back where I grow some herbs and even a few fruit bushes. It’s not much, but it’s been a hobby of mine. Though I do wonder if I should be trying to sell the house, I might as well sell the land too. It’s just too much to maintain these days. I can imagine. I mean, someone who’s in your position, with a bit of a steady income, but not a ton, you’d need to weigh your options. I’ve been through that myself – trying to decide whether it’s worth it to keep things as they are or not. But the thing is, I’ve had to deal with all sorts of things since I retired. Roadworks, junk mail, even phones – I mean, how many times have I had to explain that I’m not interested in buying that new phone with all the fancy features? Oh, I hear you. I’ve been getting more of that lately. Those mysterious letters just arrive in the post, and I can’t even tell what they’re about half the time. I mean, I still get bills, but some of the ones I get go straight to the bin.

So, do you know what’s the biggest thing I’ve learned since I started working as a nurse? What’s that? That people are more complicated than you think. You think you know someone, and then you find out they’ve got a whole world of secrets. That sounds like a soap opera, not a real life. No, it’s real. Like last week, this guy came in with a nasty infection, and it turns out he’s been taking his medication wrong for years. Didn’t even tell the doctor he was mixing it with alcohol. Oh no. That’s dangerous. Yeah, and he didn’t even know he was being watched. I caught him trying to hide the bottle from the nurse. That’s so weird. I mean, I’ve got a cousin who does that with his antidepressants. He says he’s “just trying to live his life,” but it’s not helping. That’s why I always tell people—never hide your meds, and always tell your doctor everything. I mean, we’re not in the position to judge, but we’ve got to protect ourselves. Absolutely. Speaking of protection, have you heard about that new face cream I’ve been using? It’s supposed to help with the dry skin from all the hand washing. Oh, you’ve been washing your hands a lot? Yeah, I’ve been working in a ward where there’s a lot of germs. Also, I’ve been trying to get back into fitness, so I’m doing a lot of cardio and sweating. My skin’s been a mess. Oh, I get that. I’ve been using this moisturizer that’s supposed to help with the dry patches on my hands. My wife says it’s the best thing since sliced bread. I’ve been trying to get into something too. I’ve been thinking about getting a dog. I mean, I know it’s a big responsibility, but I’d love to have a pet to keep me company while I work from home. That’s a great idea. I’ve got a cat, and he’s been amazing. He keeps me company and doesn’t ask for anything in return. That’s the best part about pets. They’re loyal and don’t judge you. I think I’d love to have a dog, though I’m not sure I’ve got the time or space.

So, how’s the part-time job going? I know you said you were trying to get into programming full-time, but I haven’t heard much about it lately. It’s going alright, honestly. I’m learning a lot, and the hours are flexible, which is great because I’m still studying. But I’m starting to feel like I need to get more formal training. Maybe even do a proper course. That makes sense. I mean, you’re already studying for a postgrad, so it’s not like you’re not working hard. But do you want to keep doing this part-time thing, or is it just a stepping stone? It’s a stepping stone for sure. I’m thinking of applying for a masters in something related to tech, maybe AI or data science. I’m really into it, and I think it could help me get a better job in the long run. That sounds ambitious, but I like it. I mean, I’d be the first to say I’m not the most ambitious person in the world, but I can see how that could work for you. Speaking of ambition—what about you? How’s your copywriting job going? It’s okay. I’ve been working on a few campaigns for a local brand, and it’s been fun. But I’m starting to feel like I need to up my game. Maybe switch industries or get more experience in something like digital marketing or branding. That’s a good point. I mean, copywriting is great, but it’s kind of a niche. I think if you were to move into a more tech or data-driven field, you could have more opportunities. But then again, I don’t know what you want to do in the long run. Honestly, I’m not sure. I like the idea of working in media, but I also feel like I need to make more money. I mean, rent in London is killing me. I’m trying to save up for a deposit on a place, but it’s not happening fast enough. Yeah, I hear that. Even though I’m not working full-time, I still have to cover the bills. It’s tough, but I think we’re both in the same boat. I mean, we’re both trying to build something for the future.

So, do you think we should get a dog? I mean, I know it's a big decision, but I feel like I need something to keep me active more. I’ve been stuck indoors all week with this cold, and I’m honestly getting a bit stir-crazy. Honestly, I think it’s a great idea, but only if you’re sure you can handle it. You know how stubborn I am when it comes to exercise—without a dog, I’d probably just sit on the couch all day. But if you’ve got the time and energy, it could be really good for you. I agree with both of you, but I think you’re jumping the gun a bit. You’ve only been sick for a couple of days. Besides, you know how much of a mess I get with pets. I’d probably end up in the vet’s office more than anywhere else. Yeah, I know, but I’ve been thinking about it for a while. I’d be the one taking them for walks, feeding them, and cleaning up after them. I’d be the one who’d have to deal with the mess, not you. You’re just the one who’d be annoyed when they start barking at the neighbors. True, but then again, you’re the one who’d be the one who’d have to take them to the park, which is a bit of a trek from here. I mean, if we’re already talking about exercise, maybe we could just start going for walks together. That way, you don’t have to rush out every day to do it. That’s a good point. But you know, I’ve been thinking about house prices lately. I’ve been looking at some properties in the area, and the prices have gone up so much it’s almost ridiculous. I was thinking maybe we should consider moving, just to get a bit more space. It’s not like we’re not already stretched thin here. I can see the appeal, but I’m not sure about moving right now. I mean, I like the location. It’s close to the shops and the train station. Plus, I don’t think we’re ready for a big change. I’d be more comfortable staying put. That’s fair. But I have to say, sometimes I think about how much easier life would be in a bigger house.

So, how’s the new job going, then? I heard you got promoted to a senior role at the firm. Honestly, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. The project I’m working on is massive—like, the biggest one we’ve had since I started. It’s a civil engineering project for a new bridge in the north, and I’m leading the team. It’s a bit of a pressure cooker, but I’m handling it. That sounds intense. I know you’ve always been good with numbers and the technical side, so it’s probably fitting. But how’s the budget looking? I heard there’s been some talk about the government cutting funding for infrastructure. Yeah, it’s definitely a topic of conversation. The budget is tight, but I think the project is still on track. We’ve been working closely with local authorities and the EU funding, so it’s not all doom and gloom. Although, if the government pulls out, it could cause some serious problems. That’s worrying. I mean, I know how important infrastructure is for the economy, especially after what’s happened with the pandemic. You don’t want to see projects fall through when they’re so crucial. Exactly. I guess it’s all about how the funding is managed. But then again, I’m not sure how much the government actually knows about the projects they’re funding. Sometimes it feels like they just throw money around and don’t follow through. I get that. It’s also funny how people always talk about the budget, but no one ever actually puts their money where their mouth is. I mean, look at the state of the public services. It’s a mess, isn’t it? Oh, absolutely. But I guess that’s a whole different conversation. Let’s talk about something lighter. I heard you were up for the musical at the university? Yeah, I’m doing  Hamilton —just the chorus, but it’s a chance to be part of something big. I’ve always loved musicals, but I never thought I’d end up being in one. It’s surreal, to be honest. That’s amazing! You should be so proud. I’ve never been the performing type, but I do love the way musicals bring people together. It’s like a whole world of characters and stories.

So, do you reckon the council will actually do anything about that new development they've got planned for the corner of the park? I mean, it’s been on the agenda for ages now, and I still haven’t seen anything concrete. I don’t know, mate. I heard they’re talking about building some sort of community centre or something, but I haven’t seen any signs of it yet. I mean, I’ve been driving past there every day for years, and I still don’t know what’s going to happen. Yeah, I guess it’s one of those things that’s just sitting there waiting for someone to take the bull by the horns. I mean, I can imagine what it’s like for the people who live near there. You’d think they’d be more vocal about it, but I don’t see much of that. I think they’ve got their own problems. I mean, if you’re a regular taxi driver, you’ve got more pressing things to worry about than planning permissions or council meetings. Besides, the people who live there, they’re not exactly the most active bunch, if you know what I mean. Fair enough. But I can’t help but think that if they had the proper infrastructure, it’d be a better place for everyone – more shops, better lighting, maybe even some kind of green space. I mean, you can’t just ignore the potential for that kind of improvement. I’d say the people who actually live there would be the ones to push for that. But I don’t know, maybe they’re just waiting for something to happen. I mean, look at the state of the gutters on this place. I’ve been telling you for weeks about that. I know, I know. It’s not like I haven’t been trying to get it fixed. But the council won’t do anything unless someone actually reports it. And even then, they just say they’ll get around to it. Exactly. I don’t know how people manage to live here with the state of things. I mean, I’ve got to do this job, and I’ve got to do it properly, but I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t a bit tired of the goings-on. I get you.

So, do you think we've got enough food for the whole trip? I know it's only a few days, but I've been thinking about the snacks and the meals we can stop for. I think we're okay. We’ve got enough for the first few days, but I don’t want to be caught without anything if we end up stopping at a place that doesn’t have much of a shop. Fair enough. I’ve got a couple of energy bars, some dried fruit, and a few packets of crisps. But I’m also thinking about the meals. I mean, we’re not going to be eating takeaway every night. Yeah, that’s true. I’ve been trying to plan out the meals. I think I’ll do some pasta dishes, and then maybe some simple things like sandwiches or wraps. Oh, and I’ve got a few tins of beans and some pasta sauce in the fridge. That sounds good. I’ve also been thinking about how we can clear out the clutter in the campervan. It’s getting a bit tight, and I don’t want to be sitting in there with all the stuff from last time we were on the road. Yeah, I agree. Maybe we should start sorting through the stuff – anything we don’t need can go in the bin or be donated. I’ve got some of my old books and things that I haven’t used in a while. That's a good idea. I think it'll make the space feel a bit more open. Oh, and what about the hitchhikers? I saw a few on the road earlier – they were waving like crazy. Yeah, they were. I thought they were just regular people, but then they started talking about going to Tarnow and then continuing further south. I didn’t want to stop, but I was curious. Maybe we’ll see some more along the way. You know, I was thinking about how different this is from when I was your age. Back then, you didn’t have all these apps or Websites to plan trips with. You just went by what you had and took the risks. I guess it’s a bit different now. I mean, I still love the freedom of travel, but I think I’m more prepared. I’ve had a few trips with friends before, and I learned from them.

So, do you think we’ll get there in time for the Hay Festival? I don’t think so. We’re already half an hour behind schedule because of the train strike. Yeah, and we’re not even halfway there yet. I wouldn’t be surprised if we end up missing the whole thing. That’s sad. I wanted to see that author I read about last week. She writes about growing up in London, which is kind of like me, except I’m not from London. Wait, I am from London. You’re from London? Yeah, I was born there. But I moved to Manchester when I was like nine. Oh, so you’re a Londoner by birth, but a Mancunian by upbringing? That’s interesting. Yeah, and I grew up in Bolton. I’ve never been to London, though. I’ve always been more into the North. But I’ve heard the Hay Festival is a big deal. It’s amazing, really. I went a few years ago. You get to meet all these writers and hear them read. It’s like a dream come true for book lovers. I want to be a writer one day. I’ve got a story I wrote about my childhood. It’s about this time I got lost in the woods near my old house. Lost in the woods? That sounds scary. What happened? It wasn’t that scary. I was just playing with my brother, and we got separated. I ended up finding a house with a woman who gave me a sandwich and let me stay for the night. That sounds like a story you should publish! I know, right? I think it’s kind of like a fairytale. Maybe it is. You know, sometimes the most ordinary things can turn into the most amazing stories. I hope I get to write about that. I’m also doing my exams next month. I’m a bit nervous. Exams? That’s a big deal. Did you ever have to do exams in your childhood? I had to. I remember my mum used to help me study. She’s a big fan of reading and writing, so she made sure I got through. I wish my mum was here to help me. She’s been really busy with work and stuff. Well, I’m sure she’s been working hard for a reason.

Oh, I can't believe it's you, Elsie! I thought you'd gone off to Scotland for good after that ridiculous argument about the garden. I mean, it was just a few weeds, wasn't it? Oh, don't start, Mavis. You were the one who said I should clear out the old stuff from the attic and not just let it gather dust. And you know I didn’t do it properly. I just moved everything to the garage. Yeah, and it’s still there. The old photo albums, the broken teapot, the…  gasp  the old jokes you used to write when you were a teacher. What were they even about? Oh, you know, just silly stuff. I used to write them for the school newsletter. “Why did the chicken cross the road? To get to the other side, of course!” – and then I’d sign it “The Great Mavis.” I remember that. You used to say it was for the students’ benefit. That they’d laugh and learn something from it. But I think they just thought you were weird. I think they thought you were funny. At least, that’s what the stickers on the photo albums said. “Mavis the Master of Humour.” Oh, don’t be silly, lad. I don’t think “master” is the right word. I just used to keep the jokes in a box under the bed. That’s where I found them when I cleaned out the attic last year. And now you’re back to clear it all out again, aren’t you? You said you’d do it yourself. I did. But then I got distracted by the TV. And the cat. And that new plug-in that plays music. That’s not a plug-in, it’s a smart speaker. And it doesn’t just play music, it tells jokes too. Oh, really? I thought it was just for playing music. Why would it tell jokes? It’s a new kind of technology. It’s supposed to entertain you. Well, I think it’s got a bad sense of humour. I asked it to tell a joke, and it said, “Why don’t skeletons fight each other? They don’t have the guts!” That’s not a bad joke. It’s not bad, but it’s not great either. It’s like the jokes Mavis used to write. I like that.

So, do you think this laptop is going to be any good? I’ve had it for a week now and it’s still not working properly. I’ve had mine for months and it's holding up fine. Maybe you just need to get used to it. Yeah, I mean, I’ve had a laptop since I was in sixth form. My dad used to say it was the best thing since sliced bread. Oh, I bet he was right. But this one—it just keeps freezing up. I tried running some software updates, but it crashed halfway through. Hmm, that’s annoying. Maybe you should check the hardware? I’ve heard that sometimes older laptops don’t handle new software too well. I know what you mean. I had to upgrade my old one because the RAM was too low. It was like trying to run a gaming PC on a toaster. That’s not a metaphor I’ve ever heard before, but I guess it’s a bit of a relief to know I’m not the only one who’s had problems. I think we all have that one laptop that we love to death and then one day it just dies. Speaking of dying—I’ve been thinking about getting back into hiking. I’ve got this old camera from when I was at school, and I thought maybe I could use it for some photos. That sounds cool. I’ve always wanted to try hiking, but I’m a bit of a wimp when it comes to being out in the woods. You don’t have to be a superhero to do it. Just wear proper shoes, bring some snacks, and try to enjoy the view. Exactly. I’ve been going to the local forest a couple of times a week. It’s peaceful, and I’ve even started taking some videos for YouTube. YouTube? Are you making content? Yeah, just some stuff about hobbies, tech, and the local area. It’s not professional, but it’s fun. That’s awesome. I’ve been meaning to start something like that. Maybe I could do some travel vlogs or something. Wait, are you saying you’re into travel? Yeah, I’ve been thinking about going to South Korea. I’ve watched a few videos about it, and it looks amazing. South Korea? I’ve been there once, and it was incredible.

So, do you know what’s really weird about this place? I mean, it's a bistro in Tarnow, and it's brand new, but the menu is all in Polish with a few English words here and there. I feel like I'm in a different country, but somehow it's still England in my head. Yeah, I know what you mean. I had to ask the waiter a few times what some of the dishes were. I mean, I’m used to seeing things like “kiszko” and “bigos” on menus, but I still get confused. I think part of it is just the contrast. I mean, I grew up in Cambridge, where everything's pretty well-known, and now I’m here in Poland, and it’s like I’m suddenly part of this whole different world. It’s kind of exciting, but also a bit overwhelming. I get that. I mean, I’m still in England for work, but I came here to teach English as a foreign language, and now I’m surrounded by people who speak Polish like it's their native language. It’s funny, isn’t it? You think you’re the teacher, but sometimes you’re the one who needs the help. Exactly. And then there’s the whole thing about the language. I mean, I know a bit of Polish, but I’m not fluent. And don’t even get me started on trying to order a coffee without using the word “kawa.” It feels like I have to dress the part, you know? I know. I think it’s all part of the experience, though. I mean, I used to think that being a teacher would make me feel more at home in any country, but the truth is, it’s still a whole new world. I think part of the reason I’m here is because I want to learn more about myself, not just about the language. That’s a good way to put it. You know, I was thinking about it the other day—the way we talk about our dreams. We all have them, right? Some of us are chasing them, some of us have given up, and others are just waiting for the right moment. Yeah, I think that’s true. I mean, I’ve had my share of setbacks. I was in a relationship for a while that ended because we were just not compatible, and I had to rebuild my confidence.

So, do you think we should go to the Dorset Steam Fair next weekend? I heard it’s a really big event and there are loads of things to do. I've heard about it, but I don’t think I’ve ever been. I’ve always been more into the countryside than big events. But if you want to go, I'm sure it’ll be fun. Just don't forget to book your ticket early though, they do sell out. Oh, I’ve been wanting to go for ages! My brother was talking about it last week. But, I’m a bit worried about getting a ticket for someone with a disability. I don’t want to miss out because of that. Yeah, I know what you mean. I think they have specific concessions for disabled people, but I’m not too sure. I’ll check the website later. It might be worth calling them to confirm. You should do that. I’ve heard in the past that some events can be a bit rough on the disabled, especially if there aren’t enough facilities. It’s important to know what you’re getting into. I’m also thinking about whether to bring my cat along. She’s pretty laid back, but sometimes she gets a bit over-excited. I don’t want her to be stressed or end up getting lost. Oh, she’s a bit of a handful, isn’t she? You know what she’s like. Still, if you do go, maybe someone can keep an eye on her while you’re exploring. It might be easier than trying to take her everywhere. I think that’s a good idea. You could even get a special seat for her, just in case. I remember when I took my dog to a fair once, they had little crates and everything. It wasn’t too bad. That sounds great. I just need to make sure the ticket includes that. I can’t have her running around all over the place. She’s not too bad, but I don’t want her to get too hot or too cold. You could always bring a bit of her favorite food too. She gets really excited if I bring her snacks. Maybe that’ll help keep her calm. That’s a good point. If you do go, I’d suggest taking some small treats and a water bowl.

I just got a message from my cousin in Manchester saying they're going to move house again. They've been living in the same place for over twenty years now, and now they're going to move to a new town. I don’t know if that’s the right thing to do. I think it’s brave of them, honestly. Moving house that many times is not easy. I’ve only moved once in my life, and I still remember the stress from that. But maybe they're just chasing a better opportunity or something. What do you think, Karen? Honestly, I don’t know. I mean, moving is just part of life, right? Especially when you're trying to find your place in the world. I know my mum has moved several times too. It’s just how it works. Yeah, and I think it's important to keep an open mind about it. But then again, I can’t help but wonder if some people move just to escape something. I’ve heard stories where people move because they’re unhappy or feeling unfulfilled. It’s a bit of a double-edged sword. I guess it’s the same with everything in life. You can’t always stay put. But I do worry about how it affects your family, especially when you’re older. My brother’s been living in a different town for years, and it’s been hard on us all. We don’t see him as much as we’d like. That’s true. Family ties are important. But also, you have to consider your own happiness. I mean, if someone’s not happy in their own home, then maybe it’s better to move. I’ve heard of people moving for a better quality of life. It's not always the best decision, but it can be the right one. I guess that’s the thing. You can’t be in a place where you don’t feel good. I mean, I’ve heard about people moving just to live by the sea or somewhere quieter. It can be a huge change, but sometimes it’s exactly what you need. Exactly. But then again, moving house can be a massive upheaval, especially if you have a family. Still, I think it’s better to make the change early rather than wait until it’s too late.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to get really excited about Easter? I think it was the chocolate that made it special. Yeah, I remember that. I think we used to collect all the eggs and then try to eat them as fast as we could. But I also remember once I got a radish instead of an egg and I was so upset. Oh yeah! I remember that too. I think that was the year when we had a school trip to the zoo, and we were all so excited about the monkeys. Didn’t you get a toy monkey for your birthday that year? No, I think I got a book. I still have it somewhere in my cupboard. It was a picture book about Monet. I remember you used to pretend to be Monet, painting the flowers and everything. I did! I would sit outside and pretend I was painting the garden. I even used to say “Voilà!” when I finished. It was so silly, but I loved it. Yeah, and I used to do the same with my toy dinosaurs. I would make up stories about them going on adventures. Did you ever do that with your book? I tried, but I was too shy. I think I just read it over and over again, and sometimes I would act out the characters. I remember the main character was a painter who couldn’t stop painting. It was so artistic. Oh, that sounds cool. I also remember when we got our first hearing tests at school. I was so scared because the teacher said it was like listening to a lot of different sounds. I was like, "What if I can’t hear anything?" I remember that too. I thought I was going to be deaf! But it turned out I just had some earwax blocking my ears. It was a relief. Yeah, I had that too. My teacher said I was a bit sensitive to certain sounds, like the buzzing of the lights. I remember once I was in the library and I had to leave because the lights were so bright and loud. That must have been annoying. I think you used to get a bit dizzy sometimes too, didn’t you? Yeah, sometimes. I think it got better as I got older, but I still don’t like loud noises as much as other people.

I can't believe it's been a year since we last saw each other! It feels like ages. I know, it’s crazy. I’ve been so busy with work and everything, I didn’t even think about getting in touch. Yeah, and with all the lockdowns and everything, it’s been difficult to make time. But I’ve missed our chats. I know, I’ve missed them too. I’ve been thinking about how we used to spend every weekend together—eating out, going to the cinema, or just hanging out at home. Oh, I remember that.
