We used to get so caught up in our own little world that we never noticed the time passing. I still feel like that, honestly. I’m in a new job now, but it’s not what I thought it’d be. It’s better, I guess, but it’s not the same as when I used to work with you. I remember when you first started working in speech therapy. You were so determined and passionate, and I always loved how you used to make everything sound so interesting. It’s still the same, but I’m working with adults now. It’s a bit more serious. I mean, it’s not like the same kind of work as when I was in school. Yeah, I can imagine. I’ve been working as a copywriter for a while now, and it’s been a rollercoaster. Some days are great, and others are just a struggle to keep up with deadlines. I feel you. I’ve had some really tough days, but I’ve also had moments where I felt so proud of what I’ve accomplished. It’s just a matter of finding the right balance. Speaking of balance, have you been keeping up with your health? I’ve been trying to get into better shape, but I’m not sure if it’s working. I’ve been trying too. I started doing some yoga and even joined a gym. It’s not perfect, but I’ve been making progress. I also have to keep an eye on my blood pressure, though. That’s good. I really need to get back into some kind of routine. I’ve been so busy, I haven’t even had time to cook properly. I know how you feel. I’ve been cooking more lately, mostly because I’ve been trying to eat healthier.

I still remember that long cycle ride we used to take when we were kids. It was like a real adventure. I think it was from Almondsbury all the way down to the coast, or something like that. Oh, I remember that! We’d pile all our bikes on the back of Dad’s van and set off at dawn. It was like a little expedition. I still get that same thrill when I ride now, even if it's just a short trip to the shop. You know, I still have that old bike. It's rusted, but I keep it in the shed just in case. It reminds me of when I was a student. I used to cycle all over Manchester for lectures. My lectures were all at sea with my oral surgeon. It was ridiculous! I had to wear a diving mask and a snorkel in the lecture hall. Oh, that sounds like something out of a novel. I remember when I was a dental surgeon, we used to have the NHS perks – like free sailing trips. I think I went to the Isle of Wight once with the whole team. We had a boat, and I don’t think any of us ever paid for a single thing. That must have been fun. I’ve been thinking about going to Prague. It’s such a bargain now. I heard they’ve got some really good restaurants and the architecture is amazing. I’d love to go there for a weekend. I’d love to go too, but I’m always too busy. I think my only chance is if we can get a group together. We’d need a proper itinerary and some good places to stay. I’ve heard the ballet is amazing there, but I’m not sure how to get tickets when the place is already full. I’ve found that if you book early, you can get into some really good theatres and exhibitions. But it’s like a lottery. Sometimes you can get in for free if you have a ticket for another event. It’s all about timing. Speaking of events, did you hear about the jive night they’re planning at the converted barn? It’s supposed to be a big thing. Some people are even thinking of turning it into a community centre or a place for local artists.

So, do you think we could actually make this work? I mean, the idea of creating learning materials that use case studies from moving images—like films or documentaries—for educational purposes, it sounds like it could be a real niche market. I think it could be, but we need to be careful. The market for educational content is competitive, especially with so many online platforms already offering free resources. But if we focus on niche case studies—like those from actual social movements or historical events—that might differentiate us. That’s a good point. I mean, if we can tie in some of the social issues that are really relevant to today’s students, like digital communication, privacy, or even social media’s impact on relationships, we could make something really engaging. Exactly. And I was thinking, maybe we could use some of the case studies we’ve already talked about. Like the film  ’71 —it’s a great example of how communication strategies in a social context can change the course of events. It’s not just a movie, it’s a real historical event with real people, and it’s educational in so many ways. Yeah, and it also highlights the importance of social networking in crisis situations. I mean, if you think about the way information spreads through social media today, it’s not so different from the way news and rumors spread in the 70s. It’s just faster. That’s true. So maybe we could structure our materials around how different communication strategies—both traditional and digital—have shaped social relationships over time. And we’d need some kind of interactive element, like quizzes or discussion prompts, to keep people engaged. I agree. We could also look into using short-form videos or case studies from other countries, like maybe something from New Zealand or Australia, to give it a more global perspective. That might also help us connect with international educators. Yeah, and if we include a variety of case studies, we can show how communication strategies evolve across different cultures and time periods. It’s such a broad topic, but if we frame it around the idea of  moving images —like how films and videos can be used as tools for teaching—it could really work. I think that’s a solid angle. But we need to make sure our content is accessible.

I just thought about the sea the other day, you know, how it's always been such a big part of my life. I mean, growing up in Norwich, we were never far from the coast. Even though I don’t live near the sea now, I still feel a pull towards it. I know what you mean. I’ve always been fascinated by the sea too. I used to go sailing a lot when I was younger. I think it's just something about the way it makes you feel calm, like it’s a constant and it's got this rhythm that’s just... soothing. Yeah, I remember when I was a kid, my parents used to take me to the beach every summer. I used to spend hours building sandcastles and just watching the waves. It was always the same, but somehow it never got boring. That’s the thing, isn’t it? The sea doesn’t change, but it does feel different every time you see it. Maybe that’s why it’s so enduring, even in our lives when everything else seems to change so fast. I guess that’s part of why I always feel like I need to go to the coast when I’m feeling overwhelmed. There’s something about watching the tide come in and out, like it’s reminding you that things cycle, that everything has its time. Totally. I remember when I was in London, I used to take long walks along the Thames at sunset. It was like the city was just a little quieter then, and the water seemed to take on this golden hue. It made me think about how the sea can be both wild and peaceful at the same time. Yeah, it’s a weird contrast. I mean, the same ocean can be crashing against rocks with such force one moment, and then the next it’s smooth and still, reflecting the sky. It’s like it’s teaching you something about balance, you know? Absolutely. I think that’s why the sea is such a powerful symbol in so many cultures. It’s a reminder of both our powerlessness and our resilience. And also how small we are in the grand scheme of things. When you’re out there, you can’t help but feel how vast and endless it is. It's humbling.

So, do you think the new fashion trends are actually going anywhere, or are they just another flash in the pan? Honestly, I’m more confused than ever. I saw a look on a fashion show that looked like someone tried to recreate a 90s grunge outfit but with chunky sneakers and a neon jacket. It felt like they were trying too hard. Oh, I’ve seen that too. I think it’s just a cycle. Trends come and go, but there’s always a new wave of what people think is “cool.” Yeah, I guess that’s true. But I’m still not sure I can pull off the “vintage” look. I mean, I tried wearing a flannel shirt and jeans last week, and I felt like I was accidentally dressed for a picket fence in the 80s. Oh, I get it. I tried that too. My sister said I looked like a character from  Friends —but without the confidence. That’s not fair! You look like a character from  Friends  with a sense of style. You’ve got the casual cool. Thanks, but I still feel like I’m stuck in between eras. I don’t want to look too retro, but I also don’t want to just follow every new trend. It’s like trying to find my own voice in fashion. I get that. I think it’s all about knowing what works for you. Like, I don’t care if it’s a trend or not, if it makes me feel good, then it’s worth it. Exactly! I think about how I dress every day. I try to mix old and new—like a vintage jacket with some modern sneakers or something. It’s fun to experiment. That’s a good point. I guess I’ve been too scared to step out of my comfort zone. I mean, I still have that one pair of jeans I’ve had since uni, and I don’t know if I’ll ever get rid of them. You can always try pairing them with something different. Like, maybe a bold pattern or a statement piece. You never know, it might work. Or maybe even go for something bold. I’ve been thinking about getting a brightly coloured bag, like a neon pink one. It’s funny how something small can make a big difference. I can see that.

Mummy, I just got back from the weekend trip with my friends. I had so much fun! That’s great to hear, sweetheart. How was it? It was amazing! We went to the beach and took loads of photos. I even got a new camera from my uncle. Oh, that’s lovely. You know, I used to take photos all the time when I was your age. I even got a camera for my birthday once. Really? What did you do with it? Oh, I used to take photos of everything – the trees, the sky, even my cat. I even tried to take pictures of my friends, but they always looked so awkward. Ha! I can imagine. I tried to take a photo of my friend last week, but he turned around and gave me the weirdest look. That sounds just like me. I remember once I tried to take a photo of my sister, and she looked so serious, like she was in a movie. I still have that photo somewhere. That’s funny. I guess I’m not as good as you with the camera. I always end up taking blurry photos. Don’t worry, sweetheart. You’re still learning. I remember when I first started, I took a photo of my mum and the photo came out completely out of focus. I was so embarrassed. That sounds like a disaster! Oh, it was! I had to explain it to her, and she just laughed. She said, “You’re still getting the hang of it.” I guess it’s all about practice, then. I’m trying to take better photos now. I even read a book about photography. It was really interesting. That’s great. I remember when I was at college, I used to read a lot about photography. I even did a short course on it. It was really helpful. Do you think I should take a course too? Why not? You’ve got a real interest in it. Plus, you’ve got your camera now, so you can start experimenting. Yeah, I think I will. I’d love to learn more about it. Perfect. I can help you out too. We could go to a photography exhibition together. I think there’s one at the gallery next week. That sounds like a fun idea. I’m excited to go. Me too. I think it’s time we both started taking our photography more seriously.

Well, I heard a noise outside this morning. What was it? It was a cockerel. I’m telling you, it was screaming like a banshee. You wouldn’t have heard it if you were still in bed. I was up, I swear. I was just about to make tea. Maybe it was a baby bird in the nest. I saw one of them flapping around earlier. You mean the ones in the garden? Yeah, the ones under the old oak tree. I thought they were just sitting there, but then one of them flew off and landed on the fence. You’d think they’d be more careful. I mean, what if they fall and break their wings? Well, maybe they’re just learning. I’ve seen kids do the same thing. You’d think the birds would have more sense than some of the kids I know. I don’t know, maybe it’s just a phase. I mean, we all had our moments. Yeah, I remember when I was a kid, I used to try and catch birds. I thought I was being clever. You weren’t being clever, you were being stupid. Maybe. But I think it’s a good sign. It means the birds are starting to get used to the area. Or maybe they’re just looking for a place to roost. Anyway, I’m not going to get too worked up about it. I’ve got more important things to worry about. Like what? Oh, I’ve been trying to get my application form for the new job. It’s been a nightmare. I know, I tried to help you. I even sent it off for you. And what did they say? That it’s missing some information. That’s what I told you. You didn’t put your address in the right place. I didn’t even get the form right. I think I might have sent it to the wrong company. That’s not surprising. I can’t believe you made such a mess of it. Well, you’re the one who said it was easy. It was easy. I just didn’t take it seriously. I thought I could do it in my head. You can’t do it in your head. You need to read the instructions. Yeah, I know, but I’ve had a bad night’s sleep. I’ve been up all night.

I just got a call from my daughter, love. She’s in Sydney and wants to come and live with me here in Brighton. She’s been thinking about it for a while, and now she’s really serious about it. Oh, that’s lovely, isn’t it? But why now? She’s been abroad for a few years, hasn’t she? Yeah, she’s been working in Australia, but she’s feeling a bit lost. She says she misses home, she misses the family, and she wants to be closer to us. She’s also considering starting her own business here. That sounds ambitious, but also a bit daunting. What’s she plan to do? Any ideas about what kind of business? She hasn’t finalised it yet, but she mentioned something about a café or maybe a community space. She’s really passionate about helping people, and she wants to create somewhere where people can come together. That’s a noble cause. But is she sure she wants to move back here? I mean, living in Brighton can be quite expensive, especially if she’s used to the lifestyle in Australia. I know, she’s aware of that. But she’s also got a savings pot, and she’s been looking into local grants and support for small businesses. Plus, she’s got some friends here who’ve offered to help her out. That’s good to hear. And how about you? Are you ready for the change? I mean, it’s a big thing: a daughter moving in, changing your routine, adjusting to having someone else around. It’s going to be a big adjustment, no doubt about it. But I’m excited. She’s been away for so long, and I’ve missed her. I just wish I could have done more to support her when she was growing up. You did what you could, love. And now you’ve got a chance to be there for her again. It’s not just about the business or the lifestyle — it’s about being there for her, supporting her as she builds her own life. Yeah, I think that’s what’s really important. And I know she’s going to bring so much energy and positivity into the house. It’s going to be a new chapter for all of us. I’m really looking forward to meeting her.

So, do you know what’s been on my mind all week? The Scottish referendum. I just can’t get it off my mind. I mean, I’m not sure I even understand all the details, but it feels like such a big deal. Yeah, I know. It’s been everywhere. I saw a few news items on the telly about it. I think it's all about whether Scotland should stay in the UK or become independent, right? Exactly. And it's not just about politics—it’s about identity, culture, and what the future holds for the country. I mean, I like to think of myself as fairly progressive, but I’m still not sure where I stand on it. I get that. I’m not sure either. I mean, I’ve lived in Scotland most of my life and I love the culture and the people, but I also know how much the UK as a whole relies on Scotland economically. It’s a bit of a pickle. Yeah, exactly. And I suppose the outcome could change a lot of things. I mean, even if they do go independent, it’s not like it’s going to be an instant shift. There’s a lot of planning and negotiation involved. True. I was just thinking about that the other day. I had a friend who was in a job interview last week, and the whole conversation was about how to handle change and uncertainty. I guess that applies to everything these days, doesn’t it? That’s a good point. I had a job interview myself last week. It was for a research position at a university. I thought it went well, but I’m still waiting to hear back. I was pretty nervous about it, but I guess the process is just part of life. I can imagine. I was in one a few years ago too, and it was quite nerve-wracking. I still remember the way my hands shook when I was walking into the room. I hope you get the job, by the way. Thanks, I hope so too. I really need a change of scenery right now. I’ve been teaching the same material for so long, and it’s starting to feel a bit stale. That’s understandable. I think I might take a break from teaching soon. I’ve been thinking about it for a while.

So, do you think we've got all the bits for the mousetrap game? I feel like we’re missing something, you know, the little plastic thing that goes on the end of the stick. I think we do. I remember buying it at the toy shop last week. But maybe I should double-check. I don’t want to end up with a game that doesn’t actually work. I think I saw it in the box. Wait, no, I think it’s still in the car. Maybe we should go and get it. You know, I once saw a guy trying to build a mousetrap game in the park, and he ended up setting off a real one by accident. It was hilarious. The mouse ran off and he was just standing there, staring at the trap like it was a conspiracy. Oh, that sounds like something that could happen. You never know with these things. I remember when I was a kid, my brother used to make mousetraps out of sticks and string. He said he was being a scientist. Of course, it never worked, but he was still convinced he was on to something. That’s exactly what I did when I was younger. I used to build these crazy contraptions, and my parents would always say, “You’re not building a mousetrap, you’re building a science experiment.” I think the point is that mousetrap games are supposed to be simple, but somehow they become these massive projects. I mean, I worked abroad once, in America, and I saw those crazy mousetrap games on sale at the store. They had all the pieces, and they were like $30. You could buy them in the toys section. Oh, I bet. My sister once tried to buy one for my niece, and she said it was just a toy. But it was a full-sized wooden mousetrap with all the parts. You could actually use it. That’s the thing about American kids, isn’t it? They just go out and do things. I mean, I remember when I was growing up in London, we never had that kind of stuff. We had to be careful with our toys. I think it’s the culture, though. In the US, they’re more into building things, and they’re more open to trying out new things. I mean, I was in a school in New York, and they had this project where we had to build our own mousetraps.

I’m home! How was your day? It was okay, just a bit busy. How about you? It was fine, actually. I had a meeting with the department head about the new course we’re planning. But I’m more excited about what I bought today. Oh, really? What did you get? I went to that new boutique on the corner of the street. I bought this beautiful coat, and a few pairs of trousers. I think they’re really nice. Oh, that’s great. Let me see. You’re wearing the coat already? No, I brought it home to try it on. I thought I’d try it on before I put it on the hanger. I just needed to see how it looked in the light. That’s a good idea. Sometimes you can’t tell how something looks in the store. I’ve been meaning to do that with my new jacket. Yeah, you should. I think the fabric is really soft, and the fit is perfect. I feel like I can move around in it without it restricting me. That’s the thing, isn’t it? I’ve been buying a lot of clothes lately, but I haven’t really found the right fit yet. I feel like I’m buying things just to fill up the closet. I know what you mean. I used to do that too. But now I’m more conscious about what I buy. I’m trying to be more sustainable, too. I don’t buy clothes just for the sake of it. That’s a good approach. I’ve been thinking about it more, too. I’ve been trying to limit the number of things I buy, especially when it comes to clothes. It’s such a waste when you end up not wearing them. Exactly. And I also like the idea of investing in quality pieces. The coat I bought today is a bit pricier, but it’s made from a really good material. I hope it lasts for a while. That’s always the thing, isn’t it? You spend more money upfront, but it’s worth it in the long run. Yeah, I think so. It’s about being patient and not rushing into buying things just because they’re on sale or because you see them in the window. I agree. I’ve made some mistakes in the past, but I’m learning.

Well, did you see the rugby match last night, Oisin? I thought it was a real thriller. Yeah, I did. I’m still reeling from it. The way they came back from 14-0 down in the second half—what a game! Oh, I didn’t get to watch it. I was helping with the toddler. But I heard it was a fantastic match. What happened in the end? They won 22-19 in the last few minutes. The fullback made a last-minute try, and the crowd went wild. I was cheering so loud I scared the cat. Oh, I’d have loved to have been there. I still remember the days when I played rugby. It’s a passion, isn’t it? Definitely. Even though I’m just a fan now, I’ve been playing a bit with the local team. It keeps me fit and reminds me of my school days. That sounds great. I always wished I could play sports, but with the toddler, I haven’t had the time. Although, maybe next week I could try something. You should. It’ll keep you active and maybe even give you a chance to meet other people. You never know, maybe even something like rugby could become a new hobby. I remember when I was in school, they used to have sports days. I was the best at cross-country, but I never thought I’d be doing it at 70. Still, it’s amazing how much you can do if you put your mind to it. Yeah, I think that’s the thing. Age is just a number. I mean, the rugby match was full of players in their 30s and 40s. Some of them barely looked like they were even in their 30s. That’s true. I bet they all had active lifestyles. I wish I could do more. I’ve been trying to get back into some exercise, but with the toddler, it’s hard. It’s always hard with kids, but you can do it. Maybe if you set aside specific times, like after the toddler goes to sleep, you can have your own little workout. And maybe you can even find a group. I joined a walking group with some other retirees. It’s a great way to keep in shape and make friends. That sounds perfect. I could really use some friends.

So, do you know what’s happening with the baby? I mean, I know it’s not  my  baby, but I’ve heard you’ve been talking about it a lot lately. Yeah, it’s my cousin’s baby. They’re expecting in a few months. It’s so exciting, isn’t it? I mean, I still remember when I was pregnant with my sister— gosh , that was a long time ago. I remember that. You used to be so obsessed with everything related to pregnancy. You even got a book called  How to Survive Your Own Baby’s First Year . I still have it somewhere. Oh, I had to read it for a seminar on parenting and language development. It was a bit of a struggle, honestly. I didn’t know what I was doing, and I think the book just made it harder. I think it was called  How to Survive Your Own Baby’s First Year . That sounds like the kind of title that would make you feel like you’re in the trenches. But I guess it was useful. Yeah, it was. I mean, it did help. But I still remember the day I tried to explain the concept of  baby talk  to my lecturer. She just looked at me like I was speaking in another language. That’s hilarious. I remember that. You were so nervous, and you started trying to mimic the baby’s intonation. It was adorable, in a way. I was trying to be a good example for the class. I thought if I could show them how babies learn language through being exposed to different tones and patterns, it would make sense. But I think I just confused them all. Well, I think you did a good job. I mean, that was the first time I heard someone actually  try  to sound like a baby for a lecture. It was like watching a movie. Exactly! You know, I was thinking about moving house recently. I’ve been considering it for a while now. It’s getting a bit small for both of us. Yeah, I heard you’ve been thinking about it. You should do it. I mean, if you can afford it, go for it. It’s about time. Thanks. I just need to make sure I don’t go too far. I don’t want to end up in a place that’s too far from the university, or too expensive.

So, do you reckon people actually notice the difference in accents in this part of the country? I mean, like, I’ve been told I have a Bedford accent, but I don’t even know what that sounds like. Honestly, I think it’s more about how you say things than where you’re from. I’ve heard people say that the Bedford accent is pretty neutral, but I don’t know if that’s true. I think it’s more about how you’ve been brought up. Yeah, and you know what? I’ve heard people say that people from Luton have a different way of speaking, even if we all sound like we’re from the same area. That’s interesting. I mean, I’ve always thought that the East of England has a pretty similar way of speaking, but maybe I’m wrong. For sure, and it’s not just about the way you say words. It’s about the rhythm, the intonation, the way you finish your sentences. Some people say the Bedford accent is more like a “lilt,” but I don’t know if that’s accurate. You know, I’ve tried to be more careful with my accent in the past, like when I was working in London. I thought if I spoke more “properly,” I’d be taken more seriously. But honestly, the people I worked with didn’t even notice. That’s funny. I’ve never really thought about it that way. I guess it’s not like the accent is a big deal in some places. I think it’s also about being comfortable in your own skin. If you’re not trying to sound like someone else, your accent is just a part of who you are. Maybe that’s true. I mean, I’ve got a Greek side to me too, so I guess I’m mixing two different accents. Sometimes I can’t even tell if I’m speaking English or Greek in my head. That’s wild. You must have a pretty unique way of speaking then. Yeah, and that’s a good thing. I think accents are just a part of who you are, not something you have to change. I agree. I mean, I’ve been told I have a “posh” accent by some people, but I don’t think I’m posh at all. I think I just speak naturally.

So, do you think I should get a car? I mean, I’m trying to save money for a flat, but the bus is so unreliable. I get what you mean. The bus can be a bit of a nightmare sometimes, especially when it’s raining or there’s a delay. But I think if you’re worried about saving, you might want to think about it carefully. Yeah, I know. I’ve been thinking about it for a while. I’ve had this idea of getting a secondhand car, maybe a hybrid or something fuel-efficient, so I don’t spend too much on petrol. But I’m worried about the cost of insurance and the repayments if I take a loan. That’s a lot to think about. I mean, I had the same dilemma when I first started working. I ended up renting a car for a couple of months and saw how it went, and then decided I didn’t need one after all. It’s not the end of the world to keep using the bus. I guess, but I work late sometimes, and it’s not always easy to catch the last bus. Plus, I’ve got to get to the university early, and there’s not much time to spare. I can see why – especially if you’re planning to move out. It might be worth looking into the cheapest options first. Maybe there’s a car-sharing scheme or something in the area? I heard about a few places in Peterborough that offer shared cars for people who don’t want to own one. That’s an interesting idea. I wonder if there’s anything like that in the area where I’m looking to live. I’ll have to check online. Yeah, I think there are a few options. It might save you money in the long run. But if you do go for a car, make sure you look into the insurance costs properly. I know some people get caught out with the higher premiums if they don’t shop around. You’re right. I should probably compare a few different providers. Also, I’ve been thinking about public transport passes – do you know if they’re worth it? They can be if you’re commuting regularly. But if you’re only going a few times a week, it might not be cost-effective.

Well, I've just marked a whole pile of GCSE maths papers, and I can tell you, some of these kids don’t even know how to do basic algebra. I mean, it’s like they’ve never seen a number before! That’s what I thought too. I mean, my maths teacher at school always said, “If you can’t do algebra, you can’t do anything else,” but I’ve never seen anyone actually do that. I just got through my exams last year, and I still don’t know why we had to learn all that stuff. Oh, I remember when I was your age, love! I used to struggle with fractions. I mean, I could do them in my head, but when it came to writing them down, I’d always make a mess of it. You know, I’d write the numbers upside down or something. It was a nightmare! Yeah, and I remember when I was at school, I used to get so frustrated with the teachers. They’d say, “Just do it like this,” but I’d look at them and think, “How do you even know what you’re doing?” It’s funny how things change, isn’t it? I mean, now I’m the one grading them, and I can’t even remember how to solve a quadratic equation without looking it up! Yeah, and I don’t even know what a quadratic equation is! I just know it’s something you learn in Year 10 and then forget by Year 11. I mean, I remember the formula, but I don’t know how it works. It’s all theory to me now. Oh, you’ll get it one day. You’ll be older, and you’ll look back and think, “Wait, that was me? I used to know that?” It’s like a kind of deja vu. I remember when I first started teaching, I used to panic when I saw a student struggling with a simple sum. Now, I just take it in my stride. I still remember the day I got my first job as a dockworker. I was 16 and I thought I was going to be the best at it. But after a week, I knew I wasn’t even good at it. It wasn’t like I had a real trade or anything. I just worked there because I needed money.

Alright, do you two want some toast? You've been sitting there for ages staring at the ceiling like it's got something to say. I was just thinking about pirates, actually. Did you know that pirates used to have a code? Like, they had rules about how they shared the treasure and stuff? Yeah, I think they had a saying like “Arrr, me hearties!” or something like that. I think they’re doing some events in Stratford-upon-Avon. Maybe we could go? It’s not too far from here. Can we stay in a hotel? I want to sleep in a real bed instead of the couch. Of course you can. It’s for kids, and they’re doing actual circus tricks with real equipment. Like jugglers and acrobats? I want to learn how to ride a unicycle! Or maybe juggle knives? Well, the workshop is for kids over six. But you’re almost seven, right? So you might be able to do it. I think they’re doing a short course on different circus skills. There’s also a magic workshop, too. I heard they’re even using real magic tricks, not just fake ones. Like the ones that make things disappear? Yeah, like that. And there was also something about stop motion animation. I think they’re making a short film about pirates using stop motion. You could be a pirate in a movie! That sounds amazing. I could play the captain of the ship. I think it’s a good idea to get your tickets early. The workshops are popular. And if we do go, we could also go to the Easter pictures display at the local library. It’s like a show with big pictures of Easter stories and things.

So, do you remember that time we were in Jeddah, trying to sail that boat from Jeddah to Cyprus and ended up getting arrested? Oh, how could I forget? That was one of the most bizarre experiences of my life. I think it was the second week of our trip when we tried to leave the port. The customs officers came on board and started asking all sorts of questions. I remember one of them looking at me like I was a terrorist. It was quite a scene. You were trying to sail with a small boat, and the customs officer said you needed a permit for the route. We didn’t have one, and we were in the middle of the Gulf. It turned out that the boat wasn’t registered properly either. I think it was because we hadn’t gone through the proper channels. Oh, and then they started asking about the contents of the boat. We had some food and a few bottles of wine, which I suppose was a bit of a red flag. I told them we were just on a goodwill mission to deliver some medical supplies to a friend in Cyprus, and they didn’t buy it for a second. They took us to the local police station, and we had to spend the night there. We were all pretty drunk by that point, and it was a total mess. I still remember the officer saying, “You’re not even allowed to sail that boat without a license.” I think he said that with a smirk, like he was enjoying the chaos. And you know what was funny? We ended up getting a fine, but it was more of a warning than anything. They told us to leave the country immediately, and we never even made it to Cyprus. We ended up taking a plane instead. I can only imagine how that must have gone down with the rest of the group. I remember one of the guys trying to negotiate with the officer in Arabic, which didn’t help at all. He just looked at him like he was speaking a different language. I think the whole thing was a lesson in how different things are when you’re not in your own country. You can't just do what you like, even if it's just sailing a boat around. That was one of the most memorable times of our lives.

So, do you think we should get a new bathroom? I mean, the one in the house is getting a bit old and the shower’s starting to leak again. I know, I’ve been meaning to mention that. It’s not the best time, with the kids running around, but maybe it’s time we thought about doing something about it. Yeah, I don’t like the way the toilet flushes anymore. It’s like it’s got a mind of its own. It just sits there and doesn’t go. It’s so annoying. I know, I’ve had that problem too. But I also think maybe we should consider where we’re going to go on holiday this year. It’s been a while since we did anything proper. I mean, we’ve got the Grand National coming up, and I was thinking of going to see that. That’s a good idea, but you know your dad’s got this idea of taking us all to the countryside for a weekend. He says it’s good for the kids to get out of the city and connect with nature. I know, and I’ve got to say, I’m not sure how the kids will take to it. They’ve been more into their phones than anything else lately. Yeah, but my friend Jack is coming over next week. He’s got a new job at a local café, and he’s been telling me all about how he’s got a great mentor there. I’m thinking of trying to get some work experience too, maybe during the holidays. That’s great, you’re thinking ahead. But do you think your parents would be okay with that? I mean, they’re not exactly the most supportive of work experiences, to be honest. I think they’ll be okay, especially if it’s something that doesn’t interfere with school. You’ve got to be careful with the balance, though. I know, but I’d like to get something under my belt. I mean, I’ve been thinking of doing some refereeing as well. I saw one of the local leagues in the park last week, and the coach said he could use someone.

So, do you reckon we’ll get to try those truffle dishes in the villages around here? I heard they have some real good restaurants with truffle on the menu. I think we might. There’s a place called Truffles & Thyme in Pula that’s supposed to be amazing. They use local truffles, and the chef’s been on TV a few times. I’ve heard they’re a bit of a local legend. Yeah, I remember hearing about that. But, like, is it worth the trip? I mean, I’ve had truffle oil in a lot of places, but I’ve never had real truffles. Is it even possible to tell the difference? It’s a bit hard to tell unless you’re used to it, but once you’ve had the real thing, you know. I think it’s like the difference between a kale smoothie and something with fresh kale. You just know. Haha, yeah, that’s true. But I also heard some people say that the truffle season is over, or that the ones they sell here aren’t the best quality. Do you think that’s true? I don’t know, honestly. I’ve read a few articles saying that the best truffles are actually harvested in the fall – but it’s also the same time as the harvest for other things. I think it depends on where you get them. In the Istria, I think they’ve got a good reputation. I guess it’s also about the chef. Like, if they know what they’re doing, you can get better quality even if the truffles aren’t the premium kind. I mean, I’ve seen some people do amazing things with even basic ingredients. That’s the thing. It’s not just about the ingredient; it’s about the whole experience. The way the food is presented, the ambiance, the service. Sometimes, it’s the overall package that makes it special. Yeah, I guess that’s true. I mean, I’ve had some amazing meals in places that didn’t have the most expensive ingredients, but the chef just knew how to bring them together. Exactly. And you know, even though truffles are a big deal here, I still think the best thing about this trip is just being here together. I mean, the food is part of it, but the time we’re spending together is what’s really special.

So, do you know what’s up with the new logo design they’re pushing for? I heard they want something more modern and edgy, but honestly, I think it’s going to look like a kid’s toy. Yeah, I overheard the head of marketing saying they want it to appeal to a younger demographic. But I don’t think they really understand what that means. It’s not like we’re selling cereal boxes or something. I mean, maybe they’re trying to keep up with the times. We’ve all seen how brands like Apple or Nike have evolved their image over the years. You can’t just stick with the same look forever. I get that, but some of the older staff are really resistant to change. The head of publishing is like, “We’ve been here for decades, we know what works.” And the younger ones are saying, “We’ve got to evolve or we’ll be left behind.” Haha, yeah, it’s like the old and the new are in a constant battle. I mean, I guess it’s a sign that the company is trying to stay relevant. But I still think there’s a balance to be struck. You don’t want to lose the identity of the brand just to chase trends. I agree. I remember when we first started working here, the logo was really traditional, like a simple black and gold crest. It had a lot of history. Now they’re talking about using more neon colors and geometric shapes. Who even knows what that’ll look like? Honestly, I’d love to see a design that reflects the intellectual side of the press. Maybe something more subtle, more refined. Not just random colors and shapes. I mean, we’re not a fast-fashion brand. Exactly. I think they should ask the readers and the academic community what they think. If they’re going to be modern, they should also be inclusive. Maybe do a poll or something? That would be a good idea. I mean, it’s not like we can’t get feedback. We’ve got a strong presence on social media. Maybe they could run a contest or something. Get people involved. Yeah, and maybe even run some focus groups with the target audience. I bet some of the younger professors and students would have some great ideas.

So, do you think we’ll make it in time for the party? I know it’s only a short drive, but the roads can get a bit messy around here, especially with all the tourists. I hope so. We’ve got the GPS on, and it’s saying it’ll take about an hour and a half, but we’ve got to be careful with the toll roads. I don’t want to get stuck in some kind of traffic jam in the middle of nowhere. Yeah, I know. I just hope the campervan doesn’t break down again. I’m still not used to driving one, even though I’ve been doing it for a few months now. It’s not that bad, honestly. You get used to it. I mean, I’ve been teaching English for a while now, and I’ve been taking the same route to and from work every day. It’s almost like second nature now. Maybe after this trip, I’ll feel more confident. I mean, you’ve got to be a bit brave to drive a campervan across borders and all, don’t you? I suppose so. But it’s not just about the driving, it’s also about the planning. I’ve got the maps, the travel insurance sorted, and even the snacks. I don’t want to be caught without anything in case something goes wrong. That’s thoughtful. I’ve been meaning to get some snacks for the road, but I just haven’t got around to it. I’ve been so busy with work and everything else. You’d better do it now. I don’t want to be stuck in the middle of a forest with nothing to eat. I mean, I’ve brought some snacks, but I don’t think I’ve got enough for both of us. I know. I’m going to grab some crisps, chocolate bars, and maybe some fruit. I can’t believe I’m driving all the way to Poland just for a party. I mean, I’ve been meaning to go for ages, but I’ve never had the chance to do it properly. It’s not just the party. It’s the whole experience. Meeting new people, seeing new places, and just getting out of the routine of everyday life. I think it’s good for both of us, even if we’re just driving to a friend’s house.

I can’t believe the new Tottenham kit. It’s so bold. I mean, it’s not even close to the old design. I think they went for something more modern, but honestly, it looks a bit too flashy for my taste. Yeah, I agree. They’ve been trying to reinvent themselves every single season. I think they’ve gone too far with the sponsorships as well. The kit looks like it’s been designed by a marketing team, not a football club. Exactly. And why do they keep doing the same thing? The sponsor logos are everywhere. I mean, I get that they need money, but when every kit looks like it’s been taken out of a commercial campaign, it’s a bit much. I know, right? I think the main issue is that they’re not thinking about the fans. You can’t just slap a brand on the front and expect people to still love the club. It feels a bit inauthentic. Yeah, and the design’s not even that great. I mean, the colours are okay, but the way they’ve arranged the sponsor logos is so chaotic. Like, it’s like someone tried to fit a whole magazine page onto the chest of the jersey. I remember when they used to have simpler kits. I think the old red and white was more classic. Some clubs still manage to do it right, like Manchester City, but even they’ve had some clunky designs lately. That’s true. I mean, the fans are the ones who really love the club, so they should be involved in the design process. It’s not just about making money. It’s about representation. Yeah, that makes sense. And maybe that’s why some clubs are starting to get more creative with their designs. You know, some of the smaller clubs are using their heritage in a more meaningful way, rather than just pushing for the latest trend.

I just got a message from my cousin, and she’s mad at me because I didn’t reply to her last email. She said I’m being rude, and I don’t even know what she’s talking about. What did she say? I mean, you’re not like that, are you? She said I’m one of the most unresponsive people she knows. And honestly? I didn’t even realize I’d ignored her. I don’t want to be seen as someone who just sits around all day. I know, but it’s not like you can be successful in this economy. I mean, I tried applying for jobs, and I got rejected every time. I even had one offer, but it was for a job that paid less than my benefits. Yeah, I remember when my dad was laid off. He tried everything. He got a bit desperate, actually. He even tried selling things on eBay. I was like, “Dad, that’s not a good idea.” But he did it anyway. And then he got scammed. Lost a couple of hundred quid. I mean, he was so upset. He kept saying, “I just want to be useful again.” It’s like everyone’s got a story. I mean, I’m not even in the same boat as him, but I can see how it all adds up. Yeah, it does. And I know I’m not helping things by constantly complaining.

So, do you think we should go to the new convenience store down the road or just stick with the larger retailers? Plus, I have my own car, so it’s easier for me. I think you’re both overthinking it. I always just take the back roads and drive slowly. It’s not the fastest, but it’s safe. I’ve never had any problems with the traffic or the sat nav. I just like to be in control.

So, do you know what’s happening with the new trainee teachers? I heard they’re coming in next week. Yeah, I heard that too. I think they’re going to start teaching in the first year. So, do you think nuns are really bad or what? Like, I heard they do some weird stuff. Oh, don't be so negative, sweetheart. Nuns are just people who choose to live a certain way. Some are really kind and help others. But I saw a movie about the Matrix once. It was like, you know, people are being controlled by a big system. Is that like what nuns do? No, wait, the Matrix is a sci-fi movie. It's like a virtual world. But nuns aren’t like that. They just pray and help people. Exactly. They’re not trying to control anyone. And that’s what friends are for—helping each other grow. So, if I’m not a good person, my friends can help me? Yeah, that’s the whole point. Friends help you be better.

So, do you think I should actually go to those dancing lessons? I mean, I’ve been meaning to get back into it, but I’m not sure if I’m ready. Honestly, I think it’s a great idea. Maybe somewhere in the south of France. I’ve been meaning to go there for ages. France? That sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to go there, but I’m not sure if I can afford it. It just depends on what you’re looking for.

So, do you think we should stop at the next market? I’ve heard they have some amazing olive oil and wine here in Istria. I think we should. I've heard the markets here are really good. So, do you know what’s up with the whole recording thing? I saw this video of someone doing something really... intense and it was just so weird. I mean, I don’t even know if it’s real or not. So, do you know where the best coffee in this whole building is? I swear, the one in the first floor café is just... meh. Honestly, I've been trying to find something better than that.
