They’ve been talking about it for weeks. It’s been ages since we last went. Yeah, I’d love that. It’s been so long since I’ve been on a horse. I remember when I was younger, I used to ride all the time. I still remember the first time I flew over the jump – I was so excited! Aye, I can still remember the first time I rode a horse. Felt like I was flying myself. Although, I wasn’t quite as lucky as you, love. I fell off the first time and got covered in mud. Oh, that sounds like a classic story. I remember when I was a kid, I tried to ride a pony and ended up getting stuck in the paddock for an hour. My father was so proud of me, even though I was covered in dirt and crying. Oh, I remember that! You were the youngest one who ever tried to ride a pony. You were only six, and you wanted to be just like your older brother. But you ended up climbing the fence and getting chased by the horse. That’s hilarious! I can still picture it. I think I was in the same paddock, watching you run off after the horse. I was so scared for you, but you didn’t look too bad. Well, I didn’t look too bad, but I was covered in horse dung for the rest of the day. My mother was furious. She said I was a disgrace to the family. I think that’s the theme of the day – being a disgrace to the family. Let’s not forget the time I tried to fix the boiler and ended up setting the kitchen on fire. Still remember that. Oh, that was something else. I remember your face when you came out of the kitchen, and the smell of smoke was everywhere. It was the worst thing ever.

So, do you think we’ll get there on time? I mean, the traffic’s been absolutely mad today. I got stuck in a queue for half an hour just to get out of Gillingham. I feel like we’re all stuck in some kind of giant traffic jam. Honestly, I don’t think we’ll make it. I told the kids to leave early, but I guess they thought it was a day off. Anyway, I’ve been trying to get a disabled parking space for ages. I know it’s not just me—everyone’s got some kind of problem these days. You’d think the council would have more spots, but they’re always booked up. Yeah, I’ve had the same issue. I work in care, you know, and I deal with people who need help getting around. I can tell you, the disabled parking spaces are a joke. I’ve had to wait for an hour just to find one, and even then, sometimes it’s not even accessible. I mean, it’s one thing to have a space, but it’s another to have it actually usable. That’s so frustrating. I mean, I’m not even disabled, but I’ve had to use a disabled badge once or twice when I was driving my dad to the doctor. I just want to make sure that people who actually need it can get it. It’s not fair that the spaces are getting taken by people who don’t need them. Exactly! And the council’s never done anything about it. I think they just don’t care. I remember once trying to get a housing application for my mum, and they said there was no available council housing because all the spots were taken. I mean, we’re talking about elderly people who need support living on their own. It’s not just about parking—it’s about housing too. I know. I’ve seen so many people in Harlow struggling to find somewhere to live. Some of them are in really bad conditions, and they don’t have a choice. I mean, I don’t blame them for waiting in line for a parking spot if they’re struggling to find a home. It’s just sad that the system doesn’t work for them. It really is. I think it’s a reflection of the whole system—just not working well for people who are already vulnerable.

So, do you think we should go for the allotment in Mitcham? I've been checking the website and there's still a few plots available. Mitcham? I think that’s a bit far from here. Why not go for one in Croydon? I heard the soil’s pretty good there and there’s more support for new growers. Hmm, I heard Croydon’s got a lot of competition. I don’t want to end up with a plot that’s already taken over by weeds. That’s true. But maybe we can check the ones that are still open. I’ve been reading up on allotment rules and it seems like you have to have a bit of a plan before you even apply. Yeah, I’m thinking about what I want to grow. I’ve always wanted to try growing my own tomatoes and maybe some herbs. Do you think that would be possible? Definitely. Tomatoes are pretty straightforward as long as you get the right kind of soil and the right amount of sunlight. I’ve been thinking about starting a vegetable patch too, maybe some potatoes and carrots. That sounds great. But what about the time commitment? I’m still teaching and I’m not sure I can dedicate a lot of time to gardening. It really depends on how much you want to do. You don’t have to be a full-time gardener. Even a few hours a week can make a difference. Plus, it’s a good way to unwind after work. I guess that’s true. I do feel like I need something to keep me busy outside of work. Maybe it’ll help me with my stress levels. Exactly. And it’s a great way to meet other people too. I know some of the local growers, and we often swap tips. It’s like a little community. That sounds nice. I’d like to meet more people who are into gardening. I’ve always liked the idea of having fresh vegetables at home. You’ll love it. Once you get into it, you’ll start to see the difference it makes. Even just having a small plot can make a big impact on your diet and your mental health. I suppose I should start looking into the application process then. Do you know where I can get more information? There’s a local council website that lists all the available allotments in the area.

So, do you know what’s up with Lucy? I haven’t seen her in ages, and it’s like she’s just disappeared off the face of the Earth. I know, right? I was going to text her last week, but I just never got around to it. She was in Cambridge for a while, but I guess she’s back now. I think she’s living with her mum again. Oh, that’s so sad. I mean, I know she was going through a tough time, but I just hope she’s okay. Didn’t she split up with that guy from Leeds? Yeah, that’s what I heard. I think he moved back to Leeds, and she’s been kind of… lost ever since. I mean, she used to be so full of energy, always going out, always doing things. Now she just stays in her room all the time. That’s really worrying. I mean, she’s only 23, right? She should be out there having fun, not just sitting around. I guess she’s taking time to figure things out. Yeah, I guess that’s what it is. But I don’t know, sometimes I wonder if she’s just not interested in relationships anymore. Or maybe she’s just not ready for anything serious. I mean, I get it. Some people take a break from everything, you know? Maybe she’s just trying to find herself again. But I hope she doesn’t stay like this forever. It’s not healthy. Definitely not. I think she needs someone to pull her out of that rut. But I don’t know if she’s ready for that yet. I mean, she’s been through a lot. Yeah, but I think it’s time she started making some plans again. I mean, we’re all going to the gig next weekend, right? Maybe she should come. It’s going to be fun, and it could be a chance for her to get out of the house. You’re right. I’ll talk to her and see if she’s up for it. I mean, I know it’s not the same as the old days, but it’s something. And who knows, maybe she’ll meet someone there. Exactly. If nothing else, it’ll be a chance for her to get out and meet people again. You know what they say—every cloud has a silver lining.

So, do you play any games? I’ve been trying to get into the new FIFA, but it’s like,  so  complicated with all the transfers and stuff. I can’t even figure out where to start. Yeah, I played FIFA a bit before, but now it’s just too much. I mean, I’ve got a friend who’s like a pro at it, and he just tells me what to do, but I don’t even know what I’m doing half the time. It’s like trying to understand a whole new language. Oh, I get it. I play a lot of Stardew Valley. It’s like farming, but with a weird, cute twist. You can have like a pet turkey, and you can make your own store. It’s super chill, honestly. That sounds cool. I’ve heard of it. But I’m more into something like Animal Crossing. I’ve been trying to get into it, but I’m just not into the Japanese style of games. I mean, I like the idea of having a virtual island and stuff, but I’m not into the aesthetic or the way they design the games. Yeah, I tried Animal Crossing once. It’s nice, but I just didn’t feel like it was for me. I’m more into games where you actually have to do something, you know? Like, you can’t just chill and collect stuff all day. I want a challenge. I get that. I’m more into action games. But I’m not great at them. I’ve tried some of the newer ones, like God of War, but I can’t even beat the first boss. I’m like, "This is a game for people who know what they’re doing." Man, I feel you. My cousin is into that stuff. He plays everything. He’s like, "Oh, just try it for 10 minutes, it’s easy," but then he just shows me a 3-hour tutorial. I give up. I think that’s the problem with games now—they’re just too complicated. I mean, when I was a kid, you just played Mario and you knew what you were doing. Now, it's like, "Oh, you need to go to this map, collect this item, and beat this boss, and then you can go to the next level." It's all so convoluted.

I just watched this new film on Netflix, and I thought you’d love it. It’s called  The Quiet Girl , and it’s really moving. I’m not sure if you’ve seen it yet? No, I haven’t. I’ve been so busy with work. But I’ve heard good things about it. Is it based on a true story? I think it’s inspired by a real-life experience, but it’s more of a fictional narrative. It’s about a young girl who moves to a new place and struggles to fit in. The acting is brilliant, and the cinematography is just stunning. It really captures that sense of isolation and belonging. That sounds like something I’d like. I’ve been meaning to watch more films that are emotionally intense. I’ve been watching a lot of documentaries lately, but I think I need something more... personal. Yeah, I get that. I think that’s why I like this one so much. It’s not too dramatic, but it’s deep. I remember when I first saw it, I was sitting there with tears in my eyes. It’s one of those films that stays with you. I need to start making more time for films like that. I’ve been so caught up in work and trying to keep up with everything else. I feel like I’m missing out on a lot of good stuff. It’s easy to get lost in the hustle and bustle. But you know what? I think it’s important to take a break and really sit down with something that touches you. You deserve that. You’re right. I should make more time for things that make me feel something. I’ve been so focused on productivity that I’ve forgotten about the little things that bring me joy. That’s what I like about you, Sarah. You’re so thoughtful and reflective. It’s one of the reasons I enjoy our conversations. I feel like we can always open up and talk about anything. I feel the same way about you, Ann. We’ve been friends for so long, and I think we always have this special connection. It’s nice to have someone who really listens and understands. You know, I sometimes think about how different our lives are. You’re so driven and focused on your career, while I’ve kind of settled into a quieter life.

So, do you remember that board game we tried to play last week? The one with the weird rules and the minigames? Oh yeah,  The Ultimate Quest ? I thought we were going to be the first to finish, but we got stuck on the bonus round for ages. It was like a different game entirely. Yeah, I think it was supposed to be a strategy game, but it turned into this weird mix of trivia and luck. I swear the dice were conspiring against us. You mean the one where you had to answer random questions about history and pop culture? I think I got stuck on the question about  The Undateables  and had to explain the whole series to the group. I didn’t even know what it was called back then. Oh, you were the one who said the show was “so cheesy it was brilliant.” I still remember when you tried to apply the dating strategies from the show to your friends at work. It was  so  not working. I still think it’s a good idea though. Like, if you know what to say, you can smooth talk your way through any awkward situation. I mean,  The Undateables  taught us that, didn’t it? Sure, but the show’s been on for years, and none of those people have ended up with a real relationship. All that “chemistry” and “right time, right place” nonsense. Well, someone had to try. Although I do wonder why they never brought up the  real  point—like, the awkwardness of being on camera and being judged by a panel of strangers. Exactly! I mean, I wouldn’t want to be the focus of a whole show just to see if I can “get a date.” Not that I’d ever do that.  I  have a life, thank you very much. Speaking of life, did you hear about the interview I had last week? It was for a research position, and I had to talk about language and culture for an hour. I think I did okay, but I was nervous about the whole thing. Was it for the  Language Research Co-ordinator  role? That’s the one that’s been open for ages. I thought you were going for it. Yeah, I was. But I had to explain what exactly I do in my job. I mean, to someone who’s never worked in linguistics, it’s hard to make it sound interesting.

So, do you know what’s going on with the washing machine? It’s been making this weird noise all morning. Ugh, I’m so fed up with it. I think it might be the drum. I remember reading somewhere that the bearings can go bad and make that grinding sound. But I’m not sure if that’s what it is. Yeah, I’ve heard that before. I’ve been thinking about getting a new one too. I’ve had enough of this old thing. It’s been giving me so many problems lately. It doesn’t even spin properly anymore. I know, I’ve been trying to avoid doing laundry for days. It’s been so frustrating. I think I’m going to look into getting a new one soon. I’ve been saving up, but I still need a bit more. Yeah, I can relate. I’ve been doing all my washing by hand just to avoid the hassle. It’s not ideal, but at least I’m not getting annoyed every time I use it. Although, I still miss the convenience. I can imagine. I’ve been cooking more too, since I don’t want to do any more laundry. I’ve been experimenting with some new recipes. I tried making a stir-fry the other day. It was actually really good. Oh, that sounds nice. I’ve been meaning to try making more meals at home instead of relying on takeaway. I think I’ll give the stir-fry a go. I’ve got some veggies in the fridge that I haven’t used yet. Yeah, it’s a great idea. I think it’s better for the body and your wallet too. I’ve also been watching some old films lately. I picked up a few from the library. There’s this one called  The Grand Budapest Hotel  that I’ve really been enjoying. Oh, I’ve heard of that. I think it’s one of those quirky, stylish movies. I’ve been meaning to watch it too. I’ve been so busy with work and everything else, I haven’t had time. Yeah, it’s a bit of a slow burn, but once you get into it, it’s really engaging. I’ve also been thinking about watching some classic films. I remember my mum used to love  The Wizard of Oz  when she was a kid.

I just can’t believe how long it’s taking to get a house in the south. You know, when I was working, I could have bought a semi in London for what I can now buy a terraced house in Hunsonby. It’s just… I don’t know, it feels like the whole system’s rigged. I know, it’s really frustrating. I’ve been trying to buy a place in Manchester, but even there, the prices are just out of reach. I mean, I’ve got a stable job and all, but I still can’t afford a deposit. It’s like the housing market’s frozen, isn’t it? Yeah, and the thing is, I’ve been in the oil industry for years, and I’ve watched the prices go up and up. I mean, I was in Nottingham, and even then, the prices were just ridiculous. I was lucky to find something decent when I was working, but now I’m out of a job and I don’t even know where to start. I hear you. I’ve been thinking about moving south for a while, you know? I mean, I’ve got the pension, so it’s not like I’m desperate for a huge house, but I’d like something manageable. But it’s like, the longer I wait, the more it seems like I’m not going to get anywhere. I’ve been telling myself that if I can just wait a bit longer, the market will settle. But honestly, I don’t think it will. I mean, the government’s been talking about building more houses, but it’s just not happening fast enough. I think the politicians are more interested in keeping the prices high so they can collect more taxes. And then there’s the whole issue of the south versus the north. Everyone says the north is cheaper, but even here in Cumbria, it’s not easy. I mean, I was in Walsall before, and even there, the prices were way too high for a salary like mine. Now I’m in a place where I can afford a place, but I’m not working anymore. It’s like the system’s designed to keep people like us out. Exactly. And don’t even get me started on the VW scandal. It’s like everything’s been a scam from the start.

I don’t know, I just feel like I’ve been sitting around for ages, you know? Since I retired, it’s been years and I still haven’t found my feet. Aye, I know what you mean. I’ve been out of work since the early ‘90s. Got the pension, but it’s not enough to live on. I reckon the government's all about making sure people like us don’t have a decent standard of living. Oh, don’t get me started. I’ve been in and out of childminding for years, but now I just sit at home like a ghost. Still, I’ve got the pension, and the kids are all grown up. It’s just the loneliness that gets to me sometimes. Yeah, I hear you. I used to love the work, you know? Civil engineering. It was a proper job, and I felt useful. Now I just sit here watching the telly and playing with my grandkids, but it’s not the same. I remember the days when we all had something to do. Now, it’s like we’re just waiting for the next thing to happen. The housing developments around here are all going up, but they’re not for people like us. They’re all for young families, or people with money. I tried staying in a bed and breakfast once. It was quite nice, but the owner was always asking questions. I didn’t want to explain why I was there. It’s not easy being old and not having a proper job. You feel like a burden sometimes. I know. I used to be able to fix things around the house, but now I can’t even lift a ladder. I’ve had a few falls, you know. It’s hard being old and not being able to do anything. And the computers? I don’t even know how to turn one on. I tried once, and it took me three hours. I think I’d rather use a typewriter. I tried to teach my grandkids how to use a computer. They think it’s the most amazing thing. I keep telling them it’s just a box with a screen, but they don’t listen. That’s the thing, really. They don’t understand. They think we’re all made of stone. I’m not. I just don’t know how to use the modern world anymore.

So, do you guys remember that video that went viral last week? The one where this guy tried to explain evolution to his girlfriend and it ended up being a total disaster? Oh yeah, that was wild. I mean, he started off okay, like, explaining natural selection, but then he just went off into this whole rant about how humans are just animals and that’s why we’re all basically the same. She just stared at him like he’d grown a second head. And then he said something about how men are just programmed to be dominant and women are just naturally more emotional. She just stood up and walked out. I couldn’t believe it. That was so weird. Yeah, like, what even was that? I mean, I get that he was trying to be funny, but he didn’t realize how offensive it was. Especially with the whole sexism angle. It’s funny, though, because I feel like everyone has a different take on evolution. I mean, I’m in science, so I kind of get it, but I still don’t like how people twist it to justify all sorts of stuff—like, you know, racism or sexism. Exactly. Like, I’ve heard people say, "Oh, evolution just means we’re all the same," but that’s not true. Evolution is about adaptation, not about equality. It’s not like we’re all born equal, it’s just that we all have the same basic biology. It’s kind of like saying that because we all have two arms and two legs, we’re all the same. That’s not how it works. Yeah, and I feel like that’s where a lot of the confusion comes from. Like, people take the idea of evolution and then apply it to social issues in a way that doesn’t make sense. It’s like mixing up biology with sociology. I think that’s part of the problem with the internet too. There are so many conspiracy theories and misinformation. Like, I saw this video the other day where someone said that all humans evolved from apes, so that means we’re all just animals and there’s no difference between us and other species. That’s just not accurate. I mean, it’s not the same as saying we’re all the same, though. We’re all different.

So, how’s the weather been down your way, Ann? I’ve been trying to get out for a walk, but the rain’s been relentless. It’s been pretty much the same here, Karen. Rain, rain, and more rain. I’m starting to think the forecasters are just messing with us. But I’ve been keeping the house tidy, if you know what I mean. Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to keep the place clean, but it’s just so hard with the damp and the cold. I can’t even get my knitting done without my hands getting wet. That’s the thing, isn’t it? It’s like the weather’s been playing tricks on us. I remember when I used to drive, the roads would be clear, and I’d head off for a little trip. But now, with the MOT coming up and all, I just stick to the house. Speaking of the MOT, I had mine done last week. I had to get new tyres as well, which was a bit of a shock to the system. I mean, I thought I had quite a few left. Oh, I’ve been meaning to get mine done. I’ve been putting it off because I’m just not sure I can afford it, and I know the cost goes up every year. It’s all about priorities, isn’t it? When I was younger, I used to take my car out every weekend, but now I just don’t have the energy. I think I’m more interested in sitting by the fire and listening to the radio. Yeah, there’s something comforting about sitting by the fire. Although I do miss the days when I was out on the road. There was something about the open highway that made me feel alive. I can imagine. I’ve always liked the idea of driving somewhere new, even if just for a day. I used to go skiing with my husband when I was younger, but now I just don’t have the time or the energy. I used to ski too, but I got injured a few years back. The doctors said I shouldn’t be doing it anymore, and I’ve been trying to get back into shape. It’s not easy. I’m trying to get back into shape too, but I’ve had some issues with my joints.

Alright, do you know what we're going to be talking about today? I thought it might be good to start with something that's been on my mind for a while. What is it? Well, we've been learning about history at school, and I think it's important that we understand things like slavery and war. It helps us learn where we come from and how people have lived in the past. Yeah, I guess it's important to know how things were before, like, you know, before everything was the way it is now. Exactly. I think it's also good to talk about how people were treated, especially the people who were enslaved. It's not something that's easy to talk about, but it's important to be honest about the past. But why do we have to talk about slavery? It feels like such a sad part of history. I don't know if I want to think about it too much. I understand that, but it’s part of the story. And I think it helps us learn about the values of freedom and equality that we try to live by today. It also helps us understand how far we've come—and how much there's still to do. But how do we even start talking about it? I mean, I know it's a big topic, and I don't know where to begin. That’s okay. We can start with the basics. For example, what do you think slavery is? What does it mean to be enslaved? Well, I think it means that someone is forced to work without being paid, and they can’t leave. They’re treated like property. That’s a good start. And that’s exactly what happened a long time ago. People were taken from their homes and forced to work on plantations in places like the Americas. It was a system that was based on racism and control. That sounds really cruel. I don’t know how people could do that. It’s hard to imagine, and that’s why it’s so important to learn about it. It wasn’t just about money—it was about power, too. People who had power used it to keep others in chains. And then there were wars, too. I remember reading about how wars led to more people being enslaved, or how some wars were fought to end slavery.

I just watched this new show on BBC iPlayer, it's called  The Great British Bake Off: The Professionals  – and I thought it was absolutely brilliant. The level of skill in that show is just incredible. You know, I’ve worked with a lot of people in the hospital, but I haven’t seen anyone who can make a soufflé that doesn’t collapse like a deflated balloon. I’ve been watching it too. I think it’s a bit more intense than the regular  Bake Off , though. You can tell these bakers are really serious about their craft. But honestly, watching them get tense over a croquembouche is like watching a doctor at a critical moment in surgery – it’s all about precision and pressure. Yeah, but I still think the regular show is more fun. I mean, I love the banter between the judges – it’s like a comedy show wrapped in a cooking challenge. I just happened to be at the café last week and I saw the host, Prue, ordering a coffee. She looked exactly like she does on TV—wrinkled, scowling, and very focused. That’s because she’s a real foodie, isn’t she? Her face is always tight with concentration. I remember once when I was working at the local estate agency, I tried to bake a cake for a client’s birthday. I didn’t have the right ingredients, and the cake was so bad it looked like it had been hit by a hammer. I almost cried. That sounds like a nightmare. I’ve had a few funny moments with food myself. My wife and I tried to make shepherd’s pie once, and we ended up with a pot of stew that looked like a sludge. We ended up eating it with spoons and calling it “Mystery Meat Surprise.” It was barely edible, but it gave us a good laugh. Oh, I’ve had that happen too. My friend once tried to make a soufflé for a dinner party and it collapsed before anyone could even taste it. I told her it was “never going to take off.” She looked so devastated, she started crying and said, “This is the first time I’ve ever failed at something.” I told her it’s all part of the process. You know, I think one of the reasons we love these shows is because they remind us that perfection isn’t everything.

Alright, do you two want some toast? I think I’ve got some left from this morning. Yeah, please! I’m starving. Me too, mum! I ate a whole bag of chips yesterday, and now I’m hungry again. Okay, okay, I’ll make some toast. But first, let me get the dishwasher out. I’ve been meaning to do that all week. Can I help? Sure, why not. You can grab the plates and put them on the counter. Let me get the glasses. Is it easy to take out the dishwasher? I’ve never done it before. It’s not too bad, really. Just pull the doors open and take out the dishes. You’ll get the hang of it. I’m not sure if I’m ready for that. I’ve got a bit of a fear of dishwater. Me too, but it’s not that bad, honestly. I think the worst part is when you open the door and it’s all wet. Exactly! I remember the first time I did it. It was like opening a floodgate. But once you get used to it, it’s manageable. Yeah, but I’m also thinking about the mess. I just don’t want to make a bigger mess than I already have. I understand. But you’ll be surprised how clean it is once you’re done. And also, it’s a good way to get some fresh air in the kitchen. Wait, can we talk about Harry Potter for a minute? I’ve been thinking about it a lot lately. Of course! What’s on your mind? I was just wondering, do you think Harry would have been able to beat Voldemort without the prophecy? That’s a tricky question. I think it depends on how you look at it. If he didn’t know about the prophecy, maybe he wouldn’t have been as motivated to fight him. But then again, he had a lot of support. And what about the prophecy itself? Was it even fair that Harry had to be the one who defeated Voldemort? I think it was more about the choice he made than the prophecy. He chose to stand up for what he believed in, even when it was hard. Yeah, and he had this amazing group of friends. Ron and Hermione helped him all the way. Definitely. And let’s not forget about the Sorting Hat.

So, do you play Words With Friends, Lila? I’ve been trying to get back into it, but I keep forgetting the rules. Oh yeah, I do. I think I’ve been playing it more than I should. It’s kind of like a way to pass the time when I’m baking. I’ve never really got into it. I’m more of a Scrabble person. Though I have to admit, I’ve got a few friends who are into Words With Friends and they keep trying to drag me in. Honestly, the only reason I know what it is is because I’ve seen my mates talk about it. I mean, I can do the word game, but I still don’t get the obsession. I get it. It’s like a mix of strategy and luck. Sometimes you just get a word that’s impossible to place. Yeah, I mean, I’ve been in games where the only word you can place is “a” or “the,” and then you just sit there waiting for someone else to do something. I once had a game where the only words left were “bee,” “bee,” and “be.” I thought I was going to win, but the last move was someone just adding “be” to the board and then it was all over. Alright, so I was just thinking about metals and fabrics the other day. I was making a list for the kids to help them understand what they can make in Minecraft, and I realized how much of a difference different materials can make. Oh, I love Minecraft! So, do you still play the guitar, then? I saw you at the gig last week, and you looked like you were having a good time. Yeah, I do. I’ve been picking it up again. It’s been a bit of a hobby lately. So, do you know what’s happening with the Montenegro trip? I heard they’re moving it to next year because of the weather or something. Yeah, I think it was because of the floods last summer. I mean, what if you’re at school and you want to eat something

I can't believe we've got to pay for our own utilities now. I thought uni would take care of everything. Yeah, I know, it's so unfair. So, do you remember that time we tried to fit all the family into the car for Christmas? I think we ended up taking three cars just to get everyone there. Oh, I remember that! It was chaos. My daughter had her own little car, and my son had to drive his brother’s old van. I swear, we were like a convoy heading to the same place. Yeah, and I had to drive the oldest one, which was me. And then there was the cousin who insisted on playing the Christmas carols on the radio the entire way. You couldn’t even have a conversation without the music blaring. That way, we can go somewhere really nice for Christmas, like the coast or something. That’s a good idea.

I've been thinking, you know, about the old days. Back when I was working in the factory, and everyone knew each other. It wasn’t as busy as it is now, but it had its own kind of rhythm. Oh, I remember those days too. I used to take the kids to the park every afternoon, and the whole street would gather. There was always someone to chat to, and you could tell if someone was having a bad day just by looking at them. It's a different world now. I mean, I run a business, so I’m used to the pace, but even I miss the sense of community. People seem to be more isolated, don’t you think? Yeah, I suppose you could say that. It’s not that I’m not used to being on my own, I just… I don’t know. It feels like there’s something missing. I still go to the shops, but it’s not the same as having a regular group of people to catch up with. I know what you mean. It’s not just the lack of company—it’s the way things are done now. Back then, we had to wait for the post, for the radio, for the newspapers. Now it’s all instant, all the time. It’s like we’re constantly being bombarded with information, but somehow, we’re more disconnected. That’s true. I think part of it is the internet. It gives you access to everything, but at the same time, it takes away the real, face-to-face interaction. I remember when you had to wait for a letter to come through the post. You felt like you had a connection with the person who wrote it. Now, even if you get a message, it’s just a few words on a screen. I think I’d rather have the old way, even if it was slower. At least you knew when someone was coming. You could see them walking up the street, or hear them before you saw them. Now, people just vanish into the distance, and you don’t even know where they are. It’s sad, really. I think we’ve become so reliant on technology that we’ve lost something fundamental. We’ve forgotten how to slow down, how to talk to each other properly. I suppose that’s part of the cost of progress.

So, do you live here in Northern Cyprus full-time, or do you just come for weekends? Just weekends, mostly. I’ve been coming here since the late 70s, actually. I used to work in London, but I retired and decided to take things slow. That’s a long time. Do you like living here? Yeah, I do. It’s peaceful. Not like the hustle and bustle of London. The weather’s better, too. Though, you know, it’s not always the easiest place to get used to. I guess it’s not the same as being in the UK, then? No, not really. You’ve got to get used to the pace of life, the way people do things. But once you do, it’s actually quite nice. How did you get here in the first place? My wife and I came for a holiday in the 70s. We fell in love with the place and decided to stay. It’s not like we had a plan, really. Just sort of… a whim. That’s brave. I mean, moving to a place like this, when it’s not really on the map for most people. It was a bit of a risk, yeah. But we did it. And now, I’d say it’s one of the best decisions I’ve ever made. What’s the hardest part of living here? The bureaucracy, honestly. It can be frustrating. Getting things done, like renewing your passport, or even just getting a visa. You have to jump through a lot of hoops. I can imagine. I mean, I’ve had trouble with things like that back in the UK too. Yeah, but here, it’s even more complicated. And the language can be a bit of a barrier too. I bet. I’ve heard that the local dialect is different from English. Is that true? It is, to some extent. It’s not like you can just speak English and get by. You need to pick up a bit of the local language, or at least understand the basics. That must be tough, especially if you’re not used to it. It is, but you adapt. You learn. And after a while, you start to appreciate it. I guess when you’re here, you can’t really leave. Unless you want to, of course. Exactly. You see, once you’ve settled in, it’s hard to go back.

I mean, it doesn't fix the problem, but it makes the place feel a bit more like home. I guess we’re lucky we live in a part of the city that’s not the worst. I was talking to a colleague the other day, and she mentioned that her son is studying environmental science. He’s obsessed with urban sustainability and green tech. I wonder if he’ll ever be able to live in a place like this. He probably will. I mean, there’s a lot of talk about smart cities and green infrastructure. I just hope it doesn’t take another decade for that to happen. I’m not sure I can wait that long. I know. I think we both need to take a break from the city for a little while. I’ve been meaning to reach out to some friends who live in the Lake District.

Alright, do you think we've got everything for dinner? I mean, the chicken's in the oven, and the veg is in the pan. I think so, but I’d say we’re missing the salad. You know, the one we usually have with our chicken. Yeah, I noticed that. I think I’ll just grab the lettuce and some tomatoes from the fridge. Maybe some cucumber too. Oh, and don’t forget the dressing. I’ve got that in the cupboard. Didn’t I see a bottle of balsamic vinegar in there? Maybe that’s the one. I think that’s it. Yeah, and it would be nice to have some time to ourselves. I mean, it’s been a while since we’ve all just hung out like this. Exactly. And maybe we can plan to do something fun this weekend. Maybe go out for dinner or something. That sounds great. Although, I was thinking about trying a new TV show. I’ve heard a lot about this one called  Stranger Things . Oh, I’ve heard of that! I think it’s set in the 80s, right? Yeah, that’s what I remember. It’s about a group of kids who find a portal to another dimension. It’s supposed to be pretty good. Cool. I’ve been meaning to watch something like that. I think I’ll start watching it this weekend. That sounds like a good plan. And maybe we can all watch it together? Definitely. It’ll be fun. And maybe after that, we can catch up on some photos.

So, do you know about the new bus route they're planning to start from the town centre? I heard it’s going to go all the way to Cambridge station, which would be a huge convenience. Yeah, I think I read about that in the local paper. They’re trying to reduce congestion and make public transport more efficient. But I’m not sure if it’ll actually make things better. Speaking of which, I went into the Cambridge University Press bookshop the other day. I was looking for a textbook for my course and found some really interesting books. Oh, the bookshop? That sounds amazing. I think I need to start doing that more. I’ve been so focused on work and studying that I haven’t really had time to explore the city properly. You should. I mean, Cambridge is full of history and culture, and the bookshop is just one of the many things that make it unique. But then again, I have to say, I still miss the days when I could hang out with my friends at the university and just chat about everything. I know, it’s such a different experience now. I remember hearing about student protests on campus last year. I think it was over something to do with tuition fees or the cost of living. Yeah, I remember something like that. Some people were really passionate about it, but I think it was more of a symbolic gesture than anything else.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about food a lot lately. It’s strange, since I was a maths teacher, I never really gave much thought to recipes or cooking. But now that I’m retired, I’m trying to get back into the kitchen. That’s great! I mean, cooking’s a nice hobby to take up. It’s also a good way to bond with family. You should try making something with your grandkids. I bet they’d love it. Yeah, and you know, I’ve been meaning to ask you, how’s your family doing? I heard you’ve got a grandchild now? You know, I used to be in front of a class all the time, but now I’m trying to get her to sit still for more than five minutes! Oh, I can relate. I have a son who’s about the same age. He’s in primary school now, and he’s always asking me to play games with him instead of doing his homework. That’s the age, isn’t it? They’re so full of energy. I swear, they can’t sit still for five minutes, not even if it’s a school day. Exactly! And then when they do sit still, they’re just staring out the window or drawing random things on their desks. It’s so frustrating. I know, I know. But you’d be surprised how quickly they grow up. Before you know it, they’re off to secondary school and you’re just left wondering where the time went. I remember when I was in secondary school. I was so obsessed with boys. I even had a crush on this guy in my class. His name was James. He was so into music, he used to play the guitar all the time. James? That sounds familiar. You must have been in the same class as him. No, not exactly. I think he was in the year above me. But he used to come into our classroom and play his guitar during break time. It was so cool. I used to sit there and just listen to him play. That’s a lovely story. I’ve always thought that music is such an important part of growing up.

So, do you remember when we first walked this stretch of the Thames? I think it was around the time we were planning our big holiday to France. Remember how we got lost for ages trying to find where the river actually started? Oh, I remember! We were so confused. I was trying to figure out if we were walking east or west, and you were arguing about whether the Thames actually flows into the North Sea or not. It was ridiculous. Well, it does flow into the North Sea, you know. It’s just that it takes a while to get there. Still, I think it’s amazing how the city has changed over the years. All those old warehouses, now turned into trendy bars and restaurants. It’s like the river itself is evolving. Yeah, I guess it is. It’s funny how places you used to walk past every day can become something entirely different. I remember when we first moved to London, we’d walk this path every morning on our way to work. Now we’re out here on a weekend, just taking in the view. Exactly. I’ve been thinking about our upcoming holiday. I’m really nervous about not having a car. But you’ll get the hang of it. Besides, it’s not like we’re going anywhere that’s a million miles away. We’re just going to the south coast—maybe a couple of days in Brighton, then a few days in Portsmouth. It’s not that far. I guess. But I still worry about the logistics. What if we miss a train? What if the ferry doesn’t run on time? It’s all so unpredictable. I get it. But you know what? It’s also a chance to unplug. You mentioned you’ve been working so much lately, you’ve barely had a break. This holiday is supposed to be about relaxation, not stress. Yeah, I guess you’re right. It’s just that I’m so used to having a car. I mean, even in the city, it’s easier to just hop in and drive somewhere.

I can't believe it's already raining again. I was just going to go out for a run, but now I might as well stay in. Oh, it's been like that all week! It's like the sky's decided to have a dramatic meltdown. I wouldn't be surprised if it started leaking from the clouds. Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s been so wet that even the dog’s been reluctant to go outside. I’ve had to carry him into the house like a little umbrella. That’s not fair. You can’t just make your dog feel like he’s a wet dog! I mean, I get it—it’s raining, but can we at least let him have a walk? I’ve already missed my yoga class twice this week because of this. I know, I know. I tried to take him for a walk this morning, but it was just buckets of water and wind. He looked like he was thinking, “Is this the end of the world?” I felt awful. I even gave him a treat for being brave. You didn’t have to give him a treat! He’s a dog, not a human. Although, I will say, he did look kind of proud of himself after that. I swear he was pretending he was a hero. Yeah, and then he came back and sat on the kitchen floor and just stared at me like, “Well done, you! You made me wet and then gave me a treat. What a suspiciously generous human.” I can definitely picture that. He’d be like a cartoon dog with a tiny crown and a sword. I think he’s got a personality. That’s the thing, though. He’s not just a dog. He’s like this little sister to me. I barely even get to see my real sister these days, and here I am, bonding with a four-legged friend. I feel you. My sister is in London, and I haven’t seen her in months. You know what’s worse? She’s been sending me these weird photos of her new apartment with weird captions. It’s like she’s trying to be a social media influencer, but she’s not. That sounds frustrating. I tried to be more active on social media once, and I just started getting messages from random people asking me to be their friend.

So, do you think we should start thinking about what we want to do next? I mean, with the house-sitting and everything, it’s kind of like a break, but maybe it’s time to start planning for the future. I was thinking the same thing. It’s funny, isn’t it? And maybe we could make it a bit of a family thing. I know your sister mentioned she’s thinking of starting her own business, and I’d love to see her take the leap. Maybe we could support each other. That would be nice. I mean, family planning is something we’ve both touched on, isn’t it? I think we both know we want to have kids eventually, but we haven’t really pinned down the timeline. Yeah, and that’s okay. We’ve both got our careers to think about, and it’s important to make sure we’re both on the same page. I go back and forth — sometimes I feel like I’m ready, other times I just want to enjoy the moment.

So, do you reckon we should go to the shop? I’m running out of after-eights. Are you serious? You’ve had more than enough of those this week. Honestly, I think you’ve had like, ten of them since yesterday. Yeah, but I’ve been so stressed with work. I think it’s the only thing that helps me calm down. I get that, but you can’t just keep eating them. You’ll be in trouble with the Fitbit. Oh, come on, you can’t blame the Fitbit! It’s not like it’s got the power to stop you. It’s not the Fitbit. It’s the fact that you’re behaving like a child who hasn’t eaten all day. Hey, I’m not a child. I’m a grown woman with a job and a life. And I’m not saying you’re not, but maybe you should try something else. Like, I don’t know, getting out of the house. Like camping? Or going to the countryside? I’ve been meaning to do that with my mates. Camping? Are you serious? I can’t even sleep in a tent without getting paranoid. I know, right? It’s like, what if a bear comes? Or a wolf? Or worse—what if the Wi-Fi dies? Oh, calm down. It’s just a bit of fresh air. You’d be surprised how much you can do without your phone. Yeah, and it’s about time you stopped relying on all that technology. You can’t live your whole life on a Fitbit and a phone. I don’t even know what I’d do without them. I’ve got like, a hundred notifications a day. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to cut down on social media, but I just can’t help it. It’s like trying to stop smoking. You can’t just do it overnight. I’m not smoking, though! I’ve quit that. Oh, come on, you don’t even look like you’ve smoked in years. You know what your problem is? You’re too comfortable. You’ve got this nice job, you’ve got your Fitbit, your phone, your everything. Yeah, but sometimes you need to step out of your comfort zone. I mean, if you’re going to be in the pub all the time, you might as well get out and do something.

Well, I've just had a look at the post, and there’s a bit of a squabble going on over in the village about the new local park. They want to put in a community garden, but some folks are concerned about the wildlife. Oh, I heard about that. My cousin’s on the committee. She says it’s a brilliant idea, but the council seems to be dragging their heels. They’ve got all these plans and no one’s putting their foot down. It’s always the same, isn’t it? They talk about community involvement, but when it comes to actually making a decision, they’re too scared to take a stand. I think the real issue is that they’re worried about the backlash from the older folks who still like things the way they are. I couldn’t agree more. I’ve been to a few meetings where people just sit there nodding and saying, "Well, that’s up to the council." No one wants to be the one to rock the boat, especially when the council’s got so much power. Yeah, and it’s not just about the park. I remember when they tried to introduce a new bus route last year. All the old-timers were against it, even though it would’ve been better for the younger folk. They just weren’t willing to change. That’s true. I think a lot of people are just afraid of the unknown. If something’s been done a certain way for years, changing it feels like a risk. But sometimes, you have to take a risk to make things better. Speaking of risks, have you seen the new TV show that’s been on? It’s about a small village trying to save their community from a development project. It’s got this real-life feel to it. Maybe they’re basing it on something like the park debate? I have! It’s actually quite good. The characters are all based on real people, and the dialogue’s spot on. I was laughing when they had a scene where the mayor tried to explain the benefits of the development, and the locals just rolled their eyes and said, “We’ve been here longer than your plan.” That sounds exactly like something that would happen here! I could see the goings-on on that show if it were set in Costessey.

So, do you think I should drop out of uni? I mean, I know it's a big decision, but honestly, I’m just so stressed all the time. I can’t even remember the last time I felt happy. Hmm, I mean, you’ve been struggling for a while, haven’t you? I can tell. But dropping out feels like a big step. What’s making you feel like you’ve had enough? It’s just... everything. The workload, the deadlines, the pressure to do well. And I don’t even know if I want to be doing this anymore. I mean, I like some of the stuff I’m learning, but the constant anxiety is wearing me down. I get that. I’ve had moments where I thought about taking a break too. You know, maybe take a gap year or just switch courses. But I’m still going. How do you know you want to quit for good? I don’t know, maybe I just don’t want to be here anymore. I mean, I’m not even sure what I want to do next. I feel like I’m just going through the motions. That’s understandable. But have you talked to anyone about it? Like, your lecturer or a careers adviser? They might be able to help you figure out what you want to do next. I’ve tried, but I don’t think they really get what I’m going through. It’s like they just want me to keep going and not worry about my mental health. I can see that. But you’re not alone in this, you know. Even if you drop out, there’s still a lot of people out there who have taken a different path. And honestly, you don’t have to figure it all out right now. I guess. But it’s just so hard to imagine life without university. I mean, I was always told that it was the best thing for me. But I feel like I’m not even getting anywhere. You know, I remember being really into school when I was younger. I used to love the lunches, the friends, the sense of being part of something. Even though I was a bit of a kid, I had a good time. Yeah, I guess I was like that too. I used to love school, but now it feels so different.

I can't believe it's been so long since we last saw each other. It feels like ages. Yeah, I know. I’m so glad we finally got together. I was thinking about you the other day, actually. I saw this article about Oxford and it made me want to catch up. That’s nice. I’ve been meaning to get in touch too. Life’s been pretty busy with work and everything. I’m thinking of taking a break from work for a while to figure things out. Maybe travel or do some freelance work. That sounds like a good idea.

Right, so I’ve just got this thing on Amazon, you know, the one that’s supposed to be a really good wireless keyboard. And it came in today, and I’ve been trying it out. It's alright, but I don’t know if it's worth the price. Yeah, I tried one of those a while ago. It was supposed to be the best, but it kept crashing and the battery died in like three hours. I ended up just using my phone for everything. Oh no, that’s not good. I thought these things were more reliable. Maybe I should have gone for the cheaper one on eBay instead. I mean, I've heard the ones from eBay can be a bit of a gamble, but sometimes they're better quality. Yeah, I think that's the thing with eBay. You get what you pay for. Sometimes you get a great deal, sometimes you end up with a piece of junk. But if you're careful, you can find some real gems. Exactly. I’ve seen some pretty cool stuff on eBay, like vintage electronics or things you can’t find in shops anymore. I mean, did you know that some of the early versions of the Xbox were sold on eBay for hundreds of pounds? People are still buying them just because they’re rare. Oh, I remember that. There was a huge buzz about that. Some of those boxes were like museum pieces. I think I saw one once with a broken disc drive, but still someone bought it just for the nostalgia. It's amazing how people can get so sentimental about technology. I guess it’s the same with cars, clothes, even books. If it’s got a bit of history, people will pay a fortune for it. For sure. I’ve seen some books on eBay that are like 50 years old, and people are still paying top dollar for them. Maybe it’s just the idea that they’re original or something. Or maybe it's just the thrill of the hunt. I mean, I always get a bit of rush when I find something on eBay that’s not too expensive but still a good buy. It’s like treasure hunting, isn't it? Yeah, I can see that. I still do it sometimes, although I've started using Amazon more because it's just more reliable.

So, do you know what’s going on with the council? I’ve been trying to get my garden sorted for ages, and they keep saying they’re going to do something about it, but nothing ever happens. Yeah, I heard they’re planning to do some work on the roads near here. I think they’re going to build a new pathway or something. But I don’t know how that affects your garden. It’s not that. It’s more about the trees. There was this big oak tree in front of my house, and it’s been dying for months. I told the council about it, but they said they couldn’t do anything until they get more funding. I don’t know what I’m going to do if it falls down. That’s worrying. I had a similar situation with my neighbor’s tree. It was leaning over her roof, and it almost fell during the storm last week. She had to call the council, and they sent someone out to assess it. They said it was dangerous, and they had to cut it down. It was a mercy, really. Yeah, I can imagine. I don’t want to be responsible for any damage if the tree falls. I tried talking to the council again last week. I said, “If you’re not going to do anything, maybe I should hire someone to take care of it myself.” They just said, “We’ll get back to you.” And they haven’t. That’s not very helpful. I think they should be more proactive. You know, maybe they have some sort of emergency service or something. Or maybe you could get some advice from the local community centre? I heard they’ve got a gardening group that helps people with issues like this. That’s an idea. I might go and talk to them. I’m tired of waiting for the council to act. I mean, I’m not even sure if they’re even taking my complaints seriously anymore. They just say, “We’ll get back to you,” and then nothing. You could always get a second opinion. Like, maybe a professional gardener or a tree surgeon. If you’re worried about the tree falling, maybe you could get it checked out. Then you’d have some proof that it’s dangerous, and you could use that to push for action.

So, do you think we're actually going to be able to get everything sorted for Christmas? I mean, like, the tree, the food, the presents... I think we’re going to be okay. I’ve already started planning the menu. It’s going to be a proper Christmas feast—roast turkey, Yorkshire pudding, all that stuff. But I reckon we’ll need to buy some extra vegetables just in case. Oh, I’m so excited about the Christmas food. I’ve been thinking about making my famous Christmas cake for years. It’s got brandy in it, and I like to add a bit of cinnamon and nutmeg. It’s the real deal. That sounds amazing, but I’ve never had a Christmas cake. I’ve always just had the basics—mince pies, maybe a bit of Christmas pudding. Although, I was at a café once where they had this really weird Christmas cake that was covered in chocolate and had a whole almond on top. It was amazing, honestly. Wow, that sounds intense. I mean, do you even get Christmas cake in Australia? Yeah, we do. It’s a real tradition. But we’ve got this thing where we always have to fly on Christmas Day. It’s like a tradition for us, you know? I mean, flying on Christmas Day is the only way we can get back to see our family. That’s not for me. I’m not someone who wants to fly on Christmas Day. I’d rather just stay home and chill. I can see why. I’d be stressed flying on Christmas Day, especially with all the crowds. I think I’d rather travel a few days earlier. Yeah, I can’t imagine flying on Christmas Day. I think I’d get so annoyed. But I guess if you’re in a place like Australia, you have no choice. Exactly. And the flights are so crowded too. I once had to sit next to someone who was eating a whole bag of chips and then spilled it all over me. It was the worst. That sounds terrible. I mean, you can’t even get a seat on some of the flights. I remember one year I ended up sitting next to a guy who was crying the whole time, and I had to pretend I didn’t notice. That sounds like something out of a movie.

So, do you think we’re gonna get a lot of different accents on the way back? I mean, we’re going to pick up a few people on the way, right? Yeah, I was just thinking about that. I mean, I heard someone from Manchester on the phone earlier, and it was like,  bleep , I could almost see them in a flattop. Oh, yeah, I know. I was in a café yesterday, and this guy was talking to the barista, and he had this  distinct  northern accent. It was like,  boom , right? I thought, “Is he from Newcastle or is he from Leeds?” I couldn’t tell. It’s wild, isn’t it? I mean, I grew up in Birmingham, so I know the Birmingham accent pretty well, but every time I hear someone from somewhere else, it’s like, “Wait, is that a London accent or a West Country one?” I think the thing is, even within the same city, the accents can be so different. Like, I’ve met people from Birmingham who sound like they’re from Manchester. It’s like a whole different vibe. Exactly. I’ve got a mate who’s from Liverpool, and when he’s in London, he pretends he’s from the South East. I mean, it’s like he’s trying to fit in, but you can still tell. I’ve heard that. Like, some people will switch accents depending on who they’re with. It’s a bit of a social thing, isn’t it? Like, if you’re with your friends from home, you speak like you did in school, but if you’re with people from another area, you try to sound more “normal.” Yeah, and I think it’s not just about the accent. It’s also about how you speak. Like, some people use more slang, or they drop their ‘g’s. It’s all part of the culture. I think that’s what makes it so interesting. We all come from different places, but we all have our own way of speaking. I mean, even in the same region, there are so many variations. I think the biggest surprise to me was when I went to Cambridge for the first time. I thought I’d be in a place that was more like Oxford, but the accent here is completely different. It’s like, “Wait, is this the South of England or is it somewhere else?”

So, did you guys see the new Marvel movie last week? I heard it was insane. Yeah, I did. I thought it was okay, but I wasn’t really sure what the big deal was. Alright, skipper, you've got your pizza, and I've got mine. You know, it's like a proper meal after that long drive. Yeah, it was a right proper drive, wasn’t it? I couldn’t believe how far we went. You worry more than my dad does.

So, do you know what’s the biggest thing about pubs in Sunderland? They’re like the heart of the community, you know? You go in there, and it’s like, everyone knows your name. It's not just a place to drink—it's where people hang out, chat, and catch up. Yeah, I can see that. I mean, I’ve been to a few pubs in Cambridge, but they’re all so quiet and formal. I mean, it’s not like you can just walk in and expect to have a conversation with the barman. It’s more like a café with a bar. Oh, I know, but I think that’s the thing—people in Sunderland don’t like that. They like to be part of the conversation. I remember one time, I was at the local pub with some friends, and the whole place just stopped to listen when someone started telling a story. It was like a scene from a play. That does sound like a different vibe. I guess it’s the way people are raised there. I mean, I’ve heard that in places like the North, pubs are more of a social hub than just a place to drink. I think the vegetables here are also different. In Cambridge, most of the veggies you get are like, fresh and healthy. But in the North, they’re more like, heavy, like roasted or baked. I mean, I’ve had a whole side of mashed cauliflower with a side of grilled carrots, and it was like, wow, I didn’t know I could eat that much vegetable. Oh, you’re not the only one. I’ve tried to eat veggies in the North, and it’s like, they’re not just veggies—they’re like a main course. I think it’s more of a cultural thing.

So, do you think I should go to university or do an apprenticeship? I’m really confused. I think it depends on what you want to do. If you like studying, then uni is probably better. But if you want to get into work straight away, an apprenticeship might be good too. Yeah, I mean, I’m doing an apprenticeship now, and I love it. I’m learning so much, and I’m already getting paid. That sounds great! But I was in university for a few years. It was tough, but I got a good degree, and it helped me get my job. I’m not sure yet. I’m thinking about doing both, like a degree apprenticeship. But I’m scared I’ll waste time. Yeah, I’m scared too. I’ve heard so many stories about people going to uni and then not getting a job. That’s true, but not everyone’s the same. Some people do really well, and some don’t. It’s all about what you want to do. I think it’s also about your personality. If you’re more hands-on, apprenticeships are better. If you like reading and thinking, uni might suit you. Exactly. And it’s not just about the job. Uni gives you a lot of skills and opportunities for the future. But what if I’m not interested in what I’m studying? I don’t want to waste my time. I get that. It’s hard to choose. Maybe you could do a gap year or take some courses to see what you like. Yeah, that’s a good idea. You could try different things and then decide what you want to do next. I know someone who did that. They worked for a year and then went to uni. It worked out well for them. I used to work part-time while studying. It helped me get my head around what I wanted to do. That sounds like a good plan. I’m just worried about the money. I know, it can be expensive. But there are loans and grants. If you work hard, you can manage it. Yeah, and you get a qualification either way. It’s all about what you want to achieve. And think about your long-term goals. If you want to be a manager or in a high-paying job, uni might help.

Well, do you know, I’ve been thinking about going for a walk this evening. The weather’s been so nice lately, and I’ve been feeling a bit more spry than usual. That sounds good, Mum. You should go. It’ll do him good too. And it’ll do you good as well. You know, I’ve been telling my cousin about how much I miss walking. She said she’s been trying to get back into it too. You know, I was thinking about getting a bike again. It’s been a long time since I’ve had one. Maybe I could take you out for a short ride. So, do you know much about the Basque language? I’ve been reading a bit about it for a project I’m working on. A bit, I guess. I know it’s a language spoken in the Basque Country, which is in Spain and France. But I’m not sure if it’s related to any other language. Isn’t it considered a unique language? That’s a good question. The Basque language, Euskara, is indeed quite unique. It’s not related to any other known language family. It’s one of the few languages that isn’t Indo-European, which makes it very interesting from a linguistic standpoint. That’s fascinating. I’ve heard it’s considered a language isolate, right? So it doesn’t have any close relatives. I was also wondering, do you think it’s used much in modern times? Or is it more of a heritage language? I think it’s used in some areas, especially in the Basque regions. But I’m not sure how widely it’s spoken. I know there are efforts to keep it alive, like education and media, but I’m not up to date on the numbers. Actually, it’s quite a vibrant language in some parts. There are schools where it’s taught, and it’s used in government and media. However, it’s still considered a minority language, and the younger generation might not be as fluent as the older ones. It’s a language that’s been in the news a lot lately because of the political situation in the Basque Country. I had no idea it was so politically charged. It must be a complicated situation. I’ve also been thinking about China and how the government has been influencing language policies there. Do you think language preservation is a global issue? Definitely. I think it’s something that happens in many countries. In the UK, for example, there’s been a lot of debate about the Welsh language and its preservation. And in Scotland, the same goes for Gaelic. It’s about identity, culture, and national pride, really. Exactly. Language is deeply tied to identity. And that’s why places like Wales and the Basque Country have been so vocal about maintaining their languages. Even in places like London, there are communities that are fighting to keep their languages alive. I can see that. I suppose it’s not just about the language itself, but also about the culture and history that comes with it.

So, how’s the kid doing? I heard you’ve been going through the adoption process again. Oh, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. We had a few setbacks, but we’re finally getting close to a match. It’s such a long process, though. Yeah, I can only imagine. I mean, I’ve seen how stressful it can be. You’ve got all these forms to fill in, and then you have to wait and wait and wait. It’s like a game of patience. But, honestly, it’s worth it if it works out. I mean, I can’t imagine not having the kids, you know? I know. It’s just frustrating when things don’t go smoothly. I had to go through the same thing with my brother. He wanted to adopt, but it was just a mess. Wait, your brother? He’s the one in America? Yeah, he moved there a few years back. He tried to adopt a kid, but the system over there is just so different. He ended up giving up after a while. It was heartbreaking. That’s rough. I can't imagine going through that. But I mean, I know how it is with family. Sometimes, you think you’re ready, and then the system just doesn’t work with you. Yeah, and then there’s the dialect thing. Our parents always said we should stick with the way we speak, but I’ve noticed that some of the kids in the area have such different accents. It’s like they’re from a different place. I know. I think it’s the way the school system is set up. Some kids come from different backgrounds and grow up with different ways of speaking. It’s not a bad thing, just different. I mean, I can see that. I’ve been working with a lot of people from different parts of the country, and it’s fascinating. You can tell where they’re from just by how they speak. Yeah, and I think it’s part of the charm. I mean, you can get a whole bunch of different accents in one room, and it’s like a little world. True. I just hope the kids we end up adopting can feel comfortable with all that. I mean, you don’t want them to feel like they’re different, you know?

I can't believe we've got this coffee machine now, can we? I was just thinking, it's like having a café in the kitchen. Yeah, it's a bit much, isn't it? I mean, we're not even that into coffee. But I guess it's a nice touch, especially with the weather being so grim out. Honestly, I don't know why we didn’t get one earlier. I mean, this one's top of the range. It even has a milk frother and everything. You can make cappuccino in your own kitchen now. You don’t even need to go out. That’s the thing, though. I think it's more about the convenience than the coffee itself. Besides, I heard the cost of replacing the machine if it breaks down is going to be a bit of a shock. I remember reading somewhere about the removal and storage costs when you have to send it back for repairs. It's like a whole other bill. Oh, I’m sure the warranty will cover it, though. It’s a new machine, so maybe we’re in the lucky category. But if we’re not, it might be worth considering a cheaper model. You know, something that doesn't require a second mortgage to fix. You know what's even more expensive, though? The politics these days. I mean, Labour's leadership is a mess. I don't know what they're doing with the economy. It’s like they're trying to fix one thing and breaking another. I just don’t see how they can keep up with all the demands. I agree. The whole thing feels like a giant game of Whac-A-Mole. One problem is solved, and another pops up somewhere else. I remember when I was in the classroom, I used to tell my students that idealism is a beautiful thing, but it has to be tempered with realism. Otherwise, you end up in a mess. You know, I think that's true. I mean, I used to be idealistic too. I believed in making a difference through words. Now I just try to do my best with what I have. It’s not about changing the world, it’s about trying to make a small impact where I can. I think that’s the real key, though. It’s not about trying to be perfect or fix everything.

So, do you think we’ll be able to get away with going to the coast for Christmas this year? I’d really like to go somewhere with the kids, just for a bit of peace and quiet. I know it’s a big decision, but I support you. If you’re going to move, I’d rather be waiting for you somewhere warm than stuck in England with the rain and cold. I’m not sure yet. I’m trying to get a teaching license and find a good school. But I think it’s time I stopped putting it off. I’ve been working here for over ten years, and I’ve got a lot of experience.

So, do you remember that time we were all at the pub last week and one of the lads started snoring so loud it sounded like a chainsaw? Oh, I remember that! So how’s life treating you these days? You mentioned you were going to take a break from teaching for a while... What’s the plan? It’s been a bit of a rollercoaster, honestly. I’ve been trying to figure out what I want to do next. I’ve been doing some freelance work here and there, but it’s not really enough to keep me going. I’ve been thinking a lot about going back to work with kids, maybe in a different setting. I’m not sure yet. That makes sense. I mean, you’ve always had such a passion for working with children. It’s just a matter of finding the right fit for you. I’ve been thinking about my own work too. I still teach, but I’m starting to feel like I need more variety. I’ve been considering learning another language for the sake of it, just to challenge myself. Oh, that’s a great idea. I mean, I’ve always been curious about languages, especially Spanish and French. I remember when I was at school, I used to be obsessed with learning vocabulary and conjugations, but I never really got around to putting it into practice. What about you? Did you ever study a language as a kid? I did! I was pretty good at languages. I remember doing German at school and I even took some Spanish classes during university. I loved it, but I think I got too caught up in the work and never really pursued it further. It’s kind of funny because now, with my job, I often find myself needing to teach languages, so I’m kind of in the opposite position. That’s kind of ironic, isn’t it? I mean, I did the same thing. I was always interested in learning languages, but I never really thought about doing it as a career. I guess you end up ending up in a role that kind of forces you to do that. Maybe it’s not so bad. Yeah, maybe not. I think it’s actually quite rewarding. I mean, there’s something about helping someone learn a language that gives you such a sense of accomplishment. But I still want to expand my own skills. I’ve been thinking about going back to learn French, maybe take some classes or even consider a course abroad.

Well, I've just been out in the garden, and I found a bird's nest in the old birch tree. You know, the one by the side of the shed. Oh, really? I didn’t notice anything. Did you see what sort of birds it was? I think it’s a sparrow. It was all nicely lined with twigs and bits of string. I reckon it’s got a couple of eggs in there. Oh, how nice. I like birds. Especially when they’re feeding. I’ve got a couple of feeders up by the window, and the tits and sparrows come in every morning. Yeah, I’ve got one too. My wife used to put out seeds, but she’s not around anymore. I still do it sometimes, just for the company. That’s a good thing. Keeps you active, and you get to see the birds. I remember when I was younger, we used to have a lot of birds around the place. I used to feed the pigeons every day. Yeah, I remember that too. Used to be a lot of birds. But now, with all the development, it’s quieter. I suppose people don't care so much about feeding them anymore. Maybe they just don’t have the time. I know some of the younger people don’t know how to feed birds properly. They just throw the seeds out and don’t think about it. Well, I think it’s good to keep them around. Besides, I’ve got a new puppet I bought at the market. I named him Pip, and he’s got a little basket for the seeds. I think he’s going to be the best bird feeder ever. A puppet? That’s a good idea. I suppose you could say the puppet is the real bird feeder. Oh, I like that. It’s like the puppet is taking care of them. You know, I was thinking about getting a puppet too. Maybe for the cat. He’s always knocking things over. Oh, you've got a cat? I thought you told me you were allergic. I am, but I’ve got a little one called Muffin. He’s not too bad. He’s got a soft spot for me. I think he knows I’m the one who feeds him. That’s nice. I used to have a cat when I was younger.

I think I’ll go for the moussaka. It’s one of the best things in Cyprus, isn’t it? Yes, I agree. I’ve had it so many times, but it’s always delicious. I think I’ll go for the grilled halloumi and a side of hummus. Sounds good. You know, I’ve been meaning to ask—did you ever learn to count in Turkish? Oh, I did. It was part of my language studies when I was in the army. Funny how things come back to you. That’s amazing. I’ve always wanted to learn a bit of Turkish, just for the travel. Though I’m not sure I’d ever use it. Probably not. But it’s nice to have a bit of a connection. You know, I used to help a friend of mine who was studying abroad in Turkey. He found it so frustrating trying to navigate the language, even basic things like ordering food or asking for directions. I can imagine. I once tried to order a coffee in a shop in Istanbul and I think the barista thought I was trying to tell a joke. Sounds like a classic situation. Well, I got to say, I’ve always found language learning a bit of a way to stay connected to places I’ve been. It’s not just about the words, it’s about the culture and the people. Definitely. I think it’s also part of the way we remember places and people. Like, when I think about my father-in-law, I can still hear him talking about the time he was in Turkey teaching English. He had this funny habit of always trying to teach the locals how to say “hello” properly. Oh, that’s a lovely story. You know, I remember my father telling me once that he used to believe in dowsing. He said that if you could find the right stick, you could find water anywhere. I always thought it was a bit of a gimmick, but I suppose it’s part of what makes people who they are. I guess it’s like the way some people believe in spiritual matters or shamanism. It’s not about being scientific, it’s more about believing in something. Exactly. I think it’s the same thing as learning a language. It’s about connecting with something deeper.

Mum, do you know when we’re going to start the renovation on the house? I’ve been thinking about it a lot lately. Oh, I know, I’ve been meaning to talk about that too. It’s just been such a long time since we’ve had the chance to really make some changes. I was thinking maybe after Christmas? Yeah, I think that makes sense. The weather’s been awful all winter, and I’d rather not be working on the roof or anything while it’s still so cold and damp. Plus, the kids will be home then, and we can all chip in a bit. That’s true. I was also thinking about the kitchen. You know, the old one’s a bit outdated, and I’d like to modernise it a bit. Maybe even add a bigger island? Oh, an island would be nice. But wait, have you thought about what you want the new kitchen to look like? I mean, do you want it to be more traditional or more modern? I think maybe something in between. I like the idea of having some sleek appliances but keeping the overall look a bit warm. Maybe with some wooden accents. Sounds good. I reckon we should start by getting a few quotes from local builders. You know, get a few different opinions and see what the market rate is. Let’s not go overboard, though. We don’t want to spend more than we need to. Definitely. I was just thinking about the Christmas presents too. I know we’ve been doing a lot of Christmas stuff, but I think this year we should be more mindful with our spending. Yeah, I agree. I mean, I know you all want to give something nice, but let’s not be too extravagant. We can always go to the market and pick up a few decent gifts that have some heart behind them. Exactly. I remember when I was younger, my grandmother used to make Christmas gifts for everyone. She’d knit scarves, or make cakes, or something like that. It was more about the effort than the price. That’s a good point. I think we could do something like that. Maybe have a family gift swap or something? Let’s all contribute something we can make or find cheaply. That’s a great idea. And it would be nice to get the kids involved too.

So, do you know what’s up with this Catfish thing? I saw this episode the other day and it was wild. Oh yeah, I remember that! It was like a dating game show where people pretend to be someone else online, right? It was so creepy. Yeah, and the host, Jeremy Kyle, he was like, “You’ve got to be careful with who you’re talking to online.” Like, he’s always giving those warnings. I know, but it’s just so weird how people can lie about themselves. Like, I mean, I’ve seen some of those profiles and they’re just made up. I don’t know how they even do it. It’s not just that they lie about their looks or their age – they lie about who they are. Like, one guy in the show said he was an ex-soldier and had a big house, but it turned out he was just some guy in a flat in Manchester. That’s insane. I mean, why even bother? It’s not like they’re getting anything out of it other than a bit of fun. I guess some people just like to play games. Yeah, but it’s so dangerous.
