I think they’ve been seeing each other for a while. Doesn’t seem like a big deal, but I’m sure the whole village will be buzzing about it. Yeah, I imagine so. Now, I did hear something about their wedding. I think they’re planning to have it at the local hall. Who knows, maybe they’ll even get a few of the Reverend’s old friends to come out and make a speech. Hey, what about food? I had a curry last night, and it was just amazing. I think the restaurant here has been getting better. I had a chat with the owner last week, and he said they’re thinking of expanding. You know, more tables, maybe even a takeaway window. Oh, that sounds nice. I always prefer to eat out when I can. Do you know if they’ve got any special things on the menu? I’m getting a bit tired of the same old dishes. I think they’ve been trying some new recipes. I saw a flyer in the village shop the other day mentioning a special seafood night. I might go check it out.

So, do you think we should get a log burner for the living room? I mean, it’s been a bit chilly lately and the old fireplace isn’t really up to scratch. Yeah, I was thinking the same thing. I’ve seen some really nice ones online, but the problem is the budget. We’re already spending a lot on the new restaurant down the road. Oh, I heard about that restaurant. It’s supposed to be amazing, isn’t it? I’ve had some lovely dishes there. But you know, I still think the best food is homemade. Especially mashed potato. That’s true, but I also think a log burner could make a big difference. It’s not just about the heat, it’s about the ambiance. I remember when I was a school master, we had a fireplace in the staff room, and it made the place feel more like a home. Yeah, that’s a good point. I was in the market for a few different models last week, but I couldn’t decide. I was also thinking about the upholstery—should we do something with the living room furniture? It’s getting a bit worn out. I think that’s a good idea. We could maybe get some new cushions and a rug. I’ve seen some lovely ones at the antique shop near the town centre. It’s a bit of a trip, but the selection is amazing. Oh, I went there last weekend. There was this one old rug that looked like it could have been from the 1920s. I almost bought it, but the price was a bit too steep. Still, I think it’s worth it to invest in something that lasts. I agree. Investing in good quality furniture is always worth it. I’ve seen some very nice pieces that are still in use in our old school, even after decades. But, I must say, I still miss the days when we had a school with real character. You know, I was talking to my neighbour about the new school academy. They’re really pushing for more funding, but I worry about the quality of education. I think it’s important to have a strong, consistent system. I agree. I think the key is to balance tradition with innovation. I mean, I’m not against outsourcing some of the work, like the administrative side, but we can’t let it take over completely.

I just got a letter from the council about the new housing developments near Wymondham. They're talking about building a lot of houses, but I don’t think it’s going to help anyone. It’s all just for the young people who are moving in and then they’ll be gone in a couple of years. Yeah, I heard about that too. I reckon it’s all about the government trying to boost the economy, but if they’re not putting money into proper infrastructure or services, what’s the point? I mean, we’ve got the same old schools and roads, just more houses. That’s true enough. I remember when I was a childminder, I’d always tell the parents that if they wanted a good area to raise kids, they should look for somewhere where the schools are good and the community is strong. But now, the only thing people care about is whether the house is near a train station or not. Exactly. I used to live in Norfolk, and I remember when the area was quieter. So, do you think we've got this all figured out? I mean, the string breaking issue is a real problem, and I don't think we can just keep replacing them every time. I agree, it's not sustainable. We need a better solution. I've been thinking about using cable ties instead of the traditional string. They’re stronger and more durable. Plus, they’re easy to replace if they break. I mean, the strings need to be tight enough to keep the racket in shape, but not so tight that the frame gets damaged. That's a good point. Maybe we could experiment with different types of cable ties—both plastic and metal. Metal ones might be sturdier but harder to adjust. I was thinking we could also use some sort of tension gauge or tool to measure the tightness. I like the idea of a tension gauge. It would be a helpful tool for users, especially in schools. I know when I was teaching, I had to explain to parents and students about the importance of proper string tension. It's not just about making it tight—it's about balance and rhythm in the game. Exactly. And talking about the school, I think there's a big opportunity there. Primary schools might not have the budget for expensive racket repairs, so a simple, cost-effective solution like cable ties could be a game-changer. That's true. It's also worth considering the cost—what's the average cost per repair? If we can bring it down, we might be able to market it as an affordable alternative to professional stringing. I've been thinking about that. If we can make the system easy to use, even for kids, it could be a hit. I mean, they could do it themselves, right? No need for a specialist. You know, I was thinking about the word "fleet" the other day. I've heard it used in different contexts, but I'm not sure if it's the right term for the strings on a racket. Maybe "set" or "string set" is better. Yeah, I think you’re right. "Fleet" sounds like it's referring to a group of things that move quickly, which doesn't quite fit here.

Well, I've been having a look through some old books, you know, the ones I used to read when I was a lad, and I came across a few interesting things about art. I just don’t get how people can still smoke. I mean, I know it’s a vice, but it’s got to be so harmful. I tried once, and I couldn’t even get past the first cigarette. I felt like I was being poisoned. I know, but it’s not just about the harm. It’s about the habit, the routine. Some people use it as a crutch. Like, I used to smoke after work every day. It felt like a ritual. It was a way of switching off from the day. I don’t know if I could do that now with just a cup of tea. I guess that’s a form of self-medication, isn’t it? But I think you have to be intelligent enough to know that it’s not healthy. I mean, I’m not saying everyone is smart, but if you’re aware of the risks, you’ve got to make the right choice. That’s true, but I think people often confuse intelligence with discipline. You can be smart, but if you don’t have the self-control, you’ll still do things that are bad for you. Like, I mean, we all know smoking is bad, but the real question is, why do we still do it? It’s got to be about the dopamine hit. The way it makes you feel, even if it’s just for a few minutes. It’s like a quick fix. You know what I mean? It’s not just about the habit, it’s about the psychology of it. And then there’s the alcohol, which is so much more socially accepted. It’s like a cultural thing. Yeah, I think that’s it. Alcohol is seen as something people do to relax, to celebrate, to bond. Whereas smoking is often seen as a bad habit. But it’s not that different. It’s just a matter of how society views it. I mean, I can see the point of feminism. I think it’s important to challenge the status quo and give women the same opportunities as men. But I also think there’s a difference between common sense and intelligence. Like, some people can be highly intelligent but still make irrational decisions, like smoking or drinking too much. That’s the thing, isn’t it? You can be educated and have a good job, but if you don’t have common sense, you can still make bad choices.

So, do you ever just rage-quit on Twitter when someone gives you a bad review? Like, I saw this one yesterday about a restaurant in Margate, and it was just  so  harsh. Oh man, that’s the worst. I mean, sometimes you just want to phone them up and go, “You literally ordered the wrong thing?” Like, someone said our bakery’s bread was “damp” once, and I was like,  damp?  It was fresh out of the oven. They probably just didn’t like the texture. I mean, I’ve had bad customers too. One time, a guy came in and said he wanted a latte, but then he barely even looked at it. You can write a review in five minutes, but you can’t just go up to someone and say, “Hey, you know, you’re being a bit of a prat.”

Alright, Oisin, you've got to try the raspberries. They’re sweet and juicy, and they’re really good with ice cream. Yeah, I know, I've had them before. So, do you think we’re ready for weaning? I mean, the baby’s starting to show some interest in food, and I’m starting to feel like maybe it’s time. I think it’s probably time. I just love the way the hills roll out here. You can see everything from the top of that hill over there. Yeah, it’s like the whole countryside is laid out like a map. So, do you remember that film we watched last year? The one with the guy who gets stuck in a time loop? Oh yeah,  Groundhog Day ? I've been thinking about it again lately. So, do you think we've seen all the best spots in this part of the countryside yet? Not really. There's still a few places we haven't even considered. So, do you think it’s even possible to do that kind of thing without getting caught? I mean, like, laundering money through the banks? There are ways to manage without breaking the law. And besides, the fines can be huge. I’ve heard of people getting hit with hundreds of thousands of pounds for something like this. Wow, that’s serious. I guess it’s better to be honest and take the risk of not getting enough money than to try and do something illegal and end up with even more problems.

Well, I've been feeling rather under the weather these past few days. I've got this terrible cough that won't seem to go away, and I've been feeling pretty weak. That's a shame, old chap. You should have seen the doctor, you know. I had a bad cough last winter, and it turned out I had a chest infection. It was really unpleasant. I agree. A cough like that can be a sign of something more serious. I think you should get checked out, just to be safe. I've been meaning to go myself, but with all the work I have on, I haven't had the time. Yeah, I think that's wise. Being older, you know, it's better to be cautious. I had a bit of a cold last month, and it turned into bronchitis. It took me weeks to get over it. I suppose I should go. It’s just that I’ve been feeling a bit down about it. I mean, I’m not the sort of person to go to the doctor unless I’m really ill, but I can’t ignore this anymore. You’re not the only one. I’ve been feeling a bit sluggish lately too. I think it’s the weather. It’s been so damp and cold here in Norfolk. I can’t stand it. Yeah, the weather’s been terrible. I’ve been trying to keep the house warm, but it’s just not working. I've got this new electric heater, but it's not even worth the trouble. I had the same problem. I installed a new central heating system last year, but it's been giving me more trouble than it's worth. I think I’m going to have to get it fixed. I thought you were doing well with the heating. Didn't you say it was working quite nicely? It was at first, but now it's starting to play up again. I'm told it's the boiler. I don't know how long it will last. I'm really fed up with all these electrical things breaking down. I know what you mean. I had an old TV that just kept going off. I had to replace the entire thing. I was really upset about it, but I guess it was just time. It’s funny how these things happen, isn't it?

So, do you know if Lucy is going to be coming over for dinner tonight? I was supposed to text her, but I completely forgot. Oh, I think she said she would, but I’m not sure. She’s been pretty stressed with work lately. I wouldn’t be surprised if she’s decided to skip out again. Yeah, I think she mentioned something about needing to finish a big project before the weekend. But I mean, if she’s not coming, we can still have dinner. We’ve got enough people anyway. Yeah, but don’t forget about the wedding planning. We need to get that sorted. I still haven’t heard back from the venue about the dates. Oh, I know! The venue is so indecisive. I sent them an email two days ago, and I haven’t even heard a reply. I was hoping we could get the date set by the end of the month. I think they might be planning on moving the event, though. I heard they’re thinking of relocating to a different venue because of the weather forecast. Wait, I thought the original plan was to do it in early June. That’s still open, isn’t it? Yeah, but the weather is unpredictable at this time of year. I mean, we were all set for a summer wedding, and now it feels like it might be pushing into autumn. I’m already starting to get nervous about the whole thing. I get it. I mean, it’s a big decision, and we can’t just ignore the weather. But maybe we can talk to the venue and see if there’s a backup plan? Like, maybe a rainy day option? That sounds like a good idea. I could reach out to them and ask about that. I mean, it’s not like we’re entirely committed yet, right? We can still change our minds if needed. Yeah, but the more we keep putting it off, the more it feels like we’re waiting forever. I think we need to stop overthinking and just make a decision. I agree. But I do have a feeling that no matter what we decide, someone’s going to end up complaining about it. Either about the venue, the date or maybe even the food. Oh, that’s true. I’ve already heard about the last one from Mike.

Well, I've been meaning to ask you both, what do you think about this new tablet that came out? I got one for my grandad, but he keeps putting it in the microwave to charge it, and it’s gone all funny. Oh, you know what they say, if you want to make an egg, you don’t put it in the microwave. You just crack it and cook it. That’s what I always say. I tried explaining to him, but he thinks it’s a new way of charging. He’s been telling me he’s going to start using it for his garden. “It’s like a miniature computer for growing vegetables.” That’s not a bad idea. I’ve been thinking about starting a small vegetable patch in my back garden. It’s just that I’m not sure how to get started. I’ve got the seeds, but I don’t know about the soil or the timing. I’ve been trying to watch YouTube tutorials, but I’m not very good with technology. I keep getting distracted by the ads for smart gardening tools that tell you when to water your plants. Oh, I’ve seen those. I think they’re a bit over the top. I mean, I still use a stick to measure how deep the soil is. It’s got more sense than a machine that tells you to water your tomatoes every other day. You can’t trust the weather, can you? One day it’s sunny, the next it’s raining. True, but I think the kids are getting more into it. My granddaughter wants to grow her own food. She’s got a little plot at school, and she’s being taught how to plant things like carrots and potatoes. She even made a little sign for her patch. I think the teachers are trying to encourage them to be more self-sufficient. That’s a good point. I remember when I was a kid, we used to grow things in the garden with our grandparents. It was all manual, no screens or apps. But I think it’s a skill that’s been lost. I sort of miss the days when you had to know how to do things without a manual. You just figured it out by trial and error. Yeah, I remember that. Sometimes I think the younger generation go too quick.

So, how’s the weather been down in Essex? I heard it’s been a bit of a damp start to the year. Oh, it’s been alright, not too bad. A bit chilly, though. I’ve been complaining about the weather more than usual these days. You know how it is, when you’re retired, you start noticing the little things. I can imagine. I’ve been working from home a lot recently, too. It’s nice being able to set your own hours, but it can get a bit isolating. I never thought I’d be the type to work from home, but here we are. That’s the thing, isn’t it? You never think you’ll be in that situation. I used to think I’d be working till I was 70, but now I’m just trying to keep my mind active. I’ve started learning Portuguese. It’s a bit of a hobby, but I find it quite fascinating. Oh, that’s amazing! I didn’t know you were into languages. I teach Spanish, so I get a bit of a kick out of it. It’s funny, really. You think you’re going to be teaching, and then you end up learning something completely different. Yeah, I suppose that’s the cycle of life, isn’t it? I’ve always had a thing for languages. My father was a French teacher, so I grew up around it. I used to listen to him talk about grammar and all that. It’s a bit of a family tradition, really. That’s nice. I think it’s cool that you’re still keeping that part of your life alive. I’ve been trying to get back into reading more, but I’m the type who starts something and then gets distracted by something else. I need to be more disciplined. You know, I used to be like that too. I used to tell myself I’d read a book every week, but by the time I got to the third chapter, I’d be watching too much telly. Still, I think it’s important to keep learning. Even if it’s just for fun. Definitely. I think it’s part of what keeps you engaged with the world. I’ve been thinking about going on a trip somewhere, maybe to Spain or Italy. I’ve always wanted to go to Barcelona.

So, did you go out on Friday? I heard you were going out with someone. Yeah, I did! I met this guy at the cinema. We saw  Tenet  — I know it’s not the best film, but I thought it was cool. Oh,  Tenet ? I tried to watch it but I got so confused. I thought I was watching a sci-fi version of  Inception ! Haha, yeah, I felt the same! But the guy I went out with was super into it. He even made me explain what the word “inversion” meant. What? You’re joking. That’s like asking someone to explain  Quantum Mechanics ! No, he was serious. He said, “If I don’t understand this, I don’t understand the universe.” Wow, that’s deep. But honestly, I think he just wanted to be the smartest person in the room. Maybe. But he was nice. We went out for dinner after, and he paid for everything. Oh, nice! So, did you like him? I mean, he was pretty good-looking. And he’s into the same stuff I am — like, he knows  Breaking Bad  and  the Matrix . That’s a win. But don’t get too serious, you never know what someone’s like in real life. Yeah, I know. I’m just having fun with it. But hey, I thought it was a great way to spend Friday. I guess. I didn’t go out. I spent the whole night at the library. I’ve been trying to finish this essay for my history class. You’re so serious. You’re like the opposite of me. Yeah, I guess. But I do like to focus. I mean, I tried to go out with someone last week, but it didn’t go well. What happened? Well, I took him to a café near campus, and he kept talking about his dog. I mean, that’s not a bad thing, but I think he just wanted to talk about his dog all night. That’s not bad. It’s just… not really a conversation. Exactly. I mean, I don’t mind dogs, but I expected a bit more from a guy. True. But you know, I think it’s all about chemistry. Yeah, but where do you even find that? I don’t know. Maybe you just have to keep going out and see. I guess. But I’m not sure I want to go out again this weekend.

So, do you think the housing crisis is just a symptom of capitalism or is it something deeper? Honestly, I think it’s both. Capitalism drives the market, sure, but there's also systemic racism and classism that plays a huge role in who gets to afford a home and who doesn’t. Yeah, I mean, I think people forget that housing isn’t just a commodity. It’s a basic human need. Why is it so hard for people to get a place to live? Exactly. And when you look at the stats, it's not just about supply and demand—it's who is being excluded. I've read reports where people of color are more likely to be denied mortgages or face higher interest rates. It's not fair. I know, and it's not just in the UK either. I saw a documentary about the US where Black families are still dealing with redlining and the legacy of that. It’s a long-term issue. Yeah, it's so frustrating. And now with all the talk about inflation and interest rates, it's like the system is designed to make things harder for people who aren’t already in the privileged class. I feel that. I mean, I got a good job as an architect, but even I’m not immune to the pressure. Rent is going up, and I don’t know if I can afford to buy a place in London. I get it. I’m a freelancer, so my income can be a bit unstable, but even when I’m steady, the housing market is just too expensive. I’m in a shared flat with a colleague, but it’s not ideal. I can imagine. I’m currently living in a rented flat, and I feel like it’s not worth the price. I mean, we pay way more than what we should for the space. I know. And I think part of the problem is that land is treated as an asset, not as something people need to live on. It’s such a bizarre way to think about it. Yeah, it’s like the system is set up to make money off of people's basic needs. I sometimes think we need a complete reset on how we handle housing. I agree. But I’m not sure how we go about changing that.

So, do you know when the nursery starts? I’ve been trying to get a slot for the baby, but it’s all so competitive. Yeah, I know. I've been looking online and it's like booking a holiday in peak season. Every place is fully booked. But I was told that there’s a new nursery opening in the next town, just over the border. Maybe we could check that out. That’s a good idea. I’ve heard some good things about it, but I’m not sure how to go about applying. Do you think it’s worth the drive? It might be. I mean, the baby is only 6 months old now, so it’s not like they’ll be too overwhelmed. Plus, the staff there are said to be really patient and understanding. I hope so. I’m just worried about how it will affect our routine. I was planning to go back to work in a few months, and I don’t want the baby to get too used to me being around all the time. I mean, I know it’s normal, but I want to make sure they’re ready. You’re right. It’s a big step. Have you thought about when you’d like to go back? I know it’s a tough decision – on one hand, you want to be with the baby, but on the other, you need to get back to work and have some independence. I know. It’s just hard because I don’t want to leave them with someone else, but I also need to start earning again. I mean, I have a mortgage and all the other bills. I can’t just keep living off savings forever. I hear you. I’m the same. It’s just so hard to balance everything. But maybe once the baby starts nursery, it will feel more manageable. Maybe we can take a holiday after that. I’ve been thinking about going to Spain or somewhere warm. Just for a few weeks. That sounds nice. I’ve been meaning to go back to Spain. It’s been so long since I’ve had a proper break. But I guess we’ll have to wait until the baby is in full-time care. Yeah, maybe. I’ve also been thinking about the weaning process. I’m not sure if I’m ready for that yet.

So, did you get the statement sorted with the police, Tom? I heard you had to go through a lot of paperwork. Oh, it was a bit of a headache, to be honest. They wanted a full account of what happened, and I had to go through every detail again. It’s like they’re trying to make sure there’s no mistake, but honestly, I’m just glad it’s done. That’s the thing with the police, isn’t it? It’s all about being thorough. But I guess it’s better to be safe than sorry, right? Although I can’t imagine what it would be like if it was something serious. Yeah, I can see that. But honestly, I’m just glad I’m not in that situation. I mean, I had to give a statement too last week about the phone bill. That was a bit of a mess. Oh, really? What happened with that? Well, I got a phone bill from EE, and it was way higher than what I expected. I thought I was on a capped plan, but apparently, they had upped the rate without telling me. I had to call them and explain that I wasn’t aware of the change, and they ended up refunding some of it. It was a bit of a hassle, but at least it was sorted. That sounds frustrating. I’ve been through that with my credit card company once. They changed the terms without giving me a heads-up, and I had to fight them to get a refund. That’s not fair at all. It shouldn’t be so easy for companies to change things without your knowledge. I mean, I’ve been through this with my energy bill too. They just increase it without warning. Yeah, I know what you mean. I had to complain about my gas bill last month. It went up by 20%, and I had to write a formal complaint to them. It took weeks to get a response, and in the end, they just gave me a small discount. It was a bit of a disappointment. I’ve got a feeling that the week ahead is going to be busy. I’m going to a meeting with the team on Monday to discuss the new project. It’s about expanding our outreach, so I think it’s going to be interesting.

So, how’s the new life treating you, mate? You’ve been married now for a few months, right? Yeah, it’s been a few months, and honestly, it’s been a bit of a whirlwind. I mean, I didn’t think I’d be getting married so soon after moving to Bedford, but here we are. That’s great! You must be happy. I’ve been thinking about starting serious relationships myself, but I’m still in the “don’t get too attached” phase. You know, just enjoying the single life for now. You’re not too old for that. I mean, I was in the same boat just a few months ago. But now that I’m married, I’ve realized how much I missed out on. I was so focused on working, on the garden, on being a good gardener—like, I thought that was all I had to offer. Fair enough. You know, I’ve been teaching English for a while now, and I’ve picked up a few things. One of the things I’ve noticed is that people often underestimate what they can do if they put their mind to it. You might think you’re just a gardener, but if you’ve got the mindset, you can do a lot more. I suppose that’s true, but I still feel like I’ve got so much to learn. I mean, I’ve always been interested in history, especially Roman history. Do you know anything about that? I found an old book in the attic the other day, and it was about the Roman Empire and how they used things like mortar and pestles in their kitchens. Oh, that’s interesting. I did a bit of Roman history in my undergrad. They actually had quite an advanced culinary culture. They used herbs and spices that we still use today, like garlic, cumin, and coriander. And they baked bread in ovens that were pretty sophisticated for the time. That’s something I never thought about. I always thought of them as just a bunch of conquerors, but they were pretty innovative. I also always liked the show  Spartacus —it was such an intense series. Do you ever watch it? Yeah, I go back and forth. It’s got some great storytelling, but it can get a bit dramatic. I mean, I can’t deny that the characters are well-written.

So, do you know what’s happening with the English test tomorrow? I’m so nervous, like, I don’t even know where to start. Oh yeah, I know. I think we’re all panicking. I can’t even read the questions properly sometimes. What about the essay part? I’m not even sure what I’m supposed to write about. I know, right? I’ve been trying to practice but I just keep getting confused. The teacher said it’s going to be about “personal experiences,” but how do I even start? I mean, what’s a personal experience? Is it like, going to the park or something? No, no, no. It’s like, your opinion on something. Or maybe an event that’s happened to you. I think the teacher said something about it being a short essay, but I still don’t get it. Wait, I heard that the school orchestra is doing a concert next week. Do you think we’ll get to go? I mean, I’ve never been to one before, and I really want to see it. Yeah, I think it’s next Friday. I’ve heard the wind-band is playing some really cool pieces. I don’t know if we’ll get to go, though. I think the tickets are limited, and I’m not sure if they’re giving them out to everyone. Ugh, I hope so. I’ve always wanted to see the orchestra up close. I mean, music is my favorite subject. I even like the art lessons, but I’m not so good at drawing. I just can’t get the details right. Yeah, I know what you mean about art. I’m not bad at it, but the teacher keeps saying my colours are too dark. I think she’s just being harsh. I mean, it’s not like I’m the best, but I do try. I know, but I also have French lessons. I’m so bad at French. I can’t even say “bonjour” properly without messing up the accent. What if I fail the test? What if the teacher gives me a bad grade? Don’t worry, you’ll be fine. I mean, the English test is tomorrow, but I think we’re all stressed. I was just talking to my friend Emma, and she said she’s not even sure what the test is about.

So, how’s the new school? I heard you’re back in full-time education again, David? Yeah, it’s been a while since I’ve been in a classroom. I think I’m doing A Levels now. It’s pretty intense, but I’m enjoying it. You know, I’m thinking about going to uni after this. Oh, that’s great! You’ve always been a bright kid. I remember when you were in primary school, you used to ask me questions about everything—history, science, even the stars. You always had such a curious mind. Yeah, he was like that. Always climbing on things, asking why the sky was blue, why the sun went down… you know, the usual. But I think that curiosity is still there, just now it’s directed more towards books and exams. I suppose it is. I mean, it’s a bit stressful, though. I’m trying to balance work and study. I got a part-time job at the local library, helping out with the kids’ section. It’s not much, but it helps cover some of the costs. That’s a good move. You know, I was in the same position years ago—trying to juggle work and study. I left teaching to take care of the kids, but I didn’t stop learning. I did some evening courses and eventually got my postgrad. You never know where life will take you. True. I remember when you first started teaching, you were so passionate. You used to talk about the importance of education—how it could change a person’s life. It’s funny how things come full circle. Yeah, I still believe that. I mean, I know it’s not easy, especially with the cost of living and everything. But I’m trying to make the most of it. Maybe I’ll do something in education after all—maybe even get back into teaching. That could be a good path for you. You’ve got a natural talent for it. You always had a way of making even the dullest topics interesting. I always used to say you were the kind of teacher the world needs. I’ll say. You were like a walking encyclopedia. But go on, I think you’re supposed to be studying now. Let me know if you need any help with your exams. Thanks, Mrs. Harris.

So, do you think the government is doing anything about the obesity crisis? I mean, it’s everywhere now. I saw a news report about a local school having to install extra chairs because kids were so big. Yeah, I heard about that. It’s a real shame. But honestly, if they’re not doing anything, maybe we should be doing more at home. You know, eating better, exercising more. I don’t know, I think it’s easier said than done. I mean, I’ve tried to cut down on sugar and stuff, but when you get used to it, it’s like,  what even is life without a biscuit?  Exactly. It’s not just about willpower. There’s a genetic component too, you know. I read somewhere that some people are just more prone to weight gain than others. It’s in the genes. Yeah, I remember reading that too. But still, I think there’s a social aspect to it. Like, if you grow up in a family that eats a lot of junk food, you’re more likely to carry on that habit. It’s not just about what you choose to eat, it’s about what’s available. That’s true. I remember when I was a kid, we didn’t have all that processed stuff in the house. Now, it’s like the supermarkets are just selling more and more of it. It’s almost like they’re engineering people to be fat. Oh, I heard about that! Like, they use all these additives to make the food taste better and keep people eating more. It’s a bit scary, honestly. I think it’s a combination of everything. There’s the food industry, the environment we live in, our upbringing — and of course, genetics. But I think the government should do more to regulate the food industry. Maybe put stricter rules on advertising to kids, or make healthier options more accessible. I agree. And it’s not just about adults, either. I mean, kids today are already being diagnosed with diabetes and heart conditions at younger ages. It’s a real problem. That’s terrifying. I mean, I remember when I was a kid, we had to walk to school every day, played outside all the time — no screens, no junk food. Now, kids are glued to their phones, eating pizza for breakfast. It’s a world apart.

I just can’t get my head around Moodle. I mean, I’ve used it for years, but every time I update the system or add a new module, it’s like I need to start from scratch. Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s one of those things that’s so intuitive when you’re used to it, but if you try to change anything, it all falls apart. I remember last week when I tried to add a new quiz, and suddenly the whole course layout shifted, and I couldn’t find the assignment section anymore. That’s the worst. You spend hours setting something up, and then it’s like the system has a mind of its own. Exactly. I think the problem is that Moodle is so flexible, and that’s both a blessing and a curse. You can do so much with it, but if you don’t know exactly what you’re doing, it can be really confusing. I agree. I’ve been trying to figure out how to integrate some of the new learning analytics tools, but it’s like trying to solve a puzzle without the instructions. Oh, I feel that. Did you try the support forums? I’ve read through a few of them, but honestly, it’s like reading a different language sometimes. Yeah, I tried that too. Some of the answers are helpful, but most of the time, they're just people talking about the same issues, and it's not really giving me a clear path. It’s frustrating, isn’t it? I mean, we’re supposed to be experts in teaching, but when it comes to the tools we use, it feels like we’re just trying to survive. Totally. I think maybe we need to get some kind of training or workshop. I mean, it’s not like we’re the only ones struggling with Moodle. Yeah, I’ve been thinking the same thing. I’d love to see a dedicated session where we can go through some of the more common issues. Maybe even a group of lecturers from different departments could come together and share tips. That sounds like a good idea. We could even set up a regular check-in to see how things are going. Maybe even create a shared document or something where we can log our problems and solutions. I like that.

I can't believe how much jetlag I'm still feeling. I swear I was up at 3 a.m. last night and then I was up again at 6 a.m. this morning. It’s like my body’s still in New York. Yeah, I can totally relate. I was on a flight that landed at 2 a.m. and I was still up until 5 a.m. trying to get some sleep. I think my brain just refuses to switch off. Honestly, I haven’t even had a full night’s sleep in days. I keep getting these weird dreams where I’m back in the lecture hall, and I’m talking about something I haven’t even prepared for. That sounds like my nightmare. I keep dreaming about grading essays, even though I’m not even teaching anymore. I think our brains are just trying to make up for the lack of sleep. I know, it’s so strange. And don’t even get me started on the babies. We’ve been trying so hard to get one, and it’s like the universe is actively trying to keep us from having any. I’m starting to think we’ve made a pact with the universe to stay childless. I’m not sure if it’s the universe or just the fact that we’re both incredibly stubborn. I mean, if we were more open to the idea of adoption, maybe things would be different. But no, we’re both too focused on the idea of having a baby in our own body. Exactly. I mean, I’m not saying it’s not possible, but I feel like we’re just not ready. We’ve been so busy with work, and I’m not even sure we’ve really had the time to talk about it properly. Yeah, and then there’s the whole issue of timing. We’re both in our late thirties now, and I can feel it. I’m not sure how much time we have left. I think we should maybe start looking into some options. I know, and I agree. But I also don’t want to rush into anything. I mean, I do love the idea of having a child, but I want to make sure it’s something we both really want. That makes sense. I think we should go to that local drama performance this weekend, just to take our minds off things.

So, do you still keep in touch with people from back in Iraq? I know you’ve been living in the UK for a while now, but I imagine you’ve got a lot of friends and family over there. Yeah, I do, but it’s not easy. The political situation there has been pretty unstable, especially after the war. It’s hard to know who you can trust anymore. Some of my old friends have moved to Europe or the US, and I’ve lost touch with a lot of people who stayed behind. It’s like the country’s been torn apart. That’s sad to hear. I’ve been reading a bit about the Middle East, and the oil politics there have been a real mess. My lectures on post-colonial studies always touch on how oil has shaped so much of the region’s history, for better or worse. It has, definitely. And it’s not just about oil—there’s this whole other layer of religion and ideology. People like the Wahhabi movement have had a huge influence, especially in places like Saudi Arabia. I’ve seen how that’s affected the way people think and live, even in areas that don’t seem as directly connected to it. I’ve read a bit about that too. It’s interesting how religion can be both a unifying and a dividing force. I mean, take Libya—Muammar Gaddafi was a leader who did a lot for the country in terms of infrastructure and education, but his regime was also very authoritarian. Now, with the country in chaos, it’s a real struggle for people to find stability. Exactly. And the younger generation is really affected by all this. A lot of them have grown up in a world where there’s been so much conflict and uncertainty. Some of them are looking for new opportunities, even if it means moving to another country. I know a few people in my community who are planning to move to the UK or Europe for work. That makes sense. I’ve been thinking about my own experience with moving around. I was born in Germany, but I grew up in Liverpool. It’s funny how different places shape your identity. I think it’s the same for a lot of young people who move between countries now. Yeah, it’s a really complex time for a lot of people.

I just love this roast lamb. It’s so tender, and the gravy is just perfect. I think it’s the best I’ve had in ages. I know, don’t you? It’s like it’s been marinated for weeks, not just hours. I mean, the way it’s cooked, it just melts in your mouth. It’s like a little luxury. Oh, I’ve always said that Scottish lamb is the best. I mean, it’s got that smoky, earthy flavor. You can’t get that kind of taste from anywhere else, really. Yeah, but I’ve heard you can get some amazing lamb in the Highlands, too. I’ve never managed to get the chance to try it, though. I think I’d have to go on a proper trip. You should. I’ve been thinking about going on a cruise for a while. Maybe a trip to the Scottish islands? It’s not just for the scenery, though. I think it would be good for the mind. You know, getting away from the daily grind. A cruise? That sounds like a great idea. I’ve been meaning to do something like that. I’ve been feeling a bit stuck in my routine lately. But I’m not sure if I’d be able to afford it. Well, it’s not just about the money, you know. It’s about taking the time for yourself. And if you don’t have the money, then you just have to be resourceful. I’ve been working on a few side projects, and I think I’m getting closer to something that could fund a trip. That’s impressive. You’ve always been a bit of a risk-taker, you know. I still remember when you decided to take over that old school. It was a bit of a gamble, but it paid off in the end. Oh, I wouldn’t say it was a gamble. I just had a vision and I went for it. It was a bit scary at first, but when the first students came in, it all just clicked. I think I’ve always been able to see the potential in things. And it shows. You’ve got a real head for business, even if you go about it in your own way. I mean, you don’t always follow the rules, but that’s what makes you special.

So, do you think we should get a fridge? I mean, we’ve been eating out so much lately. It’s getting a bit expensive. Yeah, I mean, we’ve got a freezer, but it’s not exactly the same as a fridge. Plus, with uni starting soon, we might need to start cooking more. I agree. I’ve been thinking about it too. I mean, I’m not sure if I’ll be staying here for much longer. I’ve got some applications out, and I might be moving to Germany for a while. But if I do, I don’t want to leave without a fridge. That’s fair. I’ve been thinking about it too. It’s kind of strange not having one. I mean, we’ve got a microwave, but I still feel like we’re missing something. Plus, I’ve got a job now as a teaching assistant, so I need to start managing my money better. Maybe a fridge would help with that. Yeah, you’re not the only one. I’ve been saving up, but I’m not sure if I can afford it. My dad said I should get one, but he’s not exactly the most helpful when it comes to financial advice. He just says, “you’ll get used to it.” I know what you mean. My mum keeps telling me to “get a proper set of utensils” and “start cooking for yourself.” But honestly, I’m not sure what she thinks I’m currently eating. I mean, I’ve been surviving on cereal and toast. I had the same problem when I was living in Germany. I had to buy everything from scratch, and it was a bit of a culture shock. I used to cook so much back home, but here… it’s all about convenience. I think I’m starting to understand that. I mean, I’ve got a few recipes I’ve been trying to remember, but I’m not exactly a cook. Last week, I tried to make a stir-fry, and it ended up being more like a soup. My flatmates laughed, but they were trying not to be too mean. That sounds like me. I once tried to make a lasagna and ended up burning the whole thing. I think it was more of a fire hazard than a meal. Still, I’m trying to be more responsible with my budget.

Alright, so I’ve got this baking lesson planned for tomorrow, and I need to make sure I’ve got everything ready. I’m thinking of making something simple but tasty—maybe some cupcakes or cookies. What do you think? Cupcakes sound good! But you know, I saw a recipe online for these chocolate chip ones with a twist—like they add a little bit of chili powder to give it a kick. It’s actually pretty popular now. Chili powder? That sounds weird. I wouldn’t want to eat something that burns my tongue. Maybe you could just do the regular ones. I like chocolate chips, but I don’t like surprises. Yeah, I guess that’s a fair point. My mum’s class is going to be a mix of kids and parents, so I need to make sure it’s not too adventurous. Also, I need to check if there’s a specific ingredient list they want, just in case. Oh, right! The teacher’s said they want to include a bit of history about baking in the lesson. I think she wants to talk about how baking has changed over time and how it’s part of culture. Maybe we can do a quick activity with the kids where they guess what ingredient was used in the past. That sounds fun. I remember my nan talking about how they used to make bread with just flour, water, and some kind of salt that they harvested from the beach. It was super simple, but it made the bread taste better somehow. That’s interesting. I wonder if we could incorporate that into the lesson—maybe talk about how ingredients have changed and how baking has become more precise with measurements now. Exactly! I think that could be a nice way to tie in the history part. Also, I heard that the kids are having a half birthday celebration this week. Should we do something special for that too? Maybe! If it’s a half birthday, perhaps we could have a small cake or a treat. I think it would be a good way to make the kids feel celebrated. But I’d need to check with the teacher first to make sure it’s okay. That’s a good idea. I think the kids would love it. Oh, and I was thinking of getting a book from Morrisons today.

So, do you still drive that old Honda? Ugh, yes, it’s like a relic. I told myself I’d sell it after the last trip to Cambridge, but I just haven’t got around to it. Honestly, I wouldn’t trust it to get me across a puddle without breaking down. Oh, I know, but it’s reliable enough. I mean, it’s got more miles on it than most people have on their lives. You’re not even joking. I tried to get my mum to sell hers last year, and she said, “It’s got character!” I said, “It’s got rust, and it’s got a dead battery.” Yeah, but you know what I think? I think the real issue is not the car, it’s the way we use the internet. I mean, we’re all so used to getting everything delivered, like a car in a week. Exactly! And now, if you want a new car, you can just order it over Facebook, and it’ll be delivered in three days. I mean, even the dealership is like, “We’ll get it for you.” But then it turns out it’s not what you thought – it’s a different model, or it’s been modified, or something. And then you’re stuck with that. It’s like the internet! You click on something, you think you’re getting one thing, but you end up with a different version. I mean, I tried to order a new pair of shoes the other day and ended up with a pair that looked like it came out of a 1990s ad. Oh, I’ve seen that. It’s like you are getting the product, but not the experience. Facebook, Instagram, all of them – they show you the perfect version of something. But when you get it, it’s not the same. Exactly. I mean, I remember when I first started using Facebook, I thought it was just a way to keep in touch. Now I feel like it’s the only way people communicate. Even my lectures are getting more likes and shares than actual engagement. It’s funny, isn’t it? We’re all connected, but we’re more disconnected than ever. You know, sometimes I think we’d rather talk to a machine than to a person. Yeah, and that’s even more true with cars.

I just want to say, I’ve had a right mess of a day today. You know, work was like a shitstorm. Oh no, what happened? It’s just, I was trying to process some returns, and the system was down. So I ended up spending three hours just waiting for it to load. It was ridiculous. I reckon I could’ve gone out for a coffee and come back in half the time. That’s not great. I can imagine how frustrating that must have been. Yeah, and when it finally did load, it just crashed again. I had to call the help desk. I swear, the people there were more confused than me. Maybe they’ve just got too much on their hands. I hear the shop’s been struggling with the customer service lately. I know, it’s a mess. I guess I just need to take a step back and not get so stressed over it. I’m not getting anywhere. You should try to take a break. Maybe that’ll help you reset. I know, I know. But with all the work to do, it’s hard to switch off. You know, I’ve been thinking about the film we’re watching –  Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs . It’s been on all day, and I don’t know if I’ve ever seen it before. It’s a bit strange, isn’t it? Yeah, it’s got that weird charm. It’s like a kids’ movie, but it’s also got these weird messages in it. I mean, the idea that giant food is coming is absurd, but then there’s this whole subplot about a girl trying to save the planet. It’s a bit of a mix. I think the film is trying to be both funny and serious, but it doesn’t quite land. It’s like it’s trying to be too many things at once. Exactly. I don’t know if it’s just me, but the deeper themes seem to be lost in all the slapstick. Maybe it’s just the target audience – kids. The messages are probably more subtle than they need to be for the intended viewers. I guess. Still, it’s a weird film. I don’t know if I’d call it a classic, but it’s got some weird charm. Yeah, and the way they explained the plot with the cartoon characters is so simple.

So, do you watch much football, mate? I do, yeah. I grew up in Liverpool, so it's in my blood. I support the Reds, of course. Right, Liverpool. I’ve read a bit about your city—very culturally rich, but also a bit divided. Yeah, it has its ups and downs. But football? That’s what brings people together. I suppose so. I used to live in Manchester, so I can relate. The rivalry between the cities is intense. Absolutely. I’ve driven through Manchester a few times—always a bit tense when the Red Devils are playing. I know what you mean. But football isn’t just about the teams, is it? It’s about the culture and the community. Definitely. You’ve got to admit, when the lights are on and the crowd’s behind you, it’s a different world. I remember when Tony Blair was in power. He was all about unity, wasn’t he? Yeah, I remember that. He said he was the “new Labour,” but let’s be honest, it didn’t always work. Politics is tricky, isn’t it? You try to bring people together, but it’s hard to ignore deep-seated differences. Definitely. I think the government’s been struggling with that ever since. They keep talking about unity, but the divisions are still there. I guess it’s the same with football. Even though we all love the game, the clubs and the fans are still divided. Exactly. And then there’s the politics of it all—how the government supports the clubs, how it affects the economy. Right. I’ve heard debates about whether the government should give more money to football clubs to keep them competitive. It’s a tough call. If they give money, you risk creating more inequality. If they don’t, the clubs might struggle. It’s a classic dilemma. I’ve read some articles about it, but I’m not sure there’s a perfect solution. I think it’s more about how the money is distributed and who benefits. Some clubs are doing well, others aren’t. Exactly. And with the rise of streaming and global audiences, the game has changed a lot since I was a kid. Oh, for sure. Back then, it was all about local fans and local matches. Now, it’s global. It’s fascinating, really. I think football will always be a unifying force, even if the politics and economics make it complicated.

So, do you ever think about how much social media affects how we talk? I mean, I’ve been thinking a lot about the BNC recordings lately, like how people use abbreviations and slang now compared to, say, 20 years ago. It’s kind of interesting. Yeah, it’s kind of like a language evolution. I mean, I feel like people use so many abbreviations on LinkedIn and Twitter now. I think I’ve even seen people use “u” instead of “you” or “ur” instead of “your.” It’s like the whole internet is changing the way we communicate. Totally. I mean, I still use LinkedIn sometimes for professional stuff, but honestly, it’s like the same as any other social media. You just post updates, and people comment. It’s kind of a microcosm of how people behave in real life, just in a more condensed format. I think that’s true. I’ve noticed in my own experience, even when I’m scrolling through Instagram or Twitter, the way people phrase things is so much more casual. I mean, if I had to write a LinkedIn post about my job, I’d probably end up paraphrasing the whole thing in a way that sounds like a tweet. Exactly. And I think that’s part of it too, the fear of being judged. Like, if you write too formally, people don’t get you. You have to be conversational, you know? It’s like they’re trying to make themselves more relatable. That’s probably why so many people are scared of flying. Like, it’s a major life event, and they feel like they have to document it online. I mean, I remember seeing someone post about their Maldives trip, and then they had comments from other people who said, “Wow, that’s amazing,” and it felt like they were being judged. I’ve been thinking about that too. I actually went to Spain last summer, and I told my friends I was going to take some photos, but when I got there, I didn’t even take any. I just didn’t want to take photos of myself and then post them. It’s like, why even bother? I mean, I’m not even the type of person who cares about their appearance that much. I think it’s just the whole culture of being online. People feel like they have to share everything, even if it doesn’t make sense.

So, do you think we should get the Christmas tree up this week or wait until after the 24th? I’m trying to decide whether to start decorations or not. I think we should wait until after the 24th, honestly. It’s easier to keep the tree up for longer if you do it later. Plus, I’ve got a few things to sort out at work before then. You know, the Christmas rush tends to catch up with me. Yeah, I get that. But I’ve been thinking about the new intern who’s coming in next month. She’s got a tattoo, right? I couldn’t help but notice it when we met last week. Oh yeah, she does. It’s a small one on her arm—some kind of symbol, I think. She didn’t say much about it, but I got the feeling it was a personal thing. You know, not something she’s too keen to talk about. I guess that’s fair enough. I mean, I have a tattoo too. It’s on my forearm, a simple one, just a quote from a book I really liked. It’s not like it’s hiding anything. It’s just part of me. That’s good. I think tattoos are becoming more accepted, especially with people in our generation. I mean, I had a few back in my twenties, but I got them done when I was younger and more impulsive. Now I’m more cautious. Yeah, I remember when tattoos were seen as a bit of a rebellious thing. Now it’s almost like a fashion statement. I guess it’s changed a lot over the years. Definitely. I suppose it’s a reflection of the times. People today are more open to self-expression. Maybe that’s part of the reason why so many people have them now. I think so. But I still feel a bit nervous about getting one. I mean, I don’t want to regret it later. I want something I’ll be proud of when I’m older. That’s smart of you. I always say take your time. Don’t rush into anything. And if you do get one, make sure it’s something that means something to you personally. That way, you’ll be more likely to keep it forever. That’s a good point. I’ve been thinking about getting one for a while, but I just haven’t found the right design yet.

So, do you ever find it hard to balance work and looking after yourself? I mean, I’ve been thinking about it lately. I teach languages, and I’m pretty busy, but I also try to keep up with my fitness. Do you do any exercise classes or anything like that? Honestly, I wish I did. I used to go to yoga classes when I was in London, but with the job I’ve got now, it’s just so hard to find time. And honestly, I don’t know if I’ve got the energy. I mean, when you're a journalist or an editor, your brain is like on overdrive all the time—especially when you're working on a tight deadline. You can’t really switch off, can you? Yeah, I can see that. I’ve been trying to get into a routine, but it’s tricky. I did start going to a Pilates class last month, and it actually helps me feel better, both physically and mentally. It’s like a way to reset, you know? I bring my dog along sometimes, and it’s nice to have some time to myself without thinking about work. Oh, a dog? I’ve always wanted one, but I think I’m too busy. I mean, I’m not even sure if I’m ready for that kind of responsibility. I’ve got a cat, but she’s more of a couch potato. I don’t know if I’d be able to handle a dog’s energy. Although, I suppose if someone else could take care of it while I’m working, maybe? That’s a good point. I think it’s all about being realistic. If you don’t have time, there’s no point in forcing yourself. But I think you can still do little things, like going for a walk or doing some light exercise. I find that even a short walk helps me clear my head and feel better. I agree. I do like to cook, though. I think cooking is one of the few things that can really ground me. I’ve been trying to make more meals at home lately, and I’ve even started experimenting with some new recipes. I’ve been thinking about trying to make some healthy meals, like stir-fries or soups. Oh, I love soups! Especially if you add some fresh herbs and veggies.

So, did you get the email from Sarah about the meeting tomorrow? I was just thinking about it on the walk here. Yeah, I saw it. I think she mentioned it in the group chat too. She said it's going to be important for our research collaboration. Right, I remember she was really excited about it. I hope it goes well. I’m still trying to get my head around the new module I’m teaching this semester. It’s so different from what I was doing before. I can imagine. I’ve been working on my own module too. It’s a bit of a juggle, honestly. I keep thinking about how to make the content more engaging for the students. My lectures are going okay, but I feel like I’m not quite hitting the right notes yet. I’ve been there. I remember when I first started teaching, I was so nervous I could barely speak. But now I’ve got a bit more confidence. Still, there’s always room to improve, right? Definitely. I think we’re both in the same boat, though. Speaking of which, have you seen the new lecture room? It’s got this amazing projector and everything. I’ve been using it for my seminars, and it’s actually pretty cool. Oh, I saw it last week. It’s a bit of a step up from the old one. I wish all the rooms were like that. I’ve heard that the university is trying to modernize the teaching spaces, but it’s taking forever. I know. I think it’s all about funding. Or maybe they’re being held back by some bureaucracy. Either way, it’s frustrating when you’re excited about something and it’s just not happening. Yeah, I get that. Speaking of bureaucracy, I had to fill out this massive form just to get my pay raise approved. It was ridiculous. I mean, I passed all my reviews, and I’ve been here for over a year. Why can’t they just make it easier? I know, right? It’s like they don’t see us as real people. I think it’s just the way things are. You know how it is. I do. But still, it’s annoying. Anyway, enough about work. How’s your toe nail? I saw you had a bit of a mess last week.

So, did you watch that new film with the guy from  Doctor Who ? I think it was called  The Time Traveler’s Wife  or something like that? No, I didn’t get to see it. I’ve been so busy with work meetings and all. But I heard it’s pretty good. I liked the idea of time travel, but I think it got a bit… messy with the plot. A lot of people said the ending was just confusing. Yeah, I heard that too. But I still thought the acting was pretty solid. Although, I’m not sure how they managed to make that guy from  Doctor Who  look so different. I mean, he’s got that same kind of look, but it’s like he’s playing a completely different person. Maybe it’s the hair? Ha! That’s the thing. I think everyone was confused at first. But honestly, I think the director tried to do something different with the time travel concept. I remember reading an article that said they were trying to bring in some conspiracy elements, like the idea that time travel could be used for political manipulation or something. It got a bit too sci-fi for me, to be honest. Yeah, I can imagine. I mean, I do like the way they handled the – uh –  publicity  around it. They had all these huge billboards and promo videos. I saw one where the guy’s face was all glitchy and the text said, “Time is just someone else’s problem.” It was weird. I felt like they were trying to push a conspiracy theory about time travel and the government or something. That’s what I heard too. Some people think it was just marketing, though. I mean, the guy who played the main character is a pretty big name. He’s got that sort of ‘celebrity’ status, so I guess the film was going for that kind of buzz. But I still think it was a bit over the top. I’d rather have seen something more grounded. I can see that. I’m not sure if I’ll ever watch it, to be honest. I’m more into the quieter films. I mean, I just saw  The Crown  again. It was so good. I can go back and forth between that and  Killing Eve  depending on my mood.  Killing Eve  is great, but I can’t stand the latest  Doctor Who  series.

Dad, do you remember the book  Jamaica Inn ? I read it for English class and it was so spooky. I thought it was about a haunted house and all that. Oh yeah, I remember that one. It’s one of those old mystery books, isn’t it? I think it’s by a guy named Ralph Fiennes, or was it someone else? Either way, it’s a classic. A lot of people think it’s based on a real place, but I’m not sure. I think it’s based on a real inn in Cornwall, though. I mean, we’re going there now. I wonder if it’s haunted. That’s what I thought too when I read it. You know, I remember reading  The Wizard of Oz  when I was a kid. It was one of those books that made me want to go on an adventure. Do you remember when we used to read those stories together when you were little? Yeah, I remember that! You even showed me the original book with all the pictures. It was so cool. That’s right. And I remember you loved  Sherlock Holmes  too. It was funny how you tried to solve the mysteries in the book. You’d write down clues and everything. You were such a detective back then. I was! And I still like reading books. I just finished  Alice in Wonderland  again. It’s so weird and fun, even though it’s a bit confusing. That’s because it’s a classic. Lewis Carroll was a bit of a mad genius. I think he wrote it while he was at university, which is why it’s so full of wordplay and nonsense. Oh, I get that now. It’s like a fairy tale but with more rules. I wonder if it’s based on real things or just made up. It’s a bit of both, honestly. Some of the stories were inspired by real places he lived, and others were just his imagination. You know, I remember reading about how he used to send telegrams to his friends using Morse code. He was into that sort of thing. That’s cool. I’ve heard of Morse code before. Is it like a secret language? Yeah, kind of. It was used a lot in the old days, especially with the telegraph. People used it to send messages quickly over long distances.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to play that game where you had to guess which teacher had a secret crush on someone? Oh, I remember that! It was a disaster. I think it was Mr. Battersby, the math teacher. He used to get all flustered when Mrs. Thompson walked by. But no one ever caught him. You’re exaggerating, Dad. I mean, I don’t think anyone actually  cheated  at games back then. It was just playful. Oh, it was  very  playful. I remember one time, we made a bet that if someone could beat Mr. Jenkins at chess, they could have a free ice cream. I lost, and I still owe him one. That sounds like a sad story. But seriously, how did you all manage to afford ice cream back then? I mean, I know rents are still a bit tight, but back in the 60s, you didn’t have to worry about that. Oh, we had to. We used to save up for special occasions. But honestly, I think the best thing about those days was the freedom. No phones, no social media – just playing games and running around. Yeah, I guess there was something pure about it. But I can’t say I miss those days. I mean, I was the one who had to sit through the homework and all that. You were the lucky one, then. You didn’t have to worry about cheating at games or getting caught in the act. That’s true. But there was one time I did get caught. I was trying to beat the school’s old computer in a game of chess, and I accidentally left the data on the screen. The teacher saw it and thought I was trying to hack the system. Wow, that’s a story. I mean, it’s a bit dramatic, but it does sound like something you’d do back then. It sounds like it. And I bet you were in for a lecture. Oh, I was. But in the end, it was just a misunderstanding. The guy was really nice. He even gave me a free game of chess after that. That’s the kind of thing that makes the old days worth remembering. It’s not all about the rules and the roles. It’s also about the people and the stories. Exactly. And I bet the food was better too.

Mum, do you remember when we were kids and you used to make that weird fish stew? I think it was called weaver fish or something like that. Oh, I remember! It was a Sunday thing, wasn’t it? We’d go to the market and pick up the biggest fish we could find, and then you’d have to sit there and wait while I tried to figure out how to cook it. Yeah, and every time I’d say, “Mum, what are you doing with that?” and you’d just say, “Wait, it’s almost ready!” And then you’d burn the kitchen down. Well, it wasn’t  that  bad. It was just that the fish had a bit of a strong taste. I think you just needed to get used to it. I think I still have a piece of that recipe in the old notebook. Wait, do you remember if I ever got sick after eating it? Oh, you were  so  sick. I had to take you to the hospital once. You were throwing up for hours and had a fever. I thought I’d lost you. That’s the one. I still remember the nurse saying, “You’re going to be fine, just take it easy,” and then I looked at you and you were crying because you thought I was going to die. Oh, you were a handful, weren’t you? Still are, in a way. You just don’t act like it. But I know you, son. You always knew me, didn’t you? Anyway, I’ve been thinking about moving out again. I’ve got a flat in London now, but I’m not sure if I should stay there or come back. Why not stay here? You know I’d love to have you back. You’re the only one who can put up with my cooking. Well, I have my own kitchen now, and it’s all set up. I just need to pack up my stuff. We were talking about moving house items earlier. Do you think you could help me figure out what to bring? Absolutely. You know, I’ve got this list of things I think you should bring. I even wrote it down in my head. Let me think. Okay, what’s on the list? Well, obviously you’ll need your bed, your sofa, and your TV.

I can't believe the NHS is still struggling like this. It's been ages since I last had an appointment, and when I did, it was like a marathon. Yeah, I know. It's frustrating. I mean, I've got a cousin who's been waiting for a hip replacement for over a year now. I don't think they even have the capacity to handle the backlog. I know, but I think the government’s got to be doing something. It's just not happening fast enough. I agree. But when are they going to fix the system? I mean, it's not just the NHS. I've been reading about the A-Level reforms, and they're making things even more confusing for students. Yeah, I heard about that. I think they're trying to make it more rigorous, but honestly, it feels like they’re just making it harder for everyone. I mean, why not just keep the exams the way they are? Exactly. I think the whole idea of reducing the number of A-Level subjects is just leading to more stress and less creativity. I mean, what about the students who want to explore different areas before deciding on a career? True. I was always told to pick three A-Levels, but I wanted to do more. It felt like I was being forced into a narrow path. I know what you mean. And don’t even get me started on the petrol crisis. Prices are through the roof. I just tried to fill up my car, and it cost me almost £50. I know, it’s ridiculous. I mean, we’re about to go through another winter, and the cost of heating is already going up. How are people supposed to afford it? It’s not just the petrol prices either. My sister had to put her car up for sale last month because she couldn’t afford the fuel. She’s got a job, but it’s not enough to cover everything. That’s so sad. I mean, how are we meant to live like this? It feels like the cost of living is going up every day, and there’s no sign of it slowing down. It’s exhausting. I guess we just have to keep pushing through. Yeah, but I can’t help but feel like we’re all just waiting for something to change.

So, do you think we should still be smoking in the garden? I mean, it's not like we’re doing it in front of anyone, but I’m just not sure if it's the best idea anymore. Honestly, I don’t know. I mean, I like the idea of being able to chill and relax without worrying about the rules, but I feel like it’s not as harmless as it used to be. I’ve heard so many stories about how even secondhand smoke can affect people. Yeah, I get that. But for us, it’s just a way to unwind after a stressful week of university. I mean, we’re all students, we’re not even getting paid. It’s like a small rebellion, you know? I can see that. But I’ve been thinking about feminism and how we’re supposed to be leading the way in health and wellness. If we’re smoking, does that mean we’re not really living up to the standards we preach? Wait, are you saying we should stop because of feminism? That feels a bit like hypocrisy, don’t you think? I mean, we’re not even in a position where we can afford to be perfect. I’m not saying we should stop. I’m just saying we should be more aware of the choices we make. I mean, we’re all in our early twenties, and we’re trying to find our place in the world. It’s okay to make mistakes, but we should also be conscious of the impact we have on others. Yeah, but we’re not the only ones who smoke. I mean, if we’re being honest, most of our friends do it too. It’s not about being perfect, it’s about being realistic. I guess that’s true. But I also think it’s important to make informed decisions. I’ve been reading about how the black plague had a huge impact on society, and how people had to adapt. Maybe we should be doing the same with our habits. That’s an interesting angle. I mean, the black plague was over 700 years ago, so it’s not exactly the same, but the idea of adaptation is there. Still, I’m not sure if stopping smoking is the way to go. I think it’s about balance. I agree.

So, do you ever find it hard to say goodbye to people you’ve known for years, even if you don’t really want to be in touch anymore? I mean, I’ve been thinking about it a lot lately. Yeah, honestly, I do. It’s weird because you start to feel like you’re kind of  stuck  with them, even if you don’t want to be. Like, you’ve got all these memories and stuff, and you don’t want to erase them, but you also don’t want to be in their lives anymore. Exactly. I mean, I don’t like to ghost people, you know? I think it’s rude. But at the same time, I’m not sure how to just… fade out. It’s like, you don’t want to be the one who ghosts, but you also don’t want to be the one who’s always there when you’re not really into it anymore. I get that. I think the hardest part is not being direct, you know? You don’t want to hurt their feelings, but you also don’t want to keep being in their lives just because you feel guilty. Like, I’ve had this friend who sent me a message last week asking if I wanted to catch up, and I just felt so awkward. I didn’t know what to say. That’s exactly what I’ve been thinking. It’s like, how do you even start the conversation? You don’t want to say, “Hey, I don’t really want to be friends anymore,” but you also don’t want to keep pretending you’re still interested. It’s a mess. I know. I think maybe the best way is to just let things fade naturally. Like, not respond to messages, not show up to events, and just… not be there. But then again, I don’t want to be the one who just disappears. It feels so unfair. I think it’s just about boundaries. You can’t be responsible for everyone’s feelings. You have to do what’s right for you. If you’re not into them anymore, you have to make that choice. It’s not easy, but it’s also necessary. Otherwise, you’re just stuck in this uncomfortable limbo. Yeah, I guess you’re right. I just feel like I’m not doing it the “right” way.

So, how’s the new exhibition coming along? I heard you were working on something for the gallery in London. Oh, it’s going well, thank you! I finally got the funding for the exhibition, and I’m quite excited about the pieces I’ve chosen. It’s a mix of my old work and some new sculptures I’ve been experimenting with lately. I think it might be something people will really connect with. That sounds amazing! I’d love to see it. You know, I’ve been thinking a lot about art lately. I’m currently working on a project for my history of art course, and I’ve been reading a lot about how different movements influence each other, especially between Europe and the Americas. Oh, that’s fascinating. I remember when I was studying art in Vienna, I was really drawn to the way modernist movements were influenced by Eastern European traditions. It’s quite different from the more traditional British art I grew up with. Yeah, I think that’s one of the things that’s so interesting about studying art. It’s not just about the techniques, but also the cultural and historical contexts. I mean, did you ever think about how your Austrian background shaped your art? Oh, absolutely. I think it’s hard not to. I was born in Vienna, but I grew up in Italy because my parents were working in the film industry there. That experience exposed me to different artistic influences, and I think it’s why I’m so passionate about blending styles. I always felt like I was between two worlds, and that’s something I try to capture in my work. That’s really cool. I can imagine how that must have influenced you. I’ve been thinking about travel a lot too. I’m planning to take a trip to Spain this summer, and I want to visit some of the historic art museums there. Maybe even Barcelona to see Gaudí’s work. I’ve always wanted to see the Sagrada Família in person. That sounds like an incredible trip! I remember visiting Barcelona once when I was younger, and I was completely enchanted by the architecture. It’s one of those places where the past and the present feel like they’re in perfect harmony. I can’t wait to see it. I’ve also been thinking about my family back in London.

I can't believe we've been on the road for three days already. I thought it would take less time. I feel like I've been driving forever. I know, I feel the same. It's like time just stretches out when you're driving. It's weird how the hours add up so quickly, isn't it? Yeah, and if you're not actually doing anything, like you're just driving, then time just... fades. I remember when I used to go to the gym, it felt like time flew by. But now, when I'm driving, it's like the hours are frozen. I guess that’s because when you're working out, you’re focused and you're moving, but when you're just driving, you’re in this kind of limbo state. You're not really doing anything, but you’re also not really resting either. Exactly. I've been trying to keep myself occupied. I’ve been eating before the gym, you know, to keep my energy up. But now, I feel like I'm eating just to stay alive. I can relate. Sometimes I feel like I just eat as a coping mechanism. It’s like when you're feeling down or stressed, you just reach for a snack. It’s so English of me, isn’t it? Oh, don’t start. You're not the only one. We’re all just trying to survive. And honestly, I think we’re all kind of just trying to survive in this country. I mean, it's not just about the driving or the gym—it's the whole system. It’s like the politicians don’t care about us. You know, I’ve been thinking about gender issues a lot lately. I mean, I'm a woman in a male-dominated profession, and I feel like I have to work twice as hard to be taken seriously. It’s exhausting. I can’t even imagine. I mean, I used to work in a male-dominated field too. I always felt like I had to prove myself. It’s such a shame. I mean, we’re all so qualified, but we’re not given the same opportunities. Yeah, and it’s not just in the workplace. It's everywhere. Even when I'm out with friends or on a road trip, I feel like I have to be the one to speak up, or else people might not take me seriously.

So, do you remember that time we had that power cut last winter? I was in the middle of making a cup of tea and then— poof —everything went dark. I was so confused, I thought I’d hit the switch or something. Oh yes, I remember that. You were standing there in the kitchen with the kettle still on, and you looked like you'd been hit by a train. I had to go and check if you were alright, I swear. I know, I know. It was ridiculous. But at least we had the candles. I love candles. They add such a nice ambience. Especially when it's cold and dark out, like it is now. Oh, I know, it’s been so cold this week. I had to put the bin out earlier this morning, and it was like handling ice. I was thinking, “Is this really winter, or have we just moved to Antarctica?” It’s not even the end of March, and we’re already in a thick fog. I swear, the only thing I can see is the garden, and even that’s half-hidden by the spider webs. Did you know I found a new species of spider in the shed last week? No, really? What kind was it? I don’t know, honestly. It was this big, black thing with these shiny legs. I couldn’t even tell if it was a spider or a beetle. I just left it alone in the shed and hoped it would find its own way out. That’s the best approach. Don’t mess with the spiders, they’re the garden’s best defenders. Although, I have to say, I’m not a fan of the ones that crawl into my coffee. Oh, I know. I had one the other day. It was so small, I thought it was just a speck of dust. Then it started moving. I almost choked on my tea. It was terrifying. I tried to tell you when we were out last week, we should have gotten a professional to check the garden. I’ve been meaning to call someone to do the weeding, but I keep putting it off. I know, I know. But I think it’s more about not wanting to admit that I can’t do it myself. You know how it is, the older we get, the more we like to have things done for us.

Mummy, can we go to the beach this year? I really want to go to the beach. Oh, I was just thinking about that too. We need to plan our holiday properly. You know, the beach is always a good idea. But it’s been a while since we went. Yeah, I remember when I was little, we used to go every summer. I miss those days. Oh, I remember too. We used to have so much fun. I think it's time we take the kids again. But I don’t want to go to the same place every year. I’d rather do something different this time. Like what? Maybe somewhere a bit more exciting? I was thinking of going to Cornwall. I’ve heard it’s really beautiful there. Cornwall? That’s a good idea. It’s not too far from here, and it’s a popular holiday spot. I like the idea.
