I’ve been there a few times, and it’s always nice. But maybe we should check the weather first. Yeah, I was thinking about that too. If it’s too rainy, we might have to change plans. Well, we can always have a backup plan. Maybe a staycation if the weather doesn’t work out. That’s a good point. I know some people who have a cabin in the countryside. It could be a nice alternative. But I really want to go to the beach. I miss the waves and the sand. I agree. I think we can manage it. Let’s book the trip and see what happens. Speaking of trips, have you thought about who we’re bringing along? Just my friends from school. We can all go together. That sounds nice. It’ll be a good way for you to see your friends while you’re away. Yeah, and it’ll give you a chance to talk about things you haven’t had time for lately. I was thinking of asking my best friend, Emily, if she wants to come too. That’s a great idea. She’s always up for an adventure. I can imagine the group. You’ll all be out having fun, and I’ll be the one trying to keep up. You’ll be fine! You’re a musician, so you’re used to going out and having a good time. I think I’ll be the one who’s worried about the weather, though.

I can't believe we just watched  10 Things I Hate About You  again. It’s like the first time, but I’m so tired now. I know, right? It’s so cheesy, but I still love it. Especially Heath Ledger as Patrick. He was  so  good. Yeah, he was amazing. But I feel like the movie is just… not very realistic. Like, how does a guy get so obsessed with a girl in high school? It’s so over the top. I mean, it  is  a comedy. But I think the message is still sort of true—like, you don’t have to like someone to be attracted to them. And that’s kind of what happens with Kat and Patrick. Maybe, but I still think the whole “I hate you” thing is just a way to make it dramatic. Like, why not just be straightforward? Haha, I guess. But it’s fun to watch. I mean, even if it’s cheesy, it’s got that classic teen romance vibe that’s just so nostalgic. Yeah, I guess. But I’m more excited about our trip to London next month. I was thinking—what if we go to the British Museum? I’ve heard it’s amazing. That sounds cool! But don’t you have to do your school project first? You still have that history assignment due next week, don’t you? Ugh, yeah. I’m so behind. I was supposed to write about the Industrial Revolution, but I just haven’t got around to it. It’s so hard to focus when I’m thinking about London. I feel you. I’ve been procrastinating on my science report too. But I think we should make a plan. Maybe we can go to the museum after we finish our schoolwork. That way, we can both enjoy it without stressing. That’s a good idea. But I was also thinking—what if we go to the Tower of London too? I’ve heard it’s really cool. They have all those royal weapons and stuff. Oh, I love the Tower of London! I’ve been wanting to go there for ages. But I wonder how much it’ll cost. I don’t want to spend too much, especially since we’re still figuring out our budget. Yeah, we’ll have to be careful with the money. But I think it’s worth it.

Well, I've just seen this on Facebook, and it's absolutely ridiculous. You know how they always say that everyone's got a story, but this one’s just... I don’t even know what to say. What’s it about, then? You look like you’ve seen something shocking. It’s about this guy who was obsessed with cleanliness to the point of being utterly obsessed with it. I mean, he had to wash his hands like, twenty times a day. It was like watching someone go insane. OCD? That’s not new, is it? I mean, I’ve known a few people who had mild cases. But this sounds like it’s getting out of hand. Yeah, I’ve met someone like that. It was a friend of a friend who had to check the door three times before he’d leave the house. It was bizarre, really. And the worst thing is, he still didn’t feel safe. He’d be out in the garden, thinking he’s got the door locked, and then he’d have to go back and check, and then again, and again. I mean, it’s not even about being clean anymore. It’s about control. I can imagine. I remember when my cousin was a kid—he had chicken pox, and I swear he was obsessed with making sure that his hands weren’t touching anything. Even when he was at school, he’d be fiddling with his sleeves and trying to make sure he didn’t get infected. I think it was a bit of a phase, but it was really annoying. I think the body’s way of trying to make sense of something that’s out of your control. I mean, chicken pox can be really uncomfortable, and for a kid, it can be very scary. I suppose that kind of instinct makes sense. Yeah, but I think the real lesson is that even if you’re not religious, you have to find a way to cope. I mean, some people find comfort in faith, and others find it in routines or even in being overly tidy. Exactly. I think I’ve seen that in the church too. Some people use religion as a way to deal with anxiety or fear. It can go either way, though—sometimes it’s a great comfort, and sometimes it just makes things worse.

So, do you remember when we all went on that holiday to Germany back in 2012? I still remember the time we got lost in Munich and had to ask for directions in broken German. It was hilarious. Oh yeah, I remember that! You were so nervous about speaking German that you just mumbled something and then the guy just laughed and said, “You’re from Kent, right?” It was such a relief when he understood us. Oh, I was there too! And it wasn’t just the directions. I tried ordering a coffee and somehow ended up with a glass of milk. It was like the barista thought I was a baby or something. That’s like the best story! I remember you all laughing so hard that the whole café was looking at you. You were so red, and I think the waiter thought you had a heart attack. Wait, you were there too? I thought you were in London working on that design project. I remember you saying something about not being able to get a holiday because of deadlines. Yeah, I was stuck in a meeting all week. I even had to call my mum and say I couldn’t come home. She just laughed and said, “It’s not like you’re not going to be there for Christmas anyway.” That’s true, but I think we were all glad to see each other again. Even if we were all a bit grumpy from work. It’s funny how time flies. And don’t even get me started on the language. I tried to learn a bit of German before the trip, and it was so frustrating because all the words I learned were completely different from what people actually said. I think I picked up more from watching movies than from any book. Yeah, that’s the thing with accents. You can sound so different to the locals, even if you know the words. I remember trying to order something in a village in Germany and it took me ages to get it right. I ended up shouting, “Ich will ein Brot!” and they just looked at me like I was crazy. That’s what I love about accents – they add so much character. You can tell instantly where someone’s from, even in a room full of people. It’s like a language of its own, really.

So, how’s the new gig going? You mentioned you were doing some work at that restaurant in Exeter last week. It’s going alright, I guess. Busier than I thought, but it’s a good place to be. I’m kind of getting the hang of the routine now. Got a few regulars who come in every night. That’s great. I heard you were doing some drumming stuff too. Got any new projects or bands you’re into? Yeah, actually! I’m in a few small bands now. We’re doing some live gigs around the county. It’s a bit of a struggle to keep it going, but I love it. You know, playing music is like a second home for me. I think I’m going to try and start working on a new album next month. That’s awesome. I’d love to catch one of your shows. Maybe I can come along if you’re doing something in Nottingham. I’d be the first to support. Definitely! I’ll let you know when we’re doing something. By the way, have you heard of the new album by that band  The Hollows ? It’s really good. Their live performance at the Exeter Arts Centre last month was incredible. Oh yeah, I’ve heard a bit about them. I think I’ve seen some of their videos online. Their music has this kind of raw edge to it that’s really catchy. I mean, it’s not anything like what I’d normally listen to, but I can’t stop listening to it. Exactly! It’s like they’re channeling some kind of energy that’s really hard to describe. I think it’s because they’ve all been through a lot of different phases in life. It shows in their music. That makes sense. I’ve been thinking a lot about the idea of music reflecting personal experiences lately. I mean, I know it’s a cliché, but it’s true. You know, I’ve been trying to write some songs recently. I’m not sure if I’m ready to share them yet, but it’s been a good way to process some things. That’s cool. I’ve been trying to do the same. I even go to some open mics in Exeter now. It’s a bit intimidating at first, but once you get up there, it’s actually kind of liberating.

Alright, love? How's your day been? It's been alright, Mum. I had a few tests today at school, and I think I did okay. But I’m really tired. You should’ve had a proper sleep, love. You’re getting up early for school, and then you’re running around with your mates. I reckon you need more sleep than that. I know, I know. I just can’t get to sleep at night, Mum. My mind’s always going. I keep thinking about the things I need to do tomorrow. That’s normal, I suppose. But you need to start thinking about your summer plans. You’ve got the whole holiday, and you’ve got to plan something. I know, but I’m not sure what to do. I mean, you said you’re going to Durham with your friends, right? Yeah, I’m going with the girls for the weekend. We’re going to the city and maybe do a bit of shopping. It’s been ages since we’ve all had a proper weekend together. Cool. But I was thinking of going on a domino drive. You know, the one we used to do when we were kids. Oh, I remember those. It was always a bit of fun, wasn’t it? You know, the whole family would pile in the car, grab some food, and just drive around. Yeah, but my mates are talking about doing it again. They said it’s the best way to spend a summer. That’s a good idea, love. But I’m worried about the noise. You know the radio always starts playing at full volume. I don’t know how you can hear anything. It’s not that bad. My mates like to have the music on. It’s like their own little vibe. Well, as long as it doesn’t distract you from your studies. You need to keep up with your grades. I know, Mum. I’m trying. But sometimes the noise from the restaurant is so loud, I can’t even concentrate. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to work here, and the background noise is making it really hard. You should try getting a loyalty promotion or something. The staff said there was a new offer on. I might do that. But I still have to think about the coffee I’m having.

So, how’s the new flat? I heard it’s in Sussex. That’s pretty far from where you used to live, right? It’s actually not that far, honestly. It’s a little town called Hove, just a bit outside Brighton. It’s got great beaches, decent pubs, and—oh, I almost forgot—there’s a really nice park nearby. Plus, the rent is a bit cheaper than in Birmingham. Not that I’m complaining, of course. That’s great to hear. You’ve always said you wanted to live somewhere with more of a coastal vibe. I can’t imagine you living in the middle of a city anymore. Yeah, I think I’m finally getting the countryside vibe I’ve always wanted. Though I have to admit, I’m still getting used to the fact that I have to walk to the local supermarket instead of just driving there. It’s almost like I’ve been living in a different country for the past few years. I remember you used to talk about moving out of the city for a while. It’s about time, honestly. You’ve been working in assurance for three years now, right? Yeah, and I’ve been thinking a lot about my future. I mean, I have a good salary, but I’m starting to feel like I’m not really living the life I want. I’ve been talking to my sister about maybe taking a break for a while—maybe doing some travel or even learning a new language. Wait, you’re thinking about learning a new language? I thought you were already pretty fluent in Spanish. I still am, but I’ve been thinking about picking up Korean. I’ve been watching a lot of K-dramas lately, and I’m pretty hooked. Plus, I’ve got this friend who’s studying in Seoul and says it’s a great way to meet people. That’s not a bad idea at all. I mean, you’re already bilingual, so it’s not like it’s going to be too hard. I’ve been working on my own Spanish over the years, though I’m not nearly as good as you. You’re an English language instructor for crying out loud! You should be fluent by now! I know, I know. I just haven’t had the time to really focus on it.

I just got a call from the hospital. It's about Mum. They said they think it's cancer. Oh no. Is that for sure? I mean, they've been struggling with a lot of symptoms. I know, it's really hard to hear. They said they're going to run more tests, but they’re pretty sure it’s something serious. I’m so sorry. I wish I knew what to say. You know, she’s been through so much. She’s been dealing with the grief of Dad for years, and now this. Yeah, it’s just so unfair. I can’t even imagine what she’s going through. I know. I’m thinking about how we should be there for her – not just in words, but in actions. Maybe we should all go and visit her this weekend? That would be good. She’s been feeling really down lately, and I know she needs support. Yeah, and we should make sure she knows we’re here for her, no matter what happens. Exactly. You know, I’ve been thinking about how much she’s always been there for us, especially when we were little. She was so strong. She was, and I think that’s what we should remember – her strength. I just feel so helpless. I don’t know what to do. That’s okay. You don’t have to have all the answers. Just be with her. Be there for her. That’s all we can do. You’re right. I just hope she’s okay for a while. Me too. And if there’s anything else you need, I’m here. Thanks. I really appreciate that. Of course. We’re a family, and we stick together. Yeah. I know we’ll get through this. We will. We always do. I just wish I could take the pain away from her. I know. But we can’t. All we can do is love her, support her, and be there for her every step of the way. Yeah. I’m going to make sure I’m there for her. That’s all we can do. And that’s what matters most. I hope she feels that. I’m sure she will. She’s got us. Yeah. She’s got us. And that’s all that matters. Yeah. That’s all that matters. I’m going to go and check on her, just to make sure she’s

Alright, lads, how’s the schoolwork going? I know it’s been a tough term with all the exams and everything. Honestly, it’s been a bit of a struggle. I’m trying to keep up with all the stuff, but football practice takes up so much of my time. I’m not even sure if I’ll finish my English assignment on time. Yeah, I can see that. I used to play football when I was your age. It’s a great way to burn off energy, but you’ve got to balance it with your studies. Did you know that some of the best players in the country are also top students? They manage to do both. Yeah, like that guy from our town, Marco. He played for a local team and still got into university. You just have to push yourself. That’s true, but it’s not easy. I remember when I was your age, I used to spend all my time at the tennis club. I never thought I’d end up running a business, but here I am. Wow, you’ve got a lot on your plate. I guess that’s why I’ve been thinking about apprenticeships. I heard they’re a good way to get into the workforce and learn on the job. What do you think? I think they’re a solid option, especially with the current job market. You get hands-on experience and a chance to earn while you learn. Plus, they’re more stable than just relying on university degrees these days. Yeah, I’ve heard that too. But I’m not sure if I want to be an apprentice. I’ve always wanted to be in business, like you, Dad. Maybe I’ll start small, like a stall at the market or something. That’s a good idea. I started small, too. Maybe you could do something like that. You know, sell stuff or offer some kind of service. It’s not all about big business – sometimes the little things can make a big difference. I guess. But I’m not sure what I’d do. I mean, I like sports, but I don’t know if I want to be a coach or something. Maybe I’ll just stick with football and go to university after all. That’s not a bad plan either. Just make sure you don’t let your grades slip.

So, do you think we’ll get to Lancaster on time? I’ve been trying to get a signal on my phone all the way from Aylesbury, and it’s been like a ghost town out here. Yeah, honestly, I don’t know. It’s been like a nightmare trying to get a connection. I swear the train’s got more signal than my phone. Yeah, I’ve been trying to text my mum to let her know I’m on the way, but it just keeps dropping. I can’t even check if the car’s ready for when we get there. Oh, I know. I tried to send her a message earlier and it just said “failed to send.” It’s so frustrating. I was going to tell her about the cockle disaster, but now I’m not even sure if she’ll get it. Wait, the cockle disaster? What happened with the cockles? Oh, right! We went to the coast last weekend, and we thought we’d grab a few cockles for dinner. But we got them from this guy at the market, and they turned out to be like, super squishy and full of sand. I swear, they looked like they were made of wet paper. We tried to cook them, and they just… dissolved in the pan. Oh no! That sounds like a real disaster. Did you even manage to eat anything? We did. We just had to stick with fish and chips. Honestly, I think my mum’s already written a letter to the council about it. She said it’s a public health issue. That’s your mum? She’s still in about the same place as us with the fish and chips obsession. She’s always going on about how you can’t cook decent food at home. Yeah, she’s right. My sister tried to make baked beans once, and it was like a science experiment. I think she’s still waiting for the results. I can only imagine. I’m doing a master’s in linguistics, so I’ve been working on my dissertation about dialects and regional speech patterns. It’s basically going to be a giant essay on how people from different places talk. That sounds intense. I’m doing a similar thing, but in language research administration. It’s not as exciting, but I get to work with your kind of people.

So, do you know what’s up with the new band that’s been playing at the Doncaster pubs? I saw them last week, and they were  so  good. Yeah, I heard about them. I think they’re from Leeds, right? They’ve been getting a lot of buzz on social media. What’s their name again? I think it’s  The Black Tornadoes . Their lead singer has this really raspy voice, and their music is like a mix of indie and punk. It’s wild. Oh, I’ve heard of them! I think they’ve even opened for some bigger acts. Have you seen any of their videos? Yeah, I did. They’ve got this really cool aesthetic—black clothing, glitter, and a lot of attitude. I think it’s like a throwback to the 90s grunge era, but with a modern twist. That’s interesting. I’ve always liked that kind of vibe. I mean, I’m not really into the whole punk scene, but I do like the raw energy of it. Yeah, it’s kind of the same with me. I’ve been trying to get into more alternative music lately. I got into bands like Nirvana and Foo Fighters, but I’m still figuring out what I like. It’s hard, isn’t it? I mean, there’s so much music out there now. So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to play with those plastic dinosaurs? I think I still have mine in a box somewhere. It’s like a box of memories, really. Oh, I remember those! So, do you think we should bring up the satnav thing again? I know it’s been a bit of a running joke, but I feel like we should be more careful when we’re out driving. It was so much easier when I was just analysing it in a seminar with the teacher and the course mates. Now, I’m just trying to not fall asleep in the middle of  Othello . Yeah, I can’t even look at  Othello  without feeling like I’m in a situation where I’m being manipulated by someone else. I mean, I get it’s a tragedy, but I don’t know how you’re supposed to handle it without feeling like you’re the next Desdemona. Don’t even get me started on the play. I think it’s just too bloody dramatic for me. I tried to read it when I was doing my GCSEs and I just wanted to scream at the characters. I mean, I think I screamed at Othello once. I was like, “You’re not even a good man, you’re just jealous!” Haha, I laughed at that. I think I would’ve done the same. But maybe I’m just not the right person for Shakespeare.

So how have you been? It's been a while since we last caught up. Honestly, I’ve been okay, just juggling work and life. I’ve had a few crazy days with the marketing campaign we’re running. It’s been non-stop, but I’m managing. I can imagine. Work can be so demanding sometimes. How’s the team handling it? They’re mostly handling it. I think we’re all pretty stressed, but we’re pulling through. I just feel like I need to take a break soon. Didn’t you get the email about the new project you’re co-ordinating? Yeah, I did. It’s a bit of a big project, but I’m excited. I’m actually hoping it’ll give me more opportunities to move up in my career. I’ve been thinking a lot about my future lately. That’s great! I hope it goes well for you. I’ve been in a similar spot, thinking about where I want to be in five years. I mean, I’m not sure yet—maybe I’ll stay in marketing for a while, but I’m also thinking about studying for a master’s. Do you think you’ll do that? I’m considering it. It all depends on the project and how it goes. I’m not sure I want to stay in project coordination forever. I think I want to get into something more strategic. But I’m not sure what yet. That makes sense. It’s good to have goals. I just hope I can find the right path. Speaking of goals, how have things been with your family? Still in touch with your parents? Yeah, I talk to them every week. They’re doing okay, though they keep asking when I’m going to settle down. I don’t know if I’m ready for that yet, but I do miss them. How about you? I miss them too. I have a great relationship with my parents, but they’re always talking about my love life. I’ve got a few friends from Oxford, and I’m still in touch with some of them. We keep in touch on social media, but it’s not the same as meeting up in person. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to meet up with some of my old friends from uni, but with work, it’s hard to find the time.

So, do you know, I’ve been trying to get my mum to start growing her own vegetables again. She’s got this big garden out back, and I think she could really take to it. She’s always been into gardening, but she’s just… I don’t know, been busy with work and everything else. Yeah, I can see that. My gran used to grow everything. She had these massive tomato plants, and they’d be this big, like, bushy thing. She’d always say it was because she used to feed them with this special mix of compost and stuff. Oh, right. I remember when I was a kid, she used to let me help her plant things. My brother, he was always trying to grow potatoes and he’d just dig them up and then they’d be all green and sad. He’d be like, “Mum, look at these!” and she’d just laugh and say, “You’ve got to be patient.” Yeah, I remember that. My brother was like that too. He tried to grow his own basil, and it just turned out all slimy and sad. He ended up giving it to the cat. Oh, that’s not the worst. I remember when I was about ten, I tried to grow a sunflower from a seed, and it just sat there for weeks and didn’t grow. I was so upset. I was like, “Why won’t it grow?!” and my mum just said, “Remember, plants take time.” I can definitely see what you mean. I think my mum wants to get back into it too, but she’s been so stressed with work and about starting this new job. She’s been having these weird headaches and stuff. I think it’s all the pressure. Yeah, it’s a tough time for her. But, honestly, I think being in the garden helps. It gives her something to focus on. You know, when you’re dealing with all that stress, there’s something calming about getting your hands in the soil. Definitely. I’ve been thinking about starting a small garden myself. I’ve got this little patch of land near the house, and I’ve been planning to plant some herbs. I think it would be nice to have fresh herbs for cooking. That’s a good idea. You could grow thyme, rosemary, and maybe some parsley.

So, how was your weekend, Colin? You mentioned you were going to the mountains again. It was alright, Bob. Just a bit of a downer, actually. The weather turned bad, and we ended up staying in the car the whole time. It was quite funny, honestly. My son and his wife were arguing about who was going to take the blame if the car broke down. You know how they are. That sounds like a typical family squabble. I remember when my daughter was that age—always blaming the other person for everything. But I suppose it’s all in good fun. Yeah, it was. Anyway, enough about the weekend. I heard you were talking about snooker players last week. Any luck with that? Not really. I tried to get some of the younger ones to take part in a tournament, but they all said they had exams coming up. I think they’re too busy with marking assignments and preparing for their own assessments. It’s quite a challenge to get them out of the university bubble. I can imagine. I’ve had similar issues with my students. I even had one who wanted to join the police force instead of taking the exams. Told me he wanted to work with young people and help them stay out of trouble. That’s admirable, but I don’t know if the police would take someone who’s already in the middle of his studies. You’d have to balance both, and I’m not sure how they’d manage that. Maybe the armed forces? It’s a different world, but some students seem to be attracted to the idea of discipline and structure. True. I think it’s a question of finding the right fit. Some students are interested in different areas—like gardening. I’ve got this one who’s been telling me about his garden for weeks. Says he’s planning to grow his own vegetables and even has a guesthouse for his plants. That’s a unique hobby. I’ve always said that if you can’t find a hobby, gardening is a safe bet. At least you know what you’re getting when you take a bite of your harvest. Exactly. I think it’s a great way to relax. I’ve been trying to go back to my own garden, but I’m not sure I have the patience for it.

Alright, do you know what’s happening this weekend? I’ve got a few things to discuss with you both. What’s happening? Well, first of all, your birthday is coming up. I was thinking we could have a little celebration at home. You know, just the three of us. I’ve been meaning to do something special for you, and I think this would be a good chance. That sounds nice! I’d love that. But are we going to have cake? Of course. I’ve already called the bakery and ordered a big one. I even got some candles. I thought maybe we could do something different this year, like have a little party atmosphere. That sounds great. I’d love to help out. I can bring some decorations or maybe some music. I’ve been learning how to play the guitar, so maybe I can play something while we have the cake. That’d be lovely. You’d be the perfect addition to the day. Now, what about the Christening? I’ve been thinking about when we can plan that. Is it going to be soon? I think we need to get the confirmation from the church first. I’ve been in touch with the vicar, and they’re happy to do it in a few weeks. But I need to organise the venue and the guest list. Should we invite all our friends and family? I’d love to have everyone there. Yes, I think that’s a good idea. But we need to make sure we don’t overdo it. It’s important that it’s a meaningful day for the family, not just about the celebration. I agree. But I’m excited to see everyone. I can’t wait to see my little brother get baptised. I know. It’s going to be a special time. I’m going to start working on the invitations next week. I’ll let you know as soon as I have more details. Sounds good. I can help with that too. Maybe I can design some nice ones for you. That would be perfect. You’re really good with design. I’ll make sure to include you in the details. I’m just so grateful for this family. It’s amazing to have you both here, planning all this. We’re lucky to have you too, sweetheart. You’re the heart of everything we do.

So, do you think we should go to New York this year? I’ve been thinking about it for ages. It’s been so long since we went on a proper holiday. Yeah, I think it’s a good idea. I’ve been meaning to go there for a while too. I’ve heard it’s amazing. But I guess we need to plan it properly. When are you thinking of going? Well, if we can get the timing right, maybe in June. It’s not too hot yet, and we can still enjoy the city. Plus, it’s the perfect time for some sightseeing. Can I come? I want to see the Empire State Building! Of course you can, sweetie! We’ll have to take you. But I’m not sure about the timing yet. We need to check the flights and make sure everyone’s available. Yeah, and we should probably book the flights early. I’ve heard that flights to New York can get quite expensive, especially during the summer. Right, that’s true. I’ve got a cousin who went last year and said it was a bit of a shock to the wallet. We need to budget properly. Can we stay in a hotel? I don’t like staying with strangers. Of course, we’ll find a hotel. Maybe something near the main attractions so we don’t have to travel too far. You know, like the area around Times Square. Sounds good. I think it’d be fun to explore the city. I’ve heard about all those museums and the subway system. But I’ve never used the subway before. Do you think it’s safe? Oh, it’s fine. It’s pretty reliable. I used to take the Tube all the time when I lived in London. You just need to be careful with your belongings. And the trains are always on time, mostly. I like trains. I used to go on the train to my aunt’s house every weekend when I was little. That sounds lovely. I remember you always coming with your big bag and your little toys. You were the best little traveler. You were a regular on the train, I remember. I think your bag was bigger than you were! I was a big bag! I had a big backpack and everything. I even had a sleeping bag.

So, do you know what’s going on with the paperwork for the thesis? I’m trying to get it sorted, but it’s like a giant maze. Honestly, I feel the same. I’ve been stuck on the same section for days. I think it’s the part about the methodology. I just don’t know where to start. Yeah, I know what you mean. I tried watching some tutorials online, but they all seem too basic. I’m not even sure what the professor expects. It’s like the more I read, the more confused I get. I thought I had a clear idea of what I wanted to do, but now I’m questioning everything. It’s so frustrating. I’ve even asked my advisor, and he just said, “Just keep going,” which is not helpful at all. Yeah, I’ve had that too. I mean, he’s busy and all, but still... I feel like I need more guidance. I don’t want to waste time going down the wrong path. I was thinking about it the other day—what if we meet up and go through it together? We can split the sections and tackle them as a team. It might help. That sounds like a good idea. I was thinking of asking someone else, but I don’t really know who. You’re the only one I feel comfortable talking through this with. No problem. I’d rather be stuck with someone than alone. It also helps to have a second opinion. Sometimes you just need a different perspective. Exactly. I think I’ve been overthinking it all. Maybe I just need to start writing, even if it’s not perfect. That way, the real work can begin. Yeah, that’s the thing. I think I’ve been too scared to start because I’m worried it won’t be good enough. But if I don’t start, I’ll never finish. That’s true. I feel like I’m stuck waiting for the “right” moment, but there is no right moment. You just have to do it. Exactly. Let’s set a time tomorrow. We can meet at the library and work on the methodology. I’ll bring my notes, and you bring yours. Sounds good. I’ll bring some coffee too. Nothing like a bit of caffeine to get you through a brain-scorching session.

So, do you ever think about what you want to do in life, you know, like, real big dreams? Like, not just what you're doing now, but like, what you really want? Honestly, I think about it all the time. I mean, I love teaching, but I always kind of dreamed of writing children's books. You know, like, stories that actually make kids think and feel something. It’s not just about teaching; it's about inspiring them. Can you read to us? I’d like to hear one of your stories, Mummy. Oh, I’d love to, but I don’t think I’m ready yet. I’ve written a few, but they’re not quite right. I keep changing the endings. I think I’m afraid of what the kids might think. I think it’s cool, Mummy. I want to be a dragon when I grow up. A dragon? That’s awesome. I remember when I was your age, I wanted to be a superhero. I thought I could fly and save the world. But then I realized I couldn’t even ride a bike without falling over. I want to be a doctor. Like, a doctor who can make people feel better. And maybe a dog too. I want a dog. I think I should get a dog. Oh, you want a dog? That’s great. But you know, dogs need a lot of care. They need to be walked, fed, and given a lot of love. Yeah, and they’re not just pets. They’re family. I used to have a golden retriever when I was about your age. His name was Max. He used to follow me everywhere. I miss him now. Can we get a dog? Can we? Well, we can talk about it. But first, we need to think about the responsibility. And maybe the cost. You know, food, toys, vet visits, stuff like that. I have a goldfish. It’s not a dog, but it’s a pet. That’s a start. Goldfish are easy, but dogs are more work. I mean, they really need your attention. If you’re not careful, they can get lonely and start doing things they shouldn’t. And what if they cause a mess? Like, I heard some dogs chew up furniture or dig holes in the garden. But I can clean up the mess!

So, do you know what’s going on with Jess? She’s been acting really weird lately. I think she’s got something serious going on. Yeah, I heard something about her being in A&E. What happened? I don’t know the full story, but I think she got into a fight at the weekend. She was with some friends, and there was an argument that turned physical. I heard she got hit in the head. Oh no, that’s bad. Did she get a concussion or something? I think she did. She was really out of it for a while. She’s still not back to normal. Her head’s been hurting her a lot, and she’s been throwing up. That sounds really serious. I hope she’s getting the right treatment. Have they done any scans? They did a CT scan, and they said it was a mild concussion, but they’re keeping an eye on her. She’s not allowed to do anything too strenuous. Also, she’s been having trouble sleeping. I get that. I’ve had a few concussions myself, and it’s not fun. It affects your memory, your concentration, and your mood. Yeah, I know. She’s been really down lately, and I think it’s because of the injury. She keeps saying she can’t focus and that everything feels fuzzy. Maybe she needs more rest. I mean, she’s not in a position to work right now. I hope she’s taking it easy. You should check in on her. I will. I just feel so worried about her. She’s always been so strong, and now she’s just… broken. It’s hard to see someone you care about going through that. I’d be there if she needed anything. Maybe we can go visit her tomorrow? Yeah, that would be good. I think she’s been feeling really isolated too. She doesn’t like asking for help, but I think she needs it now more than ever. I’ll bring some soup and a couple of books. She might need something comforting. Let’s make sure she knows she’s not alone. Thanks. I think that would help. I just hope she gets better soon. I don’t know what we’d do if she had to take time off work. Yeah, it’s a lot to handle. But we’ll get through it together.

I've been thinking a lot lately about starting something new, you know. Maybe a small business, or at least a side hustle. I’ve got this idea for a local artisan market—selling handmade crafts and local produce. I've seen how successful some of the pop-up markets are in Brighton. That sounds like a solid idea. I mean, with the way things are going, people are starting to value local products more than ever. But I have to say, it’s easier said than done. You know how it is—getting the right space, finding reliable suppliers, and then the marketing. Yeah, I know. But I’ve been doing a bit of research, and I think there's a gap in the market. You know, there are a few markets around, but nothing really focused on sustainably made, eco-friendly items. I think there’s an audience for that. I see your point. I’ve been thinking about expanding my own business too. I’ve got this plan to introduce some new products—maybe environmentally friendly packaging, or even some locally sourced ingredients for the things I sell. But I’m not sure I can afford the investment right now. That’s understandable. I was thinking about how the economy is shaping up, and I don’t want to risk too much. But I’ve got a few friends who are in the same boat, and maybe we could pool our resources. Maybe even collaborate on some projects. That’s an interesting thought. I’ve been talking to a few people about starting something like that. I mean, with the recent news about the economy, and the way people are becoming more conscious about where they spend their money, it might be the right time. Exactly. And with the recent news about climate change and sustainability, I think that’s a key factor. People are more willing to pay a little extra for products that align with their values. I agree. I remember reading an article about a local shop that started offering eco-friendly alternatives and saw a huge increase in customers. It’s good to stay ahead of the curve. Yeah, and it’s not just about profit—it’s about making a meaningful impact. I’ve always believed in supporting local businesses and making the world a better place, one small step at a time.

So, do you reckon we should go for the fish and chips or the burger? I mean, it’s a bit of a toss-up, isn’t it? Honestly, I think the fish and chips is the way to go. It’s a classic, you know? Plus, it’s been a while since we had proper British food. I mean, I know we’ve had the burger, but it’s not the same as proper fish and chips. Yeah, but I’ve been craving a burger lately. Especially with the weather being so cold. I mean, it’s not even winter yet, but it’s like a mini-winter in Woolwich. Plus, the burger’s only a few quid more. I get that, but think about the Happy Valley show. We had the episode last night, and it reminded me how much I miss the old days of university. You know, when we could just grab a burger and a pint without a second thought. Oh, I remember those days. It’s funny how time flies. I still remember that one time when we got caught smoking in the library and had to sneak out through the back. And you thought you were so clever. I mean, we got caught by the security guard, and he was like, “What are you two doing out there?” And you just stood there, like, “Uh… nothing.” Silly me. I still laugh about that. But, hey, speaking of university, have you seen the new season of Happy Valley? It’s amazing. I mean, it’s so gritty and dark, but I can’t stop watching. Yeah, it’s brilliant. I love how they bring back the old characters. But honestly, I miss the days when we could just walk into a pub and not have to worry about the décor. This place, the Guardhouse, is so much better than the ones back in Edinburgh. I agree. I mean, the décor is great, it’s got that old-school vibe. You can tell it’s been around for years. I love the wooden beams and the warm lighting. It’s like stepping back in time. Yeah, and the music is nice too. I mean, the playlist has that classic pub feel, you know? If it wasn’t for the cat sitting in the corner, it’d be perfect. Oh, that cat’s a menace. I swear it’s been following us around all evening.

So, do you know what’s the deal with the weather in Scotland these days? One minute it’s sunshine and the next it’s like we’re in a blizzard. I was out this morning trying to take some photos of the castle, and it was clear, then within ten minutes, it started raining so hard it looked like the sky was crying. I know what you mean. It’s like the weather here has a mind of its own. But honestly, I think it’s a good thing. It keeps things interesting. You never know what to expect, which is why I love taking photos here. You can get some of the most dramatic shots when the light changes so fast. Yeah, I guess that’s the thing. I mean, I’ve taken some decent photos when the weather was just right, but I’ve also seen some of the worst attempts at photography ever. I was at a café last week, and someone was trying to take a photo of the skyline, but it was overcast, and they were using a flash. It looked like a horror movie scene. Oh man, that’s a classic. I’ve seen that too. You know, it’s like the camera is trying to fight the light, but in the end, it just ends up looking worse. I think the key is to know when to take the shot, and sometimes that means waiting for the clouds to clear or the sun to come out. I’ve been thinking about taking a trip to the Highlands for a few months now. I’ve got this idea to do a photo series of the landscapes there. Some of the views up there are just stunning. It’s got that wild, untamed feel to it that you can’t get in the city. That sounds amazing. Have you thought about when you might go? I mean, the weather can be a bit of a problem up there, but the scenery is worth it. I’ve been planning a trip myself, actually. I want to take some photos of the lochs and the mountains. It’s a way for me to relax and get some inspiration for my work. Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that too. I mean, I do love the Highlands. It’s got that kind of raw, natural beauty that you can’t really find anywhere else.

So, do you know what’s happening this week? I’ve got a few things on my mind, and I’d love to hear what you’re planning. Honestly, I’m pretty much just surviving this week. I’ve got some stuff at school, and I’m trying to get everything sorted for the nursery. I’m really stressed about the start date, you know? Yeah, I can imagine. I had a bit of a panic when I first thought about nursery. But you know, once you get into it, it’s not so bad. Just makes you realize how much you’ve been doing already. I know, but I’m worried about the transition. I don’t want to be too overbearing, but I also don’t want to leave her alone. I keep thinking about the first day, and how I’ll be sitting there, crying in the corner, while she’s playing with the other kids. Oh, you’ll be fine. You’ll get used to it. I remember when I first dropped off my son. I was so nervous, but after a few weeks, it became routine. He started to make friends, and I realized he was happy. That’s all that matters, isn’t it? Yeah, I guess. But I still feel like I’m preparing for something huge. I mean, it’s not just about the nursery. It’s about life moving on. I have to get back to work full-time, and we’re starting to think about starting a family. It’s all happening so fast. I know, it’s a lot to take in. But you’re doing it, and that’s what matters. I’ve got a few meetings about some old work stuff I need to wrap up. I’m not sure if I’m going to take the job offer or not. It’s a bit of a dilemma. That’s a big decision. You need to think about what you really want. I’m trying to figure it out too. I think I want to stay in teaching, but I’m getting a bit burnt out. I need something different. I get that. I think it’s important to find something that makes you happy. I know you’re not happy with the current job, even if it’s stable. You deserve something better. You’re right. I’m just not sure what that ‘something better’ is yet.

So, how’s the new job going, then? I heard you got promoted last month. Oh, yeah, it’s going okay, I guess. I mean, it’s not exactly a dream job, but it’s better than before. I got promoted to a senior role in the warehouse. Got more responsibility and a bit more money. It’s not much, but it’s a start. That sounds good. I would’ve killed for a promotion like that. I’m still in the same place, same role, grinding it out. But at least I’ve got the kids and the house to take care of. Yeah, I know, but the thing is, you’ve got to be in the right place at the right time. I think I got lucky with the promotion. I mean, I wasn’t even sure I’d be considered for it. But I guess they needed someone to take over when the manager left. Yeah, I suppose it’s the same for everyone. You just have to keep your head down and do the job properly. I mean, I was getting annoyed with the workload, but I stuck with it. And then, boom, promotion. That’s the thing, isn’t it? I mean, I’m in a good job, but I can’t seem to get the same recognition. I work just as hard as anyone else, but no one seems to notice. It’s frustrating. I know what you mean. I’ve had that too. I think part of it is just the way the system is set up. You can be brilliant, but if you’re not in the right clique or don’t know the right people, it doesn’t matter. It’s like the old adage: the right connections make all the difference. Yeah, I know that feeling. I mean, it’s not like I haven’t tried. I’ve got a few contacts, but it’s like they just don’t want to open up. I think a lot of people in my position don’t even try to network because they don’t see the point. It’s just hard to get ahead when you’re stuck in a rut. I think it’s also about expectations. I mean, I thought I’d be moving up in the world by now. I’ve got a postgrad, I’m in a stable job, I’ve got a family, and yet I still feel like I’m standing still.

Well, I've just made the tea, so I suppose we can all have a cup. It's been a bit of a cold morning, hasn't it? Oh, it's been a proper chill, hasn’t it? I was just thinking about how things used to be when I was younger. I remember the days when we used to sit round the fire with tea and stories. Aye, I can still remember those days. My mother used to make the best tea. It would always be strong and sweet, just the way I liked it. Do you remember the days when we used to fetch the tea from the shop ourselves? Oh, I do, though I was too young to do the shopping. My grandmother would always make the tea and tell us stories while we waited for it to brew. It was like a ritual, wasn’t it? Yeah, it was. I still miss those days when everything happened at a slower pace. Nowadays, everything’s too quick. You finish your tea and it’s time to do something else. I don’t know how people manage. I think it’s about how we choose to live. Some people like to keep things simple and slow, like we did back then. Others like to rush about all the time. I think the key is to find a balance, though I know it’s not always easy. That’s true. I think we all have our own pace, but it’s nice to have moments where you can just sit back and enjoy a cup of tea, like we are now. It’s something that brings people together. It does, doesn’t it? I think in a world that moves so fast, having these quiet moments is really important. It reminds you of where you come from and what matters most. Speaking of which, have you heard about the new tea shop that opened up near the village? It’s supposed to have the best tea in the area. I might go there next week and see what they’ve got. Oh, I’ve heard about it. I think they serve both traditional and modern blends. It’s a bit of a novelty, but I suppose it’s good for trying new things. Maybe we could all go together sometime. It would be nice to meet up and have a chat over a cup of tea, like we used to do when we were younger.

So, do you think we should go to the new pub in Norwich next weekend? I heard it’s got a really good selection of local ales. I’d love to, but I’m not sure if we can. We’ve got the CRB checks to do for the new staff, and it’s all taking more time than we thought. Not to mention I still need to finish the report on the customer satisfaction survey. That’s a shame. I was really looking forward to going out. But maybe we can go to the one in London instead? I heard it’s got a great bar and a fantastic menu. London? That’s a long drive, especially with the traffic. But if you’re up for it, I’m sure it’d be worth it. Although, I hear the new pub in Norwich is supposed to be quite the experience. They even have a live music night on Fridays. Yeah, I think it’s worth checking out. But we’d have to make sure we’re all on the same page about the timings. I don’t want anyone to feel left out, especially with the family stuff going on. Absolutely. We should plan it properly. But let’s not forget, we’ve also got that protest coming up in Norwich. I’ve been thinking about joining it. It’s about better working conditions for the local staff, and I’m pretty passionate about that. That sounds important. I’m not sure I’d be up for it, though. I’ve got a lot on my plate with the new training program we’re rolling out. But I’d support you if you wanted to go. That’s the spirit. We should all be about standing up for what we believe in. But I still think the pub is going to be a better way to unwind. I love the atmosphere, and it’s a great way to catch up with everyone. Definitely. And if we’re going to London, maybe we can check out some art galleries too. I heard there’s a new exhibition on display at the Saatchi Gallery. It’s supposed to be really good. That sounds like a good idea. I’ve been wanting to see more art, especially with the new course I’m teaching. It’s always inspiring to get a fresh perspective.

So, did you have a good holiday? Yeah, it was really nice. I went to Cornwall with my family, and it was just so peaceful. I haven’t been anywhere like that in a while. That sounds amazing. I just got a call from Lucy. She’s been going through a really tough time. She’s got cancer, and it’s advanced. She’s been more withdrawn lately, and she’s not really talking about it much. I feel awful knowing she’s going through this. I can only imagine how hard this must be for her. I hope she’s getting the support she needs. Have you spoken to her about her options? We had a conversation a couple of weeks ago. She doesn’t want to go through with aggressive treatment anymore. It takes a lot of strength to make that decision. I wonder how her family is handling it. They must be going through a lot. They are. Her husband is trying to be there for her every step of the way, and the kids are really close. They’ve been helping her with everything—medical appointments, managing her care, even just being there to listen. It’s been a tough few months for all of them. I’d hate to be in their shoes. It’s heartbreaking to see someone you care about go through something like this. I hope she finds peace in whatever time she has left. Me too. It’s not easy to be around someone who’s so sick, but we’re all trying to be there for her. I keep thinking about how things could have been different if she had caught it earlier. But I guess that’s not something we can change now. No, it’s not. All we can do is support her and make sure she knows how much she’s loved. I’m going to reach out to her tomorrow and see if she wants to talk. I can’t imagine what she’s going through, but I want to be there for her in any way I can.

So, do you ever just get fed up with things at work? I mean, I know it's not the best job in the world, but sometimes I just feel like I'm stuck in a loop. Yeah, honestly, I feel the same. It's not like I hate my job, but there are so many things I don’t like about it. Like what? I mean, I know I don’t like the hours sometimes, and the fact that we’re always on duty, but you know, it’s part of the job. I know, but it’s not just the hours. It’s the people. Some of the residents are just… hard to deal with. You know, the ones who never clean up after themselves, or constantly throw things around. Oh, I get that. I’ve had some of those too. But honestly, the worst part is the lack of support. I mean, I’m not even being paid properly for the extra work I do. If I have to stay late to clean up or handle a complaint, it doesn’t get reflected in my pay. Right, and it’s not like we’re given any extra time or help when we need it. We’re basically expected to just handle everything on our own. Yeah, and it’s not just the workload. I don’t like the fact that we’re always trying to be the ‘good guy’ with the residents. You know, someone’s always expecting us to be understanding or overly helpful, but if you’re not, you’re seen as the bad guy. Exactly. And I don’t like the fact that we’re not even considered part of the staff. We’re just these weird mix of officers and support staff, and no one knows where we fit in. I know, and that’s just frustrating. I mean, we’re not even allowed to interact with the residents in the way that the other officers can. It’s like we’re always being kept at arm’s length. It’s really annoying. I mean, I understand the need for boundaries, but sometimes I just feel like we’re not even given the chance to build any kind of rapport with the people we’re supposed to support. Yeah, and I don’t like how the management treats us. They’re always giving us the run-around when we try to speak up about issues.

So, do you remember that time we bumped into that group of English people in Antwerp last year? I swear, they were all dressed up like it was Christmas, and I thought, “Oh, they must be on a package tour.” Oh, I remember that well. We were just walking past the Christmas market when they all started singing “We Wish You a Merry Christmas” in full voice. It was so loud, I thought someone had turned on a car radio. It was quite a scene. I was with my mum at the time, and she said, “You know, some people just like to perform in public.” I thought she was being funny, but honestly, they were really into it. Yeah, I mean, it’s not every day you see a bunch of middle-aged Englishmen trying to sing carols like they’re in a talent show. They looked like they were waiting for someone to clap. They did have a point though. I mean, it’s the Christmas season, and everyone’s in a festive mood. I remember that one guy with the red scarf—his face was glowing like he’d just finished a litre of mulled wine. Honestly, I’ve seen some wild things at Christmas markets. I was in Herne Bay last week, and I bumped into a guy who was dressed as Santa, but he was actually a teacher. It was so bizarre. That sounds like a real Christmas miracle. I mean, you just never know what you’ll run into when you’re out and about. Exactly. And speaking of out and about, I was thinking about going to Dorset this weekend to caravan. I’ve been meaning to take the boys there for a few years now. It’s a lovely place, and it’s not too far from Brighton. That sounds like a great plan. I’ve always found caravanning to be such a peaceful way to spend time with the family. Plus, the kids love it. They think it’s like a mini holiday. Yeah, I can imagine. I mean, being out of the city, with the sea right there, it’s the perfect escape. I just hope the weather’s not as miserable as it was the last time I went. Oh, don’t worry, I’ve checked the forecast. It looks like it might be a good one. I’ve already booked the caravan and made some arrangements with the campsite.

Mm, so, um, what’s the deal with the equality vote? I heard it’s about same-sex marriage or something? Yeah, more or less. It’s about giving equal rights to same-sex couples as heterosexual ones. Like, marriage, adoption, all that. But it’s been a big topic in Ireland, especially with the referendum they had a while back. Oh, right! I remember hearing about that. I think it passed, didn’t it? Like, a lot of people voted yes? Yeah, it did. It was a huge deal. People were really passionate about it. Some people thought it was a good idea, and others were really against it. But in the end, the majority said yes. Cool. So, does that mean same-sex couples can get married now? Yeah, that’s exactly what it means. It’s a big step forward for equality. But it’s not just in Ireland. People are talking about it in lots of other countries too. England’s got its own version of the equality vote, I think. Yeah, I’ve heard that too. But I’m not sure how it works there. Do they vote on it like in Ireland? It’s a bit different. It’s more of a legislative process, not a direct referendum. But the idea is the same—making sure people are treated equally, no matter who they love. That sounds fair. I mean, why shouldn’t people have the same rights? Like, if you love someone, it should matter who they are, right? Exactly. It’s about fairness. But I guess there are still people who don’t agree. Some folks think it’s not the government’s job to change the law like that. They think it’s a personal matter. Yeah, I can see how some people might feel that way. But I think it’s important for the law to protect everyone. Even if you don’t agree with someone’s choices, you should still be able to treat them the same. That’s a good point. And honestly, I think it’s about making sure everyone feels included. Even if you don’t agree with the idea, the law should still go out of its way to be fair. I guess. But I also heard that some people in Ireland were really embarrassed about their mothers. Like, you know, their moms were against the vote and stuff?

Well, I've been having a bit of a think about the lathe tools I had in the workshop when I worked. You know, back in the day, I used to fix all sorts of things. Now I just sit here and eat my lunch and read the paper. Oh, I remember when you used to fix things. I used to watch you from the kitchen. You were always so precise with the tools. A lot of people would just throw things away, but you'd fix them. It was amazing. Yeah, I remember that. Didn’t you once get the whole lathe stuck because you were trying to make a special part for that model plane you were building? Oh, that was a good one. I spent an entire Saturday trying to get that thing unstuck. I had to take it apart and reassemble it three times. In the end, it worked, but it almost made me give up on the whole project. Still, I’m proud of it, you know? You were always a bit of a tinkerer, weren’t you? I can see it in you, Dave. You always had that knack for putting things back together. I think that’s what made you such a good childminder too. You had a way of making things feel safe and comfortable. Yeah, I suppose so. But these days, I’m not quite as hands-on. I have a feeling the kids these days don’t even know what a lathe is. Let alone how to use it. It’s true. I think the younger generation just uses gadgets. Everything’s instant these days. Even the way we cook has changed. You know, I was about to make a steak for lunch, but the oven wasn’t working. I had to use the microwave. That’s not how I was brought up. Oh, that’s not fair. The microwave’s not the end of the world. I mean, I used to make a lot of things in the microwave when I was a childminder. You could make a good soup or even a decent lasagna in there. Although, I do admit, I’ve never tried to cook a steak in it. You know what I like about the microwave? It’s quick. I don’t want to stand there for hours waiting for the food to cook. I’d rather just pop it in and let it do the work.

I can't believe I've been doing this for so long. I mean, transcribing for hours on end, it's exhausting. But I suppose it's better than nothing. I know, it's a job that doesn't really have the same sort of glamour as, say, being an administrator or running a school. But I guess it pays the bills. Oh, don’t you start on me, Stephen. I've had my fair share of administrative work, and I can tell you it’s just as grinding. I used to be the headmistress of a school in Edinburgh, and I swear I had more paperwork than the entire staff combined. That sounds terrifying. I mean, you had to manage staff, budgets, and students all at once. Oh, it was. I think I turned into a machine. I’d wake up at 5:30 in the morning and not stop until 9:00 at night. And the worst part? You always felt like you were never doing enough. I can relate. I’ve had to manage a team of people in the office, and it’s the same thing. You’re always running late, always catching up. Speaking of running late, have you heard about the new policy on charging for plastic bags? I think it’s been going on for a while now, but I still don’t know what to make of it. Oh, that’s just one of those things that’s been around for ages. I remember when we had to use paper bags, and then the government started charging for plastic. It felt like the planet was crying out for help, and yet we kept buying the same thing. I think it’s a good idea in principle, but I’m not sure it’s actually making a difference. I mean, do people just stop buying plastic bags if they’re charged? Or do they just start buying more eco-friendly alternatives? I’ve heard that some people just buy more reusable bags instead. It’s a bit of a win-win, if you ask me. Well, I suppose the point is that it’s a start. You can’t just stop all the plastic goings-on overnight. But if you start making small changes, it could add up. I think the same could be said about your credit card debt. It’s not like you can just eliminate all of it overnight, but if you start paying it off bit by bit, it can make a difference.

Alright, do you two want to stop playing with your toys and do something more educational? No, mummy, we’re having so much fun! Yeah, we’re building a whole kingdom in Minecraft! So, how was your holiday, love? You mentioned you went to the Lake District. It was amazing, Mum. The weather was perfect, and we got to do a bit of hiking. Did you go anywhere specific? So, do you guys want to get some sandwiches? There’s that new place near the cinema that’s supposed to have really good ones. Yeah, actually I’m starving. So, do you remember Mr. Thompson from physics? He’s like the worst teacher ever. Oh yeah, he’s so strict. I mean, he used to take away our homework if we didn’t do it. And he’d shout at us like we were in a lab and not in a classroom. I know, right? But he’s got this weird habit of talking about quantum physics like it’s something we all understand. Like, “If a particle is in two places at once, you can’t really blame it for being confused.” That’s the worst. I think he’s just trying to sound smart. But honestly, I don’t think he even knows what he’s talking about half the time. I mean, he once said the sun is made of fire, and then he got confused when we asked how that works. Oh, he definitely got confused. He said, “Well, it’s just a big ball of fire in the sky. It’s science, not magic, you know.” I mean, that’s not even a real answer. Yeah, and then he got all defensive when I asked him about the Big Bang. He said, “It’s not for you to understand.” Like, that’s not a thing people say in class. That’s what you say to a kid who’s actually trying to learn. I think he just wants to be the cool teacher. Like, he’s got this whole vibe, but he’s just not good at explaining things. And don’t even get me started on his tie. It’s always mismatched. Oh, and he’s got this obsession with  Star Trek . He used to say, “In the future, we’ll be able to bend space-time like it’s a piece of paper.” I mean, that’s not even a real theory. It’s just his way of trying to make us feel smart. I heard he’s starting up a science club. I think he wants to make it look like he’s actually helping us. But I don’t know, I’m not sure we want to be part of it. Yeah, I think he just wants to feel like he’s doing something. But honestly, I think he’s more of a show-off than a teacher. I mean, he got a promotion last year just for being “innovative,” but I don’t know what that even means.

So, do you know what’s happening this weekend? I’ve got a few ideas for the weekend. Yeah, I was thinking about that too. I’ve got this friend who’s going to Transylvania this weekend. You know, the vampire stuff? Oh, really? I saw that on a travel blog the other day. It looked pretty cool. I’ve always wanted to go there. That’s a bit of a trek, though. It’s not exactly a quick trip from here. You’d have to drive all the way to the north of England first. Yeah, but I’ve been thinking about going to Australia, actually. I’ve heard the people there are pretty laid-back, you know? That’s what I heard too. I think it’s a bit of a culture shock for people who are used to the UK. Yeah, I think it is. I mean, I’ve got this idea to go on a road trip from Sydney to Perth. You know, just to see the country. That sounds like a lot of work, though. I mean, you’d have to drive for days. Yeah, but it’s a real adventure, you know? I think I’d like to do that. I think I’d like to go somewhere else, though. Maybe Europe? Like, somewhere cheap with good food. Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that too. Europe has so much to offer. I mean, I’ve been to Paris, but I still want to go to Berlin or something.

Alright, do you two want to go to the party tomorrow? It’s at the community hall, and there’s going to be a live band playing. I think it’s going to be really fun. A live band? You mean like the one from the local school? Yeah, the same one. They’ve been practising for ages. I think they’re going to play some of their original songs. It’s going to be a good night out. It’s a good chance to have a laugh and maybe even get a nice photo to put on the wall.

Well, I heard the news about the exam results. You know, I was just watching the telly when they showed some of the results coming out. I’m not sure I like how it’s all done now with all the grades and everything. It seems like a bit of a mess. Yeah, I saw that too. I think the system’s gone too far. My teachers are always telling me I need to do better, and I feel like I’ve got to work so hard to get good grades. It’s not always fun. I know what you mean. I still do, though, just not as much as I used to. I love watching the matches on TV, even if I can’t do much myself anymore. Yeah, I used to play football too. I remember when the school had a team, and we used to go to matches on weekends. It was a good way to clear your head. Now, though, I don’t get out as much. I just stay home and do the things I like. You know, I think the key thing is balance. You have to work hard, but you also have to find time to relax.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to play Chinese chess with your dad every Saturday? It was always the same thing—him setting up the board and me trying to sneak a pawn forward just to see if he’d notice. Yeah, I remember that. You were always trying to get your pieces to move faster than the rules allowed. I think he caught you once and gave you a lecture about the importance of strategy. Not that you were listening, of course. Oh, you were a menace back then. I remember once you tried to move your queen three squares in one go just to see what would happen. Dad made you start over, and you were so annoyed you almost left the table. Oh, you were just like me, you know. I used to do the same thing, push the rules aside because I thought I was clever. But then I learned that Chinese chess isn’t just about moving your pieces—it’s about understanding the board, the flow, the moves of your opponent. Yeah, and it’s funny how those rules still stick with you, even when you’re not playing. I still think about the game every time I see a chessboard, even though I haven’t touched one in years. Speaking of rules, have you ever thought about how different they are from Western chess? I mean, in Chinese chess, the pieces move in a completely different way. It’s like the board is a whole different world. I remember trying to explain it to my sister once, and she said it was like a game from another planet. That’s not far from the truth. The pieces have their own lives, their own movements, and their own stories. I think it’s why I always loved it so much. You’re not just playing a game—you're telling a story. Yeah, and the way the pieces interact with each other is like a lesson in strategy. You can’t just rush ahead. You have to think several moves ahead. It’s like trying to navigate a world you don’t fully understand, but you have to figure it out anyway. Exactly. I think that’s what makes Chinese chess so interesting. It’s not just about winning—it's about understanding the game, the players, and the world it comes from.

So, do you think you’ll be able to get a teaching job in Poland? I mean, you know how it is with the English teachers here—there’s always a lot of them, and the demand isn’t that high. I don’t know, honestly. I mean, it’s not that I don’t like teaching, but the pay isn’t great, and I still have to deal with the bureaucracy. Plus, I’m not sure if I want to be here forever. I think I’d rather go back to the UK eventually. Yeah, I can see that. But you know, I’ve been thinking about working abroad too—maybe somewhere with a better pension system, you know? I mean, in the UK, I’m not even sure if I’ll qualify for a state pension because I haven’t been working for years. I think I’d be better off if I’d stayed in a job longer. That’s true. I mean, I’m not in the best position financially, but I’ve got student loans to pay back, and I’m not sure how I’ll manage it if I don’t get a proper job here. I’m also not sure about the visa situation—do you think it would be easier for me to get a work permit if I was from the UK? I’m not sure. I think it might depend on what country you’re applying to. I mean, I miss the weather, the culture, even the coffee. I’ve been drinking this Polish coffee all week, and it’s different from what I’m used to. It’s not bad, but it’s not the same as the stuff back home. I tried it once. It was like black tea with a hint of something else. I don’t know if it was just the coffee or the water.
