I think it’s more mineral-rich, so it has a different taste.

So, do you know what you're going to study when you go to uni? I mean, I know you're thinking about Human Sciences or maybe something else? Yeah, I think I might go for Human Sciences. It's pretty broad, and I like the idea of studying things like psychology and sociology. Plus, it gives you a lot of options for different careers. That sounds cool. I’ve been thinking about Maths, actually. I like the logic part, but I’m not sure if I’m ready for the pressure. I mean, what if I fail? You’ll get through it. I mean, if you’re passionate about it, you’ll work hard. Plus, you’ve got the rugby team to help you stay focused. Yeah, we’re still on for the match next week, right? Yeah, definitely. I’m looking forward to it. We’re going to need to get some new gear though. My old boots are falling apart. I heard the shop in Westfield has some good rugby boots on sale. Yeah, I saw that too. I think we should go together. I can help you pick out something that fits. And maybe grab a drink while we’re there? For real? That’d be nice. I haven’t had a proper drink in ages, and I know you’re trying to be responsible, but maybe a soft drink or something? I mean, I’m not sure if I’m allowed to drink yet. Yeah, I’m not sure either. But maybe once we’re older, we can try something. Mom always says we can’t drink until we’re 18, but she’s not here to stop us. Anyway, let’s not think about that now. Fair enough. But you know, I’ve been thinking about cooking more. I mean, we both cook sometimes, but I’ve realized I’m not very good at it. I burnt my last attempt at making a lasagna. I can relate. I once tried to make a soufflé and it collapsed like a balloon. I think I scared my mom with that one. She didn’t say anything, but I could tell she was disappointed. Haha, yeah, that’s the kind of stuff that happens when you’re trying to be a chef. But I think we’re both getting better. Maybe we can start a cooking club or something.

Right, right, so I was thinking, love, about how the government's handling things these days. It's all got to do with money, you know. Taxes and how they're used. Yeah, I know. I've been reading a bit about it. It's all a bit confusing, honestly. I mean, I understand the basics, but the policies... it's like they're trying to do one thing, but it feels like they're not really getting it right. It’s not just the policies, luv. It's how the money is being directed. You know how we used to have more of a system where tax was used to build things like roads, schools, and hospitals? Now it feels like a lot of it's going to the wrong places. I heard something about them increasing the national debt. Is that true? Or is that just the government trying to make it sound worse than it is? Hmmm. It’s a bit of both, really. They say they’re investing in the economy, but I don’t see where the money’s really going. I mean, listen, I’ve been in the accountancy business for years, and I can tell you, the figures don’t add up the way they should. I’m not denying that. I just wish I could understand it better. I mean, I teach languages, but even I can’t wrap my head around the way the government talks about money. Well, that’s the problem, isn’t it? They use a lot of jargon. It’s all about ‘fiscal responsibility,’ or ‘economic growth,’ but what does that actually mean? I’ve seen it all in my time. When I was young, the government had a different approach. It was more about what was good for the people, not just what sounded good on the news. That does make sense. I guess the pressure is high. They have to deal with all sorts of issues – inflation, unemployment, all that. But I still think there should be more transparency. We should know exactly where our tax money’s going. Absolutely. I think that’s the main thing. People should have more say in how the money is spent. I mean, I can go out and get a tax return, but I don’t feel like I’m really part of the decision-making. It’s all top-down.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about switching jobs again. I’m just so bored with the same old stuff. I mean, I love the project co-ordination, but it’s starting to feel a bit stale. Oh, I can imagine. You know, after a few years in the same role, even the best jobs start to feel like just another day at the office. What’s making you feel that way? Honestly, it’s just the lack of challenge. I feel like I’m not growing anymore. I keep doing the same tasks, same meetings, same deadlines. It’s like I’m just going through the motions. I know what you mean. I’ve been in the same role for over ten years. I left teaching to do exams management, and I thought it would be more dynamic. I mean, the variety of exams, the different schools, the deadlines – it was all new and exciting at first. That does sound more varied. But I guess I never thought about moving out of the education sector. I mean, I like working with people, but maybe I need something a bit different. You know, I’ve been thinking about that too. I’ve been talking to a few people in the local council about maybe moving into a different area of education policy. It’s not something I’ve really pursued, but I’ve been curious about it. That’s interesting. I never thought about education policy. I mean, I’ve always been more on the operational side. But maybe there are opportunities to move into a more strategic role? Exactly. I think the key is to find something that challenges you in a different way. I’ve been feeling like I’m not using all the skills I’ve developed over the years. I’ve been pretty good at managing people and processes, but I haven’t really had the chance to take that to the next level. I can see what you mean. I guess I’ve been so focused on the day-to-day that I haven’t really looked at the bigger picture. Maybe I should start looking into some professional development courses or networking events. That’s a good idea. It’s always good to stay ahead of the game, especially in the education sector where things are constantly changing. You know, I’ve been thinking of taking some online courses in digital learning and education technology.

So, do you two ever actually get through a whole meal without arguing about something? Oh, come on, Dad. You're the one who insists on putting the ketchup on the table instead of the plate. I mean, it's not like it's a big deal. It's just a condiment. Oh, it's a big deal to me. I've had enough of people spilling ketchup on their shirts. You know, you could just use a spoon. That's not how you do it, Liza. It's about  tradition . Yeah, and tradition is why you still use a fork for everything, even when it's not necessary. Oh, shut up, Tom. I’ve been doing this since I was a kid. I think the real issue is that you’re still using that old silverware set from the 70s, Dad. It’s not old, it’s  classic . Yeah, classic in the same way that your idea of a good wine is a bottle of cheap red that’s been sitting in the cupboard for six months. At least it’s not been opened. I know what I’m doing. You’re not doing anything, Dad. You just keep buying the same bottles and never even finish them. Oh, come on. I think it’s a bonding experience. You’re both pretending to enjoy something that you don’t. I  do  enjoy it. I just don’t have to like it to drink it. Well, I think you should try something new. Like, maybe that Pinot Noir I got from the shop last week. Pinot Noir? That’s for people who are supposed to be  into  wine. I prefer a strong, bold red. And that’s exactly why you’re still stuck in your ways. You’ve never even tried a white wine. I’ve tried white wine. I just don’t  like  it. So, what’s the plan for the weekend? Any chance of getting out of the house? I was thinking maybe we could go to the pub. The one in the village has a new live music act. I’ll pass. I’ve got a job interview tomorrow. Oh, really? Are you applying for something new? Yeah, I thought I’d try my hand at something different. Maybe a job in retail? It’s not like I have anything else to do. You could always apply for a job on the internet.

I can't believe I actually got the conference slot. I mean, I applied like three months ago, and it felt like I was just throwing my CV into a black hole. But apparently, they wanted someone with experience in teaching English as a foreign language, and I guess my background in TEFL counts. That’s great news, really! I was going to say the same thing about the conference. I thought I might have to settle for something more local this year, but then I saw the email come through. It said you were selected to present on the topic of digital tools in the classroom. Yeah, I was nervous at first. I mean, I've never presented at a conference before. But I figured if I don't take the chance, who will? I’ve been wanting to talk about how technology can enhance language learning, and I think there’s a lot to say about it. That sounds really interesting. I’m curious—what kind of digital tools are you planning to focus on? Well, I’ve been using a few apps and online platforms in my own classes, and I’ve noticed a real difference in student engagement. There’s one called LinguaFolio, which helps students keep track of their progress, and then there’s this interactive quiz site that uses gamification. It really makes learning feel less like a chore and more like a game. Oh, I’ve heard of LinguaFolio! I think my sister uses it for her Spanish lessons. I’ve been thinking about using it in my classes too. But honestly, I’ve been a bit overwhelmed with the amount of work that goes into preparing for these conferences. Between grading, lesson planning, and now this, I’m starting to feel like I don’t have enough hours in the day. I can totally relate. I’ve been trying to manage everything, but sometimes I feel like I’m just running on fumes. I mean, I love teaching, but when work starts to take over your life, it's easy to feel burnt out. You’re not alone in that. I remember when I first started teaching, I thought I’d be able to balance everything with ease. Now, it’s like there’s always something on the horizon. But I think it’s worth it. I mean, how else would we learn and grow?

I can't believe we've made it this far. I still feel like we're just starting out. Yeah, I know. I’m more used to driving in cities, not on highways with no traffic. It’s quite different. I wouldn’t say it’s easy. I mean, there’s the language barrier, the directions, and the fact that I’ve never been to Poland before. That’s true. But honestly, I think we’re doing pretty well. We’ve got the map, the GPS, and the camcorder to record everything. Yeah, I’m just hoping we don’t end up stuck in some small village with no signal and no one to help. Don’t worry, I’ve got the satellite phone. I don’t know how I’d get through without it. That’s reassuring. I still can’t believe I’m driving a campervan in Eastern Europe. I used to teach in a classroom, not on the road. I know, it’s a bit of a change, but it’s also exciting. You get to see so much more. I mean, we’ve already passed some beautiful countryside. Yeah, it’s nice. I remember reading about the Polish countryside in my books. I never thought I’d see it. You know what’s funny? I used to think that travel was something for people who had more time. Now, here I am, driving through Poland with a map and a camera. That’s the thing, isn’t it? Even if you’re not young, you can still make the most of your time. Exactly. And I think this trip is going to be more than just a holiday. I’ve been thinking about volunteering abroad, and this could be the start of that. That’s a good point. I’ve been thinking about doing something like that too. Maybe helping out with language programs or something. I think you’d be great at it. You’ve always been passionate about teaching. It’s just a different setting. I know, but I’m feeling a bit rusty. I go to the gym sometimes, but it’s not regular. I think I need to get back into shape. You should. I mean, we’re in a campervan, so we might as well make the most of it. Maybe we can stop at some parks on the way and do a bit of hiking or something.

So, do you know what’s really interesting about the Vikings? I was reading this article the other day about how they were actually quite advanced in terms of their medicine and their understanding of the human body. It’s a bit surprising because you think of them as raiders and warriors, but they had some pretty cool knowledge. Yeah, I remember reading that they used herbal remedies and even had some kind of surgical techniques. But I also heard that they were really into astrology and divination. Like, they’d use the stars to predict the best time to go on a raid or something? Exactly! And I think they also had some kind of system for tracking time, which is pretty impressive for their era. But let’s talk about something else. I’ve been thinking a lot about aging lately. I mean, I’m not getting too old yet, but I’ve heard a lot about telomeres and how they’re linked to aging. Do you know much about that? A bit, honestly. I remember that telomeres are those protective caps on the ends of chromosomes, right? They get shorter each time a cell divides, and when they get too short, the cell can’t divide anymore and dies. So it’s like a clock inside our cells. But I don’t know how much of that is real – I mean, I’ve heard people say that certain things can lengthen telomeres, like exercise or a healthy diet. Is that even possible? It’s a hot topic in gerontology. Some studies suggest lifestyle choices can influence telomere length, but it’s definitely not a magic bullet. Still, it’s fascinating to think that something as simple as diet or stress management could have such a big impact on how we age. That’s true. I guess I’ve always thought of aging as something you just can’t stop, but it’s interesting to hear that there might be ways to slow it down. Although, honestly, I’m not sure I want to live to 120. I think I’d rather have a long, healthy life than a really long one with all the aging problems. Heh, I can relate. I think I’d like to be 80 and still have the energy to travel. I’ve been planning a trip to Iceland for next year, and I’d love to hike up some of those volcanic areas.

So, do you reckon we should go to the new café in town tomorrow? I heard the coffee’s really good. I don’t know, I thought we were going to try the one by the beach. The one with the outdoor seating. Yeah, that’s the one. But I saw the new place has a proper coffee machine, not just that little instant thing they have over there. Maybe we should go there. Yeah, I like the idea. It’s got a bit more atmosphere. Plus, the guy who owns it said he buys his beans from a local roastery. That’s nice, isn’t it? That’s a good point. But I’m not sure about the price. I don’t want to pay too much for just a coffee. It’s not that expensive. A cappuccino is like £2.50. Wait, is that not too much? I mean, I’ve seen places in the city charge more than that. I think it’s fair. Especially since they have free pastries with the coffee. That’s a bonus, right? Yeah, that might be worth it. But what about the vouchers we got from the supermarket? We could use those for the coffee. It’s a bit of a treat. Good idea. I’ve been meaning to use those. But I don’t know if we should go all out. I mean, we’ve got the baby chair now, but it’s still a bit of a hassle to move around. Oh, the baby chair is great. I can’t believe we got it so quickly. It’s so comfortable, and it even has a little storage compartment for the baby’s things. Yeah, it’s very practical. But are we going to need it for the café? I mean, if we just go for coffee, maybe not. Unless we plan to sit outside with the baby. Exactly. If we take the baby, it might be too hot out. I don’t know if we should risk that. Let’s just go without her for now. Maybe the next time. Yeah, that sounds safer. I mean, it’s not like the baby can go out in the sun anyway. We don’t want her to get sunburned. Right. But maybe we can get some sunglasses for her. The ones with the little visors. I saw them at the market last week.

So, do you think we should get a new Christmas tree this year? I was just thinking it’s been a few years since we had one. Honestly, I think it’s time. The old one is starting to look a bit scruffy, and I bet it wouldn’t even stand up in the corner without falling over. Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s been a bit of a struggle trying to keep it upright. But I don’t want to spend too much. I mean, it’s just a tree, right? I get that. But you know, I think we could get one that’s a bit more flexible. Maybe the ones that are bendy? Or like the ones you can put in a corner and it just stands on its own. Oh, I’ve seen those. The ones that have a metal frame inside, you know? They’re pretty popular, aren’t they? I mean, they’re not too expensive and they’re more stable. Exactly. I think that could work. But I was just thinking, maybe we could get a tree that’s a bit bigger. I feel like the one we had last year was a bit too small. It didn’t even fill the room. Yeah, I think that’s true. I mean, the room is quite big, and the tree just looked like a tiny little thing. I don’t know, maybe we could go for one that’s more decorative, too. Like, someone said there are ones with lights that change colours. Oh, I love that idea. It would make the whole house feel more magical. I mean, I’m not one for the traditional Christmas tree, but I do like the idea of having something that really stands out. I think that could be nice. But then again, I have to think about the mess. I mean, I don’t know if I’m up for cleaning up all the tinsel and ornaments again. Last year was a bit of a nightmare. You’re not the only one who thinks that. I remember Auntie Margaret saying the same thing about the tinsel. But you know, the kids really love it. I think they’d be sad if the tree was too small or too plain. True. They do have such high expectations. I mean, between them and the box of chocolates we got last year, they’re like two little Christmas elves.

So, do you feel like this place is finally settling in? I mean, it's our first day here and already I’m starting to get used to the layout. Yeah, I think so. I think it’s probably better to have one just in case. Although I’m not sure if we’ll need it. Maybe we can just use our mobiles for now. True. Although the Wi-Fi seems okay already. I mean, it’s only our first day, but I’d like to get the kitchen going. Yeah, that’s a good idea. Maybe something simple like a stir-fry or a pasta dish. I’ve got a few recipes on my phone. I think we can manage. Perfect. And while we’re at it, we should check the rubbish collection schedule. I don’t want to miss the bin day and end up with a pile of trash by the door. Definitely. I’ll check the council website tomorrow. Also, I was thinking about the seasonal produce. I read somewhere that the local market in Brighton has really good organic stuff.

So how’s life treating you since you started the graduate placement? Still loving it? Honestly, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. Some days I feel like I’m on top of the world, and others I’m just surviving. But I’m learning a lot, and I think it’s helping me figure out what I want to do next. That sounds like a good sign. It’s just the usual balancing act, you know? Totally. I think we’re all just trying to juggle work, life, and the occasional holiday. But it’s important to find that balance. Speaking of balance, how’s your family? I know it’s been a while since we last caught up. My parents are doing well, actually. They just moved into a new house in the countryside, so it’s been a big change for them. I visit them every weekend, and it’s nice to have some quiet time with them. That’s great. I’ve been meaning to visit my parents more too. They’ve been asking about how I’m doing, and I think it’s been a while since I’ve gone. Yeah, I know.

So, how’s the PhD going? Still surviving in the land of endless cups of coffee and questionable lighting? Oh, you know, the usual. I’ve got a few chapters left, but I’m starting to feel like I’m just rephrasing things I’ve already written in slightly different words. It’s like my brain is on a loop. I know the feeling. I spent a year writing that report for my research management role, and I swear I could still recite it in my sleep. But hey, at least you’re in Cambridge. I’ve never been to Cambridge. I’ve only been to the North East, which is basically the same as the rest of England, but with more rain and fewer people who know how to use a comma. You’re joking, right? Cambridge is a special place. I mean, the history, the academia, the architecture—it’s like a character in a novel. You can’t just say "I’ve only been to the North East" and call it a day. You have to have a proper experience. I get it, but I’ve never been anywhere that doesn’t have a postcode. I mean, I’ve been to Newcastle, and I’ve been to Sunderland—both of them have postcodes, and both of them have amazing fish and chips. But I’ve never been to somewhere that’s  just  Cambridge. You’re missing out. You should come up one day. I’ll take you to the old town, show you the punts, maybe even get you a pint of real ale. It’s not all just books and lectures—it’s got real life in there too. Yeah, but I’ve got about five projects on the go right now. I’m still trying to keep up with my research, let alone take a trip to Cambridge. Although, I have to say, I do miss the Northern accent. It’s got that kind of gritty charm that you just can’t get in the Midlands or the South. Oh, I hear you. I’ve been getting teased for being from Birmingham—people think I sound like a robot. But I’ve got a little bit of a Northern accent from growing up in the North East, so I can still say things like "cheerio" and "laddie" like I’m still at home. It’s like a little bit of home in the middle of all this academic madness.

Grandpa, I heard you were talking about the election the other day. What did you think of it? Oh, I thought it was a bit of a mess, to be honest. The way the politicians keep changing their minds, it’s like they don’t even know what they believe anymore. Yeah, I guess that’s true. I mean, I don’t know much about politics, but I do know that people are getting more and more frustrated with the way things are going. That’s right. I remember when I was your age, politics was a lot simpler. You had clear parties with clear ideas, and people knew where they stood. Now, it’s all about spin and soundbites. I guess it’s harder to trust anyone these days. I mean, how do you know if what they say is real or if they’re just trying to get votes? Exactly. I’ve been watching politics for a long time, and I’ve seen it change a lot. Back in my day, people had more time to think about issues. Now, everything’s so fast, and people just want quick answers. I don’t think I’ll ever get the hang of it. I mean, I remember when I was in primary school, we used to learn about the Royal Family and stuff like that. Now, it’s all about the economy and Brexit and stuff. Oh, Brexit was a big one. It was a huge decision, and it changed everything. I remember when it was all a big debate, and people were shouting about it in the shops and on the buses. Yeah, I remember hearing people talking about it at school. My teacher said it was about leaving the EU, but I didn’t really understand why it was such a big deal. Well, it was a lot more than that. It was about trade, immigration, and even national identity. It was a big moment for the country, and it still affects things today. I guess I’m just glad I don’t have to worry about that stuff right now. I’m still in school, and I’ve got exams to worry about. That’s the thing with growing up. You get to see the world change around you, but you don’t have to deal with the consequences just yet. It’s a bit like being a kid—everything’s wide open, and you don’t have to make the tough decisions.

So, do you remember the last time we had a blood moon? I think it was last year when we were all out in Fitzgeralds Park. It was like a full moon, but it looked kinda red, right? Yeah, I remember that. It was really cool. We were all in the car, and my mum kept saying it was like the end of the world or something. But it was just a blood moon, wasn’t it? Oh, I remember that too. I was supposed to be babysitting the kids, but I ended up outside with them anyway. It was such a beautiful sight. I think even the dog was looking up at it. That was quite a night. My son was here with his family, and we all gathered in the garden. We had the kids running around, and then the moon came up and it was so bright, you could see everything. I must say, it was one of the most memorable evenings I’ve had in a long time. Yeah, it’s amazing how the moon can change like that. I mean, it’s not like we see it every day, is it? Especially not a blood moon. It’s got to be rare, right? I think it happens a few times a decade. I remember my gran used to talk about them, like, it was a sign of something. But I’m not sure if that’s true or not. I think it’s just a natural phenomenon, though. Oh, my gran always used to tell stories about the moon. She said that if you’re out at night and see a blood moon, it’s a sign that someone in your family is going to have a big change. I think she was just trying to scare the kids, though. Maybe she was right. I mean, I’ve had a lot of changes in my life the last few years. Work, moving, starting a new job. It’s been quite a rollercoaster. But I think the moon was just there, watching over us. That’s the thing about the moon, though. It’s always there, isn’t it? Even when we’re not thinking about it. It’s like a constant reminder of how vast the universe is. And how small we are in it. That’s kind of spooky, in a way. I mean, it’s comforting, but also a little terrifying.

So, do you know what’s been on my mind all week? That Scottish referendum. I just can’t get it off my mind. I mean, I’m from Brighton, but I’ve got a cousin who lives in Glasgow, and he’s been pretty vocal about it. Yeah, I heard about that. I think the country’s got bigger issues than that, but I can see why people are passionate about it. I guess it’s about identity, you know? Alright, let’s get this sorted out. So, the parent’s evening came and went, and I got a few things to take on board. So, do you know what’s the funniest word game you’ve ever played? I mean, like, the ones where you have to come up with words that start or end with certain letters or something? I think the hardest part is when you’re stuck and you can’t think of a word. Sometimes you just have to go with a weird combination just to make it work. So, do you remember that time we tried to sleep in the back of the van on our road trip? I just got a call from the council. They've agreed to let us put in an application for the planning committee meeting next week. It's about the new housing development near the river. I’ve been thinking about it, but I’m still not sure. I guess I’m also nervous about leaving Cambridge. It’s where I’ve felt most at home. I understand. But sometimes, moving is the best way to grow. You could always come back later, you know. Yeah, I guess. But what if I don’t fit in at Oxford? What if I feel out of place? You’ll find your place, just like you did here. You’re not just a student—your personality and ideas are unique. Oxford will have to make space for you. I hope so. I just want to make the right decision. You’re not alone in that. We’ll support you no matter where you go. Thanks, Mum. I really appreciate that. Of course. You know, I was thinking about our own lives. I always imagined myself waiting at the gates of a university, cheering on the students as they walked through. That’s a funny thought. I wonder what I’ll be doing in ten years. I hope you’ll still be doing something you love. Whether it’s at Oxford or somewhere else, I just want you to be happy. I want that too. I just need to figure out what that looks like. It’ll come. You’ve always had a strong sense of direction, even when you didn’t realize it. I hope so.

So, do you know much about the history of the region around Cambridge? I was just reading about some ancient settlements that were discovered nearby. I’ve heard a bit about it. There were some interesting excavations in the 1980s near Trumpington. They found remnants of a Bronze Age village, which was quite unusual for that area. Yes, I’ve actually been involved in a few projects like that. The area around Cambridge has a rich archaeological history. In fact, some of the earliest known settlements in the region date back to the Neolithic period. The people there lived in wooden huts and had a complex system of trade. That’s fascinating. I’ve always been interested in how languages and cultures evolve over time. Do you think the language of the early inhabitants had any influence on modern English? Absolutely. The region was inhabited by various Celtic tribes, and while their language is mostly lost, some words and phrases have survived in place names and dialects. For example, the word "Cambridge" itself has roots in the Old English word "Camber," which referred to a river or a place where people gathered. That’s interesting. I’ve also heard that there were some Roman influences in the area. The Romans built a road known as the Akeman Street, which ran through what is now Cambridge. Did they have any impact on the local language? Yes, the Romans introduced Latin, which influenced the local dialects and even led to the development of some place names. But the real linguistic shift came with the Anglo-Saxons, who brought Old English. It's amazing how layers of history and language stack up over time. I’ve been working on a project involving language revitalization in minority communities. I was wondering if there are any efforts to preserve or revive ancient dialects or languages in England? There are, but it's quite challenging. Some dialects are at risk of disappearing, especially with younger generations moving away from traditional areas. However, there are some community-based initiatives that focus on documenting and teaching these dialects. And don’t forget the impact of Chinese and Arab cultures on the region, too. While not directly related to the local dialects, the influence of foreign languages has always been a part of England's history, especially through trade and migration. That’s true. I’ve been studying the evolution of languages and how they adapt to new influences.

Alright, so I just saw this viral video on TikTok about a student who was accused of cheating because they couldn’t read the exam paper properly. It was like,  oh no , they were dyslexic and the whole class was judging them. It made me think—how come we’re still not having proper discussions about dyslexia in schools? I know, right? I’ve had friends who struggled with reading and writing, but they were always told they just weren’t trying hard enough. It’s so frustrating because it’s not about effort—it’s about how your brain processes information. I mean, I’ve got a friend who’s a baker, like me, and she’s dyslexic. She’s got a brilliant mind for baking, but when it comes to spelling or reading, it’s a different story. Yeah, and I think it’s tied up with class too, isn’t it? Like, if you come from a working-class background, you’re more likely to have undiagnosed dyslexia, or even if you are diagnosed, the support isn’t there. I mean, I grew up in Birmingham, and my parents never really understood why I couldn’t read the same way as the other kids. They thought I was lazy—until I got to university and then it got sorted out. It’s such a shame that the system doesn’t support people like us. Exactly. It’s not just about the individual. It’s about how the education system is set up. I mean, someone like me—film and photography producer—had to fight for every opportunity. I wasn’t even sure I’d get into university, and I had to do a lot of extra work to prove myself. I think people like us—those from lower socioeconomic backgrounds—have such a different experience when it comes to education. It’s not just about grades; it’s about the support structures you have around you. And then there’s the whole generation gap. I mean, we’re all young people now. We’re not being raised with the same stigma around things like dyslexia or learning difficulties. There’s more awareness, more understanding. But I still see the same old attitudes in schools and workplaces. It’s like, “Oh, you can’t read this? Try harder.” That’s so outdated. I think it’s also about how we define success.

So, do you think we should be making more of an effort to talk about money around the house? I mean, we’ve been together for years, but I still don’t know how much you earn, or what your pension looks like. It’s not like we’re not going to be around forever, is it? Honestly, I think it’s ridiculous that we’re still not on the same page with this. I mean, I’ve been trying to talk about it for months, but you just keep deflecting. You say things like, “We’re both earning enough,” or “We’ll figure it out when the time comes.” But when does  the time come , love? I’m not deflecting. I’m just not comfortable with it. I think it’s personal. I mean, I know you earn a decent salary, I know you’re in a stable job, and I’ve seen your pension statements. But I don’t need to know  every  detail. It’s not like we’re not in a position where we need to be careful with money. I mean, look at the state of the economy—there’s inflation, rising rents, and the cost of living is through the roof. Yeah, but we’re both in higher professional occupations. We’re not just surviving. We’re actually doing pretty well, fairly speaking. But I do think we should be more open about it. It’s not just about the numbers—it’s about planning for the future. What if something happens? What if someone gets sick? What if we need to move or change our lifestyle? I know, I know. It’s just that I feel like I’ve been putting it off for so long. I mean, I’ve always been the type to avoid the uncomfortable topics. And I think part of it is that I don’t want to feel like I’m putting pressure on you. Maybe I just don’t want to talk about it because it feels like a conversation that could bring up old insecurities or unspoken fears. I get that. I think we both have a tendency to avoid things that feel like they might lead to conflict. But I do think we need to start having these conversations more often. Not just about money, but about our health, our plans, our goals. I mean, I’ve been thinking about retirement more recently, and I’d like to know where we stand.

Well, I've just made some roast potatoes and a bit of gravy. I thought it would be nice to have a proper lunch today, especially with the weather being so good outside. That sounds lovely, thank you. I’m really glad you’re feeling up to cooking. I’ve been meaning to try some new recipes, but I haven’t got the time with work and everything. Oh, you should take some time for yourself, lass. I remember when I was still teaching, I used to cook every Sunday. It was a way to unwind and spend time with the kids. You know, those little ones always loved sitting around the table and helping me with the food. That’s so sweet of you, Mr. Thompson. I wish I had someone to cook for, or someone who would take the time to sit down and enjoy a meal. It feels like everything’s always on the go these days. I know what you mean, love. It’s not just about the food, it’s about the company. I’ve been thinking about how much I miss the old days when the whole family would gather around the table, even if we were just having chips and a few bottles of something. Yes, and the conversations. Those were the best. You could talk about anything – politics, sport, even the school plays. There was never a dull moment. I miss that too. Nowadays, people seem to be more on their phones than talking to each other. I found myself thinking about that the other day when I was at the supermarket. I was just standing there, and I saw a couple of young people arguing over something – I don’t even remember what it was. That’s the thing, isn’t it? We were lucky to have a house where everyone could gather. I remember you used to take us out to the countryside on Sundays. My kids loved that. They’d always be excited about going out and seeing the birds or the cows. Oh, I had a bit of a knack for that. I could always make them feel at home. Even the most shy of them would come out of their shells when we were out and about. That’s something I’d love to do with my own family. I really need to figure out how to balance work and family life properly.

So, do you remember how we used to play with the soft toys when we were kids, Eamon? It’s like the days when we had those big, fluffy ones that you could throw around the living room. Yeah, I remember, Dad. But you were always the one who was trying to get the biggest one, and I’d just sit there and watch you. You were like a kid again. Oh, I remember that too. I used to love watching you two play, especially when you’d try to make the soft toys do tricks. Remember when you tried to make the teddy bear dance? Oh, that was a disaster. I tried to make it move with the remote control, and it just fell over. You were laughing so hard you couldn’t stop. Yeah, and then I tried to help and made it fall even harder. It was like a comedy act, honestly. Anyway, I was just thinking about how Eamon’s getting into that kind of play now. He’s got that soft toy he brought home from school – it’s the one with the little plastic eyes and everything. He puts it on the floor and starts talking to it like it’s a friend. That’s cute. He’s got a good imagination. I think it’s good for him, you know? It’s not just about the toys; it’s about how they help him express himself. I remember when I was his age, I used to make up all sorts of stories for the toys. Yeah, and I still do. Even now, when I’m at home and I feel like I need a break, I’ll get one of my old toys and just sit there and talk to it. It’s weird, but it helps. I think it’s part of growing up. You have to find ways to cope, especially with a toddler around. I’ve been trying to do more of that – just sit and think, or read, or play with the kids. It’s not always easy, but it helps. Exactly. I know being a parent is tough, but it’s also the best thing. I mean, the way he plays with his toys, the way he talks to them, it’s like he’s learning how to be a person. And you, Eamon, you’re showing him that it’s okay to be creative, to be silly, to be you.

Right, right, we've got to get the Christmas dinner sorted. I've been thinkin’ about it all week. Oh, I’m so looking forward to it. It’s been ages since we had a proper family meal. I’ve got the turkey in the fridge, and I’ve also got the mince pies ready. That’s great, but I’m still not sure if I’ve got enough guests. I think I need to call a few more people. The kids are coming, of course, and we’ve got the cousins from Birmingham. Yeah, I’m coming too. I’ve got my art project to show off, so I’ll bring that along. Cool, I’ll bring my horse pictures. I got a new one from the school art class. You’ll love it, it’s of a horse jumping over a fence. Oh, I love that. I’ve always had a soft spot for horses. Though I don’t know how I’d manage to ride one, I’m afraid. You’d be surprised, Frank. I’ve had some experience with horses when I was teaching. A few of the kids were into riding, and I even did a few lessons with them. Oh, I remember that. You were very good with the kids, weren’t you? You had a real way with them. It was a lot of fun, actually. I don’t know if I’d have stayed in teaching if it wasn’t for the kids. They kept me smiling. That’s the thing, though. You can’t really talk about anything else when you’ve got a horse, or a kid, about you. You’re always busy. Well, I guess that’s a good thing. I mean, life is busy enough without worrying about Christmas dinner and horses. Yeah, but I like the chaos. It keeps things interesting. Though I have to admit, I’m a bit nervous about the car journey. You’re not the only one. I had to take the kids to a football match last week, and I nearly missed the ferry. It took me almost two hours just to get there. Oh, I can go on about my car journey from Harrow to Norfolk. I think I once got stuck in a queue for over an hour, and the car started to make some weird noise. I had to get it towed.

So, do you know what’s on my mind, Fran? I was thinking about our old friend Sarah from university. She’s been working in marketing for years now, and I’ve heard she’s been promoted to a senior role at that agency in London. That’s pretty impressive for someone who started out as an intern. Yeah, I remember her from the time we all used to hang out in that café on the high street. She always had this way of making everyone feel important, even when she was just pulling pints. Who’d have thought she’d end up in the corporate world? Honestly, I still remember the time she tried to convince us all to start a business selling handmade candles. She said it was the future, and I swear she even had a sample in her bag. I think it was just a way to get us all to buy her drinks. Oh, and she definitely had a flair for the dramatic. I still remember the time she accidentally set a candle on fire and had to run out of the café screaming. We all thought she was joking, but she was dead serious. I still get a laugh out of that story every time someone brings up candles. Anyway, what about you, Jess? How’s the copywriting gig going? You’ve been working on that new campaign for the local café, right? Oh, it’s going well, thanks. The café owner is really keen on the idea of having a more modern look, and I’m helping them rebrand. It’s been a fun project, and I’ve actually been doing a lot of research into the local market. It’s interesting to see what people are into these days. Sounds like you’re getting a lot out of it. I wish I had your kind of creative energy. I’m stuck in the same old routine at the hospital, day in, day out. You know, I’ve been thinking about taking up some sort of hobby. I’ve been trying to get into something like gardening or maybe even painting. It’s just that I haven’t had the time or the motivation. Maybe I should start with something small. That’s a good idea, really. I’ve been trying to get into cooking more, and I’ve even started making my own bread.

I don’t know, I just feel like things have changed so much. I remember when we used to go to the park and the kids would play outside all day, and now it’s all screens and everything. Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s like the world’s gone mad. I saw a man walking his dog the other day, and the dog was running off with a tennis ball, and he just stood there shouting at it like it was a criminal. That’s not so bad. I mean, I still walk my dog every morning, and it’s a good way to clear my head. Still, I do miss the days when we used to go to the local church and everyone knew each other. I think that’s what people miss, the sense of community. It’s not like that anymore. I mean, even the church is different now. They have these fancy activities and everything. I don’t know, it all feels a bit too modern for me. I suppose it is a bit. I still go to church sometimes, but it’s not the same as it used to be. You don’t see as many people, and the conversations are shorter. Yeah, it’s funny, isn’t it? I remember when the church used to have these big events and everyone would come together. Now, the only time people come is when there’s a funeral or a wedding. And even those are different now. I mean, my cousin got married last year, and it was all done online. You couldn’t even tell who was there. It was strange. I heard about that. I think people are just getting used to it. You can’t blame them, really. It’s all about convenience now. I mean, I still like having a proper party, though. Maybe that’s the old-fashioned way. I can’t imagine not having a proper party. I remember my wife’s birthday was always the biggest event of the year. We had cake, dancing, and everyone turned up. That’s the thing about growing up, isn’t it? You remember the good times, and you wish you could have them again. But the world moves on, and you just have to adapt. Speaking of adapting, I’m trying to get used to the new heating system in the house.

So, do you know what’s on tonight? I’ve been meaning to catch that new film about that guy who’s got the same name as his dad, you know the one? Yeah, I saw it at the cinema last week. Was it good? Honestly, it was alright, but I thought the plot was a bit confusing. I mean, it’s not like it’s a complex story, but the way they kept cutting between scenes made it hard to follow. I watched it with my mum, and she kept saying, “Wait, what’s going on?” Haha, that’s classic. I remember watching that with my brother, and he kept asking, “Why is the guy in the movie still pretending he doesn’t know his dad’s a serial killer?” Oh, I didn’t even get that part. I just thought he was a normal guy with a bit of a temper. But then I started thinking, maybe it was a metaphor for something? Like, maybe he’s not actually the son? That’s what I thought too! I mean, the way they kept hinting at the past, like with all the flashbacks and the grief he’s got. It’s like he’s stuck in the same cycle as his dad. That’s why I think the ending made sense, even if it was a bit predictable. Yeah, I don’t know. I still think it was a bit of a mess. But maybe I just didn’t get it. My sister said she liked it because it made her think about family stuff. I guess it’s a good film if you’re into that kind of thing. Definitely. I think it’s more about the themes than the actual plot. Although, I still can’t believe they didn’t explain what the guy’s sister was doing all that time. It felt like a huge plot hole to me. I know, right? I thought it was going somewhere, but then it just ended up going nowhere. Like, he could’ve done something about it, but he just kept being passive. It was frustrating. Yeah, and then there was the whole subplot with the girlfriend. Was that even necessary? Honestly, I think the director just wanted to show that even in a messed-up family, there can be love. But I still don’t see how it ties in with the main story.

So, do you know what’s going on with the Scottish referendum? I’ve been trying to keep up with it, but it’s all a bit confusing. Yeah, I know. It’s a big deal, isn’t it? I mean, I’ve heard people talking about it at school. They say it’s about whether Scotland should leave the UK and become its own country. Right. And I think it’s coming up soon, isn’t it? I remember hearing something about a vote in the next few months. Yeah, I think it’s supposed to be in the autumn. I’m not sure exactly when, though. I think it’s the same way as other elections, like when we vote for Parliament. Mmm. Well, I think it’s important because Scotland has its own Parliament now, but it still has to follow the rules of the UK. So if they vote to leave, then they’d have to sort out their own government and everything else. Yeah, that’s what I heard. But why would they want to leave? I mean, the UK is part of the EU too, right? And Scotland gets a lot of money from the UK government. That’s a good point. I think some people feel that Scotland is treated unfairly by the UK government. They say they pay more taxes and get less back. That’s why they want to have more control over their own money and decisions. Oh, I see. So it’s about independence and control over their own future? It makes sense, I guess. But I don’t know much about it. I mean, I know it’s a big deal, but I’m not sure about all the details. It definitely is a big deal. I think a lot of people are worried about what would happen if Scotland votes to leave. Would it cause problems with the rest of the UK? Would it affect the economy? I think there are a lot of arguments on both sides. Yeah, I’ve heard people on the news talking about it. Some people support independence, and some people don’t. It’s a really big decision, isn’t it? Definitely. I think it’s important that everyone has the chance to vote and have their say. It’s about democracy, isn’t it? People getting to choose what they think is best for their country.

I can't believe how thick that bloke sounds on the Jeremy Kyle show. It's like he's been living in a cave for the last twenty years. Yeah, I know, right? I mean, he's supposed to be a journalist, not a poet. And yet he keeps using these weird words like "thou" and "thee." It's like he's trying to sound like he's from the Elizabethan era. I don’t even know how he got on the show. I mean, he's got the accent of someone who’s lived in a council flat in Liverpool for thirty years. It’s not even close to being a proper accent. It’s like he’s trying to be posh but he’s just not good at it. I think it’s the elision, though. Like, he just drops the endings of words so much, it’s hard to understand. I swear he said "I've been wanting to talk about this for ages" but it came out like "I've been wanin’ to talk abou’ this for ages." It’s like he’s reading from a script that’s written in a different language. And don’t get me started on the way he says "British." He says it like it’s “Bri-tish.” Like he’s trying to make it sound foreign. It’s ridiculous. I mean, we’re all British, and it’s not even that hard to say the word properly. I think it’s just part of the show. They probably use him because he’s got a strong accent and people find it entertaining. Or maybe they want to make it look like the show is more diverse or something. I don’t know. I mean, the show is supposed to be for people who don’t have a lot of money or time to get educated. So, maybe they’re trying to make it more accessible by using people with different accents. But honestly, it just makes me want to switch channels. I’ve tried to watch it before, but I just can’t take the accent. I mean, it’s not like it’s a language barrier or anything, but it’s just so difficult to follow. I get lost halfway through the first sentence. I think it’s funny, honestly. If he was from the North, like us, he’d be saying things like “I’m agin’ your face” and “I’m not havin’ it.”

I can't believe the amount of money they're spending on that striker. I mean, he's only been on the team for a couple of months and already they're talking about signing him for like, double what he was worth. I know, it's just so strange. I mean, he’s not even the best player on the team. I think the manager’s just trying to get some headlines, you know? A lot of money for a player who’s not even that good. Yeah, it’s just so out of touch. I mean, I understand that clubs want to win, but this is just ridiculous. I feel like every season it's the same thing—buying players for way over what they’re worth, and then they don’t even play. I think part of it is the way the media feeds into it. They make it seem like these players are the be-all and end-all, but honestly, I think it's just marketing. And don’t get me started on the transfers, you know? I mean, how many players do you think actually even get to play? I mean, I guess it’s part of the sport now. You can’t really blame the clubs for wanting to win, but it's just so frustrating when it's not about the game anymore. I remember when I was a kid, it was all about the passion and the skill. Now it's all about the money. Yeah, I get that. I mean, I still enjoy watching the games, but I can’t help but feel like something’s been lost. I think the game is becoming more about the money and less about the actual sport. I guess it’s just how things have changed. I wonder if the next generation of fans will even care about the same things. Maybe they’ll be more focused on the teams and the stories, not the players. I mean, I’ve been knitting for a while now, and it's kind of surprising how much the patterns can change. It's like the game, in a way. That’s true. I mean, I’ve been learning to knit too, and it’s kind of the same with the Olympics. People are starting to care more about the stories and the athletes themselves, not just the medals.

So, do you remember The Bee Movie? I think it’s one of those films that’s just… weird. I mean, I love it, but I’m not sure I can explain it to anyone who hasn’t seen it. I remember it! It was the one with the bee who wanted to be a rock star, right? I think he was called Jerry? Yeah, and he wanted to be a singer. He even had this big, loud voice. But then he ended up pulling a bee hive out of his bottom? That part was so random. Oh my god, that part is iconic. I mean, it’s not like bees are supposed to do that. It was like a comedy of errors. But I still watched it every time it came on. I think it’s kind of a cult classic now. Yeah, and I think it’s got something to do with the whole idea of working hard and wanting to be successful in your own way, even if it doesn’t make sense to others. Like the bees in the movie, they were all following their dream, even if it was a bit… off. I think it made me think about wanting to be someone famous. Like, maybe I wanted to be a singer when I was younger. Though I don’t think I had the talent, and I definitely didn’t have the hive. Haha, you’re not the only one. I used to think that if I could just be famous, I could be happy. But I think now I’m more into being content with what I have. Though, I have to say, I still wish I could sing like a bee. Wait, did you know that Queen Elizabeth II used to love bees? I think she had a whole garden full of them. She even had a special beekeeping role. It’s kind of strange to think she was so into something so… tiny. Yeah, and I heard that there’s a new royal event coming up where they’re going to have a bee theme. I don’t know if it’s because of climate change or something. I mean, bees are important, right? Without them, we can’t have fruits. Exactly! I think the royal family even go to special places to see if the bees are doing well. But I also heard rumors that they’re thinking about making the UK a republic.

So, do you know, I was just thinking about how much easier everything was back in the day when we didn’t have to worry about all this technology and stuff. Just a bit of a walk, a bit of clearing out, and that was it. No need for a tip, no need for a café. Just a bit of fresh air and a bit of gardening. I know what you mean, but you’ve got to admit, now we have this stuff, it makes things a lot more efficient. I mean, if we didn’t have the internet and all that, how would we even know about the auctions? Or the things we can do with our garden? Yeah, but I think it’s like that old saying, “No pain, no gain.” If we didn’t have to clear out the old things, we’d still be living in the same house as our granddad. And I’d still be playing with my old toys. Haha, you’re not the only one. I used to have this old television that was so heavy, I could barely move it. I still remember the way it used to flicker and crackle like it was a live thing. It was like having a window into another world, you know? Oh, I remember those. I used to watch the old Royal Variety Show, and I used to dream about being on the stage. Now, I just watch them through my tablet. It’s got the same feeling, though, just a bit more… digital. I suppose it is a bit more digital, but I still think there’s something special about live events. Like the stag or hen parties – even if they’re a bit over the top, there’s something about sharing the moment with the people you care about. Yeah, and I think it’s easier to plan now. I mean, we can book that celebration with a few clicks. Back in the day, you had to actually phone somewhere and wait for a reply. It was so much slower. It is, but I think there’s a downside too. You can’t really get that personal connection anymore with people. I mean, you can have a hundred followers, but that doesn’t mean you’re truly connected. That’s true. I think it’s like our social history – it’s been changed so much, but somehow, we still find a way to keep it real.

I just got a text from the museum about the new exhibit opening next week. You should come with me, it’s got some really cool stuff on local history. Oh, really? That sounds interesting. I was thinking about going to the museum anyway, but I haven't had the chance to check out the new things. What’s the name of the exhibit again? It’s called “Echoes of the Past.” They’re doing some interactive stuff, like virtual reality tours of old Liverpool. I think it’s a bit different from the usual museum stuff. That does sound cool. I like the idea of being able to walk through history. But wait, I heard there’s a parking fee now. My car’s not the best for long drives. Yeah, they’ve started charging for parking, which is a bit of a pain. I’m thinking of taking the bus. Do you want me to grab us tickets online before we go? That’s a good idea. I can check the website and see what time the exhibit starts. I was also thinking about getting a few books for the kids. Do you have any recommendations? I’ve been meaning to get some books for the kids too. I think there’s a new set of children’s books about local history that’s been released. I can pick those up on the way back from the museum. Perfect. I’ll also check if there are any workshops happening while we’re there. Our kids always enjoy the activities. Oh, and I read that the museum is doing a special Christmas display this year. Would you like to go with me and take the kids? That would be great. I’ve been meaning to take the kids to a real museum for a while now. I think it’ll be a good chance for them to see some history and have fun at the same time. Yeah, I think that’s a great idea. We can plan to go on a weekend. I’ll also ask my sister if she’s available to help out with the kids. We could make it a family event. That sounds perfect. I can also check with my students if they’re going to be free that weekend. I can’t believe we've got to this point. That old cupboard’s been in this room since we moved in, hasn’t it? And now it’s like a time capsule. It really is. But you know what’s funny is, we used to have this other toy—this Bako building set. It was like a giant plastic bricks set, and we used to build the entire house out of it. I think we even built that shed in the garden. Yeah, and we got so obsessed with it that we had to go and buy more bricks. I think we went to three different toy shops just to get enough. Remember how we used to knock it down and rebuild it every day? Oh, we were  so  into it. It felt like we were building the world. And you know what? It’s kind of funny that we still remember that. But it’s also kind of sad. It’s like we’re not living in that house anymore, and everything’s just accumulating dust. It’s strange, isn’t it? I think we’re going to have to start tidying it out. I mean, we can’t have it just collecting stuff for the rest of our lives. It’s not healthy. You know, it’s not just the physical stuff—it’s the memories too. Some of them are good, but some are just a bit overwhelming. Exactly. And it’s not just about the stuff. It’s also about the weather. I mean, we had this really bad winter last year, and the house started leaking.

Right, so I just wanted to bring up something that’s been on my mind. You know how ANON was sleeping in his pants last night? It was like he’d been through a war or something. So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about redecorating my flat. It’s been a bit of a dump since I moved back from Italy last year. Alright, do you two want to help me sort out the LEGO? I’ve had enough of it scattered all over the floor and the couch. Are we doing it now? It’s only 10 o’clock. I know, but I’ve had a long day. Well, I've just marked a few exam papers, and I have to say, it's been a bit of a challenge. I mean, some of the answers were so off the mark, I nearly fell out of my chair. Did you really? I bet they were like, "What’s a triangle?" and you’re like, “This isn’t a triangle, this is a pancake!” Aye, I remember when I was at school, I used to think the world was flat. My teacher said I was wrong, and I said, “Well, I’m not wrong, I’m just not wrong enough for you.” That’s a classic! I used to tell that joke to my grandson. He’d laugh so hard, he’d fall off the sofa. I think he’s got a better chance of passing than some of the students I marked. One of them wrote that the formula for the area of a circle was pi multiplied by diameter. I mean, that’s not even close! That’s like saying the weather is sunny when it’s actually a blizzard! You know, I used to tell jokes like that to my wife when we first married. She used to say, “You’re so funny, but I don’t want to laugh at you, I want to laugh with you.” That’s sweet. I always thought the best jokes were the ones that made you feel good. Like the one about the man who walked into a bar and said, “I’ll have a beer.” Then the bartender said, “We don’t serve beer here.” And he said, “Oh, well, I’ll have a wine.” And the bartender said, “We don’t serve wine either.” And he said, “Well, I’ll have a juice.” And the bartender said, “We don’t serve juice, sir.” Then the man said, “Well, I’ll just have a water.” And the bartender said, “We don’t serve water either.” And the man said, “Then I’ll just leave.” And the bartender said, “We don’t serve people who leave.” That’s a good one. I’ve heard that one before. It’s so classic, it’s like a math joke with a twist. I think that’s why we were all here today – to share a bit of laughter. It’s been a long week, and we all need some good banter. True.

So, do you remember when we watched  Peter Pan  the other day? It was such a classic film. I got so nostalgic thinking about how it was like a part of my childhood. Yeah, I loved that movie. I remember the way they made the Neverland feel so magical. But I always thought the original  Peter Pan  with the older Peter was more interesting. He had more depth, you know? I think that's because he's more like a grown-up version of the character. But I still love the way the Disney version makes it feel like a kids' story. It's funny, isn't it? I've always thought of Peter Pan as a symbol of never growing up, but I also think it's about the loss of innocence. Maybe that's why it's so popular with kids and adults alike. Exactly! And then there's  Tinker Bell —she's such a fierce character. I remember in the movie she’s so small but she’s got this huge spirit. It’s inspiring in a way. I think she’s a bit of a rebel, too. Like, she’s not afraid to be herself and stand up for what she believes in. It’s kind of like how some of the other characters in the film are – Wendy, John, Michael – they all have their own strengths. Yeah, and I love how the film shows the different sides of the characters. Like, Wendy isn’t just the perfect little girl. She’s also the one who helps keep the others grounded. I think that’s what made the story so relatable. I agree. And I remember when we watched the original  Peter Pan  at Great Ormond Street Hospital. It was the first time I had ever seen it in a real theatre. The way the lights dimmed and the music started up—it was like magic. That must have been amazing. I wish I could have been there. I’ve heard so many stories about the hospital and how it used to host special events for children. It’s such a special place. It really is. I think a lot of people who grew up in the 80s or 90s have some kind of connection to it. Even if it wasn’t about the hospital, it was about the stories and the way they made us feel.

Oh, do you know, I’ve been thinking about the ME event next year. I heard it’s going to be quite big. I’m not sure if I’ll be able to make it, though. I’ve been feeling a bit run down lately. Yeah, I heard about it too. It’s supposed to be a really important event, isn’t it? They’re talking about how women are going to be involved more in the organizing committee this time around. It was almost unheard of. I think things have improved, but there’s still a lot of work to do. I agree. I was an artist and an antique dealer, so I worked with a lot of people from different backgrounds. I always found that women brought a different perspective to the table. She was really struggling, and I could tell she didn’t know where to turn. She ended up staying with us for a while. I think she was a single mother, and it was heartbreaking to see her in that situation. That’s very sad. I had a colleague who used to run a nursery. She always said that the most important thing in childcare is to create a safe and nurturing environment. She believed that every child deserves that, no matter their background. I think that’s right. I’ve always thought that if we can give every child the chance to grow up in a stable and loving home, they have a better chance of succeeding in life. It’s not just about education—it’s about being cared for and supported. Exactly. I sometimes think about the hospice work I used to do. It’s not just about the medical care; it's about making sure the patient feels comfortable and valued.

So, do you think we should go to the Lake District this year or maybe Cornwall? I’ve been thinking about it a lot. But I do think Cornwall would be nice too. You know, the coast, the beaches, the pubs with real ales. Oh, I’d love to go to Cornwall. We could rent a cottage near St. Ives or something. But I’m not sure if the weather will be nice enough. Last time we went to the south coast, it rained for most of the week. Yeah, the weather is always a bit of a gamble, isn’t it? But I think it’s worth it. You know, it’s not just about the weather. It’s about the experience. And besides, if it does rain, we can still enjoy the pubs and the local food. I hadn’t thought about it that way. I suppose I’m a bit nervous about the cost, but if we plan it properly, we can make it work. Exactly. And if we go to the Lake District, we can do some hiking. I’ve heard the fells are beautiful in the summer. You know, I was thinking about bringing the camera again. It’s been a while since I’ve taken some good photos. That would be nice. I could take some pictures of the landscape too. It would be a great way to document our trip. But I wonder if we should go in July or August. I’ve heard those are the busiest months. So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to go to our grandparents’ house every summer? It was always so full of life, you know. I think the bigger challenge is convincing people to switch to reusable bags and being more mindful of their consumption in general. I know. I’ve heard people say things like, “Oh, this is eco-friendly,” but it’s not always the case. That’s true. I think the key is education – teaching kids the difference between what’s actually eco-friendly and what’s just marketing.

It’s a mix of things—ideas for my future home, travel destinations, and even some birthday gift ideas for my friends. I figure if I take notes now, I can be more prepared when the time comes. That’s a good idea. I’ve been using Pinterest for my PhD stuff too. I’ve got boards for research ideas, methodology, and even some quick study breaks. Seriously? I just found this really nice light fitting on eBay, it’s like a vintage one from the 70s, got a bit of patina, looks really good in the living room. Oh, that sounds fancy. You think it would fit with the new curtains we’re thinking about getting? Yeah, I think it would. It’s got that retro vibe, and the curtains are a bit of a neutral beige, so it should go well. Yeah, but maybe we could look at a few more options. There’s a few options on there that are a bit cheaper, but still look nice. I mean, if we’re going to be doing up the house, we might as well do it properly. I agree. It’s funny, I used to think of light fittings as just functional, but now I’m really into the design aspect. I mean, it’s not just about lighting, it’s about how it makes the whole space feel. I know what you mean. Our flat’s got this one really cheap LED strip that just doesn’t do anything for the room. It’s like, functional, but not stylish at all. I’m thinking maybe we should get a new ceiling light, something that actually makes the place feel a bit more like a home. Yeah, I think you’re right. I mean, we’re not exactly living in a mansion, but we do want to make it feel like it’s ours. I was also looking at some houses on Rightmove the other day. You know, just for fun. Oh, I saw some too. There was this one in Edinburgh, a bit of a countryside place, a couple of bedrooms, small but cosy. Not sure if we’d ever move, though. Yeah, I know. I think it’s more about the idea of having a place that you can call your own. I mean, maybe in five years we’ll be thinking of moving.

So, do you know what’s going on with your job hunt? I’ve been meaning to ask. Honestly, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. I applied for a few positions, but nothing’s quite panning out. I guess that’s the reality. But have you thought about training or upskilling? Maybe something like a qualification in dementia care or something like that? I have actually. I’ve been looking into doing some online courses. It might not be the easiest way to learn, but it’s better than nothing, I suppose. I might do that too. I’ve been thinking about it for a while. Maybe I can get some funding through the council or something. That’s a good idea. And if you ever want to team up and apply for something together, I’m happy to help. That would be great. I’d go mad trying to do it on my own. I’m in. It’s not like we don’t have enough on our plates already. Exactly. And if we can manage our own work, maybe we can tackle job hunting as a team too.

So, do you remember that study we read about last week about how blue light from screens affects sleep? I think it’s making a huge impact on people now. Oh, I remember. It's crazy how much we’ve all been affected by it. Especially with kids spending so much time on their phones and tablets before bed. I’ve even started making my son put his phone away an hour before bedtime. Yeah, I’ve done that too. I’ve tried using a night mode on my phone, but honestly, it doesn’t help much. I still feel like I’m wired to stay up late these days. Maybe it’s just the way we live now. I suppose it is. But then again, I’ve also been thinking about how much better it would be if we just had a proper routine. Like, no screens in the bedroom at all. It’s not about the technology—it’s about our habits. Fair point. I guess in a way, we’re all just adjusting to this new normal. I’ve been thinking about going camping again this summer—something simple like that, maybe we can get back to the basics of sleep, no distractions. That sounds like a good idea. I’d love to go camping. I remember when I was younger, we used to go out every weekend. I think I’ve forgotten how to find my way around a campsite. But that’s probably just getting older. You know, I actually got lost in London last week. It was a bit of a disaster. I had a map, but I didn’t trust it, and I ended up walking around for an hour. Can you believe it? No way! I’ve been there a few times, but I still get lost sometimes. I think it’s because the city is so big and you barely know where you are. But I guess that’s just part of living in a place like that. Yeah, and I remember when I was younger, I was always so confident about navigating. Now I just rely on my phone all the time. I think I’m losing that sense of direction. It’s funny how the world changes. I mean, you remember when you had to plan a route the old-fashioned way, drawing a map and figuring out your way there.

So, do you know what’s up with the gingers in our flat? I swear, every time I walk into the kitchen, there’s some ginger doing something weird. Oh, you mean the one that keeps hiding in the fridge? I saw it yesterday, peeking out from behind the yogurt. Yeah, that one! I tried to tell it it wasn’t welcome, but it just stared at me like I was the weird one. It’s not just that. I think it’s got a thing for the hamster. Every time the hamster comes out of its wheel, it follows it like a little puppy. That’s not creepy? I mean, the hamster is only a few inches tall. It’s like a tiny army of gingers running around the flat. I don’t know, it’s kind of funny. I mean, the hamster is cute, but the ginger? It’s like it’s got a plan. Yeah, and it’s not just the one ginger. I swear, there’s like a whole troop of them. I saw one in the hallway the other day, and it was staring at me like it knew something. Maybe it’s trying to take over the flat. I mean, it’s got the looks for it. Long hair, freckles, and that whole ‘I don’t care what you think’ vibe. Oh, that’s the one. It’s got this weird confidence. It just sits there, licking its paw, like it owns the place. I tried to make it feel welcome, you know. I even left out some cereal for it. But the next day, it was gone. That’s because it’s not a pet, it’s a  creature . It’s got a whole agenda. Maybe it’s planning a coup. I think it’s just lonely. You know, all the gingers in the flat, and no one to talk to. Maybe it’s just looking for a friend. Yeah, maybe that’s it. But I still don’t think it’s safe around the hamster. The hamster doesn’t know what it’s up against. I’m starting to think the ginger is leading a revolution. Maybe we should start a rebellion. Or maybe we should just let it be. After all, it’s not hurting anyone. It’s just… doing its thing. I think I’m gonna go check on the hamster.

Alright, Aaron, you've got to make a move here. You can't just sit there and let the others take over the whole map. You're the one with the most pieces, right? Oh, don’t be so dramatic, Jim. I’ve got a life outside of Risk. Besides, I’m not the one who’s been arguing about the pronunciation of “Genghis Khan” all night. You’ve been calling him “Genghis Can” since the beginning. Hey, that’s not fair! It’s not my fault he’s called him that. I’ve heard it in the streets of Enfield. You can’t blame me for the way the locals pronounce it! Yeah, well, if you’ve got a problem with how he’s pronounced it, maybe you should’ve spoken up earlier. Now I’m stuck with your version of the name, and I can’t even remember if it’s even spelled correctly anymore. Oh, come on, you’re not seriously telling me you don’t know how to spell Genghis Khan? It’s G-E-N-G-H-I-S K-H-A-N. I’ve seen you write it down in the middle of the game, and you got it wrong twice. I said it like “Genghis Can,” not “Genghis Khan.” It’s not the same thing! Also, I think the game is moving too fast for me. I’m not used to this level of strategy. I mean, I’ve got a degree in learning and development, not in global domination. That’s not the point, Lizzie. You’re here with us, and we all know you’ve got the potential to dominate. It’s just that you’re not taking the game seriously. We’re not just playing for fun—we’re playing to win. And you’re letting the others take the lead while you’re still trying to figure out where the borders are! Yeah, that’s true. I think it’s time for a quick strategy meeting. You need to stop stressing over the pronunciation and focus on the actual game. I mean, if we’re going to take over the world, we need to do it properly. Okay, okay, fine. But if I mess up the game because of my pronunciation, I want a raise. And maybe a new set of glasses. I’m starting to get a bit dizzy from all the alcohol and all the chocolate we’ve been eating.

So, do you ever just lie awake at night thinking about what we’re going to do after uni? Like, I feel like I’m just… stuck in this loop of studying, stressing, and then studying again. Yeah, I feel the same. I mean, I like my courses, but it’s like, what happens after? I keep thinking about celebrities and how they just…  poof —they’ve got it all sorted. Like, they’ve got their careers, their money, their fame, and it’s just… easy for them. But what about us? I know, right? It’s like, how do they do it? Like, the people I follow on Instagram, they’ve got kids, they’ve got jobs, they’re rich. It’s like, how do you even  start ? I feel like I’m just going to end up working a 9-to-5 job I hate, and then I’ll just… be a normal person. I mean, that’s what everyone’s doing. But I feel like I’m  bored  with it. I don’t know if I want to be in a corporate job or even do something creative. I mean, I like design, but I don’t know if I’m good enough. What if I’m just not? I know, I’ve been thinking about that too. I mean, I love art, but I don’t know if I can make a living off of it. I mean, someone said to me once, “If you want to make money, you have to do something with numbers.” But what if I don’t want to be around numbers? Yeah, that’s the thing about careers, isn’t it? You’re supposed to have a plan, but how do you know what your plan is when you’re still barely 20? I mean, I’ve heard of people starting their own businesses, but that’s like…  risky . And I don’t know if I’m ready for that. I think I’m just scared. I mean, what if I end up being 30 and still not having a clue what I want to do? I mean, I’ve heard stories about people who had it all planned out and then…  crash . It’s like, how does anyone even manage it? I think it’s just about taking it one step at a time. Like, maybe I don’t know where I’m going, but I do know that I don’t want to be stuck in a job I hate for the rest of my life.

So, do you know what’s up with the school project? Like, I’m supposed to do a presentation on... something, and I’m stuck. I’m like, what even is the point of this? Yeah, I know. I’m like, why are we doing this? I mean, I get that we need to learn about things, but it’s like, how does this help us? I mean, I’m not even sure what the topic is. The teacher just said, “pick something interesting,” and now I’m like, “interesting to who?” Exactly! And I was thinking about doing something on poverty, like, how it affects people, but then I’m like, do I even know what I’m talking about? I mean, I know it’s a thing, but I don’t really get it. Like, what’s the deal with people not having enough money? I don’t even know. I mean, I guess some people just don’t work, or they work but not enough to make ends meet. But then why do they not work? Is it because they don’t want to? Or is it because they can’t? I don’t know. I mean, there’s something about it that feels... I dunno, like it’s not fair. Like, some people have it, and some people don’t, and it’s not like there’s a shortage of jobs or anything. I mean, there are jobs, but maybe they’re not in the right places. Like, if you’re not from a certain area, you can’t get the jobs you need. Yeah, and it’s not just about jobs. It’s also about stuff like healthcare, education, housing. Like, you can have a job, but if you can’t afford a house, you can’t really live anywhere. And if you can’t afford healthcare, you can’t even get treated for something serious. It’s like a cycle. That’s a lot to think about, man. I mean, I guess I never really thought about it like that before. Like, I just think of it as, like, people not having money. But it’s more than that, isn’t it? Yeah, it’s like the system. It’s not just about individual choices. If the system doesn’t help people, then even if you work hard, you’re still stuck. And what if you’re not even given the chance to work?

So, how’s the recording process going? You mentioned you were doing something with a band last week. It’s been… a bit of a nightmare. I mean, I got the job because I thought it would be easy, but the guy who’s running the project is a real jerk. He’s always late, doesn’t listen to my ideas, and just wants me to do all the work.
