Though I still can’t bend my hips properly. Maybe I should try it. I’ve been putting it off because I’m too lazy, but I think I need to. I mean, if I don’t start taking care of my body, I won’t be able to do anything. That’s true. You know, I’ve also been thinking about my diet lately. I’ve been trying to lose a few pounds too, but I haven’t been successful. I just can’t stick to a diet. I end up eating all the junk food I’ve been avoiding. I know the struggle. I used to eat junk food all the time, but now I try to cook more. It’s not easy, though. I mean, I don’t have a lot of time because I’m self-employed, and I’m always busy with work.

So, do you want some of these beans? Yeah, just a bit. Okay, I’ll pass you some. Thanks. You know, I think we’re gonna need more salt, though. Yeah, I can’t taste anything. It’s like we’re cooking for a vegetarian. I don’t know, maybe I just don’t like salt. No, you said you always add extra. Yeah, but maybe the beans are just too... bland. I don’t know, maybe the water was bad. You ever think about changing jobs? Honestly, I’m not sure. I like my job, but I feel like I’m just stuck in a cycle. I get that. Sometimes I feel like I’m just going through the motions. Yeah, you know, I’ve been thinking about starting my own business. Oh? What’s it about? A little online shop for vintage clothes. I’ve been collecting stuff from my mum’s house, and I think it’d be fun to sell it. That sounds cool. You know, I’ve been thinking about something similar. Really? What are you thinking about? Maybe a coffee roastery. I love coffee, and I think there’s a gap in the market for a quality, local roastery. That’s ambitious. Yeah, but I think it’s worth exploring. I guess the only problem is funding. Yeah, it’s not easy. I mean, if you’re not in a position to take risks financially, it’s hard to start anything. I know. I’ve been saving up, but it’s not enough. Maybe you could partner up with someone? That’s an idea. I’ve been thinking about working with someone who’s more experienced. That makes sense. Maybe you could even go to some business courses or workshops. I’ve thought about that, but I’m worried about the time commitment. It’s worth it. You can’t just jump in without some knowledge. Yeah, I guess. I’ll talk to my mum about it. She’s always been supportive. That’s good. I think you’d do well. Thanks. I really appreciate that. No problem. You’re not the only one wondering about taking the leap. Yeah, I know. It’s scary, but it’s also exciting. Exactly. Sometimes you have to take a risk to find out what’s possible. True. I’ll keep you posted if I decide to go for it.

So, do you guys remember that film we watched last week? The one with the time travel and the guy who ended up in the future? It was so weird, wasn’t it? Yeah, I loved it. I mean, the plot was all over the place, but the visuals were insane. I think it was  Tenet ? Oh yeah, that’s the one! I remember that scene where the guy was running backwards through the hallway, and the whole thing was flipped. It was so confusing, but in a cool way. Honestly, I got more confused than entertained. I mean, I couldn’t even tell if it was supposed to make sense or not. But the action sequences were wild, right? Yeah, the action was epic, but I still didn’t get the whole time travel thing. I mean, how did he end up in the future if he was just running backwards? I think it was like a loop, you know? Like, he was stuck in this time loop and the whole thing was just a way to get him out of it. But honestly, I still don’t get it. I think the whole movie was more about the concept than the actual storytelling. It was like, “Oh, we’re gonna try to make a sci-fi movie with no clear plot, but with huge explosions and cool gadgets.” Exactly! I think the director was trying to be artistic and make a statement about time, but it backfired. I mean, it was a bit of a mess, but I still enjoyed it. I think the thing that saved it was the cast. Leonardo DiCaprio was in it, right? And he was so good, even though the movie was a bit of a mess. Yeah, he brought a lot of gravitas to the role. I mean, even if the story didn’t make sense, he made it feel like it mattered. I was actually really impressed by the soundtrack too. I think it was a mix of orchestral and electronic music that really helped set the tone. Yeah, the music was cool. I mean, it was a bit overwhelming at times, but it definitely added to the vibe of the movie. I guess it was one of those movies that you either love or hate. I think I’m in the love camp, even though I still don’t get half of it.

So, how was Paris? Did you have a good time? I’ve been dying to hear all about it. Honestly, it was a bit of a disaster, to be honest. I mean, we thought we were going to have a great weekend, but things just went wrong from the get-go. Oh no, what happened? Well, first of all, we got to the airport and my bag was lost. I had to wait for hours while they tried to track it down. And then when we got to the hotel, the room was completely messed up. The toilet was blocked, and there was a strange smell coming from the bathroom. That sounds awful. Was it a nice hotel? It was supposed to be a nice place, but clearly, they didn’t do the maintenance properly. And the worst part? We had to stay there for two nights. I was so angry, I just wanted to leave and find somewhere else, but we didn’t have a lot of options in the city. That must have been so stressful. Did you manage to get your bag back? Yeah, eventually. They found it and sent it to us, but it was late on the second night. We were all pretty exhausted. And then, the next day, we tried to go to the Eiffel Tower, but the weather was terrible. It was pouring rain the whole time. We ended up getting soaked, and we had to run for cover. The museums were closed because of the weather, and the Seine River was so full of water that they had to close the boats. We ended up just wandering around the Champs-Élysées, but it was kind of boring. All the shops were closed, and there was no one around. Sounds like a nightmare. How did you manage to get back? We took a bus back to the airport, and honestly, I was just glad to get home. I’ve never been so glad to see my own bed. I think I might need a holiday just to recover from this one. I can’t imagine how hard that must have been. You’re lucky you had your friend with you. It would’ve been so much worse to be alone.

Hey, how’s it going? You seem pretty chipper today. Oh, just had a good weekend. I went to Chichester with my sister, and we had a really nice meal at that new café near the castle. Oh, nice! You know, I think it’s one of the best places to grab a cuppa in the area. Definitely. I’ve been thinking about doing some creative writing, you know, maybe even a novel. Yeah, I used to write a lot more when I was in university, but it’s been a while. I’m trying to get back into it. I can relate. I think it’s just a matter of finding the time. Between work and my studies, it’s hard to fit it in. I know what you mean. Speaking of studies, have you heard about the British National Corpus? I’m trying to use it for my TEFL classes. I’ve been looking at some data on passives lately. That’s interesting. I’m actually doing a module on grammar and referencing. I think I need to get more organized with my notes. You should. I always end up procrastinating on my referencing. It’s so important to get it right, especially for academic work. I know. I’m planning to take some time off to focus on my master’s next year. I think it’s the right move for me. That sounds like a good plan. I’ve been thinking about taking a break too, maybe travel or something. I’ve been saving up for a trip to Greece. Greece? That sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to go. I’ve been reading a lot about the history and culture there. Yeah, I’ve been planning this for a while. I even thought about doing some volunteer work there.

So, do you just put the rice in the water and then let it cook? No, no, no, you have to be careful with rice. You need to rinse it first, otherwise it gets too sticky. Oh, right. So like, how do you rinse it? Do you just run it under the tap? Yeah, that’s it. Just run it under cold water until the water runs clear. It takes about a minute or two. Okay, got it. So then you put it in the pot with the right amount of water, right? Exactly. And the ratio is usually one part rice to two parts water. Like, if I use a cup of rice, I need two cups of water? Yeah, that’s the general rule. But sometimes you can adjust depending on the rice. Some rice needs more water, some less. So, like, if I’m cooking for the whole family, I need to double it? Yeah, that’s right. I mean, we’re not having much else tonight, so the rice is the main thing. Wait, are we having curry tonight? Yeah, I thought we could make some rice and curry. You’re a lifesaver. I was worried I’d have to eat something from the freezer all night. Don’t worry, we’ll make something amazing. I think I’ll add some jalapenos to the curry for a bit of heat. So, do you think I should go back to uni, Lottie? I’ve been thinkin’ about it a lot lately. I’m not really doing much else, y’know? I mean, it’s not like you’ve got much else to do. You’re unemployed, and you’re just kind of hangin’ around. It’s not good for you. Yeah, I know. I’ve been thinkin’ about it, but I’m worried about the money. I know you said you’re not in the best place financially, but I just don’t wanna be a burden. Look, you’re not a burden. We’re all in this together. But I still feel like I’m not ready. I’m just worried about what people will think if I go back. Like, I’ve already been through that once. Look, people will think what they want. So, do you ever think about getting back into work, Dave? I mean, it's been a while since you've been out of it. Honestly, I don't know, Lottie. It's not that I don't want to, it's just... I can't seem to find anything that fits. I tried a few things, you know. Some of them were okay, but not really right. I get that. It’s tough, especially with the economy the way it is. But you can't just sit around forever, can you? You’ve got to do something. I know, I know. I keep telling myself I’ll just do something, but then I get scared. What if I fail again? Although, I did get a bit excited when we found it. It was really tiny, and it looked like it was struggling. I know, right? We found it on the windowsill, all alone. It looked so helpless. But maybe it's better off back in the wild. I mean, we don’t want to get too attached. I guess that’s true. I mean, I did name it “Pip” just to be fancy. But I guess it’s not like we can take care of it. We don’t even have a proper container for it. Yeah, and we’d probably end up making it a mascot for the team. I don’t think we want to take that risk. I think we should just let it go. We can talk about it over drinks tomorrow. Exactly. And if we’re going to the party, we should make sure we’re all in the right spirits. No insects, no stress—just drinks and conversations. Let’s make it a great evening. Okay, I’m with you. Let’s just let Pip go.

So, do you know what’s happening with the school exams? I swear I’ve seen the schedule for the next term, and it’s like a never-ending list of tests and projects. Yeah, I know. I feel like we’re in a never-ending cycle of studying and then having to revise for the next thing. I don’t think I can handle another history test this week. I know, right? I was doing this project on the Industrial Revolution last week, and now we’re moving onto World War II. I feel like I’m going to forget everything by the time the exams come. I feel the same. I mean, I got an A in the last history test, but I still don’t remember half the stuff. It’s like my brain just doesn’t retain anything. I think it’s because we’re all so stressed. I mean, I’ve been trying to study for the English Literature exam for weeks, and I still can’t get the themes of  Jane Eyre  straight in my head. I know, I’ve been reading  To Kill a Mockingbird  for the English class, and I keep mixing up the characters. I think I’ve even confused Scout with Atticus in my head. Oh no, I’ve done that too! I thought Atticus was the one who got in trouble for defending Tom Robinson. It was so confusing. Yeah, I think I need to start making flashcards. I mean, I tried using the app Quizlet, but it just makes me more stressed. I tried that too, but honestly, it’s like trying to memorise a whole book in one go. I think the only way I can handle this is by watching some of my old comedy shows to take my mind off it. That’s what I do. I always tell myself that after I finish all my assignments, I can binge-watch  Friends  or something. It’s the only way I can get through the week. I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about doing that too. I’ve got this pile of work that I’m supposed to finish this weekend, and I really don’t want to do it. Yeah, I think I’m going to do that too. I mean, it’s not like we have to do anything else. It’s just school, right?

So, did you enjoy the meal, Mum? Oh, it was lovely, thank you. The steak was perfectly cooked, and the dessert was absolutely delicious. I haven’t had something this good in ages. Yeah, it was good. The fish was a bit on the dry side, though. I don’t know if it was the preparation or just the way it was cooked. I would’ve liked a bit more sauce. But overall, it was a pleasant evening. I agree. It’s always nice to get out and do something different, especially after a long week. I’ve been feeling a bit tired lately, haven’t you? Yeah, I have been. Work’s been a bit hectic. I’ve had to manage a few projects at the same time, and the client’s been making a lot of last-minute changes. It’s getting a bit overwhelming. I can imagine. I’ve been busy too, but not as much as you. I’ve been working on some admin stuff, and I’ve been trying to get some of my own projects off the ground. You know, I think it’s important to take a break now and then. I remember when I was younger, I used to work all the time and never take a day off. It got to the point where I was completely burnt out. That’s true. I think I need to start setting better boundaries. I’ve been working too much and not leaving enough time for myself. Yeah, it’s a struggle, especially with the demands of work. I’ve had to learn to say no to some things, but it’s not always easy. I think you’re doing the right thing. It’s important to look after yourself. Speaking of which, have you thought about taking a holiday soon? I’ve been thinking about that. I’ve been trying to save up for a short trip. Maybe somewhere in the south of France? I’ve always wanted to visit Provence. That sounds nice. I’ve heard it’s beautiful there. I might consider going somewhere like that too. Maybe with a friend or two. You know, if you ever need a break from work, I’m always happy to help out. I can take over some of the tasks if you need a hand. That would be great. I’m not sure I’ll take the trip yet, but it’s good to have options.

So, how’s the new house coming along? I know you’ve been working on it for a while now. Oh, it’s coming along nicely, thanks. I've been doing a bit of painting and sorting out the garden. It's a bit of a job, but it’s worth it. I can imagine. You’ve always had a good eye for detail, even when you were working at the flat. Yeah, well, I’ve had to be. I mean, you know, I’ve been cleaning for years, so I’ve learned to pay attention to little things. Right. I remember when you first started cleaning for me, you were always the one who noticed if something was out of place. It was kind of endearing, honestly. I think it’s just how I am. I like things to be tidy. I suppose it comes from growing up in a house where everything had its place. That’s fair enough. I’ve always thought that people who clean tend to have a sense of order, don’t you? Yeah, probably. I’ve always found it easier to manage my own life that way. You know, it’s not about being perfect, just being consistent. Speaking of consistency, how’s the work going these days? I know you've been working longer hours than usual. It’s been tough, honestly. Our manager’s been pushing us to get more done in less time. It’s not ideal, but I’m used to it. I suppose it’s part of being in a routine job. I know what you mean. I’ve always found that routine can be comforting, but it can also be a bit suffocating. Yeah, it is. But I guess that’s just how it is. I’ve got my hands full with the house, so I have to be careful not to burn out. That’s true. You’ve always been a hard worker, and I admire that. I’ve been thinking about changing jobs, actually. I’ve been doing some research on building societies and trying to get a better pension. That’s a good idea. I know you’ve been saving a bit, but I think it’s time to think about something more secure. Yeah, I’ve been considering it. I’ve had a few offers, but I’m not sure yet. If you’re ever looking for advice, I’m here.

So, how’s the bar workin’ for you? Still havin’ that same rush every night? It’s okay, I guess. It’s not the worst, but it’s not the best either. I mean, I love the vibe, and the people are great, but sometimes the hours get a bit too long. Especially when the weekend comes around. Yeah, I can imagine. I mean, I’ve only done one shift, but it felt like a marathon. How long are you usually on for? Usually, it’s like 10 hours a night. Sometimes even longer if it’s a busy night. I’ve been known to clock in at 4pm and not leave until 2am. It’s brutal, honestly. But I suppose it’s a good way to earn some cash while I’m studying. It must be tough, balancing work and study. I can’t imagine working 10 hours a night and then having to get up early for lectures. Do you even get much sleep? Not really. I try to, but most of the time I’m just too tired to do anything except crash as soon as I get home. I’ve started taking naps during the day, which is something I never used to do. It’s a bit of a new habit, but I think it’s helping. That’s smart. I mean, you have to take care of yourself, right? I’ve heard that working in a bar can be pretty stressful, especially if you’re just starting out. Definitely. There’s a lot of pressure, especially when you’re trying to keep up with the customers and the manager’s expectations. I mean, I’ve had a few arguments with the bar manager over the way I handled a few things. It’s not always smooth sailing. That sounds rough. I guess it’s a lot to manage. Have you thought about changing jobs or working somewhere else? Like, maybe something less intense? I’ve thought about it, yeah. I’m not sure if I want to stay in the bar scene for much longer. It’s a good job, but I’m not sure it’s the right fit for me long-term. I’m just trying to figure out what I want to do after uni. That makes sense. I mean, you’re only 20, so you’ve got time to figure things out.

So, do you know what’s the plan for the holidays, Sarah? I was just thinking about it. Honestly, I’m not sure yet. I’ve been so busy with customer service this term, I haven’t really had time to think about it. But I was considering maybe a short break somewhere in the north, maybe the Lake District. It’s been a while since I’ve gone up there. Oh, the Lake District is lovely, but you know, it can get a bit crowded in the summer. If you’re going later in the season, maybe you’ll have a better time. I’ve been thinking about going to the west coast, maybe County Clare in Ireland. My wife and I are going to Malta for a few weeks. We’ve been planning it for a while. It’s going to be our first trip abroad since the kids were born. It’s a bit of a long trip, but we’re excited. Malta’s a good choice. I’ve heard the beaches are amazing there. Are you going to take the kids? No, they’re both at university now, so it’s just us. It’ll be nice to have some time just for us. That sounds like a dream. I can’t imagine being away from the kids, though. I just don’t know if I’m ready for that yet. I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about going to Spain for a while. Maybe Barcelona or Seville. I love the culture there, and the food—especially the tapas. Oh, I’ve been dying to try tapas properly. I’ve had some in Manchester, but it’s not the same as being there. You should! It’s such an amazing way to experience the culture. You can’t beat the atmosphere in a real tapas bar. I might have to consider that. I’ve been thinking about trying something different this year. Maybe a road trip? Like, somewhere in the north of England. I’ve always wanted to see the Yorkshire Dales properly. That sounds like a great idea. I’ve been meaning to do a road trip with my daughter. We could map out a route and take it slow. Maybe stop at some of the smaller towns and villages. You know what would be fun? We could all go somewhere together. Maybe a short trip to the Scottish Highlands.

I can't believe the amount of money we're spending on this season’s football tickets. I mean, it's not even the big clubs, it's just some mid-table teams we follow. Yeah, I know. I feel like we're paying for the match and then the drinks, the snacks, and then the parking. It’s like a whole extra cost just to sit there for an hour and watch a game that only lasts 90 minutes. And then there’s the food. You know, the actual food. The ones that are called “matchday snacks.” I mean, I don’t even know what half of them are. I’ve seen people eating weird things like pretzels and chips that are shaped like a football. It’s like a food festival, not a football match. It’s not just the snacks. Sometimes I feel like the stadium itself is a sales pitch. They’re selling everything from branded T-shirts to cups with a logo on them. You’d think the main thing they’re selling is the game, but it feels like they’re selling the experience of being there. I guess that’s part of the culture, though. It’s not just about the football anymore. It’s about the community, the atmosphere. I remember when I was younger, we used to just go to the match, sit in the stands, and watch the game. Now, it feels like you have to be part of the whole package. And let’s not forget the fast food. I mean, the ones that are just a few minutes away from the stadium. Some of them are better than the ones you can get at home. But I still think it’s a bit of a gimmick. Why not just bring your own food? I get that. I’ve tried bringing my own food before, but I’ve always felt like I was the only one. Everyone else is buying from the stalls, and it’s like they all know what they’re doing. You can’t just bring a sandwich and expect to fit in. I guess it’s about the experience. I mean, if you’re going to spend that amount of money on a ticket, you might as well spend it on the whole package. But it does make me think about how much the cost has gone up since I was a kid.

So, do you remember that old film we watched last summer, Grandma? The one with the mad inventor and the secret lab? Oh, you mean  Inventor of the Future ? I loved that! I remember we watched it on a rainy afternoon, and you were so serious about it, thinking it was real. I didn’t watch it, but I heard you two talking about it. I think I remember something about a flying car, didn’t you? Yeah, that’s the one! And I still think that flying car idea is the next big thing. I mean, look at the tech these days—electric vehicles, self-driving cars, drones. It’s all leading up to something bigger. I suppose. But I still think the real future is in the home. I mean, I’ve been cooking for years, and I’ve got a few tricks up my sleeve. You know, I’ve been thinking about making some sort of cooking machine, you know, like a robot that can do everything from chopping to baking. It would save me so much time. That’d be amazing! I mean, with your skills in the kitchen, you could be on  MasterChef  in no time. I’d bet you’d beat all the contestants. Oh, don’t be silly. I barely cook for myself these days. I just make toast and tea. But I did used to bake. When I was younger, I’d make all sorts of things—cakes, cookies, even a few fancy pastries. Those were the days. That’s a shame. I used to be good at cooking too. I used to make all the meals for my family. My kids would all come home from school just to get a taste of my cooking. But these days, I just make sandwiches and toast. I don’t have the time or the energy. That’s not fair. You should be cooking more. I mean, you’ve got a great eye for it. You could start a catering business or something. You could even run a restaurant. I know, I know. I keep thinking about it, but I just can’t seem to get started. I mean, it’s not the money, it’s the hassle. But I do miss it. I miss the smell of the oven, the sound of the sizzle, the joy of someone saying, “That’s the best meal I’ve ever had.”

Alright, do you two want some pancakes? It's Pancake Day today! Can we have some pancakes, Mummy? Yes, I want pancakes, too! Of course you can. Just make sure you brush your teeth first, though. We don’t want any sticky mess on your teeth. Okay, I’ll brush my teeth now. I’ll brush my teeth too! Good. Now, while you’re brushing, let me just check the fridge to see if there are any pancakes left. Oh, and don’t forget to wash your hands before you eat. I’ll wash my hands! I’ll wash my hands too! Perfect. Now, while you’re doing that, I’ll get the pancakes ready. Do you remember what we talked about last week about the Science Museum? Yes! We’re going there this weekend! I can’t wait to see the dinosaurs! That’s great. I’ve booked tickets for both of you. We’ll leave early on Saturday morning so we don’t miss the opening. Oh, and don’t forget to bring your school uniforms—it’s an educational trip. Can we bring our toys? No, not the ones you play with at home. Just your school stuff. You know, the ones you use for lessons. Okay, I’ll bring my pencil case. Good. Now, I need to remember to remind the school about the assembly this week. It’s about growing up and what it means to be responsible. Are we going to talk about the Green Knowe story? Yes, I think we’ll be discussing that during the assembly. It’s a really important story about kindness and friendship. I like the Green Knowe story! Me too. It’s a classic. Speaking of stories, I heard there’s a short story competition coming up at the Festival Hall. Maybe you two could enter one of your own? Can we write one about the beach? I love the beach! That sounds like a brilliant idea. And go to Paris on your own? No, not yet. But maybe when you’re older, you can go with your parents. I can go to Paris when I’m older! Yes, you’ll have plenty of time. Just make sure you finish your food first. I’ve made a lovely pancake, and I don’t want to see any of it go to waste. I’m not going to waste it, Mummy.

So, do you think we should order more food? I’m not sure we’ve got enough for everyone. I think we’re okay, but maybe we could get a few more dishes. It’s been a while since we last had Chinese, and I’ve been craving some sweet and sour chicken. Yeah, I agree. It’s been ages since we had that. I remember when we first moved in, we used to order like every other night. Now it’s more of a rare treat. You know, I actually had a friend who used to get the whole Chinese meal every time. It was like his go-to when he was stressed or tired. He said it was the only thing that made him feel like he could handle the world again. That’s pretty dramatic, but I can see how it could be comforting. I mean, thinking back, when we first moved into this house, we were all so stressed about everything—jobs, bills, just being in a new place. Chinese food was our way of saying, “We made it.” Yeah, and Bob the Builder is always on when we have takeout. Like, as if he's supplying the whole kitchen with everything we need. It’s kind of weird, but it feels like a ritual. I love that. I think it’s kind of a tradition now. Though I have to say, I’ve started to realize that Bob the Builder is more than just a cartoon character. He's like someone who fixes everything for us. Just not literally, obviously. I think he’s symbolic of the things we all need in life—some kind of structure, some kind of guidance, and most importantly, someone who’s always there when you need them. Like a good friend or a solid support system. That’s a really nice way to look at it. I mean, thinking about it, we do have a pretty solid support system here. Even if we’re not all the most organized people in the world. Yeah, but when it comes to actual organization, we’re not that great. I mean, I still haven’t figured out where the remote control is half the time. I think it’s in the couch. That’s not just you. I think it’s more of a shared issue. I swear, the only thing we’re all consistent about is ordering Chinese food on a Friday.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to play that game where you had to guess which family member had the most peculiar habit? Oh, I remember that! It was a madhouse. I think we even had a whole list of things — like Auntie Muriel always tried to use the passive voice in every conversation, and Uncle Frank had this obsession with collecting bottle tops. I think that was more of a social experiment than a game. It was like a psychological test. We were all trying to figure out what made people tick, weren't we? Yeah, it was weird, but it was fun. I mean, it got us talking about things that we normally wouldn’t. I remember you once said that Mrs. Green over the road had the most bizarre routine — she’d wake up at 4 a.m. and start baking scones. And breakfast was always scones with jam and clotted cream. She did! And she’d even leave them on the fence for the birds. I swear, one time I saw her walk out in the middle of the night with a tray of scones and a plastic bag full of flour. That must have been one of the most unusual things I’ve ever seen. I still remember the look on her face when the local council came to inspect her garden — she was so excited, she started trying to explain the ‘philosophy of the scone’ to them. And don’t even get me started on the conversation we had with the postman the other day. He said he’s being tested in a driverless car pilot program. He’s supposed to be a ‘human monitor’ — you know, just to make sure everything’s going smoothly. Oh, that’s new. I heard something about that on the radio. They’re rolling out driverless cars in some cities now. I can’t believe we’re actually getting there. I think it’s a huge change for the way we travel. I mean, I remember when air safety was a real worry — the first planes were so unreliable. Now, it’s almost like flying is safer than driving. Yeah, but even with all the safety measures, I still don’t trust flying. I mean, just the thought of a plane crashing always gives me the heebie-jeebies. I get that. I still think driving is safer — especially if you’re not in a rush.

Alright, do you two want to help me make dumplings for Chinese New Year? I’ve got the dough and the fillings ready, and I’m dying to see what kind of shapes you’ll come up with. Dumplings? That sounds fun! But wait — are we making them for the real Chinese New Year or just for fun? Well, it’s not actually the real one—it’s just our way of celebrating. I thought it’d be nice to do something traditional, especially with the kids around. We’ve got the dragon drawing and the dragon dance planned, too. Dragon dance? That sounds cool! I’ve never seen one before. What’s it like? It’s a big, colorful thing with a dragon made of fabric and sticks. People move it around in a rhythm, and it’s supposed to bring good luck. It’s super exciting, and it’s been a tradition for ages. I think it’s part of the Lunar New Year festival, which is coming up in a few weeks. That’s awesome! I’d love to see it. But before that, I’ve got a question—how did you come up with the idea to make dumplings for Chinese New Year? I mean, I know it’s a tradition, but why is it associated with that holiday? Oh, it’s a long story. Let me think… It’s linked to a legend about a monster that used to eat people every year. People would make dumplings that looked like coins to offer to the monster to keep him full and stop him from eating them. Over time, it turned into a festive tradition and a symbol of prosperity. Oh! So it’s about good luck and staying safe? That’s really cool. Yeah, exactly. And besides, dumplings are delicious. I think the kids will love it. You’re both getting a chance to be creative and learn something new. I’m excited. I’ve never made dumplings before, but I’ve seen videos online. It looks like a lot of fun to fold them. Yeah! I’ve been thinking about drawing the dragon too. My friend at school showed me how to do it with markers. I was gonna do it on a piece of paper, but maybe I could draw it on a tablecloth or something? Then we could hang it up in the kitchen.

So, do you think we should go to the Pantheon tonight? I’ve heard it’s beautiful at night. Definitely. I’ve been dying to go there. I’ve heard the lighting there is amazing. But I should ask if the place is open at night. Oh, it is! I’ve been there before. It’s one of those places where you can just walk around and take in the history. Plus, the views from the top are absolutely worth it. Sounds good. I was just thinking about how cool it would be to walk around the city at night like this. But I’m also worried about the weather. I heard it might rain tomorrow. Yeah, I saw that too. I think it’s supposed to be a bit cooler tonight, but it should clear up by tomorrow. I was thinking about dinner tonight. Do you guys want to go to that little restaurant near the Trevi Fountain? I heard the pasta is amazing. That sounds perfect. I actually stayed at that hotel nearby last time I was here. It’s a bit pricey, but the view is worth it. I’ve only been there once, but I didn’t have time to try the food. I’m more of a coffee person, honestly. Though I do love the atmosphere there. It’s a good place for a first impression of the city. And the barista there is super friendly. Wait, are you a barista? Yeah, I am. I work in London, but I’m here on a gap year. I thought I’d take a break and travel a bit. I’m actually planning to head to Barcelona next. Wow, that’s wild. I’ve always wanted to go to Barcelona. I even took a Spanish class in college. Though, honestly, I’m still terrible at it. I’m actually from Birmingham. I run a café, so I’ve been to a lot of places like that. We’ve got our own little barista culture here. That’s cool. I’m studying history, so I’ve been trying to learn a bit of Italian. I think it’s helping me understand the city better. That’s a great approach. I’ve been trying to pick up some Italian too, but I’m not very good at it. I think I’ll need to practice more. I think we should all meet up tomorrow for breakfast.

So, do you think we should go to the hen do this weekend or wait until next week? I know it’s a bit of a big event, but I’m not sure if we’re all fully ready yet. I think we should go this weekend. It’s only a few days away, and I’ve already got the venue booked. Plus, Ali and Rosie are really excited about it. They’ve been planning it for months. Yeah, but I’m still not sure about the venue. I mean, it’s in the countryside, and I don’t know if the kids will like it. I’ve heard some of them talk about how they’d rather do something more urban, you know, with more things to do. I get that, but it’s supposed to be a relaxing weekend for the girls, not a full-on party. Plus, the venue is really nice, and they’re offering breakfast, so we can all just chill out and enjoy some food without having to cook. Yeah, and the catering is amazing. They’ve got a real chef doing it, so we don’t have to worry about anything. I mean, we’re not even supposed to bring anything. It’s all taken care of. Exactly. And it’s all got a really nice vibe – like a boutique hotel but with a friendly, laid-back atmosphere. It’s the perfect place to hang out and just enjoy the company. Okay, I suppose if it’s all taken care of, then it’s not so bad. But just so I’m clear, are we bringing the kids? Because I know a few of them want to come, but I don’t want to overdo it. I think we’re bringing a couple of the younger ones, but not all of them. We’ll keep it to maybe three or four. That way, we can still have some peace and quiet for the adults. Plus, it’s going to be fun for the kids too – there’s a small play area, and they’ve got a few craft stations set up. Oh, and they’re also doing a baking workshop! I’ve heard a couple of the girls have been talking about wanting to try their hand at something new. It’s a great idea, really. It’s not just a party – it’s a real event.

Alright, do you think I got the fish right? I mean, I tried to follow the recipe, but it just didn’t taste right. Honestly, I think you overcooked it. The fish was still a bit firm, and the sauce didn’t really blend in. You might want to try it on a lower heat next time. Yeah, I guess I got a bit impatient. I’ve been working all day, and I just wanted to get it done. But I’m not sure if it’s worth the effort. I mean, I could just order takeout or something. You shouldn’t give up so easily. I mean, you’re the one who wanted to cook for us. It’s a good chance to practice, and it’s better than eating out every night. I know, I just feel like I’m not good enough. What if I mess it up again? I’ve been sick the last few days, and I’m not at my best. I’m not even sure if I’m up for it. Look, I get it. You’ve been under the weather, and cooking when you’re not well is tough. But you’ve got to try. I’ll help you out if you need it. We can do it together. Yeah, I guess that would make it easier. I don’t know, maybe I should just start with something simpler next time. Like a pasta or a salad. I don’t want to mess up the whole meal. Fair enough. But don’t let one bad experience stop you. You’re doing better than most people I know. And besides, you’ve got the best kitchen in the house. I’d rather eat your cooking than any restaurant. Thanks, man. I appreciate that. I just need to take it slow and not rush things. I mean, I’ve been thinking about going on a trip soon. Maybe somewhere in the south of England. I’ve been to a few places, but I’ve never gone anywhere too far. That sounds good. You should take some time off. You’ve been working too hard lately. I heard there are some great places to visit there. You could stay in a hotel with a nice view, maybe even one of those countryside getaways. Yeah, I’ve been thinking about it. I just need to get my head straight first.

I just thought I'd pop in for a bit, love. I've been thinking about the list for the shop, and I thought I'd bring it up with you before I go out. Oh, do pop in. You know I'm always happy to see you. What’s on the list again? Well, the usual stuff – milk, bread, eggs, and then I thought maybe some fresh fruit. I've been meaning to stock up on apples and bananas since they’re in season. That sounds good. And don’t forget the coffee, or the tea. You know how I like it. Still, I’ll be honest, I’m not sure I’d go for the coffee now. My teeth are getting a bit sensitive. Oh, well, I’ll pick up the tea, then. I think there’s a new brand that’s been coming in. They’re organic, and I heard it’s quite good. Maybe you’d like to try it? That sounds nice. I’d be happy to. And I suppose I should mention the calendar fobs, yes? I saw one at the market that looked really quite fetching. It’s got a little wooden handle and everything. Oh, I remember those. They were the thing back in the day. I used to have one with a picture of the seaside on it. You know, the ones we used to carry around at school. I think they were called 'calendar fobs' then, too. Yes, they were. I used to have one with a cat on it. Just the one. It was the only thing that made me smile during all that school bullying. Still, it made me feel a bit better. Oh, you had one with a cat? That’s adorable. I wonder if they still make them. I think the ones from back then have become quite collectible. Maybe you’d like to get one for your birthday? You know, I was thinking about that. I haven’t had a birthday card since I retired. I think it’s been years. I’ve been getting so used to people not writing to me anymore. That’s sad. I still get cards from the kids. The ones from the school days were always the best, though. I think mine had drawings of ducks on it, and I had to write the alphabet in the margins. Oh, I remember that.

So, how’s the new place, mate? I heard you moved into Holsworthy last week. Yeah, it’s been a bit of a culture shock, to be honest. I’m still getting used to the area. It’s a nice place, though. Got a good community feel, and the countryside is right on your doorstep. Yeah, I heard that. But I still can’t get used to the way people talk here. It’s like a different dialect. Isn’t it? I’ve been trying to pick it up, but it’s like a whole new language. It’s not that bad. It’s more of a local twist. You’ll get used to it. I hope so. I’m not sure how I’ll manage the DIY stuff. It’s one thing when you’re in your own home, but when you’re in a new place, everything feels a bit different. I know what you mean. I had to replace the roof last month, and it took me weeks to figure out how to do it properly. You’re not the only one. I had to fix the garden fence last week. I thought I was doing it right, but the neighbour came over and said I’d messed it up. Oh no! What did you do? I tried to build a gate, but I measured wrong, and it didn’t fit. I had to take it all down and start again. That sounds like a nightmare. I’d be tempted to just hire someone, but I’m trying to save money. I can see the value in that. I had to do a bit of plumbing when I moved into my old place, and it nearly gave me a heart attack. I’ve heard that. I’ve heard about people getting stuck on minor jobs and then needing a professional. Yeah, I think that’s a good idea. Maybe we should all get together and do a bit of DIY together. It’s more fun that way. That sounds like a good idea. Plus, it’ll give us something to talk about on the way to the pub. I like that. We could even start a local walking group or something. Holsworthy’s got some nice trails, I heard. I think that’s a great idea. It’ll help us all get to know each other better, too.

So, do you ever just get fed up with online shopping? Like, I mean, it’s so easy, right? Just click a button and it arrives at your door. But sometimes I feel like I’m just buying things I don’t really need just because I saw them on a website. I know what you mean. I’ve got this thing where I see something on Instagram and then I just order it. A lot of the time I end up not even using it. Like that pink hoodie I bought last week. It’s just sitting in my wardrobe. Oh man, I feel you. I’ve got this whole pile of stuff I bought online that I never use. I think it’s like a compulsion. You just want to get something for nothing, you know? Yeah, and the thing is, it’s not just the stuff either. It’s the whole process. You see a product, you get distracted by something else on the site, and before you know it, you’ve spent £50. Exactly. It’s like the internet is designed to keep you hooked. I remember I tried to cut back a while ago, but I only lasted two days. Then I saw this cool T-shirt on a site and then I just… bought it. I feel you. I think the problem is that we’re all so used to instant gratification. You want something, you get it in a few days. It’s not like buying something in a shop where you have to wait. I guess. But what about you? Do you ever get annoyed with the technology side of it? Like, when you order something, it’s about five minutes before the delivery guy arrives, but it still takes ages to get to your door. Oh, you’re telling me. I ordered a book online last week and it took over a week to arrive. I was like, “Why did I even bother?” But then it turned out the delivery was delayed due to a national strike or something. Oh, that’s a relief. I mean, it’s not like I’m blaming the delivery guy. I just wish there was more transparency. You know, like, if the system is down or there’s a strike, you should know before you pay. Right, that’s a good point. I think sometimes it feels like we’re being sold a dream about delivery times, but in reality, it’s just a bunch of people doing their best.

So, do you think we should get a new cooker, Annie? I mean, it's been over ten years since we bought this one, and it’s starting to make more noise than a tea kettle. I think we should. Look, the one we have now is a bit of a relic, and I don't fancy having to replace it with a new one when we’re all in the middle of a holiday. What do you think, Sue? Honestly, I’d say go for it. We’ve had the same fridge for nearly twenty years, and I still say it’s holding up better than the cooker. But if we’re going to get a new one, let’s do it in the next few weeks when we’re not too busy with the walk and the furniture shopping. Yeah, I was thinking the same. We need to make sure we’re not overcommitting. I mean, we’ve got this planned coastal walk coming up in a couple of weeks, and I don’t want to be looking at a broken appliance the whole time. Exactly. I’ve got some ideas for the walk. I think we should head down to Exeter and then take a ferry to Exmoor. There are some really scenic spots there, and I’ve heard the views are amazing. Plus, I’ve got a friend who works at a caravan park there and might be able to get us a discount. That sounds lovely. I’d love to go. But I think we should also think about buying a new couch. The one we have is getting a bit worn, and it’s not the most comfortable. I’ve been trying to sleep on it, and it feels like I’m lying on a trampoline. Oh, I know. I’ve been trying not to sit on it too much. I think it’s time for something a bit more modern. But do you think we should go for leather or fabric? Well, if you’re going for something that lasts, leather might be better. I mean, I’ve seen how durable it can be. But then again, fabric is easier to clean and more affordable. It really depends on what you’re looking for. I think we should go for fabric. I don’t know about you, but I don’t want to be worrying about cleaning a leather couch every week.

So, how’s the new project at work going? I know you’ve been trying to get it off the ground for a while now. It’s going okay, I guess. There’s a lot of moving parts, and honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m just waiting for the right moment to push it forward. But I’ve been talking to some colleagues, and we’ve got a few ideas that might actually work. I’m just trying to figure out how to convince the team to commit. That sounds a bit like the kind of thing that always happens in the early stages. You know, you get excited, you think you’ve got everything figured out, and then the real work begins. Have you managed to get the funding approved yet? Not yet, but I’m hoping to submit the proposal next week. I’ve been working late a few nights to make sure it’s solid. It’s been a bit stressful, though. I mean, I’ve got a lot on my plate with the day-to-day, and this project is taking up a lot of time. I can imagine. You know, I’ve been in that boat myself. It’s one of those things where you feel like you’re juggling a hundred different balls, and if one drops, it’s hard to catch up. But it’s also rewarding when it all comes together. Yeah, I guess. It’s just frustrating when you feel like you’re not making enough progress. And honestly, I’m starting to wonder if I’m even the right person to lead this. I mean, I love the work, but it’s a lot. What do you think? I think you’re doing the right thing. You’ve got the skills, the experience, and the drive. You’re just pushing yourself too hard. Maybe you should take a step back and give yourself a bit of space. Burnout is a real thing, and you don’t want to let it take over. You’re right. I’ve been so focused on getting this project done that I haven’t really taken time to recharge. I’ve been working from home a lot, and honestly, I think it’s been contributing to the stress. I need to remember to take a break. Yeah, go ahead and do that. I know it’s not easy, but you’re not alone in this.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to have that old cat, Fido? He was a real troublemaker, always knocking things over and sneaking into the kitchen at night. Oh yes, I remember that! He used to sit on the windowsill and stare at the garden like he was plotting something. I swear one night he actually knocked over the entire watering can. We spent ages cleaning up. That sounds like a classic cat story. I used to have a tabby named Shadow who would follow me everywhere. She’d even chase me into the kitchen when I was making dinner. I had a dog when I was younger, a German Shepherd named Max. He was a real gentle giant, but he had a habit of chewing through the furniture. I had to get him a dog bed and a chew toy every week. I’ve always been more of a plant person. I’ve got this lovely collection of succulents, and they’re all very low maintenance. I can’t stand cats or dogs, they’re too much work. Yeah, I know what you mean. My sister has two dogs, and they’re like little tornadoes. They’ll run around the house and knock everything over. But I still love them. Speaking of animals, have you heard about the new wildlife reserve opening near here? They’ve got some really rare birds and even a few endangered species. That sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to visit a place like that. I think it’s a great way to connect with nature and learn about different species. I might have to check it out when I’m free. I would love to go. I’m always interested in nature and the environment. It’s a great way to take a break from work and get some fresh air. I think it’s a good idea, especially for the kids. It’s a great opportunity for them to learn about animals and responsibility. I remember when I was younger, my parents took me to a zoo and I was fascinated by the elephants. Yeah, I think it’s important for kids to have that kind of experience. It helps them appreciate the world around them. I agree. I think it's also a great way to bond as a family. We could go together and spend quality time outdoors.

So, do you reckon we should go to the market tomorrow? I’ve been thinking about getting some fresh fruit and veggies, and I could really do with a change from the same old supermarket stuff. Oh, I don’t know, lass. I’ve been thinking about that myself. I’ve had a bit of a wobble with the telly lately, and I fancied a bit of a wander. But I don’t know if I’m up for all that walking. You know how it is, the legs don’t always play ball with me these days. Well, it’s not too far, is it? Just a short walk through the village, and the market’s only a few streets away. It’s a good chance to get some local produce and maybe catch up with some of the regulars. Yeah, and it’s not like we’ve got to do it every day. Just a couple of times a week, and it’ll be a nice change. Plus, you know, we could even grab a bite to eat there. I heard they’ve got a new café that’s supposed to be really good. A café, eh? I’ve heard of it. They’ve got that open-fire pizza oven, I believe. But I’m not sure about the price. I remember the last time I tried something like that, it was a bit of a splurge. It’s not that bad. I’ve been there a few times, and the food is decent. Plus, they’ve got a good selection of local cheeses and chutneys. I buy some of that for the flat. It’s delicious and it lasts a while. Yeah, and it’s about time we stopped buying all our groceries from the same place. We’ve had that same jar of soup for months now. I’m tired of the same old thing. Fair enough, but I do like the convenience of the supermarket. I mean, I know it’s not the most exciting, but at least I don’t have to strain myself walking all over the place. Well, maybe we can compromise. We could do the market a couple of times a week, and the rest of the time stick to the supermarket. It’s not like we’re going to starve or anything. That sounds reasonable. I think I’d like that.

So, do you think we should go through the whole syllabus for the next module again? I mean, it’s got to be clear for the students, but I don’t want to bore them either. Yeah, honestly, I think we should. It’s been a while since we’ve reviewed it, and we both know how quickly things can get tangled up if we don’t stay on top of it. Plus, it’s only a few more weeks before the semester starts. True. I was just thinking about the food the other day. Do you remember the last time we cooked together? That was before we even moved to China. I think it was something like stir-fry. Oh, definitely. I remember you burned the broccoli. But hey, I think we’re getting better at it now. I mean, the other week we had this amazing noodle soup. It was so good, even the neighbors stopped by. Oh, I remember that. You even got a compliment from the old man who lives across the street. He said it was the best thing he’d had in years. Right, he did. And I think it was because I finally learned how to use the right amount of soy sauce. You know, it’s amazing how much of a difference a little bit can make. Yeah, and the way you cook now is so different from when we first got here. I mean, we used to just stick to the basics. But now, I think we’re starting to experiment more. Exactly! And it’s not just food. I feel like we’re starting to settle in more. You know, about the whole living abroad thing. It’s not as overwhelming as it used to be. Yeah, that’s true. I mean, it’s still a bit of a culture shock sometimes, but I think we’re learning to adapt. And honestly, I think we’re starting to feel a bit more at home. I agree. I was just thinking about the TV we watched last night. That British drama we were bingeing? It was so good. I think it reminded me of home, even though I’ve been here for almost a year now. Oh, I know. I felt the same. It’s funny how something as simple as a TV show can bring back so many memories. It’s like a little piece of England with us here.

I just can’t believe how much this coffee machine costs, you know. I thought it would be cheaper than that. I know, I saw one online for half the price. But you know, when you’re retired and living in a place like this, you just want things to be easy. And I mean, it’s not like we’re going to use it every day. Yeah, but I don’t even think we’ve had a proper cup of coffee in months. It’s been so long since we had anything more than instant. You’d think with the amount of time I spent in oil and gas, I’d be more used to coffee. But no, the only thing I got was a cup of tea at work, and that was only when I left. I’m not saying it’s a bad thing, I just think the price is ridiculous. I was at the shop the other day, and the guy was trying to upsell me a fancy machine with a built-in grinder and everything. I told him to take it and shove it. I just want something that works. I know, I feel the same. I think we should just get a basic one and maybe even look for a second-hand one. You know, it’s not like we’re in a rush. We can wait until we get the removal costs sorted, right? Yeah, but the removal costs are already a nightmare. You know what I mean? When you’re in a place for years, you end up accumulating so much stuff. All those boxes, all those bits and bobs. Some of them are things I haven’t even used in years. I mean, I had a colleague who used to collect golf clubs. I don’t even play golf anymore, but he still had them in the attic. I know that feeling. I’ve got a box full of old school books. My kids never used them, and I don’t think I’ll ever use them again. But I don’t want to just throw them away. It’s like, what if someone else needs them? Or maybe they could be useful for someone else. That’s a good point. I’ve been thinking about it too. Maybe we could start a sort of community swap or something. You go through your stuff, see if anything’s useful, and pass it on.

So, do you know what’s the deal with these pseudonyms? I mean, it’s like they’re trying to be mysterious or something. I don’t know, maybe they just like to keep their identities private. You know, like, not being too obvious about who you are. Yeah, but I think some people just get into the whole “anonymity” thing. Like, they’re not trying to hide, they just like to be called by a nickname or something. Oh, I get it. I used to do that with my old job. I had to use a pseudonym just to be anonymous when I was working on some projects. My friend, Simon, used to call himself “The Microwave Master” because he always had the best microwave meals. Oh, that’s a good one. I’ve heard of people using pseudonyms for fun, like in online communities or stuff like that. Yeah, I remember this one guy who was called “The River Rat” because he used to fish in the rivers around Birmingham. That’s cool. I’ve heard of people using pseudonyms for clubs too. Like, there’s this club in London called “The Condiment Club,” and they all have different names based on their favourite sauce. Oh, I’ve heard of that. I think their president was called “The Ketchup King.” Haha, sounds like a real club. I read somewhere that they even have rules about how you can only use one condiment per meal. That’s wild. I mean, how do you even do that? I think I’d be using the whole bottle of something. Maybe they’re just into that kind of thing. I mean, I’ve heard of people who take their food preferences seriously. Speaking of food, did you hear about the new Italian restaurant that opened up on the canal? I tried it last night, and the pasta was out of this world. Oh, really? I’ve been meaning to check it out. I love Italian food, especially the sauces. I think the owner is from Milan, so he’s got some real expertise. I heard he even uses authentic Italian ingredients. That’s great. I’m always looking for good food. I mean, I’ve been working at this café, so I know a thing or two about coffee and pastries. Yeah, and I’m still learning. I mean, I’m a student, so I’m not really in the business of cooking.

So, do you guys ever actually go on Tinder? Or is it just a bit of a joke? I mean, I’ve swiped left and right, but I’ve never actually talked to anyone. It’s all just selfies and weird hobbies. Yeah, I tried it once, and the guy I matched with asked if I liked dogs. I said yes, and he replied with a photo of a poodle in a top hat. I’m like, “Wow, what a guy.” That sounds like a real vibe. I mean, who  doesn’t  like dogs? Honestly, I think it’s just a way for people to feel like they’re dating, but they’re not. It’s like having a conversation with a stranger on the bus, but with more filters and less eye contact. I get that. I think it’s just too easy to swipe and move on. You know, like, what’s the point of actually getting to know someone if you can just skip them? Yeah, and then you get into the situation where you’re like, “Oh, I liked their profile, but I didn’t even talk to them in real life.” It’s so weird. I remember my roommate tried Tinder and matched with this guy who said he was a huge fan of  the Office . We ended up talking for like 45 minutes, and then I found out he’s never even watched the show. That’s the worst. That’s so rude. I mean, you’d think if you’re into  the Office , you’d at least know the basics. Exactly! I think a lot of people just use Tinder as a way to brag about stuff they don’t even know. Like, “I love hiking,” but they’ve never even gone on a proper trail. It’s like they think their hobbies are more interesting than they are. I mean, sure, it’s fun to have quirky interests, but if you’re not actually into them, why even put them out there? I think it’s also about the ego. Like, you want to be seen as interesting, so you post the most random stuff hoping someone will find you cool. Yeah, and then you end up with someone who’s just trying to get a date, not actually interested in getting to know you. I think the real issue is that people don’t want to put in the effort.

I don’t know, I’ve been thinking a lot about the benefits lately. It’s just not the same as it used to be, is it? I know, I've been feeling that too. I mean, when we were working, we had some sort of stability. Now it’s like we’re just waiting for the post to come with the latest changes. Yeah, it’s a bit of a shame, isn’t it? I remember back when I was working, even though it wasn’t the best job, it was something to fall back on. Now, I just sit at home and wait for the money to come in. It’s not the same. That’s true. I used to think, well, I’m a civil engineer, I could do more, but now I’m just sitting here, and I think, what’s the point? I’m not even really working anymore. I just feel like I’m wasting my time. I hear you. I used to have a few bits of work here and there, but now, it’s like the door’s just closed. I don’t know what the future holds. Sometimes I think about whether I should just give up and take the money as it comes, rather than try to do anything else. I can’t help but feel a bit resentful sometimes. I mean, we’ve paid our taxes all our lives, and now we’re just sitting here waiting for the state to support us. It’s not fair. I think people should be given more opportunities to get back into work, rather than just handing out benefits like it’s a handout. I agree with that. But I also know it’s not about being resentful. It’s about being realistic. If you don’t have any skills or any connections, it’s hard to find work. I mean, I’m retired, but I still feel like I could do something. I just don’t know where to start. You know, I was thinking the other day about the TV programmes. I remember when there was a show called “Benefits Scandal” or something like that. It was about people abusing the system, but now I’m starting to think that maybe some of the people on benefits are just the ones who can’t help it. They’ve had bad breaks, or they’ve been made redundant, or they’ve got health issues.

So, did you get that meeting done today? I was just thinking about it, and it’s been a while since we talked about it. Yeah, I did. It was a bit of a mess, honestly. The client was pretty difficult. I think they were expecting something more than what we could offer, and they kept pushing back on the budget. That's always the way with some of them. I mean, I know you're not a big fan of fundraising, but I suppose it's part of the job. How's the team handling it? The team’s fine, but I’ve had to make some tough calls. I had to cut a couple of the smaller projects to focus on the bigger ones. I know it’s not ideal, but I think we need to be realistic. I get that. I just hope it doesn’t affect the overall strategy too much. I still remember when we first started out, how much we used to talk about long-term goals. It’s easy to lose sight of that when things get busy. Yeah, it’s true. I think I’ve been too focused on short-term wins lately. I should be thinking more about how everything connects. Maybe I need to take a step back and re-evaluate the whole thing. That’s a good idea. And I know you’ve been working late a lot lately. Are you making time for the kids? I know they miss you when you’re not around. Oh, they do. I try to make it every night, but sometimes the workload just piles up. I feel guilty, to be honest. I know I should be more present, but it’s hard when I’m constantly juggling a million things. I understand. But don’t forget, your family is your priority. If you’re not there, they’ll feel it. And I’m not saying you need to drop everything, but balance is important. You’re right. I know I need to adjust. I’ve been so caught up in work, I’ve lost sight of what matters most. Maybe I should start by setting some boundaries. I’ll try to do more with the kids and less with the work. That’s a good start. And I know you can do it. You’re a great parent, and you’re also a great fundraiser.

I can't believe it's already April. You know, it feels like it was just last week when we were all in the UK, and now we're here in Tarnow, stuck with the cold and the grey skies. I don’t know if I’ll ever get used to this weather. I know, it’s been so strange. I mean, I grew up in Bury, and I always thought that the UK had the worst weather, but I never thought I'd miss it so much. Especially now that I'm here and it's practically always raining. Yeah, I get that. I’ve been thinking about home a lot lately. I mean, the last time I was back in Cambridge was for the funeral, and I felt like I was walking through a different world. I didn’t know what to expect, and honestly, I didn't feel like I belonged there anymore. That must have been really tough. I can imagine how strange it would be to go back to a place you thought you'd left behind for good. But I guess that’s what happens when you get older, you start thinking about where you're from more. It’s weird, isn’t it? I still feel like I’m watching the world through a window sometimes, like I’m not really part of it. I mean, I’m still here, but I don’t feel like I’m living my life. It’s like I’m stuck in this limbo between being unemployed and not knowing what's next. I can relate. I was a teacher, and I had a good job, but the more I thought about it, the more I realized I didn’t  want  that life anymore. I wanted something different. I want to be able to travel, to live somewhere where I feel like I can belong. That sounds amazing. I’ve thought about moving, too. Maybe somewhere with better weather, like Spain or somewhere in the Mediterranean. But I just don’t know where to start. I’ve been looking at social media, and I see all these pictures of people living their best lives, and I feel like I’m always trying to catch up. I know what you mean. I think sometimes we get so caught up in our own problems that we forget to live. But life is too short not to try.

So, do you know what’s the deal with the tea in this pub? It’s like it’s been sitting there for hours. Honestly, I’ve had worse. I think the real issue is that it’s not properly brewed. You can tell by the way it’s gone cold so fast. I don’t know, maybe it’s the water? I’ve heard that some places in London use water that’s just not so great. Yeah, I’ve read that. Some pubs use tap water that’s been treated with chemicals, which messes with the taste. I like to bring my own loose leaf tea just to be safe. Oh, I’m not sure I’d go that far. But I do like to add a bit of milk and sugar to my tea, even if I’m not sure how it’s made. I guess that’s a matter of personal preference. I’m more into the ritual of it, you know? Sitting down, taking a minute to enjoy the tea, not just chugging it like it’s a drink you need to get through the day. I can see that. I think I’ve been more of a coffee person lately, but I still love a good cup of tea. Especially when it’s paired with something good, like a proper scone or a bit of cake. Speaking of which, did you hear about the new café that opened up on the corner? They have these amazing scones with clotted cream and a bit of jam. No, I haven’t. I should check it out. I’ve been meaning to get out more and try new places. You should. It’s a nice spot, and they even have a little corner where you can read or work if you want. That sounds perfect. I’ve been working from home a lot lately, so it would be nice to have a place to go and actually be productive. Yeah, I get that. I’ve been working part-time on these surveys, and it’s nice to have a little break from the screen. I’m glad you’re doing that. I think it’s good for the mind to have a bit of balance. Definitely. I’ve been trying to keep things in check, but sometimes it’s hard to resist the lure of the laptop. I know what you mean.

Alright, do you two want to get up? I’m still in bed. Me too. Well, we need to get up soon, because we’re going to the Neon Moon event this afternoon. What’s a Neon Moon event? It’s an outdoor festival where they have lights, music, and activities. It’s like a big party in the park. Can I have a biscuit before we go? Not before you get up, but after you’ve had your breakfast. What’s for breakfast? Porridge, toast, and fruit. I like porridge. Great, then you can have some. Can I have a glass of juice too? Of course. Are we going to have a picnic? Yes, we’ll bring a blanket and some sandwiches. Can I have a chocolate sandwich? If you promise not to eat too much, yes. I want to bring my stickers. That’s a good idea. Maybe you can trade them with other kids there. What time do we have to be there? The event starts at 2 p.m. So we need to be there by 1:30 to get a good spot. Can we ride our bikes there? Yes, but make sure you wear your helmets. What if it rains? I’ve brought an umbrella just in case. I like the idea of a Neon Moon event. It sounds fun. It’s going to be great. There’ll be face painting, games, and even a circus skills tent. Circus skills? Like juggling or tightrope walking? Yes, they’ll have little performers showing off their tricks. Can I try the tightrope? Maybe, if you’re brave enough. I want to try the face painting. That’s a good one. You’ll look like a superhero. I think I’ll get a unicorn face. That’s a great idea. Do we need to bring anything else? Just your sunscreen, a water bottle, and your smile. I brought my sunscreen. Perfect. Now, let’s get up and get ready. Okay, but can I have one more minute in bed? Only if you promise to get up in five minutes. I’ll help you. Deal. Alright, let’s get up. The day is waiting for us. And the Neon Moon event! I can’t wait. Me neither. Let’s go! Wait, what about the traffic lights? We’ll cross them when we see the amber light. I know the different words for colours!

So, do you remember when we were driving through Cornwall last year, and we had that long stretch of road with no signal and no shops? It was one of those days where you just stared at the road and tried to make sense of the map. Oh yes, I remember that perfectly. So, do you think we should go vegetarian? I mean, I’ve been thinking about it more since I read that article about the environmental impact of meat farming. You really need to make sure you’re getting all your nutrients, especially if you’re not eating meat. I heard about a documentary called “Curb Your Enthusiasm” that talks about how people’s views on meat can affect their relationships.

I heard the news today, mate. That new immigration policy is going to be a real pain for people like us who got here in the old days. Oh, I've heard about that. It's a bit of a shame, really. So, do you know what’s up with the new software system they’ve introduced? I’ve been trying to get it to work for days, and it’s like trying to read a book written in a foreign language. I once had an argument with a guy over whether Manchester United or Liverpool is better. It turned into a full-blown debate. I know, right? It’s like, what even is the point of being there?
