I’m watching way too much football, getting too drunk, and not studying at all. I get it. I’ve been there too. But you know, sometimes you just need to let go. I know, but I’m also worried about my grades. I feel like I’m falling behind. I can relate. I’d rather be out drinking than studying, but I know I need to make a change. Maybe I should try exercising more. I’ve been so inactive lately. That’s a good idea. I’ve been thinking about it too. Maybe we can go for a run together sometime. Yeah, that sounds fun. I could use a bit of fresh air. I’ll text you later and we can plan something. Sounds good. And maybe I’ll take a break from football for a while. You’ll be surprised how much better you’ll feel. I hope so. I just need to find my balance again. I think you will. And if you need anything, just let me know. Thanks. I appreciate it. No worries. It’s what friends are for. Yeah, and I’m still up for the occasional night out. Just not every night. Agreed. Let’s keep it light, but not too wild. Deal. Alright, then. Let’s go grab a coffee and talk more about it.

So, do you think we've got everything ready for the grandmother to come over this weekend? I’ve been trying to get the house sorted, but it’s like trying to solve a maths problem with missing numbers. I think we do. The place looks tidy enough. Just need to make sure the dog’s not chewing the furniture again. You know how he gets when he’s bored. I remember when I was a kid, the dog used to chase me around the garden like he was trying to catch a football. Now he just stares at the TV and snorts when I walk past. It’s like he’s forgotten how to play. Oh, the dog’s still got that spark in his eye. Just needs a bit of encouragement. Anyway, I was thinking about the football game we watched last week. Did you see the way the team played? It was like a masterclass in strategy. I saw it. It was pretty impressive. The way they controlled the ball and moved it around, you could tell they had a plan. I almost felt like I was back in the days when I used to watch those football documentaries. I used to love the way they explained the tactics. Yeah, I remember watching those too. But I always thought it was way too complicated. You know, all that jargon about passing, pressing, and defending. I mean, isn’t football just about kicking the ball into the net? That’s the thing, isn’t it? It’s not just about the goal. It’s about the whole game. You’ve got to think about the players’ positions, the way the team moves as a unit, and even the weather. You know, I remember once seeing a game in the rain, and the players had to adapt their tactics just to keep the ball moving. I remember that. It was one of those games where the team that stayed calm and controlled the play won. I think it was the first time I really understood how important it was to be strategic in football. I still don’t get it. Why not just run at the keeper and hope you score? That seems more straightforward. It’s not that simple, mate. If you rush in without the team supporting you, you’re just getting tackled. It’s all about working together, like in the oil industry when we had to coordinate the drilling teams.

So, do you think we've got everything ready for tomorrow? I mean, the flat's still a bit of a mess from the weekend, and I was supposed to do the DIY on the bathroom mirror. Yeah, honestly, I think we're mostly sorted. Just need to make sure the bin isn't blocked again, and we’ve got the new water company sorted. I had to ring them twice last week. That’s always a hassle, isn’t it? I remember when I was living in London, the water company practically ran the borough. You’d get letters every week telling you to use less water, even if you were just brushing your teeth. Oh, I’ve had the same thing here. I’m still not used to the different water tastes, to be honest. I can tell the difference between the tap water and the bottled stuff. Sometimes it’s just too hard. I know, it’s a bit of a shock. I used to drink a lot of bottled water back when I was in college, but now I just go for the tap. Though I still need to buy some for the weekend when we’re having family over. Yeah, we’ve got a couple of bottles in the fridge already. Also, I was thinking about the SAT NAV again. I still can’t get it to work properly. I tried to set it up on my Blackberry the other day, and it just kept giving me wrong directions. That sounds frustrating. I remember when I was younger, I used to try to do the same thing. I think it’s just the way the software is. You have to make sure you’ve got the right map and everything. I know, but I’m not great with technology. I still haven’t worked out how to use voice recognition on my phone. It keeps mishearing me, and I end up shouting at it. That’s not fun. I try to help, but I’m not very good at it either. You just end up with the same problem as before. Yeah, and I think I’ve got the same issue with the TV. I’ve been trying to get it to work with the new remote, but it still goes on and off if I don’t push the buttons just right. You know, I’ve got an old TV at home, and it still works just fine.

So, do you know what’s going on with the football results? I tried to check on my phone but it’s got no signal here in Tarnow. Yeah, I saw something about a big match last night. I think it was between Manchester United and Leeds. But honestly, I couldn’t tell you who won. I’ve been so stressed about my students and exams that I haven’t really been watching much. Yeah, I can imagine. You’ve got that pressure, don’t you? Especially with the exams coming up. I remember when I was teaching, I used to feel like I was responsible for their whole future. It’s a bit overwhelming, to be honest. My students are all so different, and some of them are really struggling. I’m trying to help them as much as I can, but I’m not sure if I’m doing enough. I get that. I used to feel the same in my early days. And the thing is, even though you’re not working full-time, you still feel like you’re managing a whole team, don’t you? Exactly. It’s like running a small business. You’ve got to be on top of everything. I tried working on a farm last week just to get out of the house, but I couldn’t handle the work. It’s too much of a change. I bet. I remember when I was working part-time in Cambridge, I used to walk past the farms and think, “I could do that.” But then I’d think about what I had to do at work, and I’d be back in the classroom in no time. I guess it’s the routine. You get used to the rhythm of teaching. But I miss home so much. I know that sounds silly, but I can’t wait to go back to the UK, even for a few weeks. I can understand. I’ve been feeling a bit homesick too, especially now with the weather being so gloomy. I’m not sure if it’s just the rain or if it’s the Seasonal Affective Disorder. Yeah, I think that’s it. I’ve been feeling pretty low the past few weeks. I even started reading a book about it, just to try and understand better. That’s a good idea. I’ve been trying to read more myself.

So, do you know what’s up with Lucy? I saw her last night and she was wearing this absolutely  ridiculous  outfit—like, a neon pink tracksuit with a sequined jacket. I almost didn’t recognise her. Oh, she’s been trying to be more “flirty” lately. I think she’s been on some sort of dating app. She’s been talking about it a lot. A lot. Yeah, I heard. But isn’t she a bit… old for that? I mean, she’s like, twenty-five. She’s got a job, a flat, and a cat. What’s the point? I don’t know. Maybe she’s just bored? Or maybe she’s trying to get back into the dating scene after her last relationship ended. Yeah, but she’s been so focused on looking good lately. Like, she buys all these trendy clothes and dresses like she’s going to some sort of party every day. She even dyed her hair last week—blue. Blue? She looks like a Hogwarts student. Oh, I know! It’s so out of character for her. She used to wear more practical stuff. Like, she used to work in a warehouse, remember? She was all about comfort. Yeah, and now she’s trying to be the ultimate fashionista. I don’t know if it’s working. She’s still single, and the only guy she’s been out with was just a guy from the café who was a bit of a weirdo. Maybe she just wants to feel confident again. I mean, I get it. When you’re in your twenties, you’re always searching for something. A man, a job, a place to belong. Yeah, but she shouldn’t be putting all that pressure on herself. I mean, she’s got her job, her friends, her cat. She doesn’t need to be chasing someone. She could just be happy with what she’s got. I agree. But I think she’s still trying to convince herself that she’s not boring. I mean, what’s the alternative? Being invisible? Maybe she’s just feeling a bit lost. I go out with my mates sometimes, and I think about how different we all are. Some of us are secure, some of us are not. And some of us… well, are just trying to fit in. I think that’s the thing.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about going back to China again this year. I’ve been teaching English there for a few years now, and I’ve got a few students who've really taken to me. I was wondering if you’d like to come along as a sort of cultural liaison or something. Honestly, I’d love to, but I’m not sure about the timing. I’ve got a few things on the go with my PhD and I’m still trying to figure out what my next steps are. But you know, I’d love to go back. It’s been a while since I’ve been there. I know, it’s been a few years. You know, I still remember the time I was teaching in Chengdu and I accidentally called a panda a "bear." You should have seen the look on the students’ faces. It was classic. They just laughed and then explained that, no, pandas aren’t bears. They’re their own thing. Oh, I remember that. I think you even got a few photos of that moment. I still have them on my phone. Yeah, well, I’ve learned my lesson. I’ve since started learning a bit more about the local customs. I even picked up some phrases in Mandarin. It helps when you’re teaching, you know? It makes the students feel more comfortable. That’s smart. You know, I’ve been thinking about teaching English as well. Maybe after my PhD, I could go back to China. I’ve got a few contacts there through my work. Though, I have to say, I’d be nervous about teaching in a place like Beijing. It’s such a different environment from Hull. Oh, you’d be fine. I think you’d adapt quickly. You’ve got that kind of energy. And besides, you mentioned you have a few Chinese friends. Maybe you could use that as a way to network. Yeah, I suppose. I mean, I do have a few people I’ve met through WeChat. One of them even invited me to a Chinese birthday party last year. I think it was the first time I’d ever been to one. That’s the spirit. You go to a few of those, and pretty soon, you’ll feel like you’re part of the culture. Well, I might just have to take you up on that offer.

So, do you know where we're going again? I mean, I thought we were meeting somewhere near the university, but now I’m not sure. I think we’re going to the new café that opened up near the library. I read somewhere that they serve really good coffee and it’s got a nice, quiet atmosphere. I thought it would be good for working on some reports. Oh, that sounds nice. I just need to make sure I bring my notebook and pen. I’ve got a few things to catch up on from the weekend. Didn’t you say you had a big project due? Yeah, I did. I’m hoping we can get some work done before the deadline. It’s a bit of a tight schedule, though. I’ve been working late a lot lately, and I’m starting to feel a bit burnt out. I can relate. I’ve been juggling a few things at work and trying to keep up with my studies. It’s not easy, but I’m managing. I think the key is to take breaks and not overwork yourself. That’s good advice. I’ve been trying to remember that. I’ve been so focused on getting everything done that I’ve been neglecting my health. I need to start taking care of myself more. I know what you mean. It’s easy to get caught up in work and forget to take care of yourself. I’ve been trying to make more time for exercise and even just going out with friends. It helps to have a balance. Yeah, I think you’re right. I should start making time for that too. Maybe we can go for a walk or something after we finish our work. It would be good to get some fresh air and clear our heads. That sounds like a great idea. I’m up for it. Maybe we can do that every now and then. It’ll help us stay focused and not burn out. I’d like that. I think it would be good to have some time together like that. It’s been a while since we’ve just chilled out without trying to do anything too intense. Definitely. I think it’s important to take time for ourselves and each other. No matter how busy we get, we shouldn’t forget to enjoy the little things.

So, do you know what’s up with Lucy? She’s been really off lately. She’s like,  always  tired and not really interested in anything. Yeah, I saw her the other day at the pub. She was just sitting in the corner, sipping her drink, not even talking to anyone. I asked her what was going on, and she just said, “I don’t know, I just feel so drained.” That sounds like a serious problem. Have you asked her if she’s been to the doctor? I tried, but she just said she’s not sure. She’s been so stressed with work lately. She’s been working extra hours and staying up late to finish projects. I’m worried she’s burning out. I know what you mean. I’ve been feeling the same. I’ve been working at the factory, and it’s just non-stop. I don’t get enough sleep, and I’m always tired. But I guess that’s what happens when you’re in a tough job. I know, but it’s not healthy. I’ve been thinking about this a lot. I read an article the other day about how people in our age group are more susceptible to burnout, especially with the pressure to keep up with work and social life. Yeah, and I think it’s not just work. Relationships are also playing a part. I’ve noticed that a lot of people in our group are starting to distance themselves from others. They’re not as open about their feelings, and it’s kind of sad. I guess it’s hard to be vulnerable when you’re constantly stressed. I mean, I’ve been trying to talk to my mate about how I feel, but I just can’t bring myself to open up. I’m afraid they’ll think I’m a drama queen or something. That’s not fair. You don’t have to be perfect. If you’re feeling something, you should talk about it. I mean, I’ve been there. I had this one friend who kept everything to herself, and it ended up ruining our friendship. Yeah, I think that’s true. You can’t keep everything inside. It’s like, you’re supposed to share your problems with people you trust. But sometimes, even that’s hard. I know. I’ve been thinking of talking to someone, maybe even a therapist.

I just got a message from Lucy. She’s been acting really weird lately. What do you mean? Like, she’s been avoiding me, and she hasn’t replied to any of my messages. I even tried to call her yesterday, but her phone was off. That’s not good. Have you spoken to her at work? Not really. I mean, we’re in the same department, but we don’t really talk much. She’s pretty private. Maybe she’s going through something. You know how some people are. I guess. But it’s weird because we used to be really close. She used to come over all the time, and we’d watch movies and talk about everything. Yeah, I remember. She was always the one who made sure we didn’t feel lonely. I miss that. I hope she’s okay. I just don’t know what to do. Maybe you should just give her space. Sometimes people need time to figure things out. I know, but it’s hard not to worry. What if something’s going on at work? Maybe. You know how busy things have been lately with the new project. She might just be stressed. It’s possible. But I don’t know what to say if I do talk to her. Just be honest. Let her know you care, but don’t push her. Yeah, I guess that makes sense. I just hope she’s not going through something serious. I know. It’s always scary when people start acting differently. I feel like I should do more. I mean, she’s my friend, right? Of course she is. And I know you’ll do the right thing. You always do. Thanks. I just hope she comes back to me. She will. She’s a good person. Just give her time. Yeah. I hope so. And if you need someone to talk to, I’m here. I know. I just… I’m really worried. Me too. But we’ll get through this. Yeah. I hope so. Let’s just focus on what we can control. And that’s being there for her when she’s ready. Yeah. I guess that’s all we can do. Exactly. Let’s make sure we’re ready when she is. Yeah. I’ll be here. Always. Thanks. I feel a bit better already. Of course you do.

Alright, do you remember the story about the witch who lived in the woods? Yes! I remember that one. She had a big cauldron and she used to cast spells on people who went near her house. But wasn’t she actually just a poor old woman who didn’t have any friends? That’s what the villagers said. They used to blame her for all the bad things that happened in the village, like the crops dying or the cows going missing. But she wasn’t really evil, was she? I mean, she just wanted to be left alone. That’s the thing, isn’t it? Sometimes people are judged for things they didn’t do. The villagers didn’t understand her, so they made her the bad guy. Like the story about the three little pigs? The wolf wasn’t really a bad wolf, he just wanted to eat them because he was hungry. Exactly! And the pigs were kind of lazy too. They built their houses out of straw and sticks, which weren’t very sturdy. But the third pig was clever and built his house out of bricks. That’s why he was safe. That’s right. So the story is about being smart and not giving up, even when things are hard. What about the tale of the little mermaid? She wasn’t evil, she just wanted to be someone’s wife and live on land. That’s a sad one. She made a deal with a sea witch to get legs, but in the end, she lost her voice and her life. It shows how love can be dangerous if you don’t think carefully. I think the point is that there are good and bad things in the world, but sometimes it’s not so clear. Exactly. That’s why stories like these are important. They help us understand the world and the people in it. So, what about the story of the Three Bears? The little bear was trying to find his home and the big bear was just being grumpy. That’s another one where the bad guy wasn’t actually evil. He was just lonely and had a lot of anger. I think we could make up our own story tonight. Maybe about a kind witch who helps people instead of hurting them. That sounds like a great idea. We could even write it down and read it to the other kids later.

So, did you get the footage from the school trip? I was hoping to see some of the stuff you shot. Yeah, I got it all on my phone. I've been trying to edit it, but I’m not sure if I’m doing it right. You know how it is with editing videos—sometimes it just doesn’t look as good as you expect. I know, I’ve tried a few times. It's so frustrating. I think I’m just not into it, honestly. I prefer just taking the pictures and leaving it at that. Mummy, can I have a doughnut? I’m still full from breakfast. No, not now, Mandy. You had one already. You need to save your energy for when we go to the gym. But I don’t want to go to the gym, I just want to watch TV. Look, you’ve got a leg that’s been hurting all week. Maybe you should just rest it for a bit and see if it gets better. Yeah, you should try some of those warm-up exercises I showed you. You know, the ones that help with the soreness. It might help you get back into the rhythm of running again. I don’t want to run. I just want to play with my toys. Me neither. I want to watch Doctor Who. Okay, okay, no running for now. Let’s just get you ready for bed. You’ll be fine tomorrow. Yeah, and don’t forget, the weather’s still cold at night. You might need a bit more of a blanket, even if you’re not going to the gym. But I’m not cold. I’m warm. Well, it’s better to be safe than sorry. You don’t want to catch a chill. And if you do, we’ll have to take you to the doctor again. I don’t want to hear about another trip to the surgery. Let’s just go to the gym and then come back and watch Doctor Who. Alright, but only if you’re feeling up to it. No pushing yourself too hard. Exactly. We’ll take it easy, just like the running machines. You know, the ones that make you feel like you’re actually running, but without the legs moving. I don’t like the running machines. Me either. I prefer the bikes.

So, how’s the new place doing, Dave? I heard you took over that café in Hove last month. Oh, it’s going alright, I suppose. It’s a bit of a struggle, but I’m trying to make it work. You know how it is—running a business in this day and age, especially with the cost of living going up like it is. I can only imagine. I’ve got a few friends who tried to start up small businesses, and it’s not easy. Especially with the cost of everything. Speaking of which, how are you managing with the rent? Honestly, it’s a bit of a tightrope walk. I’ve had to cut back on a few things, but I’m not complaining. It’s just life, you know? You’ve got to adapt and find a way to make it work. Yeah, definitely. I’ve been thinking about getting back into teaching, actually. The school’s been offering me some part-time roles, and I’m kind of enjoying the idea of getting back into the classroom. It’s been a while since I’ve done any real teaching. That’s great, mate. You’ve always had a knack for it. But I have to say, I’d struggle with the whole school system these days. Politics, unions, and all that. It’s a bit of a mess, don’t you think? I’ll say. I heard the Green Party’s pushing for more eco-friendly policies in schools—like making sure they’re using recycled paper and encouraging students to use public transport. It’s a bit of a lefty thing, but I can’t argue with the environmental angle. Yeah, I hear you. I mean, the planet’s in trouble, and if we don’t start taking it seriously, we’re all in for a rough ride. But I have to say, I’m not exactly a fan of the Green Party. They’ve been more into theorizing than actually doing something tangible. Fair enough. I can see both sides. But you know, I’ve been to a few boot sales lately with some of the lads from the old school. It’s a weird experience—sort of like stepping back in time. They still sell things like binoculars, old books, and even a few pre-war posters. That’s always a good laugh.

So, do you know what’s up with the plants in the flat? I was just in there and the potted fern has gone completely brown. I tried to water it properly, but it’s like it’s not even doing anything. I saw that! You know, I think it’s because of the cat. She likes to knock things over, and I reckon she’s been knocking the pot around a bit. Yeah, she’s got a weird obsession with plants. Last week she pulled out the ivy from the windowsill and tried to chase it like it was a mouse. That’s not just weird, that’s terrifying. What if she actually eats it? I’ve heard some plants are toxic. I know, I’ve read that. I’m thinking of getting some cat-safe plants. Maybe something like spider plants or something. Yeah, spider plants are safe. My mum has a few in her flat. I’ve also heard that snake plants are good for indoors and don’t need too much light. That sounds good. I’d rather not have to worry about the cat ruining everything. You’re not the only one. I reckon the cat’s got a little plot against the plants. True. Anyway, I think I’ll go and pick up some new ones tomorrow. Good idea. Speaking of plants, you know that fashion store in the city centre? The one that’s been closing down? They had a sale on second-hand clothes. Oh yeah, I saw that. I got a few decent items from there. You know, it’s about time I updated my wardrobe. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to get into that whole “minimalist” look. Less is more, right? I like the idea. Though I’m not sure I’m ready for that yet. I think you’ll get there. Anyway, speaking of fashion, did you see that dress I bought last week? It’s this dark blue one with some kind of pattern. Yeah, I saw it. You look really good in it. Thanks! I think it’s going to be a real statement piece. Definitely. You know, I’ve been thinking about getting a new jacket. Something more professional, but still comfortable. I think you should go for a blazer. It’s classic and looks good with anything. You know what’s funny?

I just can’t believe how much time I spend grading essays now. I mean, it’s one thing when you’re teaching, but when you’re also doing research and trying to keep up with all the deadlines, it's exhausting. I know, I feel the same. I think it’s just the nature of the job, you know? It’s like you’re always on call. But then again, I’ve been thinking about applying for that part-time role at the art gallery. It’s not going to pay much, but it might give me a break from all the grading. That sounds good. I’ve been meaning to get back into art. I used to love it, you know? Before I got stuck in lectures and administrative stuff. I watched a documentary about killer whales last night, and it made me feel nostalgic for the days I used to go to the seaside with my mum. Killer whales, really? You always said you were more into the sharks. But I guess they’re not as scary on TV as they are in the water. Although, I still can’t get over the violence in some of the shows we watch. I mean, it’s not like it’s educational or anything. I know, it’s just so over the top. I got into an argument with my colleague about it last week. She said it’s just entertainment, but I think it desensitizes people. Although, I will say, I can’t blame the younger generation for wanting to watch things that make them feel alive. That’s true, but I still think there’s a line. I mean, I can’t even watch some of the more extreme stuff anymore. I remember when we were younger, we used to watch all the Channel 4 stuff. We even had that blue Peter badge for being a “young viewer.” It was a big deal. Oh, I remember that! We used to collect them like stamps. I think it was supposed to encourage kids to watch educational programmes. But somehow it just became a collector’s item. You know, I still have my first one somewhere. Probably in the attic. I bet you do. I’ve got mine too. I think it’s in the drawer with my old homework. Although, I wonder if it even means anything anymore. I mean, blue Peter is still on, but the whole concept seems a bit outdated.

Well, I've been meaning to talk to you both about that hostel we've been managing down in Bury. It's been a bit of a nightmare, honestly. I don't know what's going on with the management, but the place is falling apart. Oh, I heard about that. I think they've been trying to get more funding, but it's not coming through. It’s not just the hostel, though – I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen the pictures of the new catering area? They've done some kind of "modern upgrade" and it looks like a glorified kitchenette. I haven’t seen them, but I heard the food supply has been inconsistent. From what I understand, they’ve been sourcing from some local abattoirs, and the quality has gone down the pan. I know one of the students had to go to the hospital for food poisoning last week. Yeah, I heard about that. It's not just the food, though. The cars that come in are a mess. One of the lads had a car that was over twenty years old and it broke down in the middle of the night. He had to walk two miles to the nearest town for help. That's not surprising, really. I know some of the kids – they come from families that have been working in these kinds of shops for generations. Their parents are hardworking, but they never have much money to spare. You don’t see much in the way of modern conveniences in their homes. That's true, but I think it's also about the education system. A lot of these young people didn't get the same opportunities as others. Some of them have been through the school system where the science and engineering subjects were neglected, and now they're expected to be able to maintain cars and manage small businesses without the right support. I suppose that’s part of the problem. There’s a lot of talent in these areas, but they don’t always get the recognition. I mean, I’ve seen some of the kids getting into engineering while still at school. I just wish they had more space to develop their skills without the constant pressure of the system. And don’t get me started on the mental health support. I go in there sometimes, and I see kids who are so stressed they can’t even focus on their work.

So, do you remember when you were in recruitment? I mean, I still can’t get over how much you used to know about people. It was like you could just read them in a second. Oh, I think I had a bit of a knack for it, honestly. I was in that industry for a few years, and it got to the point where I could tell what kind of person someone was just by the way they carried themselves in an interview. I mean, some people were just clearly interviewers in disguise, and others were the ones who really wanted the job. That’s impressive. I mean, it’s one thing to be good at it, but to be able to do it subconsciously? It’s like you had some kind of radar for fitting people into roles. I suppose it was more about intuition. I remember this one time, I was interviewing a guy for a sales position. He came in looking really disheveled, like he hadn’t slept in days. But he talked about the job with such passion, and he had this real drive—like he  needed  that role. I offered him the job on the spot, and he ended up being one of the best salespeople we had. It was kind of a gut feeling, honestly. Wow, that’s incredible. I guess it’s not just about the skills, but the  fit  of the person to the role. It’s almost like you’re matching their personality to the company culture. Yeah, and I think that’s what a lot of people miss.
